body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"pirut"} -->
_Requested by **JR** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01L5dz17X3Bx5u62FiTPjbDm?thread=cmsg_01L5dz17X3Bx5u62FiTPjbDmWuM5T8zY1e386huqtAc56a)_

## What and why

Follows #1. The horizon-accel Fabric mod now swaps vanilla 26.3's TERRAIN status (noise, surface, carvers) for Horizon's Rust on a real server, and it produces the same chunks block for block. It also adds the benchmarks that measure the swap:

- **Benchmarks.** `VanillaTerrainBench` (`mods/horizon-accel/src/bench`) runs vanilla's own statuses in-process. `terrain_bench` (`crates/horizon-accel/examples`) runs Horizon's through `Accel`. `tools/accel_bench.py` alternates the two. `tools/accel_pregen.py` times Chunky pregeneration on a fresh Fabric server for each mod set, and `tools/accel_world_diff.py` compares saved worlds.
- **The mod** (`mods/horizon-accel/src/mc`, built by `tools/build_accel_mod.py`):
  - A `buildTerrain` mixin.
  - `TerrainSwap` writes packed sections through `PalettedContainer.unpack`, plus the post-processing marks and the worldgen heightmaps.
  - `AccelMod` decides once per dimension whether to swap. It checks for vanilla settings and biome source, and for vanilla worldgen data using a registry fingerprint.
  - `MixinTargets` makes the conflict rule per method, so the mod runs beside C2ME and Lithium.
- **ABI 2** adds `horizon_accel_stage_timings`. The mod logs Horizon's time per stage every 4096 chunks.

**Results** (4-vCPU cloud VM; full tables in `docs/research/java-bridge.md`):

- Terrain alone: Horizon is 1.45× faster than vanilla on 1 thread (20.1 → 13.8 ms/chunk) and 2× faster on 4 threads (7.2 → 3.6).
- Parity: 768 chunks on each of 3 seeds come out identical to vanilla, including post-processing marks and heightmaps.
- Whole server, Chunky, 4,225 chunks: vanilla 52.3 chunks/s, Lithium 56.3, horizon-accel 55.9, C2ME 70.3, and **C2ME + horizon-accel 72.5**. The combination beat C2ME alone in 3 of 3 alternating pairs.

## Vanilla reference

`NoiseBasedChunkGenerator.buildTerrain` (26.3). Checked by the in-process parity mode, `HORIZON_ACCEL_MODE=parity` in VanillaTerrainBench.

## Self-check

`cargo test -p horizon-accel` passes, and so do `python3 -m unittest tests.test_accel_java` (JDK 25), `cargo fmt --check` and `tools/check_public_tree.py`. Clippy on horizon-accel is clean apart from the existing `manual_range_contains` in horizon-world. The full `tools/pr_ready.py` run hit its 15-minute timeout in this container.

body:
> The `playground` workflow fails on every push to `main` before its first step: "This request has been automatically failed because it uses a deprecated version of `actions/upload-artifact: v2`".

## Changelog Entry

### Fixed

- 👷🏻 Fixed the `playground` and "Download localization strings" workflows failing on deprecated `actions/upload-artifact` versions, in PR [#5953](https://github.com/microsoft/BotFramework-WebChat/pull/5953), by [@OEvgeny](https://github.com/OEvgeny)

## Description

GitHub rejects `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact` v1–v3, which fails `playground` on every push to `main` and the scheduled "Download localization strings" workflow (v3). This moves every remaining v2/v3 use to `@v4`, the tag the other workflows already use.

## Design

- v4 breaking changes do not apply: artifact names are unique within each run, no hidden files are uploaded, and downloads by `name` still extract into `path`.

## Specific Changes

- `playground.yaml`, `samples.07.{a,b,c,d}.*.yaml`: `upload-artifact@v4`
- `preview-branch.yml`: `upload-artifact@v4` and `download-artifact@v4` (2× each)
- `download-localization-strings.yml`: `upload-artifact@v4` and `download-artifact@v4`

Checked with `actionlint` (no artifact findings) and a YAML parse. `playground` runs on push to `main`, so it is verified after merge.

This PR adds the unique integrated assessment from the original stacked implementation: twelve Python reasoning problems, deterministic scoring, explanations, missed-topic lesson links, retry and a learning-path entry. For example, an 11/12 attempt missing recursive frames links back to Recursion. Results reset on reload and never alter reading or project progress.

The branch is reconciled with main cb75b85 and now targets main. Existing selectable traces, current lesson/project contracts, dynamic project routing, C++ practice, stable storage formats and regression suites are retained. The obsolete alternate six-checkpoint project and stack renderer are replaced by main's canonical implementations. KnowledgeCheck preserves the lesson understanding-summary callback while adding optional assessment capabilities.

Native Python independently verifies all twelve assessment programs, recursive return order and call frames. A callback regression failed on the original PR component and passed after repair. author: izkgmd
body:
## Incident
An Android browser showed **Creating APK upload session…** for a long time. User-provided Caddy logs proved it already sent three ~8 MiB multipart requests simultaneously; FPM showed 400 responses and Caddy reported 502 client disconnects. The empty progress bar was misleading because parallel mode never updated the status until the first part was fully acknowledged.

## Changes
- Set `Uploading APK…` **immediately after** the successful session start, before any parallel `fetch()` completes.
- Android/iOS browsers prefer 2 MiB parts instead of 8 MiB, reducing burst size on mobile; desktop keeps 8 MiB.
- Server negotiates preferred part length against active `upload_max_filesize` / `post_max_size` rather than trusting the browser, and validates discrete sizes.
- Display HTTP status codes for non-2xx JSON and HTML responses so operators can distinguish 400/502 from network failures.
- Regression tests for the false spinner, mobile preference, and PHP size-limit precedence.

## Verification and caveats
Source Docker PHP limits are 64M `upload_max_filesize`, 70M `post_max_size`, Caddy max 75MB, but deployed runtime may differ. Caddy's `client disconnected` does not independently prove a PHP size rejection. Live Android transfer throughput cannot be confirmed until re-tested. No changes to actual APK patch/sign algorithms.

author: n0tfr3shm1lk
body:
## What was wrong

`sketch.extend` did not extend geometry the way the preview promised:

1. **Nothing in the way.** With no curve to reach, the preview still drew the extension, but the click reported `nothing to extend to` — the line stayed exactly as it was.
2. **Arcs would not grow.** An arc could only be extended as a *new* arc, and it refused targets whose crossing point was already the end of another curve (the shared point of two circles), reporting that the target coincided with existing geometry.

## What it does now

| Situation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Line, nothing in the way | error `nothing to extend to` | the line grows to the end of the preview (`EXTEND_REACH`, 50 mm) and is held there |
| Line, another curve in the way | grew to the curve | unchanged |
| Arc, free end, geometry on the way | new arc added on top of the old one | **the arc itself grows in place** along its circle to the first geometry, and its end is constrained onto what stopped it |
| Arc, end already carries geometry (another curve starts there, or a constraint holds it) | new arc | **new arc**, as before — the existing end keeps its place |
| Arc reaching its own far end | gap closed by a new arc | unchanged |
| Arc stopping on a crossing point that is already another curve's end | refused | joins that point with a coincident constraint instead of laying a second point over it |

So an arc now produces one arc, not two, whenever its growing end is free; a new arc is only added when the end it grows from already carries geometry and therefore cannot move.

## Reproduction

Sketch with:

1. A line at `(0,0)–(10,0)` and nothing else → `sketch.extend` on it at `(10,0)`. The preview shows the extension; the click used to fail, now it extends the line to `(60,0)`.
2. An arc centred at the origin, radius 10, from `0°` to `90°`, plus a circle centred at `(12,0)` radius 10. `sketch.extend` on the arc run end at `(0,10)` → the arc now grows to the crossing at `(6,-8)` (sweep 306.87°) instead of refusing or adding a second arc.
3. The same arc with a line starting at its `(0,10)` end → the end is fixed, so the extension is a new arc joined to the crossing.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p solidcraft-engine --lib cmd::sketch_modify` — 103 passed, 0 failed.
- Tests updated/added: `arc_extend_grows_a_free_end_in_place_to_the_first_geometry`, `arc_extend_joins_an_end_that_already_carries_geometry_with_a_new_arc`, `arc_extend_stops_on_another_circle_or_arc`, `extend_with_nothing_in_the_way_adds_the_line_the_preview_shows`, plus the hostile-input regression case in `sketch_robust_tests.rs`.
- Branch rebased onto `main` (`edf57cec`) and force-pushed with `--force-with-lease`; no merge of `main` into the branch.

## Before
[Before.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0faf025-18bf-4eb5-844d-0daf443ddd66)

## After
[After.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ee1233c-bb58-4911-a932-bd800cafb1ad)


Fix #4615.

author: trieloff
body:
Part of #758 (kept open for ai-ecoverse/slicc-kernel#1401). This fixes three of its four items. The first item needs slicc-kernel; the coordinator has the ask and a minimal repro.

**1. `https.Server#listen` (kernel ask).** This is still `ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, and the docs say so; I didn't find a way to do it in jsh:
- `ctx.net.listen` has no `tls`, and `connect`'s `tls` is client-only.
- `@ai-ecoverse/wasm-tls-engine`'s server sessions only present a P-256 leaf that the engine generates itself (`tls_leaf_new`). They can't take a caller's `key`/`cert`, and they offer only `http/1.1`.

So serving `https.createServer({ key, cert })` needs a server session from the kernel (and the engine) that takes the caller's chain and key. The repro and the test that would catch it are in the coordinator's ask.

**2. `'connection'` listener and `allowHalfOpen`.**
- `net.Server` has its own `allowHalfOpen` (`options.allowHalfOpen || false`), as Node's, and the sockets it accepts take it from there.
- `tls.Server` has Node's `'connection'` listener, `tlsConnectionListener`. A socket emitted to it gets `'tlsClientError'` with `ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, or is destroyed if nothing listens.
- `https.Server` also gets Node's `'listening'` listener.
- `http.Server`'s `'connection'` listener is now named `connectionListener`, as Node's.

**3. Fetch-path headers: now Node's shape.** The issue's premise is slightly off. I checked on host Node 22.22.0:
- a `Headers` object is ignored (it has no own keys);
- `undefined` throws `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE`;
- `null` does **not** throw: it is kept, and sent on the wire as `a: null`.

`https.request` used to map a `Headers` object to entries and drop null/undefined values. Now it hands the headers to the `ClientRequest` untouched, the same as jsh's `http` path already did. The fetch send (`http-fetch.mjs`) also sends a `null` value as `null`, as Node's wire has it.

**4. `https-client.test.mjs` runs dist.** It no longer imports `src/`. Each row runs jsh's dist in the kernel, under a wrapped `node` command whose `ctx.fetch` is the row's fake, in the same style as `fs-fd-sync-failure`. It now has a NEGATIVE of its own:
- on #750's base (ea72ea04), these rows fail: "is an http.ClientRequest: finish, response, then close; an error, then close" and the headers row;
- on main, the headers row fails.

The kernel-dependent rejection row is gated on 1.124.0 and 1.124.13. All 9 rows pass on 1.143.5 and on 1.72.0.

**Golden `https-classes-node22`**, rerecorded on host Node 22.22.0, now also compares:
- the `eventNames()`, `allowHalfOpen` (and whether it's own), and the `'connection'` listeners' names of `net`, `net({allowHalfOpen})`, `tls`, `https` and `http` servers;
- the three header shapes.

On main, all 8 new lines differ. With this PR it passes, on 1.143.5 and on 1.72.0.

**Ran locally (1.143.5):**
- 34 `net-*`, `http*`, `https-*`, `supertest*`, `express*`, `cluster*`, `fastify*`, `tls*`, `ws*`, `got*`, `axios*`, `builtins*` goldens: ok.
- Integration `tls*`, `http*`, `net-*`: 76 pass, 1 skipped.
- Lint and unit diff coverage (100%): ok.

Also found, not changed here (#784): an array `headers` (`[['a', '1']]`) becomes a header named `0` in jsh's `http` and `https`. Node writes an array of headers raw, and `getHeaders()` is `{}`.

author: claysmith
body:
## What and why

Closes #834.

Depends on #837

> **This pull request includes all of #837's changes.** It is built on #837's branch (MIDI controllers, pitch bend and aftertouch reaching the instrument; a VST3 editor showing the wheels; the centred editor window on macOS; the live-input fixes), because #837 is on a fork and cannot be stacked. Its own changes are the commits after #837's: auto-arm itself, clip slots selecting their track, and audio tracks. Review #837 first; once it merges, this one shows only its own commit.

A setting, **Auto-arm the selected track**, on Settings › MIDI, off by default and kept with the app's settings (`auto_arm = on|off`), not the project. With it on, selecting a track arms it, so a MIDI controller always plays the instrument of the track in view, without clicking its arm button first.

- **Which track:** the one the detail area shows (`App::selected_track`), so a click in the Session view's headers or mixer, in the Arrangement's track list, and keyboard navigation all count. Several selected: the first.
- **Clip slots select their track.** Selecting a slot, empty or holding a clip, by a click, a right-click or the start of a drag, now selects its track too (before, only a click on a clip did), so the detail area and auto-arm follow it.
- **MIDI and audio tracks.** An audio track is armed as its arm button arms it: one with no audio input gets the device's first input (#682), an undoable change to the track, as the button makes it.
- **What moves:** it arms the selected track through `track.setArm` (Golden rule 6: no new command) and disarms the track auto-arm armed before.
- **The issue's open question, decided:** auto-arm disarms only a track it armed itself. A track armed by hand stays armed; selecting one that is already armed leaves it as it is and does not make it auto-arm's, so leaving it keeps it armed. A track auto-arm armed that is disarmed by hand is forgotten, so arming it by hand later keeps it.
- **Skipped:** a track that plays neither notes nor audio, a return, the main track and a group (anything not on a regular channel): selecting one leaves the arm where it is.
- **While recording** (a take open, in a slot or the arrangement: `Session::is_recording`), the selection does not move the arm, so a take is not cut off; once it ends, the track selected meanwhile is armed.
- **Turning it on** arms the track selected then; **turning it off** leaves the arm as it is.
- The window remembers which track it armed, per project tab. Arming stays playing state: not an edit, not undone, not saved.

### Overlap

#810 (MIDI input: separate monitoring from record arm) changes the same area: arming and monitoring in `crates/engine/src/live.rs`, ADR 0017 and `scripts/parity/score.py`. This change only *drives* `track.setArm` from the selection and does not touch the engine's arming, so the two do not conflict in what they do; the shared documents (ADR 0017, `score.py`) may need a small merge whichever lands second.

## Where the knowledge comes from

Own design, from issue #834; documented in ADR 0017 (inputs, arming and live latency) and the settings and recording specs.

## How to check it

Platform: all. A MIDI keyboard makes steps 5 and 7 audible; the arm buttons show everything without one.

**Set up**

1. Unzip the test build and open `suhina` (`suhina.exe` on Windows). Suhina opens with nothing loaded.
2. Click **File › New or open…** (Ctrl+N) and then **New blank project**.
3. Press Ctrl+B to show the browser if it is hidden, type `FM Synth` in its **Search** field at the top, and double-click the **FM Synth** result twice. You should see: two new tracks (columns) named **FM Synth**, each with FM Synth as its instrument (an instrument built into Suhina). Their **Arm** buttons, at the bottom of each track's header (a small ring), are empty: nothing is armed.

**Check**

4. Click **Options › Settings** (Ctrl+,), open the **MIDI** page on the left, and set **Auto-arm the selected track** to **On**. Close Settings (Ctrl+,). You should see: if a track was selected, its Arm ring now has a red dot.
5. Click the name at the top of the first FM Synth track (its header) to select it. You should see: its Arm ring fills with a red dot. With a MIDI keyboard connected, playing keys sounds through it.
6. Click the second FM Synth track's header. You should see: the second track's Arm ring fills and the first one's empties: the arm moved with the selection.
7. Click **Arrangement view** at the top (or press Tab) and click the first track's name in the track list on the left. You should see: the first track is armed again and the second is not.

7b. Switch back to the Session view (Tab) and click an empty slot (a box with no clip) in the second track's column, then a slot holding a clip in the first track's column. You should see: the arm follows each click to the slot's track.

**Edge cases**

8. *A track armed by hand stays armed.* Hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and click the second track's Arm button: both tracks are armed. Click the second track, then the first. You should see: the second track stays armed throughout, since you armed it by hand.
9. *Tracks that take no notes are skipped.* Click a return track's name (A or B, at the bottom of the Arrangement's track list; click **Show returns** by the ruler if they are hidden), or the **Main** track. You should see: the arm does not change.
10. *Not while recording.* In the Session view (Tab), with the first track armed by auto-arm, click the round record button in its first empty slot (a box in the track's column): it starts recording a take. While it records, click the second track's header. You should see: the arm stays on the first track. Click the slot's button again to end the take. You should see: the second track (selected meanwhile) is now armed.
11. *Off leaves the arm alone.* Set the setting to **Off** in Settings › MIDI and click another track. You should see: the arm stays where it was.
12. *Remembered.* With the setting **On**, quit and reopen Suhina. Settings › MIDI shows it still **On**.

Parity: chapter 17 (Routing and I/O) moves from 0.38 to 0.39 in `scripts/parity/score.py`: the armed track can follow the selection.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all                                        # passed
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # passed
cargo test --workspace                                  # passed, every crate
python scripts/docs.py check                            # passed, 93 documents fine
python scripts/rename_suhina.py --check                 # passed
python scripts/license_header.py --check                # passed
python scripts/parity/update_report.py --check-inputs   # passed
cargo deny check                                        # not run: Cargo.lock did not change in this commit
```

`crates/ui/tests/auto_arm.rs` clicks track headers and clip slots in the window as a user would, on the demo project with an engine rendered offline: off by default; selection moves the arm; a hand-armed track stays; a return track is skipped; turning it on arms the selection and off leaves it; nothing moves while a slot records, and the selection is armed once the take ends; the Arrangement's track list does it too; an empty slot, a clip's slot and a right-clicked slot arm their track; an audio track is armed. Each of the later tests fails without its change. With the feature's call taken out, 5 of the 7 fail (the other two check the setting off). The settings round-trip test covers `auto_arm`.

The app builds (`cargo build --release -p suhina`), but the steps above are written from the code and the tests; nobody has walked them in the window yet.

body:
Adds `MINUTES` (5 or 10) and `PAIRS` to the recipe B baseline driver, for the one-recipe page (TJ, 21 October: "proceed with one-recipe version").

Tab 4's 5-against-10-minute comparison, with Folktales' overfitting, needs the starter recipe at 5 minutes. A 10-minute run's 5-minute moment has no score and is still at full learning rate.

```
MINUTES=5 PAIRS="tinystories:own folktales:own" bash library/make_baselines_b.sh train
```

- Each length gets its own collection, `library/baselines-b-5min/`, with weights `b5-*.pt` and logs `b5-*`.
- The original-recipe speed check runs only for the 10-minute set. At 5 minutes, TinyStories with its own vocabulary is gated at 47.5% of the 10-minute run's steps (half, less 5%).
- Recipe versions are computed in bash, as `record.version_id` does, so a dry run never calls `uv`.
- The default (10 minutes, six pairs, speed check first) is unchanged. The tests pin it: a dry run lists the same seven runs.

Merge before the morning's 5-minute pair; not while `make_baselines_b.sh` is running, since bash reads the script as it goes.

Tests: `tests/test_make_baselines_b.py` (4, with a `uv` on the PATH that always fails); full suite 220 passed.

body:
Two docs fixes. No code changes and no release.

## 1. `turboquant-serve-vlm`: which `model` id to send

`docs/guides/vision.md` said to use "the id that `GET /v1/models` returns". That is unsafe:

- mlx-vlm's `/v1/models` lists every MLX model in the Hugging Face cache, sorted by name, not only the loaded one (`server/app.py`, `models_endpoint`).
- A request naming any id other than the server's `--model` makes mlx-vlm load that model, downloading it if needed, and when the id is another chat or vision model it unloads the served one first (`get_cached_model`; image-generation ids have their own cache group).
- Reproduced on mlx-vlm 0.7.9: `"model": "default"` unloaded the 29 GB Nemotron VL build, then returned 400 after a Hub 404.

The guide now says to send the exact `--model` value, matching what `docs/RESULTS_MUSE.md` (gotchas 1 and 3) already found.

## 2. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL ternary: sustained speed

The published 16–21 tok/s was measured with the Mac cool. Re-measured on 0.30.0, on a 16-inch M4 Max with one copy of the weights, with paths rotated per prompt:

| | mlx-vlm loop | mlx-lm loop over mlx-vlm's model | mlx-lm `nemotron_h` model | `turboquant-serve-vlm` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| short prompts, cool | 49.3 ms/token | 49.2 | 49.1 | 20.0–20.8 tok/s |
| 18K context, hot | 71.8 ms | 71.6 | 71.5 | — |

- Greedy output is identical across all paths, at 33, 4K and 18K prompt tokens.
- Speed depends on heat, not on the decode path: about 20 tok/s cool, 14–15 tok/s once the Mac is hot (after long prompts or about ten minutes of continuous work).
- The README, `benchmarks.md`, `models.md` and the model page now give ~14–21 tok/s with both figures.
- The 2× over 0.29.0 is unchanged; that A/B compared the two versions in the same thermal state.

The CHANGELOG has both under `[Unreleased]` → Fixed.

_Requested by **Aitchn** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Es63oUtLoP4eVAPbYu1Fo4?thread=cmsg_01Es63oUtLoP4eVAPbYu1Fo4EPzNabp6PGHXx2rii6bVnr)_

## Summary

T11, server side of the first-time setup. Design is in ADR 0012.

- With no account the API is **closed**: everything except `health`, `auth/*` and `setup/*` answers `403 setup_required`; `GET /api/auth/me` returns `{ "state": "setup" }`.
- On start the server writes a one-time code (`XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`) to `<data>/setup-token` (mode 0600) and logs it. A restart keeps the same code; a leftover file is removed when an account exists.
- A request typed **on this machine** needs no code. Local means: loopback socket, no proxy/tunnel headers (`X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP`, `Forwarded`, `Via`, `CF-*`), and a `localhost`/loopback `Host`. So a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel on the same host does not make the internet "local".
- `POST /api/setup` `{ code?, username, password, displayName?, vault: { id, sample } }`: checks the code (constant time; 10 wrong guesses per address per 15 min, then 429), validates, creates the first vault (optionally with English sample notes and a canvas), then in one transaction the server administrator, the default roles (`@everyone`, `Creator`, `AI user`, `Reader`), vault-admin membership and an audit entry. Signs the administrator in, deletes the code, answers 201. Afterwards `403 setup_complete`. Concurrent requests cannot both win; a failed attempt leaves no vault behind.
- `GET /api/setup/status` → `{ required, needsCode }`.
- New `--dev-insecure` / `PALIMVO_DEV_INSECURE` keeps the old open behaviour while no account exists, and is a config error unless the host is loopback (`127.x`, `::1`, `localhost`). The test harness turns it on by default; `test/setup.test.ts` covers the real flow.
- New error code `setup_required` (core + three locales; zh-CN flagged for review).

## Checks

- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` pass locally (Node 22 here; CI runs 24); `pnpm i18n:check`
- [x] Changeset added
- [x] ADR added (0012; 0010 updated)
- Tests: local request needs no code, remote (proxied, and a real non-loopback interface when the machine has one) needs the code, wrong-code throttling, default roles and membership, sample content committed in the first commit, code deleted and setup cannot be reused, three simultaneous requests → one winner, validation changes nothing, cross-site request refused, `--dev-insecure` refused on non-loopback hosts.

## Follow-ups

- Wizard UI is T14. The `Reader` role has no permissions yet; its "no writing" effect is a per-vault override applied when the role is given (T52/T53).
- `palimvo admin` CLI to create or reset an administrator without the wizard is not part of this task.
- #20 (T16)'s e2e starts a real server; it needs `devInsecure` (or the setup flow) once it rebases on this.

author: wainersm
body:
C00000 patches the Subscription with proxy settings, creates the trusted-ca
configmap and clears `AZURE_IMAGE_ID` from peer-pods-cm. The operator builds the
CAA daemonset from all three, so each of those changes — and each matching
cleanup — rolls the daemonset asynchronously.

The waits guarding those rollouts let the test return mid-roll: they compare
against the generation read before the test started, which the daemonset has
already moved past on the way forward, and they gate on `numberReady`, which is
satisfied while a node still runs a pod of the previous revision. Two cleanups
had no wait at all.

The suite runs C00000 last, so that churn lands entirely outside it. In the
post-phase chain the caa suite starts next, labels the live CAA pods with
`app=cloud-api-adaptor` (the label the upstream `getCaaPod()` hardcodes) and
then finds them gone, because the daemonset replaced them seconds later. Every
pod-VM assessment in that suite then fails with `We didn't find the CAA pod`.

## Changes

- `settle the CAA daemonset before C00000 returns` — add
  `waitForCaaDaemonSetRollout()`, which takes a caller-supplied baseline
  generation and waits for the operator to move past it and for every node to
  run an available pod of the new revision. Delete the trusted-ca configmap
  from the subscription cleanup: the operator mounts it for as long as it
  exists but does not watch it (`isConfigMapRelevant` covers peer-pods-cm and
  the feature-gate maps only), so removing it reconciles nothing by itself and
  a wait placed there would never be satisfied.
- `leave no podvm image job running when C00000 returns` — wait for the image
  creation job to be gone or idle. A job that reaches completion writes the
  image it built into peer-pods-cm, rolling the daemonset minutes later under
  whatever is using the cluster by then.
- `unit test the CAA daemonset rollout condition` — extract the condition as
  `daemonSetRolledOut()` and cover the states that decide it, in particular a
  daemonset reporting every pod ready while one node still runs a pod of the
  previous revision.

## Testing

Unit tests pass. C00000 was run end to end on an Azure peer-pods cluster; it
passes and leaves every tracked field (daemonset volumes and env, AZURE_IMAGE_ID,
trusted-ca, Subscription config, jobs) identical to the pre-run state, with the
daemonset fully rolled before the test returns.

A/B on the same cluster, running C00000 and then labelling the CAA pods exactly
as `run_caa_tests.sh` does, emulating `getCaaPod()` per node every 10s:

```
without this change                       with this change
t+ 10s  getCaaPod ok                      t+ 10s  getCaaPod ok
t+ 20s  getCaaPod FAILS on both nodes     t+ 20s  getCaaPod ok
        ... still failing at t+120s               ... ok through t+120s
```

C00000 takes 58s before and 93s after; the extra 35s is the rollout wait.

author: nathaelb
body:
W1 of `docs/specs/webhooks.md` (ADR 0007). The IdentityInstance carries a deployment's desired webhooks (`spec.webhooks`, `spec.webhooksRevision`, `spec.webhookRequests`) and the operator reconciles them against FerrisKey's admin API for ready FerrisKey instances, reporting `status.webhooks`, `status.realms` and `status.webhookRequests`.

Only webhooks named `autharie:<uuid>` are ever created, changed or deleted; anything else in FerrisKey, including a hand-made `autharie:foo`, is left alone. The human name goes in FerrisKey's description. A create is followed by a rotation, the only call that returns a secret, and the secret goes to Secret `<instance>-webhook-secrets`; it never reaches the status, a log line or an error message. Header values come from `<instance>-webhook-headers`; FerrisKey never returns them, so a SHA-256 fingerprint of what was last sent (operator-private Secret `<instance>-webhook-applied`) decides when to send them again. Rotation and retry requests run once per id and survive restarts. A realm that cannot be listed blocks its webhooks, so a failed list never causes a duplicate create. The status is patched only when it changes, with explicit arrays so an emptied list clears.

The operator also reads the newest 200 deliveries of its webhooks into ConfigMap `<instance>-webhook-deliveries` (no headers, payloads or signatures), which Herald will index. The view-only FerrisKey client for Herald in the first version of the spec was dropped: a master service account only gets rights on another realm through a role per realm. The token logic shared with branding moved to `ferriskey_admin.rs`, with a cached token refreshed on 401. RBAC: the operator gains configmaps get/create/update/patch.

Verified: `cargo nextest run -p autharie-crds -p autharie-operator-core -p genesis-core` 567 passed (planner, reconciler against stateful fakes, HTTP adapter against a scripted server including the deliveries route and a check that header and signature fields never come out); clippy clean; `helm lint`. Not verified: against a real FerrisKey; that comes with the end-to-end run after W2 to W5. `users/@me/realms` is the only realm list FerrisKey exposes; whether it returns every realm for the master admin is read from the source, not observed.

Based on #262. No issue exists for this.

author: zerocodefast
body:
Ordinary `rg` work was denied with `native_workspace_containment_executable_outside_roots`. Guard is meant to be silent on developer work, so a visible refusal there is a defect.

## What picks that route

Not the command. Every one of the refused shapes allows when replayed against the parent runtime on a host where `rg` resolves from a trusted prefix. The route is picked by where the executable resolves from.

A harness that ships its own tools prepends a vendored directory to the agent shell's PATH so its `rg` is always found. That directory lives inside an installed dependency tree and is named by the harness, for example `<prefix>/node_modules/<scope>/<platform-package>/vendor/<triple>/<name>-path`, holding exactly one file. `accept_entry` admits a PATH entry outside the workspace only when it is under a trusted executable prefix, under a managed home prefix, or when `user_tools::tool_root` accepts it — and `tool_root` requires the directory be named `bin` or `shims`, or be one of the two package-manager homes that hold their shims directly. The vendored directory is none of those, so the whole entry was dropped from both the accepted roots and the sandbox PATH. `launches_outside_exec_roots` then judged the program unreachable, and `workspace_contained::convert` renamed the generic review to the outside-roots reason code instead of calling `mark_contained`.

The same shape hits a `node_modules/.bin` directory on PATH outside the workspace: `.bin` is not `bin`, so that entry was dropped too.

## The fix

`user_tools::package_tree_root` admits a PATH entry that sits below a `node_modules` directory, granting the outermost such directory as the executable root. The tree rather than the entry alone, because a `.bin` directory holds links into the packages beside it and a grant of the link directory would not reach what the links name.

It is held to everything a named tool directory is held to: absolute, outside the workspace, never a parent of the workspace, outside credential folders and agent state, and sealed from `/` down so no other account can swap what it names. Read-only inside the sandbox, like every other granted root. `tool_root` itself is unchanged, so every directory it already refuses is still refused.

This is an admission rule, not a per-command allowlist: no command text is consulted.

## Regression cases

Four cases in `rust/crates/guard-command/src/restricted_pytest/launch_roots_tests.rs`, over `launches_outside_exec_roots` — the reachability check that decides between containment and the outside-roots review. They use a scratch root under the build directory rather than `/tmp`, because `/tmp` is world-writable and no tree built there can ever clear the sealing rule.

- `a_tool_directory_inside_an_installed_package_tree_is_reachable`
- `a_link_directory_of_an_installed_package_tree_reaches_the_package_it_names`
- `a_directory_outside_any_package_tree_is_still_unreachable`
- `a_package_tree_inside_the_workspace_grants_no_root_of_its_own`

They are in the unit tests rather than the deterministic benign gate because the shape is not command-plus-cwd reachable: it is decided by a PATH entry, which that gate's cases cannot vary.

## Proven red at the parent

The first commit on this branch carries the four cases alone, against parent `638043dcd1`. `Rust workspace (test-command)` on that commit reported `3523 tests run: 3521 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped`, the two failures being exactly:

```
FAIL restricted_pytest::launch_roots::tests::a_tool_directory_inside_an_installed_package_tree_is_reachable
FAIL restricted_pytest::launch_roots::tests::a_link_directory_of_an_installed_package_tree_reaches_the_package_it_names
assertion failed: !outside_at_home(&root, "rg", &search_path)
```

The two guard cases passed on that same commit, so they are not vacuous. The fix is the second commit.

## Verified and not verified

- Verified: the two new cases fail at the parent, in CI, with nothing else failing in that package.
- Verified: `rustfmt --edition 2021` on all three changed files.
- Not verified locally: no `cargo build`, `test`, `check` or `clippy` was run on this machine. The green result for the fix commit comes from this PR's CI alone.
- Not reproduced end to end through the hook pipeline: a faithful probe needs a native runtime binary paired with a command catalog from the same build, and no such pair was available here. The route was established by reading the code path and confirming the vendored directory layout on disk.

CI on the fix commit is green, `Rust workspace (test-command)`, `test-core`, `test-runtime-1`, `test-runtime-2` and `clippy` included.

----
## Summary by Gitar

- **Sandbox masking:**
    - Hides credential files inside granted `node_modules` trees on Linux, as it does for the workspace
    - Hides unlistable tree directories whole instead of refusing the launch
- **Link target sealing:**
    - Requires package directories that `.bin` links resolve into to be sealed from other accounts
- **Mask budget:**
    - Refuses launches whose package tree holds more credentials than the mask cap

author: nickolaj-jepsen
body:
Agents can now open the iRacing replay themselves when a run needs it, and close it again once no run wants it, so the sim no longer has to stay open for hours. It's all optional: without a `[sim]` table in `config.toml`, runs wait for you as before.

## What it does

- **Sign-in:** `livery sim login` signs in to iRacing once, in a throwaway Chrome or Edge profile. Each launch first checks the session with a cheap call.
- **Launch:** a run on the preview replay that finds no sim asks a detached host process to start one. The host does it the way the iRacing UI does:
  - credentials over iRacing's client-proxy socket, asking for a replay of an online session by its session id;
  - `start_protected_game.exe -ui_port -display_mode`;
  - then it answers the sim's `getTask`.
- **When a launch may happen** (`[sim] launch = "idle"`, the default): only after `idle_minutes` without keyboard or mouse input. Never on battery, during a full-screen app or game, while you hold the sim (`livery sim hold`), or while you're in the iRacing UI. `livery sim allow` lets agents start it while you're at the PC.
- **Closing:** only a sim an agent started is ever closed, and always under the sim lock, so never mid-run.
  - It closes once no run has wanted it for `close_after_minutes` (default 30) and you've been away `idle_minutes`. That's because a sim's exit brings the iRacing UI to the front.
  - A hold, or you in the iRacing UI, closes it after the current run.
  - A sim you opened is never touched.
- **Full-screen app or game:** runs stop at once and nothing starts, but the sim isn't closed then, since the iRacing UI would come up over the game.
- **In front while you're away:** an agent-started sim that comes up in front is driven until your next input.
- **Commands and tools:** `livery sim up` / `down` / `hold` / `allow` are yours. `livery sim status` checks everything a launch needs. `livery stats` reports the launches. `preview cameras --arm` closes an agent-started sim instead of waiting.
- **No re-checks:** the `[sim]` settings are read by `livery.simrule`, off the build toolchain, so no design needs re-checking. The toolchain hash is the same as on main.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** 604 pass. They cover the launch rule, the settings, the host's records and closes, and the `SimSession` paths, with a fake sim. A review subagent's findings (a lock stall, failure loops, orphaned sims) are fixed and tested.
- **Live test on the real sim, with the owner at the PC:**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| WM_CLOSE on the owner's sim | exited in 13 s and rewrote `camera.ini`; the iRacing UI came to the front |
| A `preview sim` that finds no sim | started it, waited through each phase, shot all five views. The first try failed on the credentials request (customer ids as `sess_carids`), which is now fixed |
| `sim up` | replay open in 174–283 s. A 400 × 220 loading window takes focus for about 3 s; the main window opens behind other windows |
| An old-code session's run (Fireproof) waiting on the lock | ran on the agent-started sim, then this branch's run did |
| The host killed | the sim kept running, and the next run adopted it |
| `sim hold` | closed the sim 6 s later |
| Idle close, at a 1-minute setting | closed 1 min after the replay opened |
| A full-screen game pausing runs | unit tests only: it would put a full-screen window over the owner's screen |

The measured facts are in `docs/sim.md` (Opening and closing the sim).

body:
Closes item 3.4 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-22-online-reliability-and-capture-feedback.md`, and provides the `npm run test:e2e` gate the plan asks for before tagging `v1.3.0`.

## Why
`test:e2e` was never run in CI, and it cannot currently run on the Windows dev machine: `wrangler dev --local` answers every Durable Object request with "internal error" there (integration tests fail the same way locally but pass in CI), and the fixture's spawn breaks on paths with spaces. author: necessarylion
body:
## Problem

In some cases a query never got an answer, so the Dart side waited forever:

1. **A value Dart can not decode** (eg. a timestamp out of the `DateTime` range) threw inside `_onBatch`. One batch holds the results of many requests at once. All results after the bad one were lost. Under load that is every request in flight.
2. **A request sent to a transaction after its end** (eg. a second `rollback`, or a query sent right after `commit`) went into the transaction channel. The task stopped after the end and dropped it without an answer.

There was also no timeout at all. Any hang was silent.

## Fix

- `lib/src/pool.dart`: `_onBatch` reads each record in its own `try`. A bad record fails only its own request, with a `PgException`.
- `native/src/lib.rs`: when a transaction ends, the channel is closed and every request still in it gets "the transaction is closed".
- Safety nets (cheap: one tokio timer per request):
  - a request with no answer in 5 minutes fails with a timeout error (same as `queryTimeout` of the `postgres` package),
  - connect timeout 15 s (same as the `postgres` package),
  - a transaction that Dart does not end in 5 minutes is rolled back, so its connection goes back to the pool.

## Tests

- 2 new tests in `test/native_test.dart`. Both fail before the fix (one times out, one crashes with an uncaught `RangeError`) and pass after.
- `tool/stress.dart`: many isolates, thousands of queries at once, single queries and bursts of 20, transactions, statement cache churn, bad values, random `pg_terminate_backend`, pool of 4. Any request over 2 s is a hang.
  - 5 min, `threads: 1`, 4 isolates x 64 workers: 7.1M requests, 937 kills, **0 hangs**
  - 5 min, `threads: 0`, 2 isolates x 256 workers: 6.4M requests, 920 kills, **0 hangs**
- HTTP benchmark, 1 core, `dox-pgnative`, 5 runs each: `/db` 38.5k req/s, `/queries?n=20` 2.65k req/s, **0 errors**. Same speed as before.

## Note

The rare 256-error benchmark run did not happen again in 30+ benchmark runs, before or after this change. These are the only paths that lose answers that I found.

**It is partly wrong, and the wrong part is the expensive one.**

| claim | accurate? | what the code does |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 补全模型**列表** | ❌ | `enrichModelsResponse` widens `GET …/models` — **the gateway listing**, not the picker. `mergeDiscoveredModels` has explicitly refused to add a row to the picker since the deployment that declared 4 models saw 86 |

author: michaelcarletta-cmd
body:
## Root cause

`handleStorageUploadUrl` (`aws/functions/api/storage-write.mjs`) ran under `withIdentity`, which opens a read-only connection (`default_transaction_read_only=on`) and always rolls back. When it presigns the official rear `.checkalt.jpg`, it calls `stampOfficialRearFingerprintIfNeeded` -> `stampCheckAltRearFingerprint`, which runs an `UPDATE public.check_intake_items SET endorsement_render_meta = ... jsonb_build_object($2::text,$3::text)`. In a read-only transaction that UPDATE always fails, so the rear presign always answers 503 `provider_rear_fingerprint_stamp_failed`. The bug has been there since ba1a5d0d5.

Production evidence (2026-10-22):
- API Gateway access log `/aws/apigateway/checksops-production-prep-http`: `POST /prep/storage/upload-url` returned **503** at 00:55:00.430Z (requestId `FnvDxjR6oAMEcEQ=`) and at 00:55:35.852Z (`FnvJThSFIAMEJWw=`).
- In the same attempt the front upload-url at 00:55:00.665Z returned **200**, and `front-1792613910986.checkalt.jpg` (244940 bytes) landed in S3 at 00:55:02Z.
- RDS log `/aws/rds/instance/checksops-production/postgresql` at 00:55:00 and 00:55:36: `ERROR: cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction` on the stamp UPDATE above.

## Fix

- `handleStorageUploadUrl` now uses `withIdentityWrite`. The transaction is read-write, commits on success and rolls back on a refusal. `data.mjs` already exports `withIdentityWrite`, both live and on main. The exports of `storage-write.mjs` are unchanged.
- SQL 89 already grants column UPDATE on `endorsement_render_meta`, and SQL 89 is verified live. No SQL prerequisite is added.

## Tests

- `aws/tests/api-storage.test.mjs` has two new tests, and all 25 tests in the file pass:
  - The official rear presign stamps inside `SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE`, then `COMMIT`, with no `ROLLBACK` and no `default_transaction_read_only=on`. This test fails without the fix.
  - A refused upload-url rolls back and commits nothing.
- `node scripts/validate-release-locks.mjs`: ok.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --test aws/tests/*.test.mjs`: 3298 tests, 3274 pass, 14 fail, 10 skipped.
  - The 14 failures are 13 PostgreSQL `*-pg` tests (`initdb: cannot be run as root`) and `AWS production SPA build hardening` (no Chrome in the container).
  - A clean checkout of origin/main a50dbbf55 fails exactly the same 14 tests (3296 tests, 3272 pass), so none of the failures come from this change.

## Overlay plan (mirrors #1124 and the #1116 re-pin of `providers/webhooks.mjs`)

- `ops/deployment-guard/production-api-overlay-plan.json`: `storage-write.mjs` stays a REPLACE member in its existing place in `order`.
  - `accepted_sha256` changes from `c397c522…` to `ccc72b14288580740bd57602543caaca558ba76d18c26c1bd5565c9841becf9e`, the sha256 of the LF file bytes.
  - `expected_live_sha256` changes from `9ef5843a…` (the release 2026-10-17 pre-deploy value) to `c397c52202b564917cd9d2b62853566c765b92aa6a8cd2304b6a09e74a3ed73f`.
    - That is main's bytes, unchanged since 062535491 and identical at fd1e059b5, e4daedefe, c92fe457b, 96361081c and 008af40e2.
    - `storage-write.mjs` appears in no section of `lambda-rebuild-plan.json`, because every rebuild inspect found it equal to main. So the full-package rebuilds left these bytes live in both environments (latest: staging run 39666390516, production run 39669873076).
  - `sql_before` stays SQL 94, which is verified live.
  - A note is appended to `notes`.
- New manifest `aws/tests/fixtures/production-upload-url-rear-stamp-manifest-2026-10-22.json`, which the plan row now names.
- The 2026-10-17 release manifest row and `ops/release-2026-10-17-lock-pin-deltas.md` are unchanged and stay as evidence.
- Not changed, because nothing needs it:
  - `.github/workflows/guarded-production-lambda-overlay.yml` already offers `storage-write.mjs`.
  - None of the changed files is a protected path, so no release-lock `tree_hash` changes and no overlap-allowlist entries are needed (validator and `computeOwnershipHashes` agree).
  - `lambda-rebuild.test.mjs` needs no change, because the file is in no rebuild section.
  - There is no staging overlay plan. The staging overlay workflow takes the member by name, as in #1124.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Nothing is deployed and no workflow is run.
- No SQL is written or applied.
- No release-lock change.
- No recorded evidence is edited.

## Not verified

- The RLS outcome of the committed UPDATE against real PostgreSQL. The tests use the mock client.
- That live production `storage-write.mjs` is still `c397c522`. The read-only production overlay inspect must confirm this before any apply.

## Deploy path (each step needs its own owner approval)

1. Staging: guarded staging Lambda overlay, inspect `storage-write.mjs`, then REPLACE against the inspected live hash. Then accept it in staging by uploading an official rear `.checkalt.jpg`: the presign returns 200 and `endorsement_render_meta` holds the fingerprint.
2. Production: read-only `guarded-production-lambda-overlay.yml` inspect of `storage-write.mjs` (expect live `c397c522…`).
3. Production apply of `storage-write.mjs` with the staging acceptance reference and the owner's exact approval `DEPLOY storage-write.mjs TO PRODUCTION`.
4. Record PR: `expected_live_sha256` records the applied bytes.

author: pedropacheco95
body:
## Why (a set-2 freeze blocker)
`deploy-prod.yaml` with `rollback_to` checks out the rollback commit (PAD-338), so `rollout.sh` and `.env.prod` are that commit's, while the ssh script lines are main's. Since #769 those lines pass `--probe-host`, and since #753 `--migrate`. The `rollout.sh` at **0ee4e837d** (promotion 16) knows neither and exits 2 on `unknown option`. Once #769 is in prod, every rollback to a commit before it stops before touching a container: safe, but no rollback. Found by reading, while answering H's rollback question for the promotion body.

## What
Both deploy workflows:
```bash
RO=/home/${{ secrets.GCE_USER }}/rollout.sh
opt() { if grep -qF -- "    $1)" "$RO"; then printf '%s ' "$@"; else echo "[deploy] this rollout.sh has no $1: not passing it" >&2; fi; }
bash "$RO" --name … --upstream … $(opt --probe-host <host>) $(opt --migrate) $ROLLOUT_MODE -- \
```
`--stop-first` (`$ROLLOUT_MODE`) has been in every rollout.sh since PAD-588. #784 (PAD-695) will gate `--worker` the same way when it rebases.

## Evidence
`test_b666_rollback_runs_the_old_rollout.py` takes each workflow's real `opt` line and invocation from the YAML and runs them in the stub harness (test_pad588's docker/curl/sleep stubs):

| rollout.sh | Result |
|---|---|
| at 0ee4e837d | exit 0, `--probe-host` and `--migrate` dropped with a log line, `<name>_next` started (it rolled) |
| current | exit 0, nothing dropped, `migrate yes`, the through-nginx request made |
| 0ee4e837d called directly with the new options (2×2 control) | exit 2, `unknown option --probe-host` |

Rollout + staging sync + B-666 + B-173: 53 passed. actionlint is clean on both workflows.

## Limit, for the promotion body (in the ledger; no workflow change fixes it)
An image from before #753 runs `flask db upgrade` in its own entrypoint (0ee4e837d `entrypoint.sh:5`). After a release that adds a migration (#758 `realtime_events`, #764 the rate-limit table), that image cannot read the newer revision: its upgrade fails, the container restarts, and the rolling deploy removes it while the current container keeps serving. **So rolling back to 0ee4e837d across those migrations fails safely, but fails.** From the first release containing #753 on, rollbacks work across expand-only migrations (the image boots "schema ahead").

Deploy-only change: no web or iOS part (ships-together rule exempt).

author: soncsec
body:
## Summary
Owner report (2026-10-21): holding fire with the machine gun through a stage's exit stopped firing when the next stage loaded.

Cause: every scene makes its own keyboard input, which only heard keys pressed after it started, so a key already held at the start of the next stage counted as up.

Fix (`src/systems/KeyboardInput.ts`): keys held right now are tracked game-wide (`keydown`/`keyup` on `window`, cleared when the window loses focus). A new scene starts with them **held but not newly pressed**, so held fire keeps firing (and held right keeps running), while a held key still can't skip a card or choose a menu item. After the pause menu, keys still down count as held the same way; keys released while paused are forgotten as before.

Also adds ROADMAP M7 (the owner's requests after v1.0) with M7.2 ticked and M7.1 (the R pickup, next PR) open.

## Test evidence
- New e2e test `pickups.spec.ts` › "holding fire with the machine gun keeps firing into the next section (M7.2)": fire held down through the exit and never pressed again. **Failed before the fix** (0 shots in the next section), passes after in Chromium and Firefox.
- `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`: passed
- `npm test`: 577 passed
- `npm run build`: passed; `npm audit --audit-level=high`: 0 vulnerabilities

## Roadmap

body: ## Summary The opening cutscene pans over a fallen legionnaire in fh_r1a: a skeleton lying in the grass with his sword raised in his hand, a second sword beside him and his round shield flat on the ground. In SiegeFX only a few loose arm bones showed, one sword stood up in the air, the other lay in the generic loot pose, and the shield was missing (later, on edge). This draws him as the original does. | | | |---|---| | **Before** | | | **Original game** | | | **After** | | ## Changes **Props placed in `special.gas` are drawn** (`RegionObjects.cs`). SiegeFX read static props from every region object file except `special.gas`, treating it as logic only. It is mostly logic, but the legionnaire's body is a dozen `frag_glb_bone_dirty_*` pieces placed there. `special.gas` is now a prop file like the others. The legionnaire's swords and shield are authored at 1.35x in a specific pose, and the hero is far off on the farm while the camera is over the body, so the shield was never drawn. Gold piles keep the loot pose. **Placed items are rooted like the original roots them.** Item models are authored Z-up like props, and the stand-up rotation lives in their bones, but weapons and shields carry a `GRIP` bone that isn't an `AP_` attach socket, so the prop rule left them in raw authoring space: the sword stood straight up and the farm's hoe sat askew in the hay. An item whose geometry all hangs on bone 0 is now rooted at that bone's bind pose. When bone 0 is `GRIP` and the next bone (named after the model) hangs under it, the item rests on that model bone's absolute bind pose instead. For swords, hoes and pitchforks the model bone is the grip's own frame, so nothing changes. author: mochael
body:
**Walkthrough:** https://diffmap.dev/g/1cd7a4f2effcb8f54977921aa0bbec67

Layer 4 of the local devices stack. Builds on #588.

## What changed

- **`tools.devices.shell.run({ device, command, cwd?, timeoutMs? })`** runs a command in the person's login shell (`$SHELL -lc`) on their computer. It starts in the home folder by default. The timeout defaults to 60 s, with a 10-minute maximum. Each output stream keeps its first 8,000 and last 24,000 characters.
- **Ask once:** the first command shows a native warning prompt with the command: **Allow commands** or **Don't allow**. It says commands run with the person's full access, since folder grants can't limit a shell. Return defaults to **Don't allow**. Allowing is saved and shown in **This computer** settings with Remove. A refusal lasts until restart.
- **Stopping:** each command runs in its own process group. When the agent cancels or the workspace times out, `DeviceService` sends `{ cancel: callId }` and the device sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 1 s.
- The agent prompt now says when to use device commands instead of the VM's `tools.bash.run`.

## Verification

- `DeviceShell.test.ts`: 6 tests pass (16 in the package). They cover prompting once, refusal, working folders, killing a background child on timeout, cancellation, and output limits.
- `DeviceService.test.ts`: 5 pass, including cancel on timeout and abort.

- Electron E2E: 2 pass, the file test and the new command test.
- Live on the VM with `pnpm dev` and the real model: the agent ran `node --version; hostname` after the real prompt and answered correctly. A second command didn't prompt. Screenshots are in the walkthrough.

body:
## What and why
`egress._query_kinds` skipped every kind for a query value made only of ASCII digits. The intent was that a number (an epoch time, a page size) is not a phone number. The side effect: a 12-digit AWS account id in a query string passed the check.

Each query value's kinds are now found like any other text's. Only `PHONE` is dropped when the value is only ASCII digits; `ACCOUNTID` and every other kind still block. #113 already applies the same rule to a structured body's values.

The change is small: `_query_kinds` in `src/warden/egress.py`. `redaction.py` is untouched.

## How it was tested

- [x] A test for the change: `test_a_digit_only_query_value_is_excused_from_phone_only`. A 10-digit page size passes; an account id in a GitHub search query is refused with ACCOUNTID. It fails without the fix. The existing epoch-time query test still passes.
- [x] Plant checks:
  - main's blanket exemption fails the account case;
  - no exemption fails the number cases (2 tests).
- [ ] `docs/FAILURE-MODES.md`: not needed. This narrows an exemption inside an existing guard; no new failure mode.
- [x] No secrets, account ids, emails or real-looking tokens; the test's account id is the existing `ACCOUNT` canary, built from parts. No new suppression.
- [x] Nothing planned is described as built.

Local full suite on f50f4a0 (main 4f01b40 merged): 0 new failures against main's baseline, apart from 5 Temporal workflow tests from #182. They fail here only with NOTEMPORAL, because this sandbox has no Temporal test server; CI runs them. ruff, `check_publishable` and the complexity check are clean.

## What this does not prove
- A query value that is a phone written only in ASCII digits (for example `4155550100`) still passes as a number, by design. A phone written with `+`, spaces or dashes is still refused.
- CI and Sonar run on this PR. CodeRabbit was not triggered by hand.

author: blakebauman
body:
## Summary
A denied tool card says who denied it, and when, by matching it back to the decided `/approvals` row (`src/lib/denials.ts`). The match was by order: the n-th denied call of a tool is paired with the n-th denied row for it, and nothing is paired when the counts disagree. Its own comment explained why: *"the audit row's `tool_call_id` is not on the approval"*. Since harness 0.15 it is.

- **`ApprovalRequest.tool_call_id`** is now modelled. It's optional, because older harnesses don't send it. It also drops off `check-payload-shapes`' "nothing models this" list.
- **`matchDenials`** first pairs each row with the card whose `callId` it names, as long as the tool names agree. Only what's left is paired by order, and still only where the remaining counts agree. This fixes two failures of the order rule:
  - Rows created in a different order from the cards were paired with the wrong cards.
  - When the counts disagreed (an abandoned branch, a row past the read's limit), every card of that tool got no record at all.
- **Cards rebuilt from the session log** now keep the call id (`callId: tc.id`), as live cards always have. Without that, the exact match would be lost on every reload.
- CLAUDE.md's description of the matching is updated.

This is item 7 of the chat-ui ↔ harness parity audit, and the last in Phase 2.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/denials.test.ts`: four new cases (an exact match beats the order rule; matching by id even where the counts disagree; falling back to order for what's left; never matching across tools)
- [x] `packages/felix-client/tests/session-log.test.ts`: a rebuilt card keeps its call id
- [x] Workspace `check-types`, `lint` and `test` pass (chat-ui 1465, client 364, tui 0 failures), plus `check-payload-shapes`

author: ochnikbartek
body:
## Summary

**Check with evals** on the authoring assistant's suggestions can run on one of the agent's eval suites. Until now it showed only the run's comparison verdict, not what the suite itself would have said. A person who picks a suite expects that answer, because it is what the suite will say once the change is published.

A check made on a suite now keeps the suite and its threshold as they were when it started. Once the run completes, the run shows whether the suite would have **passed**, **failed** or found it **inconclusive**, and why, worded as the suite's own results are.

Closes #2314

## Behaviour

- **Recording the suite.** An agent, skill or context check that names `suite_id` stores a snapshot of the suite on its eval run when it starts: `{suite_id, name, threshold}` in the new column `eval_runs.suite_check`. The suite is read once, through `EvalSuiteService.get`, for both the run's dataset and environment and the snapshot, so the existing access check applies and all three values come from the same moment.
- **Reading the verdict.** `GET /eval-runs/{id}` returns `suite_check` for a completed run. Its `status` comes from `EvalSuiteResultStatus` and it carries the `ThresholdReason`s, judged by the same `eval_suite_threshold.judge` that `EvalSuiteService._settle` uses:
  - the threshold from the snapshot;
  - the candidate's summary;
  - the comparison with the baseline;
  - the real number of ungraded cases.

  A run that is still going, or ended without completing, has `status: null`. `suite_exists` says whether the suite is still there under the run's agent.
- **Nothing is written to the suite.** The check creates no `EvalSuiteResult`, appears in no suite's history and notifies nobody. Accept and the model-change gate from #2329 still go by the run's own confirmed-flip verdict, so this verdict is information only.
- **Console.** The run page shows the verdict under the run's header. Beside the batch's "Check run N" links, each of the three latest checks made on a suite shows its verdict; this is limited to readers of runs, the same people who can open the link. Each verdict is a read of its run, so a batch with many checks does not read them all. The suite's name links to the agent's suites only while that suite exists, and otherwise shows the name from the snapshot. A check on a dataset shows nothing new.
- **Schemas.** The threshold, its reasons, the snapshot and the verdict read live in `app/schemas/eval_threshold.py`. The run's read now carries them, and the suite schemas already import the run's, so this breaks the import cycle. `app/schemas/eval_suite.py` re-exports the moved types, so existing imports keep working.

## Decisions

The coordinator approved the plan with these decisions:
- **D1 – snapshot on the eval run, not on the batch.** Skill and context checks have no batch, so the snapshot lives on the run to cover all three kinds of check. This differs from the issue's proposal.
- **D2 – frozen threshold.** The threshold is frozen when the check starts.
- **D3 – computed on read.** The verdict is computed when the run is read, not stored, so a person's later decision on a score changes it, the way it changes the run's `outcome`. It is computed only on the single-run read, like `draft_changed`, and the console polls only runs still in progress. A completed run is therefore judged once per page load. Review suggested caching it when the run closes; that is left for a later change if it ever shows up as cost.
- **D4 – completed runs only.** A run that did not complete gets no verdict.

## Migration

`0157_eval_run_suite_check` revises `0156_authoring_agent_parts`. It adds one nullable JSONB column, with no backfill and no foreign key; the snapshot outlives the suite. The downgrade drops the column.

## Verification

- **Backend:** `make test` gave 15222 passed, 30 skipped, 100.00% platform coverage.
- **Frontend:** `make test-frontend-cov` gave 9157 passed; 100% statements, lines and functions, 98.19% branches.
- **Checks:** `make lint`, `make docs-build` (strict) and `alembic check` all pass.
- **Integration tests:**
  - the snapshot keeps the name and threshold after both are changed;
  - a failing run reads `failed` with `pass_rate_below`;
  - a deleted suite gives `suite_exists: false`;
  - a check on a dataset has no `suite_check`;
  - no `EvalSuiteResult` and no notification are written;
  - skill and context checks record the suite;
  - another organization's suite and check read as missing (security).
- **Unit tests:** ungraded cases make the run `inconclusive`; a running, failed or cancelled run has no verdict; a suite id belonging to another agent is not offered to open.
- **Vitest:** the verdict component, the batch verdicts (including their absence without `runs:view`), and the run page line.
- **Review session:** APPROVE at d076cd49f. The Codex fixes after it, the single suite read and the latest-three limit, are covered by an assertion and a vitest case.

Docs: in en, pl, de and es, `authoring.md` (Check with evals) and `evals.md` (what a result must meet) now describe the suite verdict.

author: allpro244
body:
Builds on #423 (it includes #423's commits; its own diff shrinks once #423 merges).

**Houses are real**
- A homebuilder's house is queued on the town's delivery queue (`supply.ts` source "homes").
- It joins the multifamily stock the month it is finished, and stands on its lot as a built house (`built.house`).
- Once a family closes, it is an ordinary house on the market again, and resells like the inner ring's houses.
- `renderView` draws houses and their frames with `deco: "house"`.
- Unreal parses `deco` and lays the house mesh. While a house goes up it gets a site fence and no tower crane. The BroadwayWall module builds (UE 5.8, Development Editor).

**Homebuilders keep books**
- Each starts with founding capital and an AD&C line at a real construction desk. The desk advances 75% of lot cost and 85% of house draws, the interagency supervisory LTV limits.
- Interest is paid from the builder's cash, and the loan is repaid at each closing.
- The debt is on the desk's loan book (`loanbook.ts`).
- A builder short of cash for three months fails. Its desk sells the builder's houses and lots to another builder 25% under market value and charges the shortfall as a loss (`chargeLenderLoss`). Its takedown contracts with the player become void.

**A&D loan for the player's streets** (`adloan.ts`)
- Up to 75% of the finished lots' value and 75% of cost, at the loan index + 2.4, for 36 months.
- Each lot sold pays a 120% release price.
- At maturity: one extension, then the desk takes the remaining lots.
- The loan is netted in net worth and shows on the desk's book.
- Street listings of financed lots are refused.

**Tests:**
- `homebuild.mjs` covers:
  - platting on the loan;
  - the net-worth identity with the loan included;
  - the sell-out repaying the loan;
  - a drained builder failing, with its desk taking a loss and another builder taking its houses;
  - a sold house standing in the stock and on the render view.
- `render-view.mjs`, `landdev`, `rng-audit` and region `conserve` (seed 11, 240 months) pass with $0 unexplained.

## 번들 46 — 코드 검사 규칙 `java.declarationOrder` (설계 29)

번들 45 가 우리 저장소에 켠 Checkstyle `DeclarationOrder`(Java Code Conventions 3.1.3)를 도구의 「코드 검사」 규칙으로도 넣는다. 지적만 한다(자동 수정은 다음 설계). 기본 등급 info, 접근자 순서도 본다. 프로필 `codecheck.rules` 의 `java.declarationOrder: { params: { ignoreModifiers: true } }` 로 접근자 순서를 끈다(사용자 2026-10-21).

| 청크 | 무엇을 닫나 | 걸리는 축 | 강제 지점 |
|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | `design/29-bundle46.md` + PLAN 번들 표·분할표 다섯 | docs | doc-lint |
| 5-32a | `rules.yaml` 항목 + `JavaRules.order` 상태기계(Checkstyle 13.4.2 실측 기반) + 픽스처 `PosOrder`·`NegOrder` + `java.json` 8줄 · 규칙 수 85 | corpus(규칙) | `JavaRulesTest`(음성 0·양성 전부·골든) · `CheckRulesTest` 85 |
| 5-32b | 가장자리 픽스처 둘(익명·enum 상수·record·지역·중첩·접근자 리셋) + `ignoreModifiers` 골든 + 우리 코드 음성 | corpus(규칙) | `declarationOrderIgnoreModifiers` · `ownSourcesAreInOrder` |
| 5-32c | `ProfileStore.saveCodeCheck` 가 손으로 적은 `{params}` 덮어쓰기를 켬·끔 저장 뒤에도 지킨다 | java | `ProfileStoreTest.saveCodeCheckKeepsParams` |
| 5-32d | corpus 골든 `check-{egov,commons,jspwiki,roller}` — 새 키·히트 목록 추가만 | corpus | `CheckCorpusTest` |
| 5-32e | checkstyle 12.3.1 test 의존성 + `DeclarationOrderCorpusTest` — 표본 13 원천 Java 전부를 두 엔진으로 맞대 차이를 B baseline 으로 | corpus · db(pom) | `DeclarationOrderCorpusTest`(`@Tag corpus`) |

**새 의존성**: test 스코프 `com.puppycrawl.tools:checkstyle:12.3.1`(slf4j-simple·doxia 둘 제외). 판은 `checkstyle.version` 속성 하나로 0-61e 플러그인과 공유. `m2/` 에 이미 있어 `offline-build.sh` 초록(받기 없음).

**차이 비교 결과**: 못 읽은 파일 0 · `ignoreModifiers` 차이 0 · 기본 모드 105줄(표본 1.46%, 2% 상한 안) — 전부 「우리만」. 105줄 모두 Checkstyle 의 이름 일치 면제다 — 접근자 역순 필드의 초기화식에 그 클래스 필드 이름과 같은 IDENT 가 들면 접근자 지적을 안 낸다(예 `ByteOrderMark.UTF_8 = new ByteOrderMark(StandardCharsets.UTF_8…)`). 플랜이 흉내를 금했다 → baseline 에 두고 새 행 **5-33**(사용자 고르기: 그대로 / 이름 면제 / 진짜 전방 참조만 면제).

**계획 밖**: 가지 `work/2026-10-22`(플랜은 `work/2026-10-21b`) · `VcsCorpusTest` 골든 `vcs-egov.json` 지적 수 갱신(플랜이 놓친 골든, 건수만 늘어남).

**검증**: 빠른 verify · `--corpus` · `--db` 초록 · `gate-probe.sh` 산다 10 · 독립 리뷰 결함 0(시험 구멍 둘 고침 — Checkstyle 쪽 경로 불일치를 차이로 남김 · 우리 코드 음성에 parseError 같이 켬).

머지 위임 없음.

author: 0xshug0
body:
## Changes

Both optimizations are opt-in; with neither option supplied, the existing execution path is preserved.

Only two optimizations are retained:

1. **Causal AudioVAE tiling:** decode bounded windows with the full causal receptive field, using the existing StreamingAudioController and session-owned decoder graph. Default `voxcpm2.audiovae_tile_frames=0` preserves full decoding, matching main. Set 128 to opt into tiling. Recomputing causal context can slow CPU decoding, so tiling is not enabled automatically. Focused validation preserves byte-identical output while reducing peak VRAM.
2. **Opt-in packed QKV and gate/up projections:** use the existing PackedLinearWeightsBuilder without changing weight dtype. Enable with `voxcpm2.perf_mode=optimized`; default remains `off`. Packing changes numerical results and can change generated audio, so it is not enabled by default.

Packing uses the existing framework builder. There are **no framework, GGML, or unit-test changes** in this PR. Specs, CLI help, documentation, and legacy embedded-spec handling cover both options. No precision changes, asynchronous CFM changes, or unrelated model optimizations are included.

## Validation

Debug C++17, CUDA RTX 5090, Q8_0, eight threads, sequential measurements with logs and `session.wall_ms`. Existing GGUF with its embedded spec, no remitting.

### Isolated packing A/B

Both variants disable VAE tiling. Fifty texts across five languages, two seeds each: **100 matched pairs**, plain TTS and three reference voices, 52-1159 characters. Guidance 2, ten diffusion steps, retries disabled. Generated audio ranges from approximately 5 to 83 seconds. Separate saved main and branch binaries were used; all 15 main-versus-packing-off control WAVs are byte-identical.

| Metric | Packing off | Packing on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean warm RTF | 0.13032 | 0.10982 |
| Total generation time | 288.028 s | 244.354 s |
| Maximum session peak VRAM | 9064 MiB | 8856 MiB |

RTF decreases **15.7%**, approximately **1.19x throughput**; total generation time decreases 15.2%. VRAM varies with generated length and full-VAE graph capacity; this is not evidence that packing itself reduces memory. Some individual language sessions use more VRAM with packing.

Whisper large-v3-turbo scores all 200 unique outputs; Whisper medium additionally checks both variants for all 20 pairs with changed error counts. Chinese simplified/traditional spelling is normalized.

| Language | Metric | Packing off | Packing on |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| English | WER | 0.078% | 0.078% |
| Chinese | CER | 0.781% | 0.781% |
| Japanese | CER | 2.915% | 2.405% |
| Korean | CER | 0.000% | 0.146% |
| Spanish | WER | 0.153% | 0.305% |

Primary recognition scores: 11 pairs worse, 80 tied, nine better. The second recognizer agrees on six worse and three better cases. These are mixed aggregate results with individual regressions, not proof of quality equivalence. **Packing therefore remains opt-in.** All 30 within-mode lifecycle repeats are byte-identical after length/reference changes.

### Tiling and supporting checks

Earlier focused Q8 checks measured peak VRAM falling from **6618 to 4428 MiB (33.1%)** with tiling alone, with essentially unchanged RTF and byte-identical WAVs. Another longer session measured 7592 to 4502 MiB, also with identical outputs. CPU/Vulkan and streaming smoke checks, BF16/original-package checks, and forced small-tile checks passed. These are focused checks, separate from the fresh 100-pair packing evaluation above.

### Scope cleanup validation

The scaled inference results above were collected before removing the loading-only deferred-upload extension. After removing all framework changes, a fresh Debug C++17 build and focused warmup/short/long requests in both modes produce six WAVs byte-identical to the corresponding saved outputs. The full 100-pair evaluation was not repeated for this loading-only cleanup.

Using the existing packed-weight builder increases temporary peak host RSS during loading: the focused final-code run measures **1002 MiB off versus 2033 MiB packed**. This trade-off is accepted to keep the PR model-local. The removed deferred-upload optimization is not part of this PR.

No claim of perceptual or speaker-similarity equivalence is made.

### Default-path confirmation

After changing the tiling default to zero, the rebuilt Debug C++17 CLI was run with neither new session option supplied, using the existing GGUF and its embedded contract. Warmup, short plain TTS, and long voice-clone WAVs all match saved main outputs byte-for-byte. Runtime defaults, spec, help, and documentation agree: `audiovae_tile_frames=0`, `perf_mode=off`. Current main adds only a MioTTS-local change since that baseline; VoxCPM2 and shared code are unchanged.

author: matthewmaker
body:
## What changes

Bumps `plugin.json` from 0.8.0 to 0.9.0 and moves the `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entries under `## [0.9.0] - 2026-10-21`. The new section opens with a short paragraph naming the two changes that can affect an existing install. Three blank lines that had split the Changed list are also removed.

After this merges, CI's `release` job tags `v0.9.0` and publishes a GitHub Release with that section as its notes. Installed copies pick it up on `claude plugin update`.

## What's in 0.9.0

- PR 9: settings are parsed by structure. Fenced samples grant nothing, only the frontmatter is read, and YAML comments are dropped.
- PR 10: project approval lists no longer need confirmation.
- PR 11: SKILL.md split. Write rules move to `references/jira-writes.md`, and session start names the skill.
- PR 12: `SubagentStart` hook injects settings into `atlassian-researcher`; its model becomes `sonnet`.
- PR 13: hook script paths are quoted.
- PR 14: the copy offer is made once per repository, not per worktree.

## Why

Asked for: release the PRs merged since 0.8.0.

## Checks

```bash
tests/hook-cascade.sh
tests/offers.sh
tests/approve-operations.sh
tests/manifest-invariants.sh
shellcheck plugins/*/hooks/*.sh tests/*.sh
claude plugin validate .
```

- [x] All six pass locally (CI runs them too). `manifest-invariants.sh` confirms the newest CHANGELOG heading matches `plugin.json`.

## If this changes behavior

- [x] `SKILL.md` carries the change; the commands still delegate rather than restating it (no change in this PR)
- [x] README and `.claude/lean-atlassian.local.md.example` describe any new or changed setting (no change in this PR)
- [x] `plugin.json` version bumped, with a matching `## [0.9.0]` heading in `CHANGELOG.md`
- [x] Breaking for existing installs? Two changes, both named at the top of the 0.9.0 section. A pending project approval list takes effect without confirmation. A settings file without frontmatter reads as unconfigured.

## Notes for review

The section's date is 2026-10-21 (local). If this merges on a later day, the heading date and the tag date will differ.

author: douglaseel
body:
## Why
The `RequestStep` comment says another client's commands may run between a request's calls and its step. After #258 that is no longer true: the runtime posts a checked request's calls and its step together, and orders a connection's commands with its requests. A reviewer asked for the stronger guarantee on #257 and #258.

## What Changed
Comment only, in `proto/reactor_wire/v1/step.proto`:
- nothing runs between a request's calls and its step, not even another client's command;
- a connection's requests and commands are handled in the order they arrive, even when one waits for an upload.

No field or wire change. `buf lint` and `buf format` pass.
