body:
Players can now collect 400 awards across 80 families, set dated personal goals, log drills and habits, and keep a private trophy profile with three pinned awards. Confirmed awards export as generic, PII-free PNG cards through device sharing or download.

Adds username-based player access, own-practice target recording, durable offline activity synchronization, deterministic browser/server evaluation, provenance-aware backfill and restores, and a revision-checked evaluation queue. Existing shared-team statistics, coaching goals, and the Electric theme remain intact.

Validation:
- 219 tests passed, including catalog, evaluator, database isolation, corrections, and offline storage coverage.
- TypeScript and production build passed.
- Production-PWA browser checks passed at 320, 390, 768, and 1440 pixels, including offline reopening, target drills, pinning, and both PNG sizes. Goals, authentication, and recording smoke regressions also passed.
- Compatible Supabase migrations, account/evaluator functions, 15-minute scheduler, and historical backfill are already deployed; the backfill completed without errors.

Physical iPhone share-sheet verification remains a manual follow-up. Merging publishes the frontend through the existing GitHub Pages workflow.

author: sebinjeong
body:
## Summary

기업 가격 차트 `1d` 요청은 정규장 구간을 정하려고 요청마다 Toss `/api/v1/market-calendar/{KR|US}?date=…`를 한 번씩 호출했습니다. 지난 날짜의 캘린더는 바뀌지 않으므로, **거래소 현지 기준 오늘보다 이전 날짜**의 응답만 프로세스 안 LRU(256개)에 보관해 재사용합니다.

- 캐시 키: `KR|2026-10-15`, `US|2026-10-15`(거래소 현지 날짜)
- 오늘과 이후 날짜는 조기 마감·임시 휴장이 생길 수 있어 매번 조회합니다.
- 날짜가 다른 응답, 정규장·직전 거래일 세션이 해석되지 않는 응답(형식 오류), 통신 오류는 저장하지 않습니다. 일시적인 형식 오류가 재시작 전까지 계속 실패로 남지 않고 다음 요청에서 다시 조회됩니다.
- 요청 시각(`to`)에 따라 달라지는 "장이 열렸는가" 판단은 캐시하지 않고 매번 계산합니다.

변경하지 않은 범위: 응답 형식·세션 결정 규칙·1분봉 캐시는 그대로입니다. 효과가 있는 경우는 과거 `to`를 지정한 `1d` 요청입니다. 현재 시각 기준 요청(대부분 오늘 날짜)은 지금처럼 매번 조회합니다.

## Traceability

- Issue: Refs #86 (가격 차트 후속 작업, 닫지 않음)
- FS / NFS / WBS: FS040 차트와 타임라인 기간 조회 · BE · `docs/evidence/raw/functional-spec_2026-10-18/06-기업-상세-타임라인.csv` 88~116행(목차 `00-명세-목차.csv` 51행) / WBS 6.7.3 (BE) 차트·타임라인 기간 조회 API 구현 · `docs/evidence/raw/wbs_2026-10-12/01-프로젝트-WBS.csv` 206행
- screen IDs / stable operationId: D-COM-05 / `getCompanyPrices`
- Work scope / affected paths: 본개발 · `api/src/main/java/com/zoop/company/market/TossMarketClient.java`, `api/src/test/java/com/zoop/company/market/CompanyMarketClientsTest.java`
- Affected apps / contracts: `api/`만. 계약·응답 변경 없음, consumer(`web/`) 영향 없음

## Evidence

| Command / input | Observed result | Actual / fixture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `./gradlew test --tests 'com.zoop.company.*'` (`api/`, 로컬 Windows) | 통과 (`CompanyMarketClientsTest` 33개, 신규 3개 포함) | 합성 입력(Toss stub) |
| `onlyAPastDaysCalendarIsKept`: 10-15(지난 날)를 두 번 → 캘린더 1회, 10-16(오늘)·10-18(이후)을 두 번 → 각 2회 | 통과 | 합성 입력, 고정 clock 2026-10-16 KST |
| `aCalendarFormatFailureIsNotKept`: 날짜가 다른 응답 뒤 정상 응답 → 캘린더 2회, 세션 10-15 | 통과 | 합성 입력 |
| `aPastCalendarWithABadSessionIsNotKept`: 직전 거래일 `endTime`이 빠진 응답 → 그 요청은 기존처럼 성공(10-15 세션), 저장 안 함 → 정상 응답 두 번 → 캘린더 2회 | 통과 | 합성 입력 |
| 캐시 저장을 끈 상태 / 저장 전 검사(`wellFormed`)를 끈 상태에서 같은 테스트 실행(검증용, 커밋 안 함) | 각각 `onlyAPastDaysCalendarIsKept` / `aPastCalendarWithABadSessionIsNotKept` 실패 → 테스트가 해당 동작을 실제로 검사함을 확인 | 합성 입력 |
| `./gradlew assemble` (`make api-build` 상당, 로컬 Windows) | 성공 | — |
| `make api-test` 전체 (CI job `api`) | PR 생성 후 확인. 로컬 Windows 전체 실행은 #280에서 본 것처럼 환경 문제(`ArtifactStoreException` 등)로 무관한 실패가 있어 CI 결과로 판단 | 합성 입력 |

**미검증 사항**
- 실제 Toss 캘린더 호출로 캐시 적중을 확인하지 않았습니다(stub만 사용).
- 여러 요청이 동시에 같은 날짜를 처음 조회하면 캐시에 들어가기 전까지 각각 호출합니다(중복 호출 가능, 결과는 같음). 1분봉 캐시와 같은 수준으로 두었습니다.

- [x] 영향받는 consumer와 테스트를 함께 갱신했습니다. (consumer 영향 없음, BE 테스트 추가)
- [ ] 생성물은 원본에서 재생성했으며 원본 경고를 숨기지 않았습니다. — 해당 없음(생성물 변경 없음)
- [x] 실패·부분 실패·복구·회귀 조건을 검증했거나 미검증 이유를 명시했습니다. (형식 오류 비저장 시험, 기존 세션·휴장·조기 마감 시험 통과)
- [x] 실제 데이터와 합성 입력, 실제 AI 결과와 예시를 구분했습니다. (합성 입력만 사용, 실제 Toss 호출 미실행)
- [ ] 새 앱의 manifest·진입점·테스트와 검증 결과를 포함했습니다. — 해당 없음
- [x] 본개발은 `prototype/` runtime import와 DB 공유 없이 동작하며 계약 정본을 중복 생성하지 않았습니다.

## Rights and privacy

새 뉴스·문서·이미지·폰트·의존성 없음. 모델 호출 없음. 외부 호출은 오히려 줄어듭니다.

- [x] 비밀 키, 실제 `.env`, 인증 헤더, DB, 개인 기록, 사용자 로그를 포함하지 않았습니다.
- [x] 새로운 유료 호출·외부 데이터 요청·권한 확대가 있다면 별도 승인을 기록했습니다. — 없음

## Review and rollback

- 필요한 리뷰 역할 및 실제 지정한 reviewer: BE 리뷰 1인(미지정)
- API/스키마/데이터 변경과 이행 방법: 없음(프로세스 메모리 캐시만, 재시작하면 비워짐)

author: poojagosika
body: Fixes #2693 ## Summary The widget compiler requires a key on keyed fields (metadata), refuses a key on any other field, and caps keys at 256 characters, but the create-time vocabulary check skipped all three, so such specs were stored and then failed on every query. The vocabulary check now applies the same three rules. ## Type of Change - [ ] feat - A new feature - [x] fix - A bug fix - [ ] docs - Documentation only changes - [ ] style - Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white-space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc) - [ ] refactor - A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature - [ ] perf - A code change that improves performance - [ ] test - Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests - [ ] build - Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies (example scopes: gulp, broccoli, npm) - [ ] ci - Changes to our Cl configuration files and scripts (example scopes: Travis, Circle, BrowserStack, SauceLabs) - [ ] chore - Other changes that don't modify sc or test files - [ ] revert - Reverts a previous commit - [ ] security - A security fix or improvement - [ ] github - Changes to our GitHub configuration files and scripts - [ ] other (please describe): ## Details - `widget-spec-vocabulary.ts`, filter loop, mirroring `widget_query.py`: - a field with `requiresKey` needs a key ("requires a key") - any other field refuses one ("does not take a key") - a key is capped at 256 characters (`MAX_KEY_LENGTH` in `filters/translate.py`), counted in code points as Python's `len()` does, so a 256-emoji key is accepted on both sides - Checked against the real compiler: `compile_widget_query` raises for exactly the three cases these checks now refuse, and compiles the 256-emoji key. - Every caller of `validateWidgetSpecVocabulary` is covered: the dashboard widget route and the write service used by the public API, agent tools and CLI. The builder UI can't produce these specs (metadata isn't offered there, and FilterRow clears the key when the field changes). - Behaviour change worth noting: a widget that already holds such a filter (stored before this fix) now gets a 400 when its spec is re-saved, instead of being stored again. That widget already fails on every query, so this only surfaces the error earlier; removing or fixing the filter makes it saveable. - Tests: three new cases in `widget-spec-vocabulary.test.ts` (missing key, key on an unkeyed field, 257-character key plus the 256-emoji key). All three fail on main and pass with the fix. Related suites (dashboards, write services, dashboard/internal/public routes): 72 files, 1112 tests pass. ## Screenshots / Recordings (if applicable) ## Checklist - [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have added/updated tests where applicable - [ ] I have added screenshots or recordings for UI changes (if applicable) - [ ] I have updated documentation where necessary --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #2693. Aligns widget spec vocabulary validation with the widget query compiler's filter key rules. The compiler requires a key on keyed fields like `metadata`, refuses a key on unkeyed fields, and caps keys at 256 characters (counted in code points like Python's `len()`), but create-time validation skipped all three rules, so invalid specs were stored and failed on every query. Validation now mirrors the compiler and reuses the shared `MAX_KEY_LENGTH` constant. Behavior change: widgets already stored with such an invalid filter now get a 400 on re-save instead of being stored again. They already fail on every query, so this only surfaces the error earlier; removing or fixing the filter makes the widget saveable. Written for commit 62e8e6a0e75c100dad10a63b308036d528997045. Summary will update on new commits.

author: mvschwarz
body:
## What a user gets

Creating or replacing a seat keeps its environment values, such as the activity-hook token and provider credentials, out of the tmux client's arguments and out of tmux error messages. A command that carries such values is written to a private `0600` file that tmux reads with `source-file`, and the file is removed afterwards.

When a seat's agent is replaced in its pane, the replacement's environment file is now written before the running agent is stopped. So a full or unwritable temporary directory leaves the working agent running, instead of a dead pane with no replacement.

This finishes #1247 by @Aschenbath. Their commits are here unchanged, then main merged in, then our commits for the changes asked for in review there. Refs #1247. Refs #306.

## The change

- **@Aschenbath's `2c72a4f0` and `dcf5c34d`:** the private environment file for `new-session` and `respawn-pane`, with exclusive creation, `0600`, a literal path, cleanup retried once, and the cold-start `start-server ; source-file`.
- **Merge of main** (`24fc6bb3`): main's tmux control client and warnings list are kept beside the private file. The startup test keeps main's PATH beside the PR's assertions that the environment reaches `createSession`, not a tmux command.
- **Ours:**
  - **Write the file before the agent stops** (`435fe7f9`). The tmux adapter can stage a respawn (`stageRespawnPane`): build it, and write its private file now. The successor launcher stages first, and stops the running agent only when staging succeeded. A staging failure returns with the agent still running. `respawnPane` then runs the staged respawn as built, and the launcher removes the file afterwards. The successor launcher is the only caller of `respawnPane` that passes environment values; in-place restart passes none and writes no file. Seat handover (`SeatHandoverService`) reaches it through the launcher.
  - **Clean up a partly written file** (same commit). When the write fails after the exclusive open created the file, for example on a full disk, the file is removed. A file already at the path (`EEXIST`) is left alone.
  - **Tests** (`88a47393`, `ef32b2de`, `4fbeb3c7`): native tmux cases (below). The native fixture now runs non-tmux commands as given, so a cutover's `kill` reaches the agent. The argv census drives the staged respawn, and four test files' tmux stand-ins gain a passing `stageRespawnPane`.

## How you verified it

- **Native tmux cases in `tmux-private-env-native.test.ts`,** in both execution modes, using the real adapter and the real successor launcher. A stand-in agent runs in the pane, and the private file can't be written: once because the disk fills partway through the write, once because the directory is unwritable. Each case expects the launcher to refuse with "the running agent was left in place", the pane to still run the agent, and no file to be left in the staging directory.
- **Without the fix** (the same test on the merge, before the fix): the 4 cases fail. The printed diff, for the shell and no-space case, shows the cutover stopping the agent and then failing: "Could not respawn the successor … ENOSPC", with `replacementStarted: true`. The other three fail the same assertion. The 8 existing native cases pass.
- **With the fix** (`4fbeb3c7`): 17 test files pass, 530 of 531, and one opt-in native end-to-end test skips. They cover the private-env, tmux adapter, argv census, agent environment, exact target, startup, successor launcher, seat handover (including the real-tmux cutover end-to-end), in-place restart and tmux option files.
- These ran in a network-off Linux container at the exact commits. CI runs the full suite. The branch merges cleanly with current main.

## Anything you were unsure about

- **The pane's own arguments.** When OpenRig scopes a seat's launch environment (a launch environment that doesn't inherit tmux's), the respawn's command is a small `/bin/sh -c "exec /usr/bin/env -i -- KEY=value …"` wrapper. That keeps the values out of the tmux client's arguments, which is what this PR covers. But the pane's `sh` and `env` processes carry them in their own arguments for the moment before the shell starts. This PR doesn't change that wrapper.
- **A fresh launch with full or unwritable temporary storage:** a fresh `createSession` that carries environment values must now write the private file first. So with no temporary space it refuses, where main's argument form would have launched. This change keeps that refusal; only the successor cutover gains staging.
- **Windows with psmux** hasn't been exercised. The native tests skip on Windows, and the scoped launch wrapper isn't used there.
- **Cost:** ours is +103/−32 source and +59/−9 tests, much of it the respawn body moved unchanged into `buildRespawn`. The whole PR against its merge base is +130/−12 source, +386/−77 tests and +15 docs.

## If this is security-related

It keeps credentials out of the tmux client's process arguments, which other local users can list. It doesn't change who can reach tmux, and the pane's own launch command is covered under the limits above.

- [x] One concern per PR; no version bump; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit
- [x] Tests added or updated where the change is testable
- [x] I listed the checks I ran, their results, and any checks I could not run

author: stevekinney
body:
Refs COR-1584

A file agent's `definitionRevision` now rises every time its file's content changes, and a run keeps the revision it started with.

## One-way doors

- **Persisted record**: `bureau-agent-revision:v1:<identifier>` holds `{"revision":<n>,"hash":"<64 lowercase hex>"}` as JSON in that key order. It is written with `conditionalBatch`, conditioned on the exact text that was read, or on the key being absent for a first sighting. A writer that loses the condition reads again; if the record then holds its hash, it reports that revision, so two processes that see one change produce one increment. A record that cannot be read, is not valid, or holds any other hash is an error and is never replaced. Deleting a file leaves the record.
- **Wire field**: `definitionRevision` (positive integer or `null`) on `bureau.agents.definitions.get` and `.list`: the persisted revision for a valid file agent, the profile's revision for a code-defined agent, `null` for an invalid file. `bureau.agents.list` reports the same value through the generation profile it already read.
- **Option**: `createAgent({ revision?: number })`, a positive safe integer, default 1. It sets the generation profile's revision and does not reach `RunOptions`.
- **Additive field on a persisted v1 record**: the per-run reference `bureau-agent-run:v1:<runId>` gains an optional `definitionRevision` (positive safe integer), named as the recovery record and the wire name it. A reference written without it, or with an invalid one, still reads. `hold` fills the field only when it is absent (or was invalid and dropped on read) and never changes a recorded value.

## How it works

- The file catalog settles revisions in a new optional `settle` step of the watched directory, between loading a scan's entries and replacing the previous ones. `refresh()` resolves and `onChange` fires only after it, so the listing, the agent's profile, and the record agree.
- Every scan reads the record of every ready file (one read per file; nothing is written when the record already describes the file). A catalog that missed a peer's edits, including an edit and revert between two scans, agrees with the record on its next scan, and a scan that finds only the revision changed reports the file in `onChange`.
- A catalog adopts the record freely but writes a new revision only from a reading it can trust is current. If the record describes other content while the scanned hash is what this catalog itself last recorded, the scan may have read the file just before a peer's edit, so the write is deferred once for that record: the revision is kept for the scan and the next scan decides. One edit therefore costs one increment even when a scan races it, and a genuine revert that a peer never saw is written one scan later. A catalog that has recorded nothing yet (its first scan after a start) has no last-recorded hash and writes at once, so the revision it lists always names the content it lists it with: after a restart that follows an offline edit, the first refresh lists the new content at a new revision. The one known property is a narrow race on that first scan, where a stale first read can over-count a peer's edit; a revision is only ever raised that way, never lowered. Each distinct record hash buys one deferral, so a third writer alternating the record between two hashes cannot hold a catalog back indefinitely.
- A failed record read or write keeps the agent listed at its last known revision (1 if none), emits a diagnostic naming the agent, and retries on the next scan. It never makes the agent invalid. The diagnostic is reported when the failure is new (the first after a success, or at a different hash), not on every scan that finds the store still down.
- A snapshot is keyed by content, so one snapshot can have been several revisions. The revision a run started at is recorded in its recovery record and on its own reference (`FileAgentBinding.revision`, written by `hold`/`recordRun`). A resumed run is rebuilt with it: the `bureau.run` recovery record, the claim-lost path (`claimed.definitionRevision`), and a restored session run (its own reference, so a session run that is not the session's latest resumes at its own revision) all pass it through `agentForRecordedRun` and `agentFromSnapshot`. A reference written before the field falls back to the session's metadata, which names the latest run's revision only. The durable session recovery resolver reads the hash and the revision from the session's metadata, as it did the hash before.
- The model catalog's revision (`FileEntry.revision`) is untouched; a model catalog change does not raise the agent's revision.
- `FileAgentBinding.definitionRevision` is optional: an agent rebuilt for a run that recorded no revision records none, rather than persisting a 1 the run never had.
- `bureau.agents.list` and `bureau.agents.definitions.*` both declare `definitionRevision` as a positive integer.

## Not changed

- Each ready file agent is built twice on the first scan after a restart (once at the last recorded revision, then again at the stored one). `createAgent` and the host's `resolveAgentGenerate` run twice per file agent per boot. A pure resolver is unaffected, and a first-call failure of the resolver is equally sticky on `main`, so this is left as an advisory.

## Verification

- `with-turborepo-cache bun run validate` passes at `7d480851`, which contains `main` `342f9a4a`: 78 of 78 tasks, the serial lane 7 of 7, and an audit with no vulnerabilities.
- `with-turborepo-cache bunx turbo run lint typecheck test test:coverage --filter=@lostgradient/bureau --filter=@lostgradient/operative` passes at the merged head.
- Bureau `test:slow` passes, the new and changed tests pass under `--rerun-each=20` (1340 of 1340 for the revision tests), `bun run lint:root` and Prettier pass, and Interborough, which reads the definitions operations, passes `typecheck` and `test`.
- Mutations that each turn a named test red: serving the cached revision when the hash matches, each of the four resume paths dropping its recorded revision, the reference not recording the revision, `sameSignature` ignoring the revision, a down store diagnosed on every scan, an unvalidated record hash, a wire schema that admits 0, and the earlier four (condition removed, returning hash unchanged, resumed run reading the current revision, diagnostic dropped).

author: wirasm
body:
## Problem and outcome

Bun merges a `mock.module()` factory over the real module, so an export the factory leaves out keeps its real implementation. When a mocked module gains an export, every factory that does not list it starts running real code (a database, the network, the filesystem) under tests that still pass. The only signal was Bun's 5 s timeout, which cost weeks across #2121, #2186, #2240 and #2306.

- **Outcome:** `bun run validate` (and the CI `static` job) now fails when a `mock.module()` factory omits an export of the module it mocks. The failure names the file, line, specifier and missing names. Adding an export to a mocked production module fails at every factory that neither provides it nor spreads the real module.
- **Invariant:** Test behavior is unchanged. The check is static and runs outside `bun test`.
- **Scope boundary:** No `spyOn` conversion, no change to the test-isolation split (`// @archon-test-isolated`, `testGroups`), and no new network or filesystem guards. The adapters `ARCHON_HOME` probe (#3719) already covers that acceptance item and is untouched.

## Review guidance

- **Feedback requested:** The rule for telling a deliberate partial mock from an omission, and the baseline-plus-ratchet way of landing green.
- **Start here:** `scripts/check-mock-modules.ts` — the header states the rule and the limits; `collectSites` and `compareBaseline` are the logic.
- **Review order:** `scripts/check-mock-modules.ts`, its test, the ratchet hook in `scripts/check-ratchet.ts`, validate/CI wiring, then the docs.
- **Lower-attention areas:** `scripts/mock-module-baseline.json` is generated by `bun run check:mock-modules --write` (569 grandfathered sites, 723 sites scanned). The check fails if the committed file differs from the computed one.
- **Known risk or uncertainty:** A factory that spreads the real module passes by declaration, so a module mocked only by spreading factories gets no failure when it gains an export. The check adds about 25 to 30 s to the CI `static` job. Where test files share a process, `await import()` in a spread can return an earlier file's mock; the docs say so.

## Solution

The check reads every `mock.module(literal, factory)` call through its package's own `tsconfig.json` and compares the factory's return keys with the module's value exports. It does not guess intent: spreading the real module (`...(await import('X'))`) is the author's declaration that the rest stays real. Any other omission fails.

The 569 sites that are incomplete today are grandfathered in a committed baseline: each site, plus the exports its module's grandfathered sites omitted at that time. A grandfathered site may omit only those names, so a new export still fails at every one of them. A fixed site must leave the baseline (`--write`), so it only shrinks. The ratchet refuses entries the baseline gains against the merge base unless a `Ratchet-Allow: scripts/mock-module-baseline.json` trailer waives them, which closes the `--write` bypass. The introducing commit carries that trailer, so the PR must keep that commit until merge.

Converting the existing partial mocks to spreads was rejected: it would turn the check green by removing its protection at every existing site. The one fix made is deleting a dead `mock.module('../../isolation')` in the core command test harness. That path was removed with the `@archon/isolation` extraction and the live mock follows it.

### Contract additions

- **Validate check id `mock-modules` and root script `check:mock-modules`.** Every existing id and script keeps its behavior. `bun run validate` with no arguments runs one more check.
- **The ratchet refuses growth of `scripts/mock-module-baseline.json`.** The file is new, so no existing change or trailer is affected. Every existing ratchet rule, ceiling and `Ratchet-Allow:` form keeps its meaning.

## Validation

- `bun run check:mock-modules` — passed, 723 sites, 569 grandfathered — proves the committed baseline matches the code.
- Seen red: appending `export function spikeProbe(): void {}` to `packages/core/src/db/workflows.ts` failed the check at 19 named sites, for example `packages/core/src/handlers/commands/test-harness.ts:324 mock.module('../../db/workflows') omits spikeProbe; ...`. Reverted afterwards.
- `bun run test scripts/check-mock-modules.test.ts scripts/check-ratchet.test.ts scripts/validate.test.ts` — 42 pass — proves omission, grandfathered-then-new-export, spread, stale baseline, unresolvable path, and ratchet growth (new export or new grandfathered factory) with and without the trailer.
- `bun x tsc --noEmit -p scripts/tsconfig.json`, `cd packages/core && bun run type-check`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check` — passed.
- `git fetch origin dev && bun run check:ratchet` — passed; baseline growth reported as allowed by the trailer.
- The 23 core test files importing the edited harness each pass when run alone with `bun run test <file>`.
- **Not verified:** The full CI suite; it runs on the PR.

## Delivery considerations

| Concern | Impact and required action | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Documentation / communication | New "`mock.module()` merges over the real module" section in the DX quirks guide with the remedy and the check's limits; `CONTRIBUTING.md` lists the new validate id. | `packages/docs-web/src/content/docs/contributing/dx-quirks.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` |
| Rollout / rollback | Tooling only; reverting the PR removes the check. | No runtime or package code changed. |

## Links

- Closes #2309

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Developer Tools**
  * Validation now checks that mocked modules include the exports provided by the modules they replace. The check reports incomplete mocks and outdated baseline entries.
  * The validation guide now includes this check, and the documentation explains mock behavior, baseline rules, and known limitations.
  * The ratchet check now flags growth in the mock-module baseline unless explicitly allowed.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for incomplete mocks, baseline changes, and ratchet behavior.

author: rcbjbluemars
body:
On 8081 (~470,000 signed-in people), Monitoring → Sessions never came back, and sign-ins and refreshes fell to 0/s for about two minutes.

**The cause:** `GET /admin-api/sessions` → `logout.liveSessions()` → `authn.sessionsMatching(() => true)` → `indexedSessions()`.
- With the session window on, that is one synchronous `loadByDigest()` per session, about 470,000 blocking bridge reads.
- On top of that, every row calls `holderKeyOf()`.
- It ran on a request worker, and through read-your-write every other worker waited for it (`STS-WORKER-0027`).
- Monitoring → Metrics and a person's page walked the same list.

**What changes (window on only; with it off nothing changes)**

| Page / API | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Monitoring → Sessions, `GET /admin-api/sessions` | every session opened, then paged | `sessionsViewAsync()`: counts from the index (`session.liveTotals`), one page newest first (`session.livePage`, on the driver's read pool via `askAsync`), only the page's bodies opened (`openAsync`, not admitted to the cache) |
| Monitoring → Metrics, `GET /admin-api/metrics` | every session drawn in the JSON | `metricsJsonAsync()`: index counts and the newest 100 rows |
| A person's page (`sessionRowsFor`) | every session walked for one person | that person's own via `sessionsHeldUnder()` |
| Users page, when the index count fails | fell back to walking every session | draws "—" (unread) |

What a reader sees differently with the window on, all stated in the answer (`windowed: true`):
- **Search is exact**: a whole username, subject or session id, matched by digest. The index holds digests, not text.
- **The protocol filter narrows the page** it is applied to.
- **Other families first:** the families held whole (Kerberos tickets, GNAP grants, directory connections) are listed ahead of the sessions.

**The queries against 8081's postgres** (477,293 live sessions):
- totals: 114 ms;
- a page at offset 200,000: 268 ms;
- an exact search: 0.8 ms.
All of it runs off the event loop.

**Not changed, and raised with rcbj:** a sign-out's inventory (`logout.ts` `sessionsByKey()`, `GET /admin-api/logout?user=`) still walks every session on purpose, so it cannot miss a session filed under neither the username nor the subject.

**Tests**
- New `console_sessions_index`:
  - S1: the queries build and shape correctly.
  - S2: the Sessions view never lists every session, and passes the search to the index.
  - S3: page 2 starts after the other families.
  - S4: Metrics counts from the index.
  - S5: a person's page reads only theirs.
  - S6: with the window off, both views answer as before.
- With session_window, api_sessions, users_population_async, the logout and metrics tests, typecheck and error_codes: 14 files, 638 assertions. One failure was S2's own expectation, corrected; it passes 7/7.
- Mutation: with the view always walking, S2 and S3 fail.
- `authn/CLAUDE.md` documents it.

author: vu1n
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"vu1n"} -->
_Requested by **Vu** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0151Cixt9chXhwo91pHVG7x2?thread=cmsg_0151Cixt9chXhwo91pHVG7x2HqrCKj2diu2cGrxSNf1dWM)_

## What

1. **`eval/frontiermemory/`** imports Letta's FrontierMemory benchmark data into kypp. It converts the 219 public source trajectories into §0 events, runs kypp's unchanged write path over them (distill, then consolidate), and checks recall offline against the 15 task prompts. No task agent ran: the sandbox refused network access for the agent inside the container.
2. **`consolidate(tag_of=…, pair_judge=…)`** adds an opt-in agreement phase. Candidates that share a tag are compared pairwise, each only with its 8 most word-similar tag-mates from other sessions. An affirmative judgment (P ≥ 0.9) counts as agreement. The survivor and its *direct* matches are promoted once at least 2 sessions back them, and the matched restatements are superseded. This builds the acceptance rule already in `memory-scope-decay#scope-keys-decay`: "affirmative agreement judgment plus distinct non-echo recurrence". When neither argument is passed, behaviour is unchanged.
3. **`eval/agreement/`** holds 600 labelled claim pairs, Clef scores, the cutoff chosen with `scripts/tune_cutoff.py`, a leave-one-tag-out check, a Clef tagging check, and a before/after run on the FrontierMemory store.

## Why

Distilling the traces gave 1,042 claims, and exact-subject corroboration promoted only 7% of them. Word2Vec's 11 restatements of the empty-corpus pitfall all stayed candidates, so `briefing` and default recall returned nothing from that task.

## Results

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| accepted | 72 | 215 |
| own-task results in top 10, default recall, 15 prompts | 26/150 | 55/150 |
| tasks with none | 8 | 4 |
| labelled not-same pairs inside merged clusters | — | 5/118 |

At cutoff 0.9 the pair judge's held-out precision is 0.96 and its catch rate 0.78, and leave-one-tag-out gives the same. Clef put 79% of claims under the right tag, and every miss is between sibling tasks built from the same source.

## Not in this PR

- No CLI, cron or MCP path passes `tag_of` / `pair_judge` yet. The production tag source would be the Brief feature map.
- `worker/src/memory.ts` doesn't have the phase. It needs porting before the phase is enabled anywhere, otherwise local and hosted promote differently. This is recorded in the Consolidation gotchas.

author: xiaoyifang
body:
Fixes #3115

### Problem

`RX::Ftx::processSearchStringForHighlight()` (introduced in #2918) hangs the GUI thread when the FTS query contains an unpaired quote, e.g. Ancient Greek elided forms such as `τὸ καθ'`.

At an unpaired quote the quoted-phrase regex finds no match, and the bare-token loop also stops immediately on the same quote character, so `pos` never advances and the `while` loop spins forever.

### Fix

In the bare-token loop, a quote that still opens a complete quoted phrase is handled as before (the loop breaks and the outer branch consumes the phrase), so existing phrase highlighting is unchanged. An unpaired quote now advances `pos`:

- follows a token (`καθ'`, `abc'def`) → kept as a literal part of the token, so the keyword stays precise instead of degrading to `καθ`;
- starts the token (`"abc`, `'tis`) → dropped, matching the pre-#2918 behaviour where punctuation was replaced by whitespace.

### Verification

Keyword results (algorithm equivalence checked outside the app):

| query | keywords |
| --- | --- |
| `τὸ καθ'` | `τὸ`, `καθ'` |
| `foo "bar baz" qux` | `foo`, `bar baz`, `qux` |
| `"abc` | `abc` |
| `'tis` | `tis` |
| `abc'def ghi` | `abc'def`, `ghi` |

author: g-ferrari
body:
## O que muda

Sai do config o campo `photo` do bloco **Contato com formulário** (`ctaContact`), fora de uso desde a #171: a foto do painel "Nossos Contatos" mora no global Contato (`panelPhoto`), e a migração `20261021_233937_foto_do_painel_de_contatos` levou para lá a foto que a home usava. Nada lê o campo: nem o mapper (`lib/mappers/blocks.ts`), nem os tipos de apresentação, nem os seeds, nem o e2e. O `variant: 'photo'` de `scripts/seed/home.ts` é o **valor do select**, não o campo.

## ⚠️ A coluna `photo_id` **não** é apagada nesta publicação

O pedido era apagar a coluna junto, partindo da premissa de que o código no ar já não a lê. Medi, e ele lê:

- A #171 só **escondeu** o campo (`admin: { hidden: true }`), e o campo continua declarado. O adapter do Postgres põe toda coluna declarada no SELECT.
- O bloco é compartilhado por **Páginas, Soluções, Segmentos e Parceiros**, então `photo_id` está em **7 tabelas**, e não 2: `pages`, `partners`, `segments`, `solutions` e as versões `_pages_v`, `_segments_v`, `_solutions_v`.
- Teste numa cópia do banco local: com as 7 colunas apagadas, o código de hoje (`origin/migracao` = o que a #172 publicou) falha em `pages`, `solutions`, `segments` e `partners` com `column pages__blocks_ctaContact.photo_id does not exist`. Com a coluna no banco, o código desta PR lê as quatro normalmente.

O `deploy.sh` roda a migração antes de trocar a versão, e a volta (healthcheck reprovado ou revert) não desfaz migração. Se a coluna saísse aqui, um deploy reprovado voltaria para a #172 e derrubaria a home e as páginas internas. É a armadilha "Deploy volta para a versão anterior" do CLAUDE.md, e o tratamento é o mesmo da Insights (`20261005_223123_insights_automatica` → `20261015_120000_insights_apaga_tabelas_antigas`):

- `20261022_013640_remove_cta_contact_photo` é um **passo vazio**. Ela traz o retrato do schema (`.json`) já sem o campo, para que `migrate:create` não acuse diferença.
- A exclusão fica pronta em `EXCLUSAO_ADIADA`: `DROP CONSTRAINT`, `DROP INDEX` e `DROP COLUMN`, todos com `IF EXISTS`, nas 7 tabelas. A volta fica em `RECRIACAO`: a coluna, a FK para `media` com `ON DELETE set null` e o índice, todos idempotentes.
- **Próxima publicação, depois desta estar na `main`:** uma migração que executa `EXCLUSAO_ADIADA` no `up` e `RECRIACAO` no `down`, sem `.json`, porque o retrato não muda.

Até lá a coluna fica no banco, sem uso. As linhas de bloco que o código novo gravar nascem com ela nula.

## Como foi testado

- **Cópia do banco local** (`pg_dump` de `atra` num banco temporário): `payload migrate` aplica só esta migração, até "Done.". Depois, `migrate:create sem_diferenca` responde **"No schema changes detected"**. O banco `atra` em si não foi tocado: ele tem migrações de outras branches e serve o dev do checkout principal.
- **Banco zerado**: `payload migrate` rodou as 122 migrações até "Done.", sem erro. Depois de mesclar a `migracao` com a #169, rodou as **127** até "Done.".
- **SQL adiado**, testado numa terceira cópia:
  - `EXCLUSAO_ADIADA` duas vezes zera colunas, índices e FKs (0/0/0), e o código desta PR lê as quatro coleções.
  - `RECRIACAO` duas vezes devolve 7 colunas, 7 índices e 7 FKs `set null`, e o código de hoje volta a ler as quatro coleções.
- O retrato `.json` difere do anterior só nas 21 peças do `photo` (coluna, FK e índice × 7 tabelas).
- `corepack pnpm typecheck`, `lint` e `test` verdes: 958 testes antes da mesclagem e 1046 depois.

### Depois da #169 (22/10)

A #169, do criador de formulários, entrou antes. O `.json` desta migração tinha sido gerado sem `forms`, `pages_blocks_form_section` e a coluna nova de `payload_locked_documents_rels`, e o próximo `migrate:create` tentaria recriar essas tabelas. Refiz o retrato a partir do config atual:

- Uma migração provisória gerada sobre o retrato de `20261021_233937` produziu só os 21 comandos do `photo_id`, nada dos formulários. Ela foi descartada.
- O retrato novo difere do anterior só nas 21 peças do `photo` e inclui as tabelas dos formulários.
- `migrate:create sem_diferenca` diz "No schema changes detected".

O nome e o SQL da migração não mudaram.

Os bancos temporários foram apagados.

body:
## 概要

対応する Node の版をリポジトリに書き、Node 25 で `use-direction-species.test.ts` の5件が落ちる原因を直します。アプリの回帰ではなく、実行環境の差でした。

## 変更内容

原因は vitest のDOM環境の作りです。Node 25 は `localStorage` を標準で持ちます。vitest は「global に同名があれば DOM 環境側のもので上書きしない」ので、happy-dom の `localStorage` が入らず、`localStorage.clear is not a function` になります。

- `vitest.config.ts`: 旗 `--no-experimental-webstorage` が使える版にだけ、テスト用の子プロセスへ渡す。旗が無い Node には渡さない（渡すと起動に失敗する）
- `package.json` の `engines.node`: `^22.13.0 || >=24.0.0`。lockfile の依存が要る下限（`jsdom@29.1.1` が 22.13、`@electron/rebuild@4.0.3` が 22.12）に合わせた。Node 20 は使えない
- `.npmrc` の `engine-strict=true`: 範囲外の Node だと `pnpm install` が理由付きで止まる
- `.node-version` と `ci.yml` / `license-check.yml` / `release.yml` の setup-node: 20 から 22 へ同時に上げた。`scripts/release-gate-check.mjs` が workflow の Node を固定している値も 22 にした
- `.github/ci/node-env.test.mjs`: `.node-version`・各 workflow・`engines`・`engine-strict` の食い違いに加えて、`engines.node` の各下限が lockfile の全依存の `engines.node` を満たすかを見る検査を足した。Node 20 のまま `engine-strict` を入れた前回の状態では、この検査が落ちる
- `.github/ci/release-proof.test.mjs`: 「別の Node は証明を無効にする」変異を 22 から 24 に差し替えた
- `README.md` と `CONTRIBUTING.md` の Node の書き方を揃えた
- `package.json` の lint-staged に `--no-errors-on-unmatched` を足した。biome の対象外のファイル（`vitest.config.ts`）だけを変えるコミットが pre-commit で止まったため

Node 20 は 2026-04-30 に保守が終わっています（nodejs/Release の schedule.json、2026-10-22 確認）。依存も 22.12 以上を要るため、CI は 20 のままにできず 22 へ上げました。24 への移行は E2E を通してから別に行います。

## 関連Issue

- Closes #160

## スクリーンショット

なし（実行環境と設定の変更）。

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- `bun ./index.html --port=abc` prints 13 lines: `error: "--port" needs a port from 0 to 65535, not "abc".` under an excerpt of Bun's own `internal:serve_cli` source, then a stack into `internal:html`. With `--hot` or `--watch` the process then waits for a file change.
- The shared flag parser (`parseServeFlag` in `src/js/internal/serve_cli.ts`, #45682 and #45828) throws for a bad flag. `bun bake` catches that (`bake.ts:387`). `start()` in `src/js/internal/html.ts:28` did not. The messages are unreleased. No user reported this.

### Fix
- `start()` catches the throw, prints `error: <message>` (same text) and exits 1, as `bun bake` does.
- Verified: `test/js/bun/http/bun-serve-html-entry.test.ts` (8 new tests, 7 fail on main). Also `tsc -p src/js` and `test/cli/bake/bake.test.ts` (84 of 85, see Notes).
- Self-reviewed: 21 concerns raised, 21 addressed.

### Background
- `bun ./index.html` runs the built-in module `internal/html.ts` as the program. A throw in its `start()` is an uncaught exception: the VM prints an excerpt and the stack, calls `uncaughtException` listeners, and keeps a `--hot` or `--watch` process alive.
- Considered a typed error in `serve_cli.ts` for both commands: every start pays for a class. Considered the error printer: it removes only the excerpt.

### Downsides
- For these errors, `--hot` and `--watch` exit 1 where they waited, and a preload's `uncaughtException` listener is not called (before: called, exit 0).
- With colours on, the whole line is red, as in `bun bake`.
- Each start costs +119,716 instructions:u (+1.2% of a `--help` start) and +1 GC cell. The binary grows by 132 B.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

**Scope**

- Only what `parseServeFlag` throws: a port that is not 0 to 65535 (`serve_cli.ts:27`, #45828), an empty hostname (`:50`, #45682), a flag with no value (`:74`, #45682).
- On 1.4.3, `--host`, `--port`, `--host=`, `--port abc` and `--host=:0` after the page start a server. On main each exits 1 under 12 or 13 lines. The next release is the first with these messages.
- The source is an automated fuzz run. No maintainer asked for this. It follows #45828, which gave `bun bake` this handling and gave `bun ./index.html` the throw.

**Not in this PR.** Each of these still prints the long form:

- A host that `Bun.serve` refuses, for example `--host=203.0.113.1` or `--host=[::1`. It waits under `--hot`.
- A pattern with no match (`bun './zz*.html'`, `No HTML files found matching`). It waits under `--hot`. Bun also prints this text for a page that exists under `node_modules` (#24953).
- A page that does not resolve (`bun ./index.html ./nope.html`).
- The flag before the page (`bun --port=abc ./index.html`, the native parser), and `PORT`, `BUN_PORT`, `NODE_PORT`.
- Arguments that `html.ts` ignores, such as `--prot=3000`.
- The error printer's excerpt for `internal:*` frames.
- `serve_cli.ts` and `bake.ts` do not change.

**Behaviour, main and then this PR** (`NO_COLOR=1`)

| Command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `bun ./index.html --port=abc` | 13 lines, 515 B, exit 1 | 1 line, 57 B, exit 1 |
| with `--hot` or `--watch` | 11 lines, then waits | 1 line, exit 1 |
| with a preload `uncaughtException` listener | listener called, stderr empty, exit 0 | listener not called, 1 line, exit 1 |
| `FORCE_COLOR=1` | `error` red, message bold | whole line red |

- One more order changes. If code in the process adds a bad flag to `process.argv` while the server is up, the next `--hot` reload exits 1. On main that reload prints the error and the server stays up. No command line reaches this state, and `--help` in the same loop already exits on a reload. A guard for it is 5 more lines. Say so if you want it.
- `return process.exit(1)`: user code can replace `process.exit`. If the replacement returns, `start()` must not go on and serve with the flag dropped. `--host=` would then listen on every interface.

**Cost.** Two local release builds: the merge base at the time (963452075e) and the same tree with this change.

- `internal/html.js`: 5129 B to 5261 B. `size -A`: `.bun_builtins` +132 B, `.text` +0 B.
- `start()` bytecode: 363 to 381 instructions, 2080 to 2170 bytes, 4 to 5 handlers. A valid command line runs 1 more `jmp` for each flag.
- Heap after a full GC at exit (JIT off, 3 equal runs for each build): 2524 to 2525 cells, +379 B.
- `bun ./index.html --port=0 --help`, 20 interleaved runs: instructions:u median 9,902,251 to 10,021,967. The same binary against itself differs by 1,918. Syscalls: 239 and 239.
- `perf`, `strace` and `bloaty` are not installed on the build machine. The counts come from `size`, a `perf_event_open` counter and a `ptrace` syscall counter.

**Tests**

- 8 new tests: three flags without a watch mode, `--hot`, `--watch`, a preload listener, a `process.exit` that returns, and one that pins the scope (`./nope.html` is still an uncaught exception). The scope test passes on main by design.
- On main, 7 of 8 fail. Checked on the release canary, on a release build of the merge base, and on the debug ASAN build with the merge-base module text. The `--hot` and `--watch` tests time out there and the runner ends the child.
- With the change: 8 of 8 on the debug ASAN build, and 15 of 15 for the file on a release build.
- Without `return`, the `process.exit` test fails. With the catch around all of `start()`, the scope test fails.
- On the debug build here, the 5 older dev-server tests at the top of the file take 3 to 8 s. Some go over the default 5 s timeout, with or without this change. All pass with a longer timeout, as CI sets.
- `test/cli/bake/bake.test.ts`: 84 of 85 pass. `--watch-kill-signal ... bake --check sends that signal before a restart` times out, also with the merge-base module text. `bun bake` does not load `internal/html`.
- Not run: macOS and Windows.

**Where the rule lives**

- The parser keeps the checks and the message text. What to do with a bad flag (exit, or wait for a change) belongs to the entry program, and the two callers differ there. `node inspect` does the same: `startInspect` catches the error of its parser and exits.
- A typed error with a reporter in `serve_cli.ts` adds a class and a function to each `bun ./index.html` and each `bun bake` start. Only a mistyped command line reads them, and `bun bake` keeps its own exit rule (`bake.ts:521`).
- A native rule for usage errors of built-in entry points leaves `start()` rejecting. The run command and the reload reporter must then both recognise that rejection.
- The error printer removes 7 of the 13 lines (checked with `BUN_DISABLE_SOURCE_CODE_PREVIEW=1`). The wait and the listener call stay.

</details>

body:
## What

Pins every `node:22-alpine` stage in `web/Dockerfile` (deps, builder, runner, worker-builder, worker) to `node:22.23.4-alpine@sha256:ebc216c22db53dbde85719a874978d5aec04e6e405ad26a3804c6f9abc4ca1a9`. Nothing else in the image changes. `web/src/test/dockerfile-stages.ts` needed no change (it asserts nothing about the base tag).

Why: Node 22.23.4 carries the October 21, 2026 security release fixes (e.g. CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write). The floating tag already points at it, but a cached Railway build can keep reusing the old vulnerable layer. The digest is the multi-arch OCI index digest, re-read with `docker buildx imagetools inspect`.

## Evidence

All local, against throwaway local Postgres/Redis (isolated compose project, no Railway, production DB or real API keys). Logs and summary: `/Users/cody/Documents/code/firstmate/data/jena-node-patch-pin/`.

- `runner` and `worker` targets both build; `node --version` inside each prints `v22.23.4`.
- CI gates (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) run in a `node:22.23.4-bookworm` container: install, migrate, tsc, lint, build, `standalone:check`, `worker:build` + `worker:check`, e2e (39 passed, 0 flaky) all green.
- `pnpm test`: 5551 passed, 24 skipped. Two suites that each run `mastra worker build` (`web-restart`, `stage-selection`) fail only inside the full parallel run in my Docker Desktop harness. The identical failure occurs on the previous `node:22.23.1`, so it is not caused by the pin, and both pass on 22.23.4 with `--no-file-parallelism` (19 tests). I did not establish the harness-specific root cause; GitHub CI on this PR is the authoritative run.
- Built web and worker images brought up against local db/redis: `/api/health` returns 200 `{"status":"ok"}` and `node /app/scripts/worker-healthcheck.mjs` exits 0.
- Caveat: local containers were linux/arm64; Railway pulls the amd64 manifest from the same index digest.

## Rollback

Revert this commit.

## Deploy note

Merging deploys the Railway `web` and `worker` services. Railway deployments are currently paused platform-wide, so the new image will not go live until that pause is lifted.

author: coder8124
body:
## Summary
- A1-A4: memories get a stable content-derived uid, a per-memory file under memories/<kind>/ as the source of truth, a correction's new memory names the uid it replaced, and a ruling's anchor can be an AND/OR of git/dep/doc/time checks instead of only the implicit git anchor.
- C5: a checkpoint records the host's own session id in its frontmatter, and sessions/<project>/_convos/<convo>/ is a derived physical layout rebuilt from that frontmatter whenever the folder and the frontmatter disagree.
- G1: `logos activity --compliance [--project P]` reports how many checkpoint-asked events in the log were actually followed by a checkpoint, with raw counts alongside the rate — measuring the Stop hook's real hit rate before anything gets built to improve it.
- Code review over the above found 8 issues; this PR includes fixes for the ones confirmed as real bugs in this branch's own changes:
  - A checkpoint filed through the MCP hook landed in a different _convos folder than one filed through transcript ingest, for the same conversation (host_session id was truncated on one path, not the other).
  - logos doctor --integration reported a cleanup failure on every run once checkpoints started landing several directories deep.
  - logos resume read and parsed every checkpoint in the vault before answering a plain project name.
  - Two conversations in the same project/agent within the same second could claim the same checkpoint filename in two different convo folders.
  - forgetRow discarded a failed vault-file removal, leaving the index and the vault disagreeing.
  - A ruling's time: anchor had an empty pathspec that made git fail the whole commit-count call, silently zeroing Drift.Commits even when a real git:/dep:/doc: anchor in the same AND clause had actually changed.
- Two other review findings (a swallowed digest-stamp write error, and Supersedes carrying a possibly-empty pre-migration uid) were investigated and left as-is: both are already documented in-code as deliberate, honest defaults, not oversights.

This completes plan0-5-5.md's decided 0.5.5 scope: A1-A4 + C5 + G1. (H1 and ci-house-rules remain separate, for 0.5.4.)

body:
Tier: 3 (core src/cost)

Fixes double-counting in the transcript token fold: Claude Code writes one JSONL line per content block of an assistant message, each repeating the full `usage`. The fold now counts each `message.id` once per session/file, at its LARGEST line; lines without an id behave as before.

Change: `parseUsageLine` exposes `messageId`; `parseTranscriptFile` and `sumSessionTokens` (src/cost/transcript-fold.ts) collapse repeats through one pure `dedupeByMessageId`. Cost-by-class, `tokensLast24h` and the per-dispatch token surrogate are all corrected together.

### Follow-up pushed during operator review

- **Keep the largest line, not the first.** `output_tokens` grows as a message streams, and only the last line carries the complete count. Measured on the 300 newest local transcripts:
  - keeping the first line under-counts output tokens by 20% (2.60M vs 3.24M);
  - in all 891 groups whose output differs, the last line is the largest;
  - input and cache counts match across repeats.

  This is the rule ccusage uses. Ties keep the earlier line, and output keeps first-seen order. On 5 real transcripts, `sumSessionTokens` now matches an independent keep-max count exactly.
- **Parse-memo invalidation.** `hydra:metrics:transcript-parse-memo` entries were valid on (size, mtime) alone, so finished transcripts would have replayed their inflated pre-fix totals for up to 7 days. Entries now carry a `parseVersion`, set from `TRANSCRIPT_PARSE_VERSION` = 2 in transcript-fold.ts. The scan's existing usability gate treats any other version as a clean miss, so the file is re-parsed and its entry overwritten. Entries persisted before the stamp load as version 0. The one-time cost is a cold re-parse of the 7-day corpus on the first scan after deploy. Eligibility is meter-only and does not wait on it.

## Files in scope

- src/cost/transcript-fold.ts
- src/cost/token-math.ts
- src/cost/transcript-scan.ts
- src/redis/transcript-parse-memo.ts
- test/transcript-fold.test.mts
- test/transcript-scan.test.mts
- .changelog/5141-transcript-message-id-dedup.md

## Acceptance

- [x] 3-line message folds once — verified by: `npm run test:file -- test/transcript-fold.test.mts` (subtests under "message.id de-duplication")
- [x] Distinct ids still sum, no-id lines unchanged — verified by: same file
- [x] The largest line of a message wins; a tie keeps the earlier line — verified by: same file
- [x] A memo entry from an older parser is re-parsed and overwritten, and a pre-stamp entry loads as version 0 — verified by: `npm run test:file -- test/transcript-scan.test.mts`
- [x] `npm test` footer fail 0 and `npm run typecheck:test` OK
- [ ] Live before/after per-class numbers — NOT recorded here: after deploy, compare `curl -s localhost:4000/api/metrics/cost-by-class`. The parse-memo version bump re-parses every in-window file on the first scan, so the corrected figures appear at once.

Downstream: `src/cost/eligibility-usage.ts` and `weighted-quota-estimate.ts` consume the folded totals; any threshold calibrated on inflated numbers will read lower after this. `scripts/cost/weighted-quota-report.ts` has its own `parseUsageLine` loop and still double-counts (follow-up, not in scope).

Glossary impact: none. ADR impact: none.

Closes #5141

author: mmontielpz
body:
Users can now configure JACK through `jack setup` instead of manually editing the four-key file. Guided setup selects workstation, Mac, or both, validates explicit destination identities with the existing rules, previews the result, and requires `yes` before saving. Scripted setup requires `--non-interactive --yes` and complete destination pairs, with no prompts or Tailscale operations.

Configuration saves preserve the other device, reject unsafe paths, use restrictive permissions (directory 700/file 600), and atomically replace the file through a private temporary file. Locks and content rechecks reject overlapping edits. Cancellation and ordinary write failures preserve existing configuration. Existing routing, authentication, and SSH invocation are unchanged.

Discovery uses the slice's permitted documented manual fallback: no JSON parser dependency or fragile JSON extraction. Interactive setup checks CLI availability and the exit status of `tailscale status --peers=false --self=false`, discarding untrusted output. It reports running/starting without claiming verified connectivity or SSH authorization. README, help, installer guidance messages, and pre-merge evidence describe this limitation.

Validation: all 12 `./scripts/dev-check.sh` groups PASS on CachyOS/Bash 5.3.20. Offline tests cover interactive targets, automation, manual fallback with valid/empty/malformed/malicious output, unavailable/disconnected Tailscale, preservation, cancellation/EOF, invalid arguments/identities, private modes, failed rename/mktemp, lock retention, concurrent edits, unsafe permissions, symlink refusal, tripwires, and existing regressions. ShellCheck clean for CLI/tests; six existing non-blocking installer findings remain. Diff reviewed and `git diff --check` passes.

No dependencies installed, live tailnet/device validation, installation paths, sudo, service/ACL/SSH changes, or key operations. No E2E. macOS/Bash 3.2 runtime NOT_RUN pending Product Owner acceptance. Automatic peer selection is not implemented. Config comments are removed on an explicitly confirmed save; abrupt kills may leave a lock. No claim of power-loss durability or protection from hostile processes running as the same user.

author: han1989
body:
GitHub moved `ubuntu-latest` to Ubuntu 26.04 on 19 Oct 2026. Since then every browser job fails in the composite setup action, so Han1989/tgt-td-cld#124 can't go green.

## What the log shows

[Run 39647226060](https://github.com/Han1989/tgt-td-cld/actions/runs/39647226060), attempt 2 (#124). The `e2e (desktop 1/1)` and `e2e (perf)` logs were read; the other five browser jobs failed at the same step. The failure is in **Install Playwright Chromium** (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`):

```
BEWARE: your OS is not officially supported by Playwright; installing dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 as a fallback.
Cannot install dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 with Playwright 1.56.1!
Error: ERROR: Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64
```

No apt package fails. Playwright 1.56.1 has no dependency list for 26.04 and stops before it calls apt. Everything earlier in the job succeeds: setup-node (Node 22.23.4), the npm cache, `npm ci`, and the Playwright browser cache (`Linux-playwright-1.56.1`, a hit). That rules out a cache key, Node or npm problem. The `test` job skips this step, which is why it passes.

## Change

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: all five `runs-on` (`test`, `changes`, `e2e`, `e2e-perf`, `ci`) are now `ubuntu-24.04`, the image the suite last passed on (17 Oct). One comment line above `jobs:` gives the reason and the date.
- Nothing else changed: no code, docs or tracker. No doc names the runner, so `docs/DEPLOY.md` stays as it is.

The browser cache key is still `Linux-playwright-1.56.1`. Its entry was saved by a 24.04 run, so it stays valid.

## Proof

This pull request's own CI run. It touches `.github`, so `changes` turns the browser jobs on and every e2e job runs on 24.04. Locally `npm test` (85 files, 1,353 tests) and `npm run build` pass. Browser tests weren't run in the session: the failure is in the runner image, which only CI has.

## After merge

Merge this, then re-run Han1989/tgt-td-cld#124 (or merge main into it). Auto-merge is off.

author: jonathanagustin
body:
## Description

Closes #79.

**The fix.** CloudTAK's generated nginx config listens on `[::]:5000`. On a node whose kernel has IPv6 disabled (`ipv6.disable=1`) there are no AF_INET6 sockets, so nginx stops with `socket() [::]:5000 failed (97: Address family not supported by protocol)` and the `cloudtak` container crash-loops. `start.sh` already rewrites the generated config with `sed`. It now also deletes the `listen [::]` lines when `/proc/net/if_inet6` is absent, just before nginx starts. On a kernel with IPv6 that file exists, so the config is left unchanged.

**A CI gap this PR hit, fixed in the second commit.** The Test workflow skips a pull request that only changes `.github/container-and-chart/**` (by design, image-only changes are built elsewhere). But Test is also the only workflow that builds the CloudTAK and PostGIS images on a pull request, and the package and scan workflows wait for those images. So a PR that only touches an image directory waited about an hour for an image nobody was going to build, then failed (`images` in the scan workflow: `does not have inputs ... for every one of amd64 arm64`). `cloudtak-image.yaml` and `postgis-image.yaml` now also run on `pull_request` for their own paths. `build.sh --if-changed` makes a second build, from the Test workflow when it does run, a no-op.

**Verified:** in an nginx container on a kernel with no IPv6, the unmodified config (`listen 5000;` plus `listen [::]:5000;`) fails with the same error 97. With the guard copied verbatim from `start.sh`, only `listen 5000;` remains and nginx keeps running. Earlier, the same change applied by hand to the running CloudTAK pod on a no-IPv6 cluster took it from CrashLoopBackOff to 3/3 Ready. `shellcheck` (repo flags), `yamllint --strict`, `actionlint`, `codespell` and `lint:shell` pass.

**Not verified here:** the workflow change itself. This PR's run is the first to build an image from a pull request that the Test workflow skips, so it is also the check that the wait in the scan and package workflows now finds the image. Because Test is skipped for this PR, the rebuilt image is not run through the install and upgrade tests before merge.

## Checklist

- [x] The pull request title follows Conventional Commits
- [ ] `hk check --all` passes (shellcheck, yamllint, actionlint, codespell and the shell lint only)
- [x] New or changed behavior has a test (or the description says why it can't)
- [x] Docs, values, or an ADR are updated if behavior or configuration changed
- [x] No private keys, passwords, or enrolled certificates are committed

author: chasem-dev
body:
**Symptom:** a Windows player with Super Mario Eclipse always sees Update & play. Every press rebuilds the same game version. Their logs show full Eclipse builds of `2026.10.21-beta.ef70f02` in `ef70f02-1896`, one after another, with no download step. Each ends `Game … is ready`, and the button is still there afterwards.

**Cause:** on Windows, picking the Vulkan renderer makes the launcher set `SMS_GX_VULKAN=ON` for the build (`port.buildEnvironment`). `build.sh` passes it to CMake, but `scripts/build-eclipse.sh` never did. So the Eclipse build's CMake cache never has `SMS_GX_VULKAN=ON`, `game.needsVulkanBuild` stays true, and `isCurrent` is false after every build. Those players also never got Vulkan in Eclipse. Linux isn't affected because Vulkan is on there by default, and macOS isn't because the script hands off to `build.sh`.

**Fix:** `build-eclipse.sh` forwards `SMS_GX_VULKAN` the same way `build.sh` does. When it's unset, the game's default is kept.

**Test:** the Eclipse builder test now checks that no `SMS_GX_VULKAN` is passed by default, and that `-DSMS_GX_VULKAN=ON` is passed when the launcher asks for it. That check fails without the fix. `npm test`: 454 pass, 0 fail. Not tested on Windows.

The next Update & play after this ships does one more build, this time with Vulkan, and is then up to date. Until then, switching the renderer to OpenGL under Settings → Graphics makes the existing build count as current.

body:
Trello: https://trello.com/c/qK3f1cpc (Tablet & iPad Layout Optimization)

## What changes

Tablets (600pt/dp and wider, measured on the window minus side insets) get layouts built for the space; phones render exactly as before.

- **Responsive module** — `constants/responsive.ts` (pure, tested) + `useResponsiveLayout`. Below 600 every helper returns today's phone values and the column styles are `{}`.
- **Reading column** (max 720) on every list, profile, settings and search screen; **Home column** (max 1100) with the two heroes and the queen/chips paired in reading-order rows; carousels show as many cards as fit, anchored right.
- **Sections** become a 3–4 column tile grid (3 on 10–11" portrait, 4 on 13" and landscape).
- **Mushaf** reader on a centred sheet (max 760) with type scaled up to 1.2×, keeping the five font levels distinct; the reading place survives rotation and Split View resizes.
- **Scholar profile** splits into a 340pt side panel + lecture list in landscape (≥900 wide).
- **Chrome** — tab bar items 96pt in a centred row; MiniPlayer, sheets and the note editor capped at 600.
- **Android tablets rotate**: `plugins/withTabletRotation.js` keeps the manifest portrait lock for phones and switches to `FULL_USER` when `smallestScreenWidthDp >= 600` (Android 16 ignores the lock there anyway).
- **iPad page sheets** — patched react-native-screens so RTL page-sheet modals sit at the sheet's origin (they were shifted ~97pt right with the right side clipped; also on main).

Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-22-tablet-layout-design.md` (v4) · Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-22-tablet-layout-implementation-plan.md` · QA: `docs/plans/2026-10-22-tablet-layout-qa.md`

## Out of scope

- Quran translation side by side — no licensed translation source in the app; needs the Foundation to confirm one.
- Two-page Mushaf spread, tablet Figma frames (none exist), store screenshots (release task).

## Verification

- `npx jest` 135 suites / 1715 tests pass · `tsc --noEmit` clean · lint 0 errors.
- Phones: iPhone 16 and a 360×800 (Realme Note 50-class) AVD screenshot-diffed against pre-branch baselines — 0% on Home, Sections, Mushaf, scholar, More (Library differs only in progress data). Phones stay portrait-locked.
- Tablets: iPad Pro 13" (portrait + landscape), Pixel Tablet API 36 and API 35 (portrait, landscape, rotation both ways).
- Web (RtlCarousel change): Playwright at 1280 and 393 — Home rows and the Library filter row pack right. Expo web needs local changes to start on main too (missing `shaka-player`, zustand `import.meta`); captured with a throwaway, uncommitted metro config.
- **iPad Split View / windowing (iPadOS 26):** tiled with Safari and in free windows at about ⅓, ½ and full width, portrait and landscape. A window narrower than 600pt gets the phone layout, a wider one the tablet layout, and the layout reflows both ways as the window is resized. That pass found that the system window controls sit over the system's leading top corner. On an English system they covered the Home bell; on an Arabic system they covered the back button of every `InlineHeader` screen, which then couldn't be tapped. Fixed in `3222e49`: a 60pt clearance on that side on iPadOS 26+ in a window. Verified in English and Arabic; full screen is unchanged.
- Not walked with a live screen reader; reading order is enforced structurally (`READING_ROW` / `READING_GRID`).

## Release

Native changes (Android config plugin, iOS react-native-screens patch) — ship in new binaries via EAS, not OTA.

  - `Edit commands` opens the workspace `.plexi/commands.toml` when present or falls back to global `~/.plexi-<channel>/commands.toml`, and adds explicit palette rows (`Edit commands (workspace)` and `Edit commands (global)`).
  - Adds a header bar in the built-in commands editor showing the `GLOBAL` / `WORKSPACE` badge, truncated target file path with full-path tooltip, `Reveal in Finder` / `Reveal in file manager` button, and in-place `Switch to workspace` / `Switch to global` button (creating `.plexi/commands.toml` with starter template on first switch and guarding unsaved edits behind an inline Save/Discard/Cancel bar).
- **0879 (`User commands run in the current pane by default instead of splitting`)**:
  - Single-line `run = "..."` user commands execute in-place inside the focused terminal pane when its shell is idle (`TerminalPane::is_idle_shell()`), and fall back to splitting right when the focused pane is busy, running an agent, is an app pane, or when `split = true` is explicitly set on the command.
- **0881 (`Open panes pick up new commands without restart (re-read on use, no watcher)`)**:
  - Re-reads `commands.toml` (global + active workspace override) when the Command Palette opens, on `commands: reload` IPC, and on unbound key presses before checking user-command keybindings.
  - Propagates `PLEXI_WORKSPACE_ROOT` from the focused pane/context to `plexi run` and `plexi commands list` so open terminal panes immediately see newly added/edited/removed commands without restarting the shell or host.
- **0883 (`config check: clear OK summary + flag misplaced tables`)**:
  - `plexi config check` prints a clear per-file status summary (`OK` / `WARNING` / `ERROR` / `not found`) for global `config.toml`, global `commands.toml`, and workspace `.plexi/commands.toml`, plus command counts (`N global, M workspace`) and final `Config check passed` / `Config check passed with N warning(s)` / `Config check failed`.
  - Flags `[commands.*]` tables misplaced in `config.toml` and `config.toml`-only tables (`[theme]`, `[font]`, `[keys]`, `[window]`, `[terminal]`, `[updates]`, `[notifications]`, `[claude]`, `[ai]`, `[network]`, `[audio]`, `[secrets]`, `[workspace]`, `[QuickNote]`, `[markdown]`, `[data_table]`) misplaced in `commands.toml` (both in CLI `plexi config check` and inline in the built-in editor status banner).
- **0885 (`Built-in editor: Cmd+/ toggles line comments (# for TOML)`)**:
  - Implements `Command::ToggleComment` (`Cmd+/` on macOS, `Ctrl+/` on Linux/Windows) in the built-in editor with language-aware comment prefixes (`#` for `.toml`/`.py`/`.sh`/`.yaml`, `//` for `.rs`/`.js`/`.ts`/`.go`/`.c`/`.jsonc`, `--` for `.sql`/`.lua`) and single-step undo (`Command::ReplaceRange`).
  - Routes `Cmd+/` to `AppTrait::handle_key` when a built-in editor pane is focused so it toggles line comments instead of opening the shortcuts overlay.
- **0886 (`run: step splits anchor to the invoking pane on every trigger`)**:
  - Captures the invoking pane ID once before running a stepped user command (both in host palette/shortcut execution and in `plexi run <name>`) and substitutes `--from <invoking_pane_id>` into any `pane split` step that omits `--from`, while preserving explicit `--from` targets.
- **0898 (`Zoom: Cmd+Enter is the only toggle; Esc no longer un-zooms and passes through to the pane`)**:
  - Removes Escape un-zoom from terminal panes (`src/app/mod.rs`), app panes (`src/app/dispatch.rs`), and `Action::CloseApp` (`src/app/mod.rs`) so bare `Esc` while zoomed passes straight through to the focused pane without changing zoom state.
  - Keeps `Cmd+Enter` (`Action::ToggleZoom`) and `plexi pane zoom` CLI as two-way zoom toggles, and updates the keyboard shortcuts overlay (`Zoom / Unzoom Pane`).

## Test Evidence
- Classification: host logic + host UI
- Automated tests:
  - `cargo test --bin plexi -- toggle_comment_single_line_selection_mixed_indented_blank_and_undo cmd_slash_toggles_comment_in_focused_editor_and_opens_shortcuts_overlay_outside_editor commands_editor_surfaces_misplaced_config_tables_inline config_check_reports_ok_summary_and_flags_misplaced_commands_and_config_tables edit_commands_shows_scope_and_path_switches_scope_in_place_and_saves_reloads single_line_user_command_runs_in_focused_idle_shell_and_splits_when_busy_agent_app_or_split_true open_panes_pick_up_newly_added_edited_and_removed_commands_without_restart stepped_command_splits_anchor_to_invoking_pane_on_every_trigger_unless_explicit_from pane_close_keys_keep_host_and_restore_zoom zoom_cmd_enter_and_cli_toggle_both_ways_and_bare_escape_passes_through_without_unzooming screenshot_edit_commands_header_scope_banner` — 11 passed
  - `cargo test --bin plexi -- two_step_play_command_opens_two_panes_via_cli_palette_and_bound_key_and_shows_in_pane_list pane_zoom_escape_still_reaches_terminal_pty scene_suite` — 3 passed
  - `just check-docs` — passed
  - `cargo clippy --bin plexi -- -D warnings` — 0 warnings
  - `just build` — release build with `-D warnings` succeeded
- Visual review:
  - Rendered and inspected `screenshot_edit_commands_header_scope_banner` via `egui_kittest` (`WORKSPACE` badge, truncated path, `Switch to global` button, `Reveal in Finder` button, and `Saved` indicator aligned cleanly with no clipping or overlap).

body:
## Story
E21-62 (c3a), the tests half of a DEC-77 pair. It implements DEC-2272, in #2088: option A, so the service reads each agent's daily research cap itself from the deployed mandate. Claim: #2028.

`mandate_gatewayd::cap` is added as `todo!()` stubs:
- `deployment`: the agent's latest `AgentDeployed` or `AgentStopped` in this environment.
- `research_cap`: reads the version's hash-checked artifact, takes `behavior.research.cost_cap_usd_per_day`, and passes it through `PolicyOverlay::internal_research_profile`.
- `DailyCaps`: holds each agent's cap with the deployment it came from, and reads it again on a change.

It reads no more of the mandate than that (DEC-2272 item 2), because the crate's layer entry forbids `mandate-spec`.

Wiring `DailyCaps` into the service's calls and the binary is c3b. The artifact store is GO's read-only mount from #2098 (DEC-2273).

## Spec clause → test
- Item 1 → `the_cap_is_the_deployed_version_s_own`, using the daemon's real fixture mandate.
- Item 3 → `no_research_envelope_no_deployment_or_a_stop_gives_zero`.
- Item 1, the latest record scoped by agent and environment → `only_the_agent_s_latest_record_in_this_environment_counts`.
- Item 4, fail closed with codes → `each_document_that_does_not_read_is_refused_with_its_code`. It covers a missing artifact, a hash mismatch, not JSON, a live document, no cap, a cap that is not an amount, a cap above the monthly budget, a cap finer than `Usd6`, and an unreadable control row.
- Items 1 and 4, the coordinator's check → `a_document_whose_hash_differs_from_the_journaled_version_is_refused`. A cap-49 document stored under the journaled cap-5 version's digest is refused, never read as 49. The true document then reads as 5.
- Item 5 → `a_version_change_is_read_again_and_a_failed_read_leaves_no_cap`. An unchanged deployment is not read again, a change is, and a failed read leaves no stale cap.
- Items 1 and 4 as a property → `any_cap_is_read_as_itself_or_refused_above_the_monthly_cap`.

## Dependencies
New internal normal dependencies of mandate-gatewayd:
- `mandate-canon`
- `mandate-journal`, moved from dev-dependencies
- `mandate-num`
- `mandate-research`

All are pure and none is forbidden. No new external crates. `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask deps` are clean.

## Journal events added
None. This code only reads.

## Not done
c3b: the binary, the cap wired into each research call, probes, `ProviderKey` zeroizing, and the secrecy row.

## Decisions needed
None. DEC-2272 is in #2088; its number was assigned by the coordinator.

## Safety checklist
- Tests first: 7 pending tests, all failing at a stub.
- The cap fails closed.
- The cap can't be asserted by the caller.

## Checks
- `cargo xtask ci pending`: all 46 fail at a stub.
- `cargo xtask ci lint`: clean.
- Main is merged in.

The first commit's message on this branch says DEC-2268. It is already pushed, and the branch is never force-pushed. Every file and this description cite DEC-2272.

body:
## What

`tmux_lane.sh` refuses to start a Coder or Tester lane whose model family is the same as the other lane's, or unknown. The family comes from the named model, else from a single-vendor agent (`lane_agent.py family`). Only where no other family is configured may the operator proceed, by setting `FACTORY_LANE_INDEPENDENCE_GAP` to the reason. Every launch record now carries `independence`: the lane's family and, beside the other lane, the tier achieved (I19).

## Why

In herald-dash-r3 Muse ran both lanes and nothing objected. The doctrine (SOFTWARE-FACTORY.md "Across the lanes", DOCTRINE-KERNEL E1 and I19) asks for different families, and other families were configured. A written rule nobody enforces failed; this makes the launcher enforce it.

## Evidence

- New tests: `test_a_lane_names_its_model_family_from_the_model_first_then_a_single_vendor_agent`, `test_the_tester_does_not_start_on_the_coders_model_family`, `test_a_same_family_lane_starts_only_with_its_gap_recorded`. The gate row LCH names them.
- Full suite, branch against main: the branch adds no failures. Both fail the same 39 `test_harness_scripts.py` flake, mutate and receipt tests, which shell out to a system python3 that has no pytest (environmental, pre-existing). Main also fails 2 `test_denial_probes.py` tests that pass on the branch.
- Live: the r3 Tester relaunched on `gpt-6.1-sol` beside the Muse Coder; its launch record reads `{"family":"openai","other_family":"meta","tier":"cross-family"}`.
- An independent review on a different model family (Sol via Codex) runs before merge.
