body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [skript](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript) | patch | `2.17.0` → `2.17.1` |

---

> [!WARNING]
> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/3311) for more information.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>SkriptLang/Skript (skript)</summary>

### [`v2.17.1`](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/releases/tag/2.17.1): Emergency Patch Release 2.17.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/compare/2.17.0...2.17.1)

### Skript 2.17.1

**Supports: Paper 1.21.5 - 26.3**

Today, we are releasing (early) Skript 2.17.1 to address some important issues that have arisen with the 2.17.0 release. Importantly, this release fixes an issue that prevented Skript from loading on Paper 26.3 build 211 or newer.

Per our [release model](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/blob/master/CLOCKWORK_RELEASE_MODEL.md), we will still plan to release 2.17.2 on November 1st (assuming there are additional changes to publish). We may release additional emergency patch releases before then should the need arise.

As always, you can report any issues on our [issue tracker](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/issues).

Happy Skripting!

#### Changelog

##### Bug Fixes

- [#​8907](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/issues/8907) Fixes an issue where folders were not working as expected in the `/skript reload` command.
- [#​8908](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/issues/8908) Fixes multiple issues with entity data/type serialization. We are still looking to make improvements here, so please report any unexpected behavior!
- [#​8910](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/issues/8910) Fixes an issue where the `record song` effect did not work on newer Paper versions.
- [#​8913](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/issues/8913) Fixes an issue where Skript failed to load on Paper 26.3 build 211 or newer.

[Click here to view the full list of commits made since 2.17.0](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/compare/2.17.0...2.17.1)

#### Notices

##### Experimental Features

Experimental features can be used to enable syntax and other behavior on a per-script basis. Some of these features are new proposals that we are testing while others may have unsafe or complex elements that regular users may not need.

While we have tested the available experiments to the best of our ability, they are they are still in development. As a result, they are subject to change and may contain bugs. Experiments should be used at your own discretion.

Additionally, example scripts demonstrating usage of the available experiments can be found [here](https://redirect.github.com/SkriptLang/Skript/tree/2.16.2/src/main/resources/scripts/-examples/experimental%20features).

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the experiments available in this release</summary>

##### Queue

**Enable by adding `using queues` to your script.**

A collection that removes elements whenever they are requested.

This is useful for processing tasks or keeping track of things that need to happen only once.

```applescript=
set {queue} to a new queue of "hello" and "world"

broadcast the first element of {queue}

# "hello" is now removed

broadcast the first element of {queue}

# "world" is now removed

# queue is empty
```

```applescript=
set {queue} to a new queue of all players

set {player 1} to a random element out of {queue} 
set {player 2} to a random element out of {queue}

# players 1 and 2 are guaranteed to be distinct
```

Queues can be looped over like a regular list.

##### Script Reflection

**Enable by adding `using script reflection` to your script.**

This feature includes:

- The ability to reference a script in code.
- Finding and running functions by name.
- Reading configuration files and values.

##### Local Variable Type Hints

**Enable by adding `using type hints` to your script.**

Local variable type hints enable Skript to understand what kind of values your local variables will hold at parse time. Consider the following example:

```applescript
set {_a} to 5
set {_b} to "some string"
... do stuff ...
set {_c} to {_a} in lowercase # oops i used the wrong variable
```

Previously, the code above would parse without issue. However, Skript now understands that when it is used, `{_a}` could only be a number (and not a text). Thus, the code above would now error with a message about mismatched types.

Please note that this feature is currently only supported by **simple local variables**. A simple local variable is one whose name does not contain any expressions:

```applescript
{_var} # can use type hints
{_var::%player's name%} # can't use type hints
```

##### Runtime Error Catching

**Enable by adding `using error catching` to your script.**

A new `catch [run[ ]time] error[s]` section allows you to catch and suppress runtime errors within it and access them later with `[the] last caught [run[ ]time] errors`.

```applescript
catch runtime errors:
    ...
    set worldborder center of {_border} to {_my unsafe location}
    ...
if last caught runtime errors contains "Your location can't have a NaN value as one of its components":
    set worldborder center of {_border} to location(0, 0, 0)
```

##### Equippable Components

**Enable by adding `using equippable components` to your script.**

Equippable components allows retrieving and changing the data of an item in the usage as equipment/armor.

Below is an example of creating a blank equippable component, modifying it, and applying it to an item:

```applescript
set {_component} to a blank equippable component:
	set the camera overlay to "custom_overlay"
	set the allowed entities to a zombie and a skeleton
	set the equip sound to "block.note_block.pling"
	set the equipped model id to "custom_model"
	set the shear sound to "ui.toast.in"
	set the equipment slot to chest slot
	allow event-equippable component to be damage when hurt
	allow event-equippable component to be dispensed
	allow event-equippable component to be equipped onto entities
	allow event-equippable component to be sheared off
	allow event-equippable component to swap equipment
set the equippable component of {_item} to {_component}
```

Changes can be made directly on to the existing equippable component of an item whether using the item itself or the retrieved equippable component

```applescript
set the equipment slot of {_item} to helmet slot
    
set {_component} to the equippable component of {_item}
allow {_component} to swap equipment
```

For more details about the syntax, visit [equippable component](https://docs.skriptlang.org/docs.html?search=equippable%20component) on our documentation website.

</details>

##### New Documentation Site
Over the past few months, we have been working hard to build our new documentation site. Not only do we have a new-and-improved syntaxes page, we are also finally launching a proper platform for official tutorials on using Skript, from writing scripts to building addons.

As we continue to prepare the site for launch later this year, the beta is available for viewing at <https://beta-docs.skriptlang.org>.

##### Join us on Discord

We have an [official Discord community](https://discord.gg/ZPsZAg6ygu) where we share announcements and and perform testing for upcoming features.

Special thanks to the contributors whose work was included in this version:

- [@​APickledWalrus](https://redirect.github.com/APickledWalrus)

If you have any bigger ideas or input for the future of Skript, you can share those too at <htt

author: erwei-xilinx
body:
Follow-up to #2145 and #2159.

## Why

The Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B DFlash examples share their kernels and arithmetic. Their host-side code existed in several copies:
- **4B:** its own runtime, `run.py`, `verify_loop.py` and `build_target.py`.
- **The two 8B models:** a second, 95%-identical set in `common/run_8b.py`, `pipeline_8b.py`, `verify_loop_8b.py` and `build_b8.py`.
- **All three models:** a copy each of the three device checks (`check_decoder`, `check_model`, `check_prepass`), the profile and the resource preparer.

Each copy found its model's modules by being run from that model's directory, so a fix had to be made two or three times.

## What changes

**A model describes itself once.** Each model directory gets a `dflash_model.py`, which builds a `DFlashModel` (in `common/model.py`):
- its checkpoints, cache defaults and decoder classes;
- its EOS tokens and chat-template options;
- whether CPU prefill is offered (Llama doesn't offer it).

**Shared code moves to `common/`** and takes the model as an argument:
- `runtime.py`
- `run.py`
- `verify_loop.py`
- `profile.py`
- `build_target.py`
- `resources.py`
- `check_decoder.py`, `check_model.py` and `check_prepass.py`
- the 8B weight-preparation driver, now `common/prepare_weights_8b.py`

The `*_8b` host modules and `build_b8.py` are removed. The 8B AIR mapping and weight adapters from #2159 (`b8_*`, `decoder_8b`, `*_weights_8b`, `prepare_*_8b`) are unchanged.

**Model directories keep short entry scripts.** Makefile targets, command lines, LIT entries and the `downloadLLMWeights.yml` invocation are all unchanged.

**Values that differed between copies are now passed in or derived:**

| Value | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel `-D` flags (`MODEL_TYPE`, RMS epsilon, layout) | Hard-coded per builder copy | `kernel_defines(cfg)` in each model's `build_target.py`, so a value can differ by role |
| Reference repo and tokenizer files | Literals in each `resources.py` | Passed by the model's `resources.py` |
| Tap width in the prepass check | Literal per model | `reference.fc.shape[1]` |
| HF reference geometry in the model check | Literal per model | The reference `config.json`; `head_dim` falls back to `hidden_size / num_attention_heads` |
| EOS, chat options, CPU prefill | `model_spec` reads in the 8B copies, literals in 4B | `DFlashModel` fields |

**Two behaviours that are now the same for every model:**
- **Attention options:** the build passes the selected attention options to the kernels. 4B previously relied on the kernel headers' defaults, which match its configuration, so its objects are byte-identical.
- **Object reuse:** when the drafter build can't reuse a target object, it compiles it and lists it under `recompiled_objects` in the build manifest. The 8B builder recompiled silently; 4B's builder raised an error. Llama's drafter now records all six of its recompiled objects. The Qwen drafters still reuse everything.

The decoder build identity also hashes `common/build_target.py`, so a change to the shared builder marks existing builds stale.

## Docs

- **Removed the dated measurement logs** `qwen3_8b/docs/qualification.md` and `llama31_8b/docs/qualification.md`, along with the Full20 figures in Llama's README. The results remain in #2145's and #2159's descriptions; the method is in each `validation.md`.
- **Trimmed the 8B docs:** removed compiler internals, PR history, toolchain version tables and XRT version notes.
- **Updated** `common/README.md` and the code maps for the moved files.

## Testing

On Krackan NPU2, all three examples were run from `main` (`3a6e9864`, baseline) and from this branch. Each run did `make weights compile`, `make profile` and `make verify`, the last covering decoder state, the DFlash loop and the HF BF16 top-5 model check.

| | Profile output (256 tokens) | Decode tok/s, `main` → this PR | `make verify` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B | identical | 21.388 → 21.393 | pass, identical |
| Qwen3-8B | identical | 13.133 → 13.141 | pass, identical |
| Llama-3.1-8B | identical | 16.162 / 16.161 → 16.168 / 16.165 | pass, identical |

- **Outputs:** every verification output (target, drafter, loop, NPU and HF captures, model comparison) is identical between `main` and this PR once timings and file identities are excluded.
- **Build:** the generated `aie.air.mlir` and all Peano objects are byte-identical for target and drafter in all three models.
- **Llama speed:** its tok/s are two alternating re-runs; a first single run read 16.242 vs 16.161.
- **CI-side checks:** all entry scripts import and parse. The host unit tests (`run_host_checks.lit`) and `python/test/api/examples_sys_path.py` pass, and black is clean.

Before: nobody had checked whether SG18–SG24 left places where Atlas silently misses symbols or edges.

After: AUDIT-9.md ranks the findings: 0 critical, 2 high, 9 medium and 3 low.
- **Highs:** (1) upgrading Atlas never re-parses unchanged files, so parser fixes reach an existing index only after `--force`. (2) Locals inside module-level callbacks become top-level symbols. On express, got and trpc they make up 61–90% of the recorded top-level names, and they can take edges meant for real functions.
- **PLAN.md:** adds SG25 and SG26 for these, together with the mediums on the same code paths.
- **Checked clean:** Atlas agreed with `tsc` on all 9,418 imports in 4 real repos.

How: real repos were compared against `git ls-files`, `tsc` resolution and Python import rules. 22 hand mutations were applied to `src/` and reverted; the 6 that survived are now caught by new tests. `test/audit/audit-9.test.ts` has 17 `it.fails` pins and 10 plain tests. body:
## Objet
Ajoute un volet repliable **dans le laboratoire Radar historique existant** : décisions A/B reconstruites sur les 7 journées prospectives archivées (14–20 octobre 2026), sans modifier ni optimiser le protocole PAPER.

- 20 paires Binance Spot **USDT**, 7 archives dont le SHA-256 est contrôlé à la lecture et en CI.

## Summary

Fixes #6118. Preserve actionable Protobuf schema-admission diagnostics: an undefined selected message points to `protobuf.schema.message_type` (`invalid_value`); malformed or unresolved descriptor definitions point to `protobuf.schema.descriptor_set_path` (`invalid_format`). Both still return `invalid_request` and retain sanitized partial capture Evidence.

## Problem and expected behavior

A valid descriptor with `capture.Missing` and corrupt descriptor bytes previously produced the same generic schema error. Callers could not tell whether to correct the selected type or replace the descriptor. Wire preflight also discarded its known byte offset/reason.

## Change and scope

`ProtobufSchema.read` now returns the existing typed `Result<ProtobufSchema, AnalysisInputError>` for schema admission. The owning stage identifies the rejected field and retains wire facts or SDK causes internally. `ProtobufCapture` forwards this result, removing its blanket catch/reclassification. SDK exception text is not copied into public issues; shared byte-budget and cancellation failures remain outside SDK catches. An entry checkpoint also honors cancellation for empty descriptors.

Within the [existing offline capture scope](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-scope); no new provider, target execution or authority requiring a separate maintainer decision.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner/earliest changed stage: descriptor-wire/SDK registry admission in `ProtobufSchema`, consumed by `ProtobufCapture`.
- Scope/maintainer decision: correction within existing schema interpretation; separate decision not applicable.
- CLI/MCP/tool-catalog: no new argument, tool or success schema. Both interfaces expose the corrected `details.issues` paths/reasons. Example: `{path:["protobuf","schema","message_type"],reason:"invalid_value"}`.
- Provider/bridge/format/platform: existing FileDescriptorSet and HAR workflow; underlying protobuf-es 2.16.0 and framing remain unchanged.
- Evidence/artifact/provenance: valid CLI/MCP Evidence IDs remain equal; failures preserve the original capture SHA and retained ordinal 0 in the generated controls.
- Target selection/authority/cleanup: selected local files only; no acquisition, network retrieval, replay or cleanup-policy expansion.
- Generated metadata/package/install: no dependency, version or installer change. No generated catalogs, binaries or build outputs committed.

Expected effects:

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.
- [ ] Launch or attach to a process.
- [ ] Inject instrumentation or run scripts/code.
- [ ] Change process memory, registers, files, or configuration.
- [ ] Contact network services.
- [ ] Recover protected code or work around protections.
- [ ] Documentation or usability only; no target interaction.
- [ ] Not sure yet; investigation or maintainer guidance needed.

The verification harness starts REA's own CLI/MCP subprocesses and writes self-owned fixtures; the feature adds no target-process operation.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- Fixed baseline: main `26356dc34a74e38b68eb2acb4befb126176ed978`, package 6.7.0.
- Before the production change, the three new CLI/MCP cases selected by test name had one valid case pass and two error-path cases fail on the incorrect issue paths. The other 21 cases were skipped in that selected baseline run, not counted as passed.
- After the change, all 24 capture acceptance cases pass through the compiled CLI and production stdio MCP, including valid/missing/malformed descriptor cases, retained views after failure, source identity, byte-budget refusal, credential exclusions and schema round trips.
- Producer tests preserve malformed unknown-field rejection with the original byte-16 overflowing-varint cause, SDK decoding/registry failures, empty descriptor versus missing type, leading-dot lookup, registry expansion budget and exact caller cancellation reasons.
- [Current-head code CI 39723699187](https://github.com/morluto/rea/actions/runs/39723699187) **passed** for `f415732d`. Source and all eight portable-shard logs executed merge `b22decce070262030bb0368eaf524b878c785ed9` against main `bd5d189a8f8aeea669bcb93e68af6c046b567939`. Raw logs confirm 21 wire/schema, 2 capture, 5 trailer, 13 failure-projection, 24 CLI/production-stdio acceptance and one MCP-contract checks.
- Source/static/docs/build, eight portable shards, Windows native artifact build, selected Linux package baseline and controlled browser/web-network lanes passed. These are remote selected-lane results, not a new local rerun or full Windows/provider qualification.
- Remaining gaps: no complete local repository suite, external customer capture or downstream-recovery frequency measurement; no local macOS/Linux run or comparative performance benchmark. Generated local controls and controlled CI fixture lanes do not establish customer adoption. Human initial-readiness declarations remain pending.

- [x] Observed, derived, and inferred claims remain distinguishable.

- [x] Unsupported, incomplete, unavailable, or uncertain outcomes remain visible.

## Validation performed

Windows x64, Node 24.18.0/npm 11.16.0. npm was invoked via the pinned Node/npm-cli entry.

## Compatibility, safety, and release

- Breaking changes/migration: valid success behavior and inputs unchanged. Invalid schema requests intentionally receive more specific correction paths/reasons; error code/category and partial-observation behavior remain stable.

body:
## Problem

After every successful compaction the gateway logged:

```
late compaction count reconcile failed: TypeError: reconcile is not a function
```

`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.compaction.runtime.ts` was the only `*.runtime.ts` module with a default export. In `dist`, `scripts/runtime-postbuild.mjs` gives it a stable alias file containing `export * from "./embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.compaction.runtime-<hash>.js"`. `export *` never re-exports `default`, so `const { default: reconcile } = await import(...)` got `undefined`. Compaction still worked, but the session store's `compactionCount` was never reconciled.

## Fix

Switch the module to a named export, like every other lazy runtime module, and update the dynamic import and the test import.

## Verification

- `vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.compaction.test.ts`: 22 passed.
- Rebuilt `dist`: the alias stub now exposes `reconcileSessionStoreCompactionCountAfterSuccess` as a function, and the gateway is running on that build.

author: skezo
body:
## What

Puts back the top padding of a Notice inside a SettingsSection. On the extension's settings page, choosing "Enter the address" with no address saved shows a warning Notice whose words and warning sign sat against the bar's top edge.

Measured in the real extension (options page, desktop density, 1280 and 600 px, light and dark):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Notice padding (block-start / inline-end / block-end / inline-start) | **0** / 16 / 10 / 16 px | 10 / 16 / 10 / 16 px (M-notice desktop) |
| Glyph and first line from the bar's top edge | **0 px** | 10 px |
| Glyph from the bar's start edge | 16 px | 16 px |
| Gap above (to the ChoiceGroup) / below (to "Server address") | 12 / 12 px (the section gap, no rule) | unchanged |
| Inline edges against the section's fields | flush | unchanged |
| Forced-colours border | top edge missing | whole |

**Cause.** `SettingsSection.module.css` gave every item after the first a rule edge (`padding-block-start` + `border-block-start`), then took it off a Notice (and the item after a Notice, a subheading, help) with `.items > :is([data-notice], …) { padding-block-start: 0; border-block-start: 0 }`. At (0,2,0) that reset outweighs the Notice's own `.notice` padding (0,1,0), so every Notice in a section lost its top padding and the top of its forced-colours border. The catalogue's "Audio, Bespoke" specimen had the same defect.

**Fix.** The rule edge is never set on those items instead of set and reset: `.items > * + *:where(:not([data-notice], [data-notice] + *, h3 + *, p))`. The `:where()` keeps the old (0,1,0) weight, so every other item's padding is as before. C-section in DESIGN.md says so.

The readout under "For the next tab cast" was checked as well. Its gaps match M-dl (16.8 px across, `--space-5`; 4 px down, `--space-2`), so this PR doesn't change it. A sweep of the page (every section, 1280 and 600 px, light and dark) found no other spacing that had collapsed.

Before/after sheet: `thaumic-design/settings-notice-before-after.png`.

## Why

Owner report: "on the extension setting page the notice bar layout is broken" / "the issue is padding".

## How to Test

- `packages/ui`: `bunx playwright test --config catalogue/playwright.config.ts settings.pw.ts pages.pw.ts`. A new check runs at both densities and in compact, medium and wide frames. For each Notice in a section it checks symmetric padding, the glyph inset by the padding, the section's gap above and below, and the fields' inline edges.
- `RUNS="1:dark" apps/extension/real-ext/run.sh`: new options checks for "Enter the address" with nothing saved (every Notice in a section keeps its padding, its glyph sits inside it, the gap round it is the section's) and for the readout keeping M-dl's gaps. 100/100 and lifecycle 6/6 pass locally.
- typecheck, test, lint (0 warnings), tokens:check, prettier --check and the root build pass.
- The catalogue's settings-section screenshot baselines are expected to change (the Bespoke specimen's Notices gain their top padding).

## Related Issue

None, owner report.

body:
## Summary

Update AGENTS.md with repository-specific native-first scripts and libraries guidance.

## Scripts: native first

Before adding a script file (`scripts/`, `bin/`, `tools/`, root `*.sh|*.py|*.mjs`) or a package script that runs one, take the first rung that works:

1. A flag or subcommand of a tool the repo already uses (`<tool> --help`).
2. Declarative config for that tool (`app.config.js`, `metro.config.js`, `oxfmt.config.ts`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`).
3. A maintained plugin for that tool.
4. A one-line package.json script that calls a native command.
5. A test in the existing runner (Vitest), for anything that asserts.
6. A custom script, only for behavior specific to this repo. Its first comment names the native rung it couldn't use and why. It has a test in the existing runner, and the PR that adds it quotes that comment.

## Code: libraries first

Before hand-writing general-purpose code, use a well-maintained library: actively released, widely adopted, typed, and a fit for this stack. Reach for one already in the dependencies first. Write custom code for domain logic and for the glue no library covers. A PR that adds a dependency says why it was picked; a PR that hand-writes something a library covers names the library and why it didn't fit.

- Runtime validation → zod for agent configuration and tool payloads.
- Secure token storage → expo-secure-store.
- Authentication → @clerk/expo.

## Evidence

- **Before:** The root AGENTS.md lacked the two requested sections.
- **After:** The sections above document the native tooling ladder and 3 library choices from the existing stack; only AGENTS.md changes.
- **Rung 2:** Verified these tracked configuration files: `app.config.js`, `metro.config.js`, `oxfmt.config.ts`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`.
- **Rungs 4 and 5:** package.json (pnpm scripts and Vitest) establish package.json script and Vitest.
- **Library choices:** Checked declared dependencies against their use in `src/utils/agent-config.ts`, `src/app/_layout.tsx`, `src/runtime/production.tsx`; the concern-to-library lines above follow those uses.
- **Verification:** pnpm exec oxfmt --check AGENTS.md with the repository's formatter configuration; git diff --check. Existing commit hooks run normally. This documentation change adds no script or dependency.

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** agent guidance only

5. **Ba nút 6 số thiếu tên tiếng Việt**: `681513`, `681519`, `903289`. Nguồn duy nhất đặt tên là **tiếng Anh** (`wco.*`). Quy ước 200+ nhóm sẵn có: `tenDien` **luôn** lấy từ nguồn tiếng Việt. Điền tên tiếng Việt = tự dịch → vi phạm luật 2. **Đã bỏ, cần người quyết định** có cho phép dịch tên WCO kèm trích tiếng Anh hay không.
6. **Ba `tieuChi6` để trống có chủ đích**: `660199`, `681599`, `821290` — tên phân nhóm là *"n.e.c."* (phủ định "không thuộc chỗ khác"), **không phải tiêu chí dương** để phân biệt. Đây chính là 3 cảnh báo `phan-nhom-chua-co-tieu-chi` của `check-cay`.
7. **`loaiTru` 9032 có 3 mục là nhánh phủ định, không phải danh sách đen**: `9025|9026|9030` và `8536` chỉ áp dụng *"Nếu không đáp ứng các mô tả được chỉ ra ở đoạn trên"*; `8536` còn nói *"nói chung"*. Đã giữ nguyên định ngữ giới hạn trong `dieuKien` — **cổng sau không được coi 3 mục này là loại trừ tuyệt đối**.
8. **Không nguồn nào bị cắt trần** khi xuất (`nguonBiCat` rỗng cả 6 nhóm) — ngược lại lô 008 có 2.

### Mục có ghi điều mà câu trích không nói

Đã quét tự động toàn bộ `text` / `dieuKien` / `tomTat` / `quyTac` / `hoi` của lô (so từng từ với nguồn của chính mục) và dùng `scripts/audit-trich.mjs` đọc câu ngay trước/sau mọi đoạn trích. **Còn lại đúng 6 chỗ, đều là chú thích đã đánh dấu, không phải mệnh đề suy diễn**:

| Nhóm | Mục | Chữ ngoài câu trích | Vì sao chấp nhận |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6815 | `dong8` 68151310 / 68151910 | *"Dòng cha không có trong nguồn — trùng chữ với dòng…, đối chiếu biểu thuế, không đoán"* | metadata về **biểu thuế**, không phải mệnh đề từ câu nguồn |
| 6815 | `dong8` 68151390 / 68151990 | *"…đối chiếu biểu thuế theo phân nhóm…, không đoán"* | như trên |
| 9032 | `dong8` 90328939 / 90328990 | *"…theo tiêu đề quốc gia 9032.89.3…, không đoán"* | như trên |

Đây đúng văn phong lô 008 đã dùng và được duyệt — nhưng cần người soát xác nhận nhất quán.

Ngoài ra đã **rút về đúng câu trích** 5 mục đang vượt: `loaiTru` 6815 (69.02|69.03), `phanBiet` 6815 (69.02|69.03), `loaiTru` 9032 ×3, `tieuChi6` 9032.20 (đổi tên `fact` vì câu nguồn **không** có chữ "tự động"), `tomTat`/`quyTac` 6603 + 9032.

### Tự soát bằng mắt — 9 lỗi đã sửa trước khi nạp (máy không bắt được)

Máy chỉ chứng minh câu trích **có thật trong nguồn**, không chứng minh nó **nói đúng điều mục khẳng định**. Hai lỗi đáng chú ý nhất:

1. **`phanBiet` 6603 ĐẢO CHIỀU.** Bản nháp đầu ghi `neuCo=6603, neuKhong=6602`; đúng phải là gậy chống chưa hoàn chỉnh → **66.02**. Đã đảo.
2. **`dieuKienVao` 8212 là điều kiện SAI CẤP — đã XOÁ.** Câu *"Phôi lưỡi… **với điều kiện là** đã được khoan lỗ sẵn"* chỉ áp cho **phôi lưỡi** (8212.20), không phải điều kiện vào cả nhóm — lưỡi thành phẩm không cần khoan lỗ sẵn. Ghi ở cấp nhóm sẽ khiến cổng loại nhầm lưỡi thành phẩm.

Còn lại: 1 lỗi gõ ký tự trong câu trích (máy bắt được), 1 `phamVi` 8212 nói thứ câu trích không có, 2 mục là **vế cụt** (thiếu chủ ngữ — 6805, 6815), 3 mục vượt câu trích.

### Chỗ cần người soát để mắt nhiều nhất

1. **Chiều nhánh `phanBiet[0]` 6601.** Nguồn chỉ nói *"Nhóm này không bao gồm: (b) Các loại lều trại trên bãi biển, **không mang tính chất** như dù che… (nhóm 63.06)"* — nhánh `neuCo=6601` là nhánh "còn lại" của câu loại trừ, không phải câu nguồn nói thẳng. Em **không** ghép thêm câu chú giải *"Dù che làm thành lều là loại dù lớn có gắn 'màn che bao quanh'…"* vì giữa hai câu có câu mở đoạn **"Nhóm này không bao gồm:"** — lược qua nó là lược mất ngoại lệ.
2. Ba `dieuKien`/`fact` của 9032 đã **rút về đúng câu trích** — kiểm xem có rút quá tay không.

### Ghi chú bàn giao

- **KHÔNG merge.** PR mở để người duyệt soát độc lập.
- Phạm vi soát đề nghị: **TOÀN BỘ** `phamVi`/`boPhan`/`dieuKienVao`/`loaiTru`/`phanBiet` = **27 mục**; sau đó tự soát ngẫu nhiên ≥ 10 % phần còn lại (67 mục `tieuChi6`/`dong8`).
- Khi đạt: `so-tay-lo.csv` dòng 009 → `trang_thai=xong` + điền `pr`.
- Chi tiết đầy đủ (kể cả bảng "sai sót đã kiểm kỹ là ĐÚNG — để người soát đừng sửa nhầm"): `TIEN-TRINH.md`.

body:
\/api\/cart accepts unvalidated item quantity \(negative\/huge\)\, causing checkout CPU exhaustion and order\-total corruption

## Risk assessment

**Severity: High**

**Likelihood: High · Impact: Moderate**

| Dimension | Recorded assessment | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reachable from attacker | Yes | Code |
| Configuration required | No | Code |
| Access required | None | Code |
| User interaction required | No | Finding |
| Attacker gains | Modify data | Finding |
| Blast radius | Other users in the tenant | Finding |
| Target value | Medium | Finding |

<details>
<summary>Assessment reasons and what could change this assessment</summary>

### Reachable from attacker

POST \/api\/cart is a Next\.js public API route exported through only InstrumentationMiddleware \(telemetry\) with no auth\/session check\. The OpenTelemetry demo is a public e\-commerce storefront exposed through frontend\-proxy\; the finding\'s steps\_to\_reproduce use plain unauthenticated curl against http\:\/\/<host>\:8080\/api\/cart\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the deployment places the Next\.js frontend behind an authenticating ingress or VPN \(e\.g\.\, Envoy auth filter \/ IdP\) that blocks unauthenticated internet traffic\.

### Configuration required

No feature flag\, non\-default mode\, or special config is required\. The handler\, cart gRPC store \(ValkeyCartStore\.AddItemAsync\)\, checkout\'s MultiplySlow loop\, and shipping\'s u32 cast are all present in default code paths and run in the standard demo deployment\. No rate limiting is configured by default\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that a non\-default config \(e\.g\.\, validator middleware feature flag\, WAF rule\, or alt code path\) must be enabled for the vulnerable code to run\.

### Access required

The handler in src\/frontend\/pages\/api\/cart\.ts performs no authentication\: it wraps the handler only with InstrumentationMiddleware \(telemetry only\) and takes userId directly from the request body\. The finding\'s rationale confirms \'no auth exists anywhere in the app\'\. Any unauthenticated client can POST arbitrary quantities\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence of an upstream auth proxy \/ IdP enforcing authentication before traffic reaches \/api\/cart \(e\.g\.\, Envoy JWT filter\, Cognito\, Auth0\)\.

### User interaction required

The attacker can issue the two curl requests \(POST \/api\/cart then POST \/api\/checkout\) entirely on their own with no victim action\. No clicking\, viewing\, or other third\-party\-user step is needed\; steps\_to\_reproduce show the attacker completes the chain unaided\.

**What could change this assessment:** A step requiring a legitimate user to trigger the vulnerable sink \(e\.g\.\, only an admin\'s checkout action iterates MultiplySlow on the poisoned cart\)\.

### Attacker gains

The finding demonstrates that an unauthenticated attacker can persist arbitrary quantity values \(negative\, zero\, or huge\) into any user\'s cart \(userId is taken verbatim from the request body with no ownership check\)\. This stored value flows into checkout\'s order total computation \(money\.MultiplySlow \-> Sum into total \-> chargeCard\) and into the Rust shipping service\'s u32 quote\, corrupting business data \(final charged order totals\, shipping quotes\, cart line items\)\. The CPU\-exhaustion effect alone would be \'neither\' \(DoS\)\, but the integrity corruption of order totals and shipping quotes is modification of business\/transactional data that does not grant elevated privileges\, so modify\_data is the correct classification\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the corrupted total modifies security\-critical state \(auth\, roles\, IAM\) rather than order business data would elevate to modify\_privileged\.

### Blast radius

The \/api\/cart handler takes userId directly from the request body with no authentication or session binding \(\'userId is taken verbatim from the request body\'\)\. An attacker can therefore write a poisoned quantity into the cart of any userId they choose\, affecting checkouts and shipping quotes placed for other users of the same deployment\. This is the OpenTelemetry reference demo — a single\-tenant application with one shared user base\, no tenant\_id isolation evident\, so the maximum demonstrated blast radius is other users within the one deployment\, not cross\-tenant\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the deployment serves multiple independent customer organizations with isolation boundaries that the attack crosses would raise this to cross\_tenant\.

### Target value

The affected data is cart contents and order totals \/ shipping quotes — business\/transactional data that drives checkout operations\. The validator rationale explicitly notes the data is \'synthetic catalog\/order data with a simulated charge service that issues uuid transaction IDs rather than contacting a payment processor\' and that there is \'no cross\-tenant data disclosure or regulated\-data or compliance exposure\'\. No credentials\, PII\, auth state\, or secrets are read or modified by this exploit\; the capability is confined to tampering with order\/cart business records and burning checkout CPU\. That matches \'business data that drives decisions or operations\' \= medium\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the corrupted total triggers a real payment processor charge for real funds\, or that cart data contains PII\/payment credentials that the attacker reads\, would raise to high\.



</details>

## Remediation

Defense\-in\-depth validation and bounds across the full data flow\:

<details>
<summary>Recorded change details</summary>

1\) src\/frontend\/pages\/api\/cart\.ts\: POST now validates the body at runtime \(the TS cast is erased\)\. Requires item object\, productId 1\.\.64 char string\, userId non\-empty\, quantity a non\-zero safe integer in \[\-100\, 100\]\; returns 400 otherwise\. Negative deltas remain allowed because the UI \(Cart\.provider\.tsx\) sends negative deltas to decrease a line\.

2\) src\/cart\/src\/services\/CartService\.cs\: AddItem rejects null Item\, empty\/over\-length ProductId\, and quantities outside \[\-100\,100\] \(zero rejected\) with gRPC InvalidArgument\, bounding in\-cluster callers that bypass the frontend\.

3\) src\/cart\/src\/cartstore\/ValkeyCartStore\.cs\: AddItemAsync clamps the resulting line quantity to \[0\, 10000\] after applying the delta\; lines reaching 0 are removed\. Authoritative server\-side bound regardless of stacked deltas\.

4\) src\/checkout\/main\.go\:357 \+ src\/checkout\/money\/money\.go\: replaced money\.MultiplySlow\(it\.Cost\, uint32\(quantity\)\) with a new money\.Multiply\(m\, n int32\) performing a checked O\(1\) multiplication on units\/nanos via int64 math\. Non\-positive quantities contribute 0\, closing the \~4\.29B\-iteration CPU exhaustion and the quantity\-0 overcharge\. MultiplySlow is left for API compatibility\.

5\) src\/shipping\/src\/shipping\_service\.rs\: get\_quote clamps each item\.quantity to 10\_000 and uses saturating\_add with a 1\_000\_000 cap\, closing u32 overflow \/ runaway arithmetic\.

Endpoint paths\, gRPC methods\, and response shapes preserved\. No toolchain available to compile in the sandbox\; changes are localized and syntactically consistent\.

</details>

## Proof

**Recorded evidence level: Static proven.**

Recorded source analysis; patch execution results are not included in this evidence.

<summary>Recorded source analysis</summary>

author: makewhatis
body:
## Summary

The idle Claude subscription usage probe (STUDIO-1269) runs by default
(`limits.claude_probe_interval_s: 600`) and spends a real Haiku turn — then repeats while Claude
work waits. It ran on **every** install, including ones that never dispatch Claude work, which got
unrequested background spend or a confusing `Claude usage probe failed` warning.

This gates the probe on a resolved Claude dispatch path being configured. An install with no Claude
harness anywhere never admits the probe and logs nothing about it. `limits.claude_probe_interval_s: 0`
stays an explicit off switch.

## Changes

- `crates/orchestrator/src/teams.rs`: new `Orchestrator::claude_harness_configured()`. Consults every
  place a harness is configured — the installation-wide and per-project `agent.backend`; each
  roster identity's own `harness` and the harness its profile names; the manager's one-shot harness
  and its manager-run harness list; and the harnesses `review.model` / `review.provider` /
  `review.effort` are scoped to. `agent.backend` is checked first so the common Claude install
  short-circuits with no I/O; the Teams half is only consulted when Teams is enabled (with it off
  those blocks are dead config).
- `crates/orchestrator/src/accounts.rs`: `claude_probe_request` now returns `None` when no Claude
  harness is configured, ahead of every other gate, so no probe subprocess is ever spawned and
  nothing is logged.
- Tests (orchestrator): no Claude harness ⇒ never probes (boot or idle) and no WARN logged; a
  teammate profile naming `claude` ⇒ probes; a manager harness list naming `claude` ⇒ probes; a
  `review.model.claude` scope ⇒ probes; a project whose own `agent.backend` is `claude` ⇒ probes;
  a Teams block that names `claude` but is `enabled: false` ⇒ stays off; a Teams install with
  every harness on `opencode` ⇒ stays off.

## Verification

```
$ make lint
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
... check-release-keychain-lock_test: all cases passed
```

```
$ env -u SYMPHONY_RUN_ID -u RHAPSODY_RUN_ID make test
...
make test exit=0
```

(The two `claude::runner` run-id-env tests fail under a bare `make test` because this run's own
`SYMPHONY_RUN_ID`/`RHAPSODY_RUN_ID` leak into the test env; unsetting them — as STUDIO-1269's run
did — is green. One transient `opencode::runner::tests::a_cancelled_run_keeps_the_session…`
timeout appeared on one attempt and passed on rerun; it is pre-existing and untouched by this diff.)

Mutation check — removing the configured-harness gate reddens the first acceptance test:

```
$ cargo test -p rhapsody-orchestrator claude_probe_never_runs_without
test accounts::tests::claude_probe_never_runs_without_a_configured_claude_harness ... FAILED
thread ... panicked at crates/orchestrator/src/accounts.rs:766:13: boot
```

## Notes for reviewers

- **Boot probe kept — this takes acceptance bullet 2's explicit escape.** The probe still runs at
  boot, but only when a Claude harness is configured and only when the other existing gates
  (`interval`, in-flight, live Claude run, fresh reading) allow it. I kept it because the account
  ledger is in-memory and empty at boot: the boot probe is what makes the subscription's usage
  visible in the console and arms the `stop-new` gate *before* the first Claude dispatch. Removing
  it would degrade every Claude install to fix a bug that only affects non-Claude ones. The existing
  daemon test `boot_claude_probe_uses_configured_fake_command_and_gates_subscription`
  (`crates/rhapsodyd/src/run.rs`) covers exactly this case — Claude configured, no queued work at
  boot, probe runs — and still passes. If the maintainer prefers no boot probe at all, that test
  needs reworking around a file-tracker + held Claude issue to have queued work at boot.
- The manager's harness defaults to `claude` (`Manager::effective_harness` / `effective_harnesses`),
  so a Teams-enabled install normally counts as Claude-configured — correct, because Teams runs
  manager turns on Claude by default. An install that has moved the manager to another harness
  (and has no Claude profile/review scope) is correctly left off.
- The gate resolves roster profiles (local file reads) when the backend is not Claude and Teams is
  on, on the control task — the same local-profile resolution dispatch already performs.

Fixes STUDIO-1469

author: cyberdudebivash
body:
## SOC Phase 12 — independently recompute bytes from the authorized SIEM/EDR source

Tracks SOC programme #360. The Phase 11 database now protects analyst review decisions, but the HMAC v2 receipt previously discarded the original signed provider `sourceEventId`; there was no concrete independent source-byte verifier.

### Changes
- Add **offline-only D1 migration 0015** `source_event_id` with a strict technical-identifier insert guard. Existing historical receipt rows remain NULL and are not silently upgraded to independently verified.
- Persist `sourceEventId` directly from the already HMAC-authenticated v2 intake envelope in the atomic D1 receipt insert. Preserve metadata-only receipt, key revocation guard, immutable audit and original event digest.
- Update tenant-bound Phase 11 review service to require this stored original source ID, never a supplied browser event path.
- Add `soc-source-byte-verifier.js`: trusted operator-provided authorized source adapter, deterministic event ID check, tenant/connector/original source matching, 256 KiB default receipt limit, 6-second deadline, and **SHA-256 recomputation over returned Buffer/Uint8Array**. Rejects source scope drift, forged verified flags, unknown fields, wrong original ID, malformed source data, digest mismatch, adapter outages and timeouts.
- Add `soc-detection-source-boundary.js` composing current pinned OIDC RS256/MFA/session checks with fresh primary D1 authorization and independent source bytes. Only internal `review` and `linkToIncident` exposed. **No live provider adapter or public HTTP route**.
- New SQLite migration tests, real-byte adversarial Jest tests, signed-RSA token to D1 to source-bytes integration tests, and Phase 12 runbook. Existing CI build-check runs SQLite suite.

### Strict release restrictions
This PR **does not** implement a real authorized customer EDR/SIEM source adapter, decrypt/re-encrypt customer telemetry, enable a webhook or a provider token, run production D1 migration 0015, deploy Cloudflare, change DNS, charge customers, claim an operational SOC or falsely certify source maliciousness.

The adapter must securely stream-limit bytes *before* buffering, handle provider credential scoping, customer consent, TLS and tenant isolation; the library's post-read max-size check is supplemental. The stored technical sourceEventId may still contain sensitive values if a provider uses an unsafe identifier scheme; production provisioning must vet/pseudonymize before any customer onboarding. Rejection, audit and review are still operator-gated.

### Required review gates
Exact-head Jest, offline D1-compatible SQLite, Blogger evidence, dependency audit, workflow security, E2E/governance/performance/resilience/coverage. Approval of actual Workerd/D1 migration and customer source integration is separate. **NO-GO for customer SOC GA.**

body:
## Summary

This adds `research/pr4535-arithmetic-check/`. It is an independent arithmetic check, with certified intervals, of hexapode's #4535 (conditional κ = 0.003020165 via #4532's critical-root compiler on #4470's unchanged p16 supplier).

**Claim type:** an independent arithmetic check. **No new κ.**

## Results

Everything checked reproduces #4535.

- **Critical exponent.** `[θ_lo, θ_hi]` brackets `T_θ = P_θ`, certified, and equals exactly 1 minus #4478's raw-root bracket.
- **Saving order.** κ < uniform saving, and `t − θ_hi = 377/10¹²` exactly.
- **Mirror at θ.** The worst window ratio is **0.56281 ≤ 141/250**, in the maximizing cell (1/48, 1/41).
- **Absorption.** `ln A ≤ 13.6223` (matching `logA_upper`). The margin is 352.33 at `ln N = 10¹²` and **236.79 at the stated `N = 2^{10¹²}`**, monotone beyond.
  - *Labelling note:* #4535's `margin_lower` is computed at `ln N = 10¹²`, not at `ln 2^{10¹²}`. It is still positive at the stated N.
- **Outer rows.** 7 of the 9 rows exceed κ, and the **binding main-transform margin equals the reported 29969798347/10²⁰**. The parameter schedule is `κ + k·d`. The ξ rows are not recomputed because ξ is not printed.

## Evidence

body:
Root cause of the incident spam: each of the three browser-suite shards wrote and pushed its own 'Incident:' commit, so every red head of main produced three commits (81 in six hours), and each replaced the previous shard's checks for the same sha. Now the shards upload their output and one incident job (needs: browser-suite) records every shard's failed checks in a single entry and one commit; a green head runs incident-log resolve, which nothing called before, so incidents finally close. addIncident merges checks for a repeated sha. No loop: GITHUB_TOKEN pushes start no workflow.

Copy check: #1251 was branched before #1249, so its deploy copy dropped the ?open=all line from void-live-deploy/index.html; void-live-deploy/void.html also lacked the share-link line. Both copies are now byte-identical to void.html.

author: denkoushi
body:
## 概要

業務ラズパイ全台（Pi5 サーバー、Pi4 キオスク、Pi3 サイネージ）に、週1回の夜間に OS の安全更新だけを入れる仕組みを Ansible で入れます。詳細は [KB-425](docs/knowledge-base/KB-425-os-security-weekly-update.md)。

- **選び方**: Debian-Security の更新、RPi がそれを `+rptN` で作り直した版、`chromium` / `rpi-chromium-mods` だけを入れる。RPi 版が Debian 版より優先されるため、unattended-upgrades で配布元を絞る方法では入らない。Pi5 の旧 unattended-upgrades も `+rpt` 版の安全更新を1つも入れていなかったので、`APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade "0"` で止めてこの仕組みに置き換える。
- **除外（手動のみ）**: docker-ce・containerd などの Docker 一式、tailscale、カーネル・ファームウェア・initramfs-tools。Debian-Security に対応する版が無い RPi だけの更新（vlc、pipewire など）も入れない。入れる前に模擬実行（`apt-get -s`）を行い、除外品が入る、または何かが削除される場合は失敗として止める。
- **再起動**: 自動再起動はしない。chromium が更新されたキオスクだけ、夜間に `kiosk-browser.service` を再起動する。Pi5 の Docker は止めない。
- **時刻**: Pi5 は日曜 02:00。キオスクは日曜 01:00 に最大90分のずらしを加える。サイネージは日曜 01:30 に最大30分。さらに本体が 0〜5 時以外は何もしない。
- **本番反映との排他**: 反映は書き換えの前に `/run/raspi-release/active` を置き、更新のロックを最大30分待つ。終わりに `always` で目印を消す。torque の8つの段階と、kiosk・pi5・signage の各役割に入れた。更新側は目印があれば見送る。4時間より古い目印は無視する。
- **段階**: 全台 dry-run（選別と模擬実行だけ）で始め、`raspi4-assembly-02` だけ apply。次の段階では `group_vars/all.yml` の mode を apply に変える。
- **通知**: status-agent に `os_update_health` を追加した。最後の実行が失敗したとき、または15日以上成功していないときに、フローティングChat へ件名「OS更新」で通知する。次に成功すると復旧扱いになる。Slack は使わない。
- **Pi5 の旧設定の行方**: 反映すると `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52raspi-unattended-upgrades` が上書きされ、`APT::Periodic` の Update-Package-Lists、Unattended-Upgrade、AutocleanInterval がすべて "0" になる。Pi5 で `Periodic` を書いているのは、Debian の `20auto-upgrades`("1")とこの `52` だけ。apt は名前順に読んで後のファイルが勝つので、`52` の "0" が有効になる。Pi5 の実際の設定一式で新しい `52` に差し替えた一時コピーを作り、`apt-config dump` で3つとも "0" になるのを確かめた(今の `52` のままなら "1")。`apt-daily*.timer` は残るが、値が "0" なので更新はしない。`unattended-upgrades.service` は停止時の後始末用で、`InstallOnShutdown` が未設定(既定は false)のため更新しない。したがって二重には動かない。詳しくは KB-425。
- 開発依存（npm / PyPI）の更新は対象外。

## 検証

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/deploy/tests -p 'test_*.py'`: 594件 OK
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s clients/status-agent/tests`: OK
- `scripts/ci/tests/test_classify_changes.py`: 38件 OK
- `run-deploy-contracts-local.sh --install-collections`: macOS では、変更していない `pi4-storage-maintenance.sh` の段階で止まった（bash 3 と BSD date のため）。そこまでの段階はすべて PASS。残りは Linux の CI で確認する。
- API の単体テスト（警報の判定と通知の文面・復旧）を追加した。

<!-- deploy-impact:start -->
| Item | Declaration |
| --- | --- |
| Risk | unknown |
| Target machines | pi3, pi4, pi5 |
| Changed surfaces | api, agent, systemd, config, deploy, docs, ci, unknown |
| Required files/artifacts | api image; /usr/local/sbin/raspi-os-security-update; raspi-os-security-update.service and .timer; /etc/raspi-os-security-update.conf; status-agent os_update_health.py on every host; signage release artifact |
| Database | no: no schema or migration change, telemetry uses existing alert and notice tables |
| Secrets/config delivery | no: no secret values, only non-secret Ansible variables and inventory mode for raspi4-assembly-02 |
| Success evidence | deploy tests 594 OK, status-agent tests OK, classify tests OK, API unit tests, CI full suite |
| Rollback/cleanup | set os_security_update_enabled false or mode dry-run and redeploy; package downgrade via apt-get install pkg=old version from /var/log/dpkg.log (KB-425) |
| Production verification | after deploy, systemctl list-timers shows raspi-os-security-update.timer on each host, state.json is seeded as pending, and after the first Sunday run raspi4-assembly-02 shows result success |

author: davideast
body:
`pyric sandbox` and the `pyric()` Vite plugin now serve Cloud Functions `onRequest` exports, v2 and v1, unchanged, at the emulator path.

```js
// functions/index.js
const { onRequest } = require('firebase-functions/v2/https');
const { initializeApp } = require('firebase-admin/app');
const { getFirestore } = require('firebase-admin/firestore');

exports.addMessage = onRequest(async (req, res) => {
  const ref = await getFirestore(initializeApp()).collection('messages').add({ text: req.query.text });
  res.json({ id: ref.id });
});
```

```sh
$ pyric sandbox
✔ functions 1 onRequest function:
    http://localhost:3473/demo-project/us-central1/addMessage

$ curl 'http://localhost:3473/demo-project/us-central1/addMessage?text=hi'
{"id":"Xb2..."}          # the document is in the sandbox before this line prints

# before a browser tab connects the sandbox:
$ curl -i http://localhost:3473/demo-project/us-central1/addMessage
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Functions are not running yet: no browser tab is connected to pyric sandbox. Open http://localhost:3473 to start them.
```

## One listener in the child, one gateway for both planes

The child loads the source, then starts an express app on `127.0.0.1:0` and reports the port in its `ready` message. The app is built from the express that the user's own `firebase-functions` depends on, so there is no new pyric dependency. Request parsing follows functions-framework-nodejs: cloudevents JSON, JSON, text, extended urlencoded, then raw, with a 32mb limit and `rawBody`. `x-powered-by` is off, and errors render as production pages.

`functions/http/gateway.ts` is the only entry for both planes:

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `/{projectId}/{region}/{name}[/...]`, served function | forwarded; the function sees `/` plus the rest, query kept, bytes undecoded |
| same shape, unknown name or wrong region | not claimed, so the plane's static 404 answers; a static directory may share the project id's name |
| same shape while waiting for a peer, starting, reloading, or failed | `503` with the cause |
| anything else | not claimed; static files and Vite carry on |

`pyric sandbox` mounts the gateway through a new `functionsHandler` option on the static server. It runs after `/__pyric/` and before the GET/HEAD-only 405, so POST and OPTIONS reach functions. Vite mounts the same gateway on its Connect stack, behind the plugin's DNS-rebinding check.

## Rows flipped, and rows left unverified

| Row | Now | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 emulator path, region resolution, both planes | conforms, unit-backed | suite `#1`, `discovery.test.ts` (options, `setGlobalOptions`, v1 `region()`), `routes.test.ts`, `vite-plane.test.ts` |
| 18 awaited admin write visible before the response | conforms, unit-backed | suite `#18`, `vite-plane.test.ts` |
| 19 scaling options | unsupported, with reason | suite `#19`: concurrent streams, and a `maxInstances: 1` function serving two overlapping requests |

The 16 rows that need a production observation (2 to 17) stay `unverified` and red. Several are already implemented from upstream source and will be judged against the capture, not against these sources:

- **Body parsing (5, 6):** follows functions-framework.
- **Malformed JSON (7):** a 400 with express's production error page.
- **Handler throw (9):** the SDK's 500 `Internal Server Error`.
- **CORS (13, 14):** the SDK's own middleware.
- **v1 (2):** served like v2.
- **Unknown function (16):** not claimed by pyric, so the plane's static 404 answers.
- **`invoker: 'private'` (15):** served, and the warning prints once per function.
- **Uncaught async throw (12):** caught in the child, which keeps serving.

## A wedged child restarts, and stops drain in-flight requests

- **Heartbeat:** the child beats over IPC every second. Ten seconds without a beat, which is a handler stuck in a synchronous loop, prints `Functions child unresponsive`, answers 503 naming it, and restarts the child. RTDB triggers restart with it.
- **Exit after ready:** a child that exits after it was ready answers 503 saying it exited, not that it failed to start.
- **Stop and reload:** the child's server stops accepting and closes idle sockets. It lets in-flight requests finish for up to 1 s, under the host's 2 s force-kill, then destroys what is left.
- **Forwarding headers:** the proxy appends the client to `X-Forwarded-For` and sets `X-Forwarded-Proto`. It drops a client's `X-Forwarded-Host` and any header the request's `Connection` header lists. The child trusts one hop, so `req.ip` and `req.hostname` are what the proxy saw, not what the client claimed.

## The child exits when its host goes away, and never spins

An earlier revision of this PR left orphaned children spinning a core after `pyric sandbox` or a test died, and they ignored SIGTERM. Once the IPC channel closed, `process.send()` emitted `'error'` on the next tick. The uncaught-error handler reported that error by sending again, which formed a next-tick loop that starved signal handlers, and the heartbeat started it. The child now does four things:
- Sends only on an open channel, with a callback.
- Never re-enters the uncaught-error reporter.
- Exits on `disconnect` or a changed `process.ppid`.
- Exits within 1.5 s of losing its host. On SIGINT or SIGTERM it uses the host's own 2 s stop deadline (`STOP_DEADLINE_MS`, shared with the host's force-kill), so Ctrl-C and the host's stop request give in-flight triggers the same time.

On Windows there is no re-parenting and the host ends children with TerminateProcess, so the child relies on `disconnect` alone there. The orphan tests read `/proc` and run on Linux only.

Main's RTDB child is not affected; it exits when the sandbox is killed.

## Risk

- **RTDB-only sources:** an `https` export is no longer listed as "unsupported trigger https; it will not run". It runs.
- **A child with any onRequest export now survives uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections.** That is decision 3 on row 12. A child with only RTDB triggers keeps today's behavior.
- **After headers are sent, a throw leaves the response open until a timeout.** The SDK logs the error and does not end the response. PR 5's `timeoutSeconds` handling ends it; row 10 waits on the capture.
- **Untouched:** no worker protocol frames change (rule 3), and none of `register/client/bootstrap.ts`, `serve/entries/worker-runtime.ts`, or `serve/worker/host/dispatch.ts`.

Stacked on #1191. PR 3 (capture) slots in once the oracle account has the roles. Main is frozen; this stays a draft.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

Integration tests:
- `packages/cli/test/functions-http/oracle-conformance.test.ts` runs the `pyric sandbox` process.
- `packages/cli/test/functions-http/vite-plane.test.ts` runs a real Vite server with `pyric()`. It covers 503 before the peer, a JSON POST under a subpath, region routing, and an admin write read back from the peer.
- The app scenarios with packed packages land in PR 5.

Verification, machine idle:
- `bun x tsc -p packages/cli/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `PYRIC_CLIMB=1 bun test .../oracle-conformance.test.ts`: rows 1, 18, and 19 green, and 3 completeness checks green. Rows 2 to 17 fail on missing observations. Rows 20 and 21 fail until PR 5, because their assertions also cover the hosting rewrite and the log line.
- `bun run packages/conformance/src/climb.ts --surface=functions-http`: 3/21 live green, registry 2/21 conforming, no regressions.
- `bun test test/serve test/cli test/bridge test/functions-rtdb test/functions-http`: 4241 pass, 45 skip, 0 fail.
- `bash scripts/ci/conformance-gates.sh`: exit 0. `bun test --cwd packages/conformance`: 480 pass.
- `bun test/apps/run.ts project-from-env-functions-off admin-writes-named-rtdb-instance`: 2 passed.

Findings from a local dump of every probe's projection:
- Query parsing, subpaths (both URL shapes), all body types, cookies, redirects, streamed writes, and the three CORS forms behave as the upstream sources

author: jacobley
body:
Fix auto-pipelining's slot calculation for string keys under a `Buffer` `keyPrefix`, so it hashes the same bytes `Command` sends.

This is more about keeping the two implementations consistent than about a bug people are likely hitting. `keyPrefix` is [typed as a string](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/852678553c805a1733ceb92d193682b8cb4212f9/lib/utils/Commander.ts#L12), and it only goes wrong for JavaScript callers passing a `Buffer` prefix whose bytes aren't valid UTF-8 (which is _technically_ supported, even if TypeScript says it is not).

### Bug

[`Command` accepts a `Buffer` `keyPrefix`](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/852678553c805a1733ceb92d193682b8cb4212f9/lib/Command.ts#L413-L431) at runtime, and prefixes each key with its bytes. Auto-pipelining [joined the prefix and a string key with a template string](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/852678553c805a1733ceb92d193682b8cb4212f9/lib/autoPipelining.ts#L184-L186), which decodes the prefix as UTF-8. When the prefix isn't valid UTF-8, the slot it computed differs from the slot of the key `Command` sends.

For example, under the prefix `Buffer.from([0xff])`, the keys `k0` and `k3` are sent as bytes that hash to slots 12000 and 7811. Decoded, they hash to 9959 and 5764. When the decoded slots share a node, and the real ones don't, both commands go into one auto pipeline, and [`Pipeline#exec`](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/852678553c805a1733ceb92d193682b8cb4212f9/lib/Pipeline.ts#L364-L372) rejects it with "All keys in the pipeline should belong to the same slots allocation group".

### Fix

[Hash the bytes whenever the key or the prefix is a `Buffer`](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/be9242143cb00a6cb2a0760aec1a16cdb700e797/lib/autoPipelining.ts#L186-L191), as redis/ioredis#2208 already does for `Buffer` keys. String keys under a string prefix are unchanged.

### Tests

A [unit test](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/be9242143cb00a6cb2a0760aec1a16cdb700e797/test/unit/autoPipelining.ts#L107-L138) queues `k0` and `k3` under the `0xff` prefix, with slots 12000 and 7811 on different nodes, and checks they get two pipelines. Without the fix, they get one.

`npm run lint`, `npm run build` and the unit and functional tests pass against Redis 8, apart from six `georadiusbymember` tests that fail the same way on `main`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow cluster auto-pipelining routing fix for an edge case (Buffer keyPrefix); string-only setups are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Cluster auto-pipelining** now computes hash slots the same way as `Command` when `keyPrefix` is a `Buffer`: it concatenates prefix and key as raw bytes instead of coercing the prefix through a string template (which could UTF-8–decode and change the slot).
> 
> A small `toBytes` helper normalizes string/number keys for that path; string prefix + string key behavior is unchanged. A unit test covers two string keys under a non–UTF-8 `Buffer` prefix that must land in separate auto-pipeline buckets when their real slots map to different nodes.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit be9242143cb00a6cb2a0760aec1a16cdb700e797. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: castrog
body:
A publish command was stopped after a fixed 15 minutes, with no way to change it. A registry entry in `callisto.toml` can now set `publish-timeout` (for example `publish-timeout = "5m"`; a whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from 1 second to 1 hour). The default is unchanged. It covers `cargo publish`, `npm publish` and `twine upload`. It is execution policy, so it stays out of the registry binding and does not make an earlier release intent stale. E025 now says where to set it.

Also fixes a spec gap from the previous change: the criterion on publish failures now says the error carries the last 8 lines of standard output followed by standard error, and that a publish echoes its standard output live.

Not done, for a decision: a limit on how long a publish may stay silent. It would stop a stuck publish sooner than the wall-clock limit, but a large upload prints nothing while it runs, so a short silence limit could cut off a slow but working upload. It would also add a parameter to the `CommandRunner` trait in the MIT `callisto-model` crate. The wall-clock limit above is the safe half.

Verified: `just ci` passes locally. The build step keeps the 15 minute default.

author: rizkyr99
body:
## What and why
Closes #26. Rollout step 2 of [RFC-0005](docs/rfc/0005-catalog-cart-gateway.md#10-rollout-plan): the Node workspace and the shared library both NestJS services (Catalog, gateway) build on, so they follow the conventions identically.

**Workspace:** pnpm (`packages/*`, `services/*`, `apps/*`), TypeScript strict (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`), ESLint `strictTypeChecked` with no `any`, Prettier, Vitest with coverage, Node 24.11 (`.node-version`).

**`@sagamart/node-common`:**

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `createLogger` | pino with the conventions §7 fields and `trace_id` / `span_id`; redacts credential headers |
| `loadConfig` | zod-validated env, every problem reported at once, empty = unset |
| `problem`, `ProblemError` | RFC 9457 with stable `code` → `type`; extensions can't replace standard members |
| `signIdentity`, `verifyIdentity` | The [identity contract](contracts/identity.md): EdDSA on `node:crypto`, no JWT library at runtime |
| `/telemetry`: `startTelemetry` | OTel SDK with auto-instrumentation, OTLP traces when configured, Prometheus `/metrics` handler |

**CI:** a `node` job in the `ci` gate runs install (frozen lockfile), lint, typecheck, build, tests with coverage, and `pnpm audit --audit-level high`.

## How it was built
- [x] **Tests first:** 7d64e4d holds the tests against stubs that throw (38 failing); a342f29 is the implementation.
  - **Identity:** a round trip; the exact header; guests without `sub`; a unique `jti`. Then **every rejection reason in the contract**: malformed input in 4 shapes, `alg: none` and `HS256`, a wrong `typ`, an unknown `kid`, another key's signature, a payload tampered after signing, wrong `iss`/`aud`, an audience list, expiry and issue time just outside the 5 s skew (and accepted just inside), a non-UUID `sub`, bad `roles`, a missing `exp`. Plus **interoperability with jose** in both directions.
  - **Logger:** field names and UTC millisecond `ts`; trace IDs only inside a span; redaction; levels.
  - **Config:** coercion and defaults; all three problems reported together; empty values.
  - **Problem:** type and title derivation; protected standard members; validation of `code` and status.
  - **Telemetry:** real spans without an exporter (a regression guard, see below); Prometheus output over a real HTTP request.
- [x] **Mutation check on identity:** removing the algorithm, signature, audience, expiry or issuer check, or doubling the skew, fails the suite every time.
- [x] Design followed RFC/ADR: RFC-0005 §4.2, §6, §10; contracts/identity.md; conventions §7–§10, §12

## How it was verified
- 42 tests pass, 96% statement coverage; ESLint and Prettier clean; typecheck and build pass; `pnpm audit`: no known vulnerabilities.
- The **built** CommonJS package works from a plain `require` (identity, problem, logger, telemetry start/stop), as NestJS will load it.

## Things that didn't go to plan
- **pnpm is pinned to 10.34.7, not 12.** pnpm 12 (and 11) can't be installed by pnpm 10's version switcher or by corepack 0.34: the binary package is missing for 12, and the CLI layout changed in 11.
- **TypeScript is pinned to 6.0.3, not 7.** typescript-eslint 8 supports TypeScript below 6.1.
- **The OpenTelemetry 0.300 SDK changed its API:** `metricReaders` is now an array, span processors moved to `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace`, and `BatchSpanProcessor` takes `{ exporter }`. Also, with **no** span processors the SDK registers no tracer provider, which would silently drop trace IDs from logs when no exporter is configured. A `NoopSpanProcessor` covers that case, and a test guards it.
- All the version notes are documented in CONTRIBUTING, so nobody upgrades by accident.

## Checklist
- [ ] CI green
- [x] Contracts unchanged (implements contracts/identity.md)
- [x] Docs and CHANGELOG updated (conventions §1 `packages/`, CONTRIBUTING Node workspace, package README)
- [ ] Self-reviewed in a later session

## Risks and rollback
Nothing uses the package yet. Rollback: revert the squash commit.

author: bestnathan
body:
## Problem

#2194: a reattach/route change onto a new Agent stream epoch seeds the new timeline over the buffer the client kept, so history the new Agent cannot replay is lost with no degraded state. The P2P Agent-restart fixture found it in CI; the `AGENT-RESTART-WIRE` diagnostic (first commit) shows the exact shape:

```text
mode=P2P before=0 degraded=0 rendererSurvived=false
attaches=[true] resumes=1 relayBegins=1
relayReady=[{epoch: A, generation: …}]
bootstraps=[{requested:5000, cut:atomic, fidelity:screen-only, epoch: B, through:0}]
```

The recovery landed on a Relay proof with a **different epoch** and no bootstrap for it; the pre-restart line was gone and nothing said so. The Relay case recovered only because its Relay attach happened to request a complete capture.

## Change

`SessionRuntime` now tracks the last adopted stream epoch from both P2P attach seeds and Relay proofs. On a change it marks the history unproven (`historyMayHaveGap` + `gapDetected`): the degraded notice is visible, `streamState` reads `degraded-live`, and the next attach requests the capture that repairs the buffer. Unlike an observed replay hole, the epoch-change path **keeps a requested bootstrap pending**, so a proven complete cut for the new epoch can still clear the gap instead of leaving a permanent notice.

The restart fixture now requires the degraded notice on **either** route when the pre-restart line is missing — the P2P-shaped loss is no longer exempt.

## Verification

- `vitest run SessionRuntime.test.ts` — 75 passed, including: same-epoch route change does not flag; different epoch flags; a pending bootstrap still clears it.

body:
Refs #615. Direct parent: #613 / draft PR #614. Zero/nonzero split: #611 / PR #612. Mertens suppliers: #151, #153, #154. Natural-scale endpoint target: #586 / PR #588. RH-E02 route: #334 / canonical target #15.

This PR performs the finite geometric-series reduction from an explicit ordinary-Mertens descendant envelope to the dyadic-tail square-root-energy supplier required by PR #614.

It does not prove a Mertens estimate, construct the pointwise-to-geometric adapter, prove the nonzero-frequency supplier, establish a zero-free region, prove finite-height RH, or prove RH.

## Exact stacked binding

- Base branch: `research/rh-parity-mertens-dyadic-tail-613-20261021`.
- Exact parent head / merge base: `aff0d4b4cff6cfb77ff695fc894058f500b41bec`.
- Exact parent tree: `2c06646c6b59b27a2ec33ca146af593a6c841d28`.
- Candidate branch: `research/rh-mertens-dyadic-geometric-envelope-615-20261021`.
- Candidate head: `771492a1d5d464f579d1a3c0147532ef182119ab`.
- Candidate tree: `3821ddb57d2653bc3ec023deba76e20a79e8a831`.
- Lean source commit: `875c81686ae725acee68b1274ac795a8062a368c`.
- Lean source blob: `9f33e04573e08c17007ce76006b141d94af4e856`.
- Mathematical note blob: `0e0efb9651a622d4ae74e2602bbc5d04611fa05e`.
- Passive target blob: `65f11e53697d3e780df547aad519dace0430ddc6`.

Exact comparison: four commits ahead, zero behind, three additive files, 727 additions, zero deletions.

## Explicit pre-squared scale

For `X=2^j`, the source defines
```text
A(j,delta)=sqrt(X)*X^(delta/4).
```

It scripts
```text
A(j,delta)^2 = X*X^(delta/2) <= X*X^delta.
```

The quarter- and half-exponent losses remain visible.

## Geometric ordinary-Mertens envelope

The source defines
```lean
DyadicOrdinaryMertensGeometricEnvelope
```
requiring, for every `delta>0`, constants `C>=0` and `0<=rho<1` such that every descendant in a dyadic endpoint family obeys
```text
|M(floor(b/2^t))|
 <= C*A(j,delta)*rho^t
```
and the same bound for the half-scale endpoint tail.

No inhabitant is constructed.

## Exact finite geometric comparison

The theorem
```lean
finiteGeometricSum_le_invOneSub
```
uses the finite identity `geom_sum_mul_neg` to prove
```text
sum_(t<L) rho^t <= 1/(1-rho).
```

No unproved infinite-series replacement is used.

The theorem
```lean
ordinaryMertensDyadicTailMass_le_geometric
```
therefore yields
```text
TailMass(b)
 <= C*sqrt(X)*X^(delta/4)/(1-rho).
```

## Squared tail and downstream transport

The exact squared constant is
```text
(C/(1-rho))^2.
```

The load-bearing theorem is
```lean
dyadicOrdinaryMertensTailSquareRootEnergy_of_geometricEnvelope.
```

It composes to
```lean
parityMertensSquareRootEnergy_of_geometricEnvelope
```
and, conditional on the independent nonzero-frequency premise, to
```lean
naturalScaleCongruenceL1_of_geometricEnvelope_and_nonzero.
```

Thus the source path is now
```text
geometric ordinary-Mertens descendant envelope
+ nonzero Fourier supplier
-> ordinary dyadic-tail energy
-> parity-Mertens zero mode
-> natural-scale congruence L1.
```

## Standard pointwise boundary

The source names
```lean
OrdinaryMertensSquareRootPlusEpsilonEnvelope
```
for the standard pointwise form
```text
forall epsilon>0,
  |M(n)| <= C_epsilon*sqrt(n)*n^epsilon.
```

The proof-relevant
```lean
PointwiseMertensToDyadicGeometricAdapter
```
owns the missing uniform conversion. No value is constructed.

## Evidence

Established:
```text
SOURCE_DRAFT
FINITE_GEOMETRIC_SUM_REDUCTION_SOURCE_DRAFT
DYADIC_GEOMETRIC_TAIL_REDUCTION_SOURCE_DRAFT
GEOMETRIC_ENVELOPE_TO_PARITY_ZERO_MODE_SOURCE_DRAFT
```

Not established:
```text
POINTWISE_MERTENS_SQUARE_ROOT_PLUS_EPSILON_ENVELOPE
POINTWISE_MERTENS_TO_GEOMETRIC_ADAPTER
NONZERO_FREQUENCY_SUPPLIER
ELABORATED
KERNEL_CHECKED
TRUST_AUDITED
EXTERNALLY_REPLAYED
NATURAL_SCALE_ENDPOINT_L1_SUPPLIER
RIEMANN_HYPOTHESIS
```

No Lean/Lake/native execution, proof-term acceptance, analytic estimate, merge, root admission, or RH claim occurred.

author: mikeagun
body:
## Description

_Describe the purpose of and changes within this Pull Request._
_Please reference an issue with a keyword such as Fixes #abc, Closes #xyz, etc., so the work can be tracked._

Adds a repository-managed portable distribution of the pinned Public Clang toolchain and integrates it with repository initialization, full builds, and bpf2c expected-output generation.

This enables developers to build with the supported Public Clang version without administrator access, machine PATH changes, or conflicts with an incompatible LLVM installation managed by Visual Studio or other tooling.

The portable provisioning workflow:

- Downloads the official LLVM portable archive for the repository-pinned Public version.
- Verifies the archive using its pinned SHA-256.
- Selectively extracts `clang.exe` and its resource headers.
- Stores the approximately 127 MiB extracted toolchain in a shared user-level cache.
- Uses locking and atomic extraction so concurrent clones and worktrees can safely share the cache.
- Removes the approximately 0.9 GiB downloaded archive after successful extraction.
- Validates the compiler version, resource headers, and ability to produce a BPF object.

Public and Internal remain compatibility channels. A separate Public acquisition source controls how the Public compiler is obtained:

- `Installed` is the conservative default and requires the pinned compiler to be installed without downloading anything.
- `Auto` prefers an exact validated installation and falls back to the shared portable cache.
- `Portable` explicitly uses or provisions the portable toolchain.
- Generated toolchain state records `Installed`, `Portable`, or `InternalNuGet`.
- Later channel-Auto initialization reuses the worktree's compatible concrete selection.
- ARM64 host-tool initialization receives the resolved channel and source.

Expected-output generation uses Public/Auto, so it prefers an existing supported installation and provisions Portable only when needed. It restores the worktree's previous Public or Internal toolchain state after generation and requires no ad hoc PATH manipulation.

GitHub CI remains explicitly Public/Installed so installer regressions are not hidden by portable fallback. OneBranch remains explicitly Internal.

The contributor workflow remains:

```powershell
.\scripts\generate_expected_bpf2c_output.ps1 .\x64\Debug\
```

**Draft dependencies:** #5667 and #5668

Part of #5666.

## Testing

_Do any existing tests cover this change? Are new tests needed?_

Portable provisioning validation covered:

- Cold download, SHA-256 verification, selective extraction, and BPF smoke compilation.
- Approximately 3.5 minutes for the initial cold operation.
- Approximately 127 MiB of persistent cache storage.
- Warm-cache reuse without downloading or changing tool timestamps.
- Two concurrent provisioning processes producing one valid cache without temporary-directory residue.
- Rejection and recovery of corrupt or incomplete cache state.

The source-selection matrix covered default, Installed, Auto, Portable, persisted Public selections, and Internal NuGet selection. In particular:

- Public without an explicit source required Installed and did not download.
- Explicit Auto preferred an exact installed compiler.
- Auto reused or provisioned Portable when no supported installation was available.
- Explicit Auto preferred Installed over a persisted Portable selection.
- Later channel-Auto initialization preserved persisted Installed, Portable, and Internal selections.
- Explicit Public source options were rejected when the resolved channel was Internal.

The following initialization selected Public/Installed without downloading and passed:

```powershell
.\scripts\initialize_ebpf_repo.ps1 -Architecture x64 -VisualStudioVersion 2022 -LlvmChannel Public -PublicClangSource Auto
```

The full Debug x64 solution build passed with 0 errors:

```powershell
msbuild ebpf-for-windows.sln /m /p:Configuration=Debug /p:Platform=x64 /nologo /v:minimal
```

Expected-output generation passed through both acquisition paths:

```powershell
.\scripts\generate_expected_bpf2c_output.ps1 .\x64\Debug\
```

- With Public/Installed state, it reused the installed compiler without downloading and restored Public/Installed.
- With Internal state and no compatible installed compiler, it reused the shared Portable cache and restored Internal/InternalNuGet.
- Neither run produced tracked fixture changes.

All bpf2c tests passed from a Visual Studio x64 developer environment:

```powershell
cd x64\Debug
.\bpf2c_tests.exe
```

Result: 126,875 assertions in 350 test cases passed.

PowerShell, XML, YAML, and `git diff --check` validation also passed. ARM64, hosted CI, and MSBuild 18 matrices were not run locally.

_If new tests were added:_
- [ ] Unit tests are added.
- [ ] Driver tests are added.
- [ ] Fuzz tests are added.

## Documentation

_Is there any documentation impact for this change?_

Yes. `GettingStarted.md` and `NativeCodeGeneration.md` document the Installed, Auto, and Portable source choices, shared portable cache, and expected-output generation workflow. The repository build and BPF verification skills are updated accordingly.

## Installation

_Is there any installer impact for this change?_

There is no product installer impact.

When Auto or Portable provisioning is selected and the cache is absent, the developer tooling downloads the official LLVM archive into a user-level cache, verifies it, selectively extracts the compiler and resource headers, and removes the archive. Later clones and worktrees reuse the approximately 127 MiB extracted toolchain.
