body:
## What

Follow-up to #440, on the merged v2.

1. **Bag `contents` gain an `nft` count**, written exactly like the `cashu` count: `["contents", "nft", "<count>"]`, after `cashu`, under the deploy bar's existing **Publish contents** switch (its hint now says "... cashu tokens and NFTs"). It is worked out from what is inside every time the bag is sealed, so it is never stale. Each distinct nonfungible.cash claim link in a message counts once (the #440 recognizer). There is **no NFT-alone form**: "Publish that money is inside" stays cashu only, because an NFT is not money, and `["contents", "nft"]` without a count is ignored.
2. **Readers:** `readBagContents` reports `nft`, the TV tape carries it, and **Cyberspace TV** counts NFTs on the chiron and in the bag caption ("1 NFT", "2 NFTS") and slams an **NFT INSIDE!** splash on the bag's cube, in the same way and place as CASHU INSIDE!. When both are inside, NFT INSIDE! takes the cube's other top corner, so the two never overlap. The splash is violet, matching the NFT card.

No other surface displays contents today (the TV is the only reader), so there is nothing else to update.

## Docs

- `onosendai/kinds.md` (33330 row and the `contents` section) now lists `nft`, with a JSON tag example and a whole-bag JSON example, and says the mcp and cli do not write or read `nft` yet.
- Spec: arkin0x/cyberspace#75, as a **draft**. The spec does not define `contents` tags at all yet, so "adding `nft` next to `cashu`" means bringing the whole tag into the protocol. That is held for the owner rather than merged.

## Tests

- `bagContents.test.ts`: the nft count (several links, duplicates, look-alikes, alongside cashu), the tags written in order, money alone never mentioning an NFT, and reading back `nft` (counted, uncounted and zero).
- `tvSegments.test.ts`: chiron words with NFTs.
- `tvPainter.test.ts`: NFT INSIDE! is painted, alone and beside CASHU INSIDE! on a different corner, and not painted without an NFT.

author: apackeer
body:
## What the person sees

Before: in Construction, when the agent starts a Unit's stage (Functional Design for Unit alpha, say), `unit start` refuses with "the engine currently routes a error directive. Run the exact directive.stage/directive.unit pair returned by aidlc-orchestrate.ts next." The agent runs `next`, gets the same step for the same Unit, and is refused again: a loop, and the person gets nothing. A live GitHub Copilot run met that refusal 11 times.

After: the Unit starts and the stage runs as the agent was handed it, asking what the stage asks. Nothing new is said to the person.

## Who meets it

The refusal comes when the stage's step, printed whole, is longer than what the host shows of one command result (19,000 bytes on Copilot, 28 KiB elsewhere), even though the agent's own step fits. Measured at Functional Design:

- On Copilot, a team that grew the stage lead's agent persona (the architect's ships at about 6 KB; 150 more lines, about 10 KB, is enough), or that keeps about 130 knowledge files for that agent (115 still start). Every Unit's start is refused once a team is there.
- On every harness, a lead persona grown past the 28 KiB limit (300 more lines on Claude Code).
- The case first reported (22,435 bytes on Copilot, the same on Windows and Linux) is a per-Unit stage that is the workflow's first stage, so its step also carries the conductor persona. I did not find a stock run on main that reaches that shape (not checked for every scope's stage list).

With stock settings and no team customization, a normal run's per-Unit step is about 11.7 KB and starts on every harness.

## Why

`unit start` (and pause, resume, and wave completion) asks which Unit the engine routes now by running `next` itself with `AIDLC_ROUTE_CHECK=1` and reading the answer off its own pipe. That `next` skips the rules delivery on purpose, so it prints the whole step: the conductor persona that the delivery sends ahead as a part, and the lead persona that the delivery lists as a file when the step would not fit. `prepareEmission` then measured that print against the host's limit and replaced it with the size error, which `unit start` read as "not this Unit". No host shows the route check's print, so the limit has nothing to protect there.

## Change

- `core/tools/aidlc-orchestrate.ts` (`prepareEmission`): the host's size limit does not apply to a route check's own print. The route stays the engine's own `next`, read by the same `requireEngineRoutedUnit` and `requireEngineRoutedWaveUnit`; nothing in `aidlc-state.ts` changes. The Stop hook's probe is delivered like the agent's step and keeps the limit, and a step the agent is handed that cannot fit is still the person's error, as before.
- `tests/unit/t-copilot-directive-budget.test.ts`: a per-Unit Construction project on the packaged tree; the agent's `next` and every `continue` to alpha's Functional Design, then `unit start` as the stage says. Cases: Copilot at the workflow's opening stage under Guard Policy off, relaxed and strict; Copilot after Inception with a grown lead persona, and with 130 knowledge files for the lead (the agent's step lists the persona and fits); Claude Code with a lead persona grown past 28 KiB. Each pins that the route check's print is longer than the limit and that the Unit starts.
- `docs/reference/06-hooks-and-tools.md`: the route check reads the step whole and the host's limit does not apply to it; the budget applies to every directive the agent is handed.

## Verification

- Red first: the six new cases fail on main (f6f213c48): the route check prints the 380-byte (Copilot) or 359-byte (Claude Code) size error instead of the step. With the change: `bun tests/run-tests.ts --unit --filter t-copilot-directive-budget`, 34 pass, 0 fail.
- Focused set, 21 files (every unit file that runs `unit start` or the route check): `t-copilot-directive-budget`, `t342-construction-checkpoint-routing`, `t-unit-receipt-only-step`, `t248-steering-content-delivery`, `t331-guard-deadlock-liveness`, `t330-authority-rebinding`, `t-request-text-file`, `t-checkpoint-approve-as-it-is`, `t-stopped-review-runs-next`, `t238-build-binaries`, `t-plan-approval-ask`, `t-gate-names-failed-checks`, `t-code-generation-completion-owner`, `t335-change-control-review-summary`, `t265-plan-approval-guard`, `t-engine-child-keeps-the-parents-chat`, `t260-unit-lifecycle-receipts`, `t324-team-unit-progress-gates`, `t-skip-mid-walk`, `t-checkpoint-unit-receipt-step`, `t-unit-receipt-recovery-ask`: all pass on Linux (the only skips are their Windows-only cases).
- `bun run check` on this head: pass (package, `package --check` deterministic across two builds for all seven harnesses, typecheck, lint).
- The reported case reproduced on Linux through the Copilot host's own hooks (the test harness's Copilot host firing the shipped `.github/hooks/aidlc.json`): the same 22,435 bytes as on Windows.

## Checklist

* [x] I have reviewed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
* [x] I have performed a self-review of this change
* [x] Changes have been tested

Four commits that can be reviewed one at a time: the tabletop tweaks, then the three steps of the [browser tabletop plan](https://claude.ai/artifact/9ZyFa3jH6i9jYTyGMqYkiy).

## 1. Tabletop tweaks (6f5fc19)
- **Box and Circle modifiers:** Shift now locks a perfect square or circle. Ctrl draws out from where the drag began (this was Shift in #20). Holding both gives a square or circle around the start point.
- **Shape tool modes (DM only):** Draw, Line, Box and Circle each get a small ▾ menu: **Drawing**, **Walls** (a box makes 4 walls, a circle a 32-sided ring, a freehand path walls along its main turns) or **Height** (a raised or sunken area at the Map tab's height). Players only ever draw.
- **Stat blocks:** double-clicking a monster in "On this map" opens its stat block in a pop-up instead of a new tab. Players can never open stat blocks or sheets from the tabletop.

## 2. Browser players join (4f32ae8)
- `lan/web.py`: a small web server on the DM's computer, standard library only. It serves the page and a WebSocket that speaks the same messages as the app. It only answers local network addresses, checks the Host and Origin headers, and allows GET only.
- Browser players are ordinary session members (id `web:…`) and go through the same password and DM approval. They can only send chat, whispers, tracker and tabletop commands, never characters or homebrew.
- Session page: a **Let browsers join** switch shows the address to open plus a QR code (`lan/qr.py`, our own encoder, checked against a reference encoder).

## 3. Browser tabletop (82a1166)
- `lan/web/tabletop.js`: the map on a canvas. It has the grid, fog, line of sight, tokens with conditions and HP, drawings, height zones and spell areas.
- Players can move their own tokens (and lift them), ping, measure, draw, erase their own drawings, and cast or adjust their own spell areas. This works with a mouse or touch (pinch to zoom).
- `lan/web/geometry.js` ports the tabletop maths, with a test that runs it in Node against `tabletop.py` (5257 cases).
- Privacy: player views no longer carry other players' install ids. Drawings and areas only say whether they're yours, and other players' tokens have no owner.

## 4. Chat, dice and turn order (f2301e0)
- `lan/web/side.js` adds a side panel with Chat, Turns and People tabs:
  - **Chat** has whispers, and dice buttons with bonus, advantage and private roll. The DM's app makes every roll.
  - **Turns** is the initiative tracker as filtered for that player. They can add their character, take damage, heal, set temporary HP and change conditions on their own character only. They get a note when it's their turn.

## Tests
- `tests/test_lan_web.py` covers the server, WebSocket framing, security checks, approval, QR codes, the Session page switch, and a browser player rolling and using the turn order.
- `tests/test_lan_web_table.py` covers the geometry parity check. There's also a new privacy test in `tests/test_tabletop.py`.
- The whole suite passes locally except 3 tests that also fail on main in this Linux setup: the player window pin and two text-drawing tests.
- I also checked it end to end in Chromium on desktop and on a phone-sized screen: join, approval, dragging, drawing, areas, the ruler, pinch zoom, line of sight, chat, rolls and turns.

## Qué cambia
- **Mi aula (Progreso):** resumen mensual de lo que el docente aplicó (evidencias aprobadas por la IA) y de sus compromisos, navegable por mes y compartible o copiable.
- **Aviso inicial único «Hagamos esto a tu medida»:** tono (sobrio o con logros), grado y qué quiere mejorar. Editable luego en Perfil.
- **Tono sobrio por defecto:** `isSoberMode()` es `true` mientras el docente no haya elegido. Quien ya había elegido conserva su preferencia.
- **Tu sesión de hoy (Inicio):** unos 10 minutos de las próximas tarjetas, del curso que corresponde a lo que quiere mejorar, con barra de avance. El grado se guarda para la constancia; no filtra contenido, porque el contenido no está etiquetado por grado.

- **Recordatorios:** el push diario y el correo de inactividad citan el compromiso del docente («Te propusiste: …») cuando no hay evidencia posterior; si no, invitan a la sesión de 10 minutos. Se quitaron «no pierdas tu racha» y el tono culpabilizador del correo.

body:
## Summary

Update AGENTS.md with repository-specific native-first scripts and libraries guidance.

## Scripts: native first

Before adding a script file (`scripts/`, `bin/`, `tools/`, root `*.sh|*.py|*.mjs`) or a package script that runs one, take the first rung that works:

1. A flag or subcommand of a tool the repo already uses (`<tool> --help`).
2. Declarative config for that tool (`cloudflare.config.ts`, `vite.views.config.ts`, `drizzle.config.ts`, `oxfmt.config.ts`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `vitest.config.ts`).
3. A maintained plugin for that tool.
4. A one-line package.json script that calls a native command.
5. A test in the existing runner (Vitest), for anything that asserts.
6. A custom script, only for behavior specific to this repo. Its first comment names the native rung it couldn't use and why. It has a test in the existing runner, and the PR that adds it quotes that comment.

## Code: libraries first

Before hand-writing general-purpose code, use a well-maintained library: actively released, widely adopted, typed, and a fit for this stack. Reach for one already in the dependencies first. Write custom code for domain logic and for the glue no library covers. A PR that adds a dependency says why it was picked; a PR that hand-writes something a library covers names the library and why it didn't fit.

- Runtime validation → zod.
- Typed Kroger HTTP clients → openapi-fetch with the generated API types.
- D1 queries and schema definitions → drizzle-orm.

## Evidence

- **Before:** The root AGENTS.md lacked the two requested sections.
- **After:** The sections above document the native tooling ladder and 3 library choices from the existing stack; only AGENTS.md changes.
- **Rung 2:** Verified these tracked configuration files: `cloudflare.config.ts`, `vite.views.config.ts`, `drizzle.config.ts`, `oxfmt.config.ts`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `vitest.config.ts`.
- **Rungs 4 and 5:** package.json (pnpm scripts, test runners, and dependencies) establish package.json script and Vitest.
- **Library choices:** Checked declared dependencies against their use in `src/services/better-auth.ts`, `src/services/kroger/client.ts`, `src/utils/d1-shopping-storage.ts`; the concern-to-library lines above follow those uses.
- **Verification:** pnpm exec oxfmt --check AGENTS.md with the repository's formatter configuration; git diff --check. `pnpm lint` also passes. Existing commit hooks run normally. This documentation change adds no script or dependency.

## 📝 Summary

- Slice Polars lazy table pages before collection, avoiding materialization of every preceding row when navigating deeper into a table.

author: leodemoura
body:
This PR fixes a `grind.debug` internal error on ground `Rat` arithmetic such as `(3 : Rat) * 2 = 6`.

When the homomorphism extension internalizes a term, it rewrites it with `Sym.Simp`, whose ground evaluator proves each step by `Eq.refl` (e.g., `Eq.refl 6 : 3 * 2 = 6`) and relies on definitional equality. The extension asserted the resulting equality with this proof directly. Its inferred type `6 = 6` is not definitionally equal to `3 * 2 = 6` at reducible transparency, since `Rat` operations do not reduce there, so the `grind.debug` check in `pushEqCore` rejected it. The equality is now asserted with an expected type hint, as other `grind` modules already do.

Closes #15867

body:
Session: gh-claude-18 [4f369d] · Head: ebf72d00

**Stacked on #1845** (S7, head `2cbefb7a`). Until #1845 merges, the diff also shows S7. This PR's own change is the last commit. It is a draft until #1845 merges, and it targets main so it will not close itself.

## Summary
S9 of #1790: Approve and Reject a journey on the Proof view. It uses the existing `POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/approve` and `/reject` (body `{note}`) with only the session's Bearer token.
- The buttons appear once a run has finished and the journey is not approved.
- A blank reason is refused in the Studio and never sent.
- After a decision the journeys are read again, and the page shows a status and a chip.
- A Runtime refusal is shown as its own text.

## Keel card

Session: gh-claude-18 [4f369d] · Head: 2cbefb7a

Keel card (full: persistence + permission act)
- Promise: on Proof, a journey with a finished run that is not approved offers Approve and
  Reject; Approve records the owner's approval, Reject records it with a required reason; the
  journeys are read again so the status (role=status Approved/Rejected, list chip
  approved/rejected) is the Runtime's; any refusal is shown as text.
- Paths in scope: apps/studio-next/src/runtime/client.ts, apps/studio-next/src/proof/
  (ProofView.tsx, decision.ts, decision.test.ts), apps/studio-next/src/styles.css.
- Routes (public, owner token only, existing): POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/approve (no body,
  no extra headers; serve/routes.rs approve_journey_flow), POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/reject
  body {"note"} (blank note refused by journey_owner::record_rejection). Neither route reads
  Idempotency-Key, If-Match or actor headers, so none are sent; Authorization: Bearer only.
- Persistence/permission: writes go through the Runtime's owner-record store only; the Studio
  stores nothing. A blank reason is refused locally and never sent. No old code copied.
- Recovery: a rejection is a new owner record (earlier records stay); an approval is undone by
  editing the flow (approval goes stale). Rollback: revert this commit.
- Proof: vitest decision.test.ts (pure logic), red by sabotage of each function; stub-Runtime
  check of method/path/headers/body for both routes and a refusal shown as its text.
- Journey studio2-proof-approve: OBSERVER_MISSING (fixture does not serve studio-next, #1808).

Refs #1790
Closes #1807



## Tests run (apps/studio-next)
- `npm ci`, `npx tsc -b`, `npm run build`: ok (dist removed)
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=4`: 17 passed (3 new in `proof/decision.test.ts`)
- Sabotage: breaking each of the 3 decision functions turns its test red.
- Stub-Runtime check of the client:
  - Reject sent `POST /v1/journey-flows/studio2%20proof/reject` with Bearer, `application/json` and `{"note":"wrong page"}`.
  - Approve sent `POST …/demo/approve` with Bearer and no body.
  - A 400 from the stub came back as text.
  - The UI was not clicked through in a browser.
- Journey studio2-proof-approve: **OBSERVER_MISSING** (fixture, C1 #1808).

## Open points
- The journey's Reject edge only clicks Reject, but the route requires a reason. The contract needs a fill act for the reason before Reject, or a fixture flow that is already rejected.
- Approve stays clickable when `approvable === false`, so the Runtime's reason is shown instead of hidden.

## Security
Owner-only routes. The session token is sent only as Authorization.

## Risk
A decision made by mistake cannot be undone from the Studio. A later rejection adds a record, and an approval goes stale when the flow is edited.

## Rollback
Revert the squash commit; the change stays inside `apps/studio-next`.

Closes #1807

author: senoldogann
body:
## Summary

- Servers the owner added showed "Left out": `select_tools` (`mcp/hub.py`) left out any server that listed more than `MAX_UNFILTERED_TOOLS` (30) tools and had no allow list, until the owner chose 30 or fewer on the Plugins page (item 426).
- A server without an allow list now offers every tool it lists, however many. The limit is gone from the hub, from `chosen_tools` (any number of the tools a server lists, at least one) and from `GET /mcp/servers/{name}/offered` (no `limit` field). Choosing every tool keeps no allow list, so the server offers the tools it adds later too.
- **Choose tools** stays, as a choice: `picks_tools` is true for a server that runs (to cut its tools down) and for one left out with an allow list (to choose the list again). The dialog opens with every tool ticked when the server has no list, counts "N of M" and has **All tools**. On a running server the button is a plain one.
- A run of more than 128 tools starts grouped whatever `[agent] tool_surface` says (`surface_for_tools`, `MOST_TOOLS_AT_ONCE` in `agent/scaffold.py`): some providers take no more in one request (Gemini documents 128 function declarations, and OpenAI's API has answered more with a 400). The reason shows in the run's tool groups line.
- `docs/extending.md` and `docs/runs.md` say what many tools cost and when a run is grouped; `docs/daemon.md` says how the two endpoints answer now.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/test_mcp_pure.py`, `tests/unit/test_mcp_connect.py`: a server of 120 tools hands them all over; any number may be chosen, and all of them keep no list.
- `tests/unit/test_tool_groups.py`: a run of 129 tools starts grouped with the reason; one of 128 keeps its surface.
- `tests/smoke/test_mcp_tool_choice.py` (browser): a server of 32 tools added on the page is ready with all of them; two chosen come back alone; every one chosen keeps no list; a choice that cannot connect leaves the server as it was; the dialog opens all ticked, All tools unticks them, and the two saved become the server's tools. Run locally with `-m "not live and not internet and not hosted and not desktop"`.
- `tests/smoke/test_mcp_sign_in.py`: a server that signs in and lists 40 tools is ready with all of them, and the tool chosen connects with the sign-in the try gave.
- Whole gate: `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy src`, unit tests (2440 passed), `dotx eval check`, smoke tests (528 passed, 1 skipped), `npm run check`.

## Risk

- With the default `[agent] tool_surface = "full"` every step carries the definition of every tool, so a server of many tools makes every request longer and costs more tokens. A model with a small window may not have room for them (Dot then refuses the run with its usual "no room" error). `tool_surface = "grouped"` keeps a server's tools out of a run until the run turns the server's group on.
- A grouped run whose groups on (those its chat used, the servers picked for its message, those it turns on) still bring a request past what its provider takes fails with the provider's error. Cutting a big server down with Choose tools avoids it.
- No change to how tools are called, judged or approved.

## How to revert

`git revert` the merge commit: servers of more than 30 tools are left out again until tools are chosen. An allow list kept meanwhile stays valid; a server whose choice kept no list goes back to needing one.

### Purpose
The surface-testing skill allows a test below the CLI for four reasons and asks each test to say which. None of the package tests under `internal/` did, so a reader could not tell an adapter test from one that should have gone through the CLI. After this, every `_test.go` file under `internal/` states why it exists, and the skill allows one comment per file for a package that is wholly an adapter or a fake.

```go
package herdr_test

// Package exception: this package wraps the herdr tool, so every test here is an adapter or contract test of it.
```

Dispatch's behavior does not change.

### Implementation
- One file-level comment in each test file of herdr, treehouse, linear, pullrequest, launcher's two drift tests, and the fakes herdrtest, treehousetest, lineartest, pullrequesttest and httpservicetest.
- A comment on each test in `delivery` (adapter tests), `history` (65 MiB line), `sessionlog` (arbitrary-byte parser input), `kickoffs` (concurrent callers), and `world` (codec round trip).
- `claimeval` and `commenteval` tests run each tool's own `Run`, so their files say no exception is needed.
- `skills/surface-testing/SKILL.md`: the fourth exception now says one comment at the top of each test file replaces per-test comments when the whole package is a wrapper or fake. A skill-creator review of the wording moved this sentence into the bullet it belongs to.
- `internal/pullrequest/export_test.go` is deleted. The drift test calls a new exported `(*CLI).Checks`, which `cliSource.Checks` also uses, so it sends the checks query through the adapter's real code path. The gh command line is unchanged.

Not changed: `internal/rules/cycle_test.go` meets no exception (it times a rules cycle). It is named on the ticket, as ENG-484 asks, not deleted.

### Verification
- `go test ./...` passes, `go vet` passes with and without `-tags drift`.
- `go test -tags drift ./internal/pullrequest/ -run Required` fails, identically on main with this change stashed. gh now reports `isRequired:false` for the `test` check on PR 76 and main's branch protection lists no required checks. I did not touch it.
- The other drift tests were not run, and no comment text or behavior in them changed.

Fixes ENG-484

author: yuyang16z
body:
## Summary

Add learning styles: the learner chooses how the tutor teaches a topic, from six built-in styles or their own files.

- **Built-in styles** (`app/learning_presets/*.md`, shipped in the Docker image): Socratic questions, Explain it back (Feynman), Worked examples, Compare and contrast, Mistake review and Self-test. Each has an escape hatch so help is never withheld: Socratic explains fully when asked or after two stuck attempts, Self-test answers a new doubt first, Mistake review confirms correct work instead of hunting for errors.
- **Custom styles**: Markdown files with a small front matter in `learning-presets/` (`LEARNING_PRESETS_DIR`; `/data/learning-presets` in Docker), parsed strictly without new dependencies, size- and count-limited, listed with a fixed reason when unusable, never shadowing built-ins (`custom:<name>` ids), excluded from Git and from releases. The guide warns that a custom file is a system-prompt instruction to use only if you trust it.
- **Per topic and per question**: the composer's **Learning style** (学习方式) menu sets the open topic's default (stored on the topic, synced to other windows and devices); each question records the style it was answered with and shows a small tag. Retry keeps a question's style; a revision uses the current choice. A style that disappears later is kept as history and answers fall back to the default way.
- **Prompt placement**: the style is the last section of the system prompt, after memory, followed once by the shared rules (the learner's explicit current request wins; quotes, notes, documents and tool results are material, not instructions; styles never lower factual standards). The stable prefix and provider prompt caching are unaffected; the style is protected from compaction and counted in every budget check. Inline explanations, branch titles, summaries and memory extraction never use styles.
- **Backups**: question styles are exported when set and restored on import; older backups import unchanged (older app versions cannot import backups that contain styles, as with understanding marks).

## Review and verification

- Three independent reviews (backend and data; frontend and end-to-end checks; the prompt texts as teaching instructions and their injection safety) raised 20 findings (9 should-fix, 11 nits). Each was reproduced with a failing test or probe first, then fixed; a final independent verifier accepted all 20 and raised one more (the budget error blamed a short style beside a near-limit question), fixed the same way.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run python scripts/manage.py check`: ruff, **1178 pytest**, **194 vitest**, `tsc`, `vite build`
- [x] `uv run python scripts/manage.py e2e`: nine Playwright smokes, including the new `learning_presets_smoke.cjs` (choose a style, the request carries it, the tag appears, reload and topic switches keep each topic's style)
- [x] `uv run python scripts/check_release.py`
- [ ] Not evaluated: how closely real models follow each style (only the offline mock model was used)
- [ ] The Docker smoke's new style checks run in CI's container job (no local Docker daemon)

## Notes

- Additive schema only (`node.learning_preset`, `knowledgetree.learning_preset`).

author: stevekinney
body:
## Problem

`createSearchTool` passed `toolbox.getAvailable()` to `queryTools`. That is a plain array, and it doesn't carry the toolbox's `embed` function. As a result, neither the toolbox's `embed` function nor vectors from `registerToolEmbeddings` ever affected the results. The returned `score` was also made up from list position (`1 - index * 0.1`), and the explain `reasons` weren't real match reasons.

## Fix

- The search tool now calls `searchTools` on the toolbox itself, so its embedder and embedding index apply.
- Unavailable tools are still left out: the search filters to the set `getAvailable()` returns.
- `searchTools` is synchronous, so the tool now waits for asynchronous query and tool embeddings before it searches. This uses a new internal `awaitQueryEmbeddingInfo` helper, which isn't exported from the package.
- `score` and `reasons` now come from `searchTools`. Scores add up across matches rather than running from 0 to 1. Reasons look like `tag:ops`, `text:name`, `text:tags(ops)`, `embedding:name:0.95`.

## Docs

- `search-tool.md`: the semantic-search section now explains how matching works, the default 0.7 threshold, what scores and reasons mean, and that the tool waits for async embedders.
- `search-tool.md` had two wrong examples. Without embeddings, "contact someone" returns `[]`, so Basic Usage now uses "send message". The explain example also showed the wrong reasons.
- `embeddings.md` and `searching-tools.md` now say that calling `queryTools` directly with an async `embed` matches by text only on the first call for a query.
- These three files carry some fence edits from the in-progress branch that type-checks the Markdown code examples, which lands later and will resolve its conflicts with them.

## Tests

- Added a "semantic search" group in `test/search-tools.test.ts`: a sync `embed`, an async `embed`, `registerToolEmbeddings`, and an unavailable tool that matches only by embedding.
- The first three fail on `main` and pass with the fix; the unavailable-tool test passes either way.
- In `test/coverage-edges.test.ts`, the one expectation that asserted the old made-up reasons now asserts the real ones.

`bun run validate` passes at `df24e35d9` (#437), audit included. `bun.lock` is unchanged.

- 显式 `globallyUnique:null`，绝不把局部满秩当作解存在或全局唯一证明。未接任何现存求解器、动画和生产接口。

### 本地实际检查（提交前）

author: clockblocker
body:
Closes #173

## What

When VAM renames a folder, Obsidian also reports a rename for every file and subfolder inside it. Those reports reached subscribers as if the user had made them. This PR marks them as Self Events. It also fixes two ordering bugs in dispatch that the leak had been hiding.

### 1. Descendant renames of VAM's own `RenameFolder` are Self (`self-event-tracker.ts`, `vault-observation.ts`)
- For each `RenameFolder`, the tracker records the source/destination pair and keeps it for that action's window (begin → finish + TTL, as in #162).
- The new `shouldIgnoreRenameEffect(oldPath, newPath)` returns Self in two cases:
  - the old path lies strictly under the source, and the new path is the same remainder under the destination;
  - otherwise, the old rule applies: both paths must match (exact entry or prefix).
- The rename listener now makes this one call, so the attribution logic lives in the tracker.
- The destination is still not a prefix. A user's create in the destination, a rename from elsewhere into it, or a rename to a different remainder is still delivered. The existing "RenameFolder keeps only the source prefix" test still passes.
- Path matching uses the tracker's existing normalisation: separators are cleaned and comparison is exact, with no case or Unicode folding. The vault root `""` as a source matches nothing beneath it, as prefixes already do. As a destination, it maps children to root paths.

### 2. Trashes under a renamed folder run before the rename (`dependency-detector.ts`)
A section-move heal trashes the stale Codexes at the folder's intermediate location and renames that folder in the same batch. The sort only ordered actions by depth, so trashes deeper than the rename destination ran after the rename and found nothing. On master, the leaked second bulk is what actually removes the nested stale Codexes, so fixing (1) alone would leave them behind. `RenameFolder` now depends on every trash strictly under its source.

### 3. `topologicalSort` no longer loses late, shallow actions (`topological-sort.ts`)
The sort re-sorted the whole queue, including actions it had already taken. An action that becomes ready late with a shallow path, such as the rename in (2), could land behind the read index. It was skipped, and the batch failed with "Cycle detected". The queue now holds only pending actions.

## Tests
- `vault-action-manager/tests/unit/rename-folder-self-events.test.ts` runs the real facade over a fake vault with nested folders. It checks:
  - nothing is published for VAM's own rename;
  - a user create in the destination during the window is delivered;
  - a user rename from elsewhere into the destination is delivered;
  - a rename to a different remainder is delivered.
- `self-event-tracker.test.ts` adds tracker tests: depth, separators, the folder's own pop, mismatches, a sibling whose name starts like the source, the vault root as source and as destination, and expiry one TTL after finish (TestClock).
- `dependency-detector.test.ts` and `topological-sort.test.ts` cover the new dependency and the lost-action case. The sort test fails with "Cycle detected" on master.
- `tests/integration/librarian/section-move-heal-real-vam.test.ts` (from the scratch repro) runs the Librarian over real VAM for a `Pie -> Fish-Pie` user rename. It asserts one bulk (the user's), one heal batch, no stop, all three stale Codexes trashed, and the exact final file list. It fails on master with the leaked second bulk.
- Removed the scratch files `zz-scratch-folder-echo.test.ts` and `zz-scratch-real-vam.test.ts`.

## Gates
`bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run test:unit` (1736 pass), `bun run test:integration` (48 pass), `bun run build`, `bun run test:obsidian-e2e:infra` (33 pass): all green. Desktop E2E not run.

## Not covered
If the destination already exists, VAM renames to an indexed path (`New 1`). The descendant reports then do not match the recorded destination and still leak. The folder's own rename already leaks in that case on master.

author: yoomee1313
body:
## Proposed changes
The problem was that at block HF-1, the ABv2 install read the Registry as of the parent block (HF-2), but initialize() in the same block reads it as of HF-1. The two steps saw different Registry states. So, if the registry activation is HF-1, the install fails and the chain halts at HF-1.
The install now reads the Registry as of the HF-1 block itself, the block being processed, instead of the parent block (HF-2). So the install and initialize now read the same Registry state.

author: natemsz
body:
Fixes the flickering while zooming: names on the map (regions, alliances, systems) were blinking on and off frame to frame. The Bleak Lands was a good example.

**Cause.** To keep names from overlapping, each name claimed cells of a 12-pixel grid. As a zoom glides a name across the screen, its claimed area jumps a whole cell at a time. So a name near a neighbour flipped between "fits" and "doesn't fit" several times as it moved. The 3–4 pixels of give meant to stop that were smaller than one cell. On top of that, each kind of name (alliances, regions, intel, your data, systems) only gave priority to names showing last frame within its own kind, so a new alliance name could push out a region name already showing and lose it back the next frame.

**Fix** (`map.js`, `drawLabels`)
- Names collide by their exact boxes, looked up through a coarse bucket grid so it stays fast with many system names on screen. A pair of names moving apart or together changes state once, not back and forth.
- Hysteresis on exact geometry: a name already showing keeps its place unless overlapped by more than 2 px; a new one needs 4 px of clear space.
- Names are gathered first, then placed in three passes: always shown (selection, hover, route ends), then **everything showing last frame, of any kind**, then new names, in their priority order within each pass.

**Measured** in a local preview by recording which names were drawn each frame during a slow zoom, counting names that vanished and came back within 3 frames:
- Sovereignty territory view, zooming in: before, **8 blinks in 32 frames** (Impass, Placid, Cobalt Edge, Tenal, an alliance…); after, **0 in 31**.
- Security view, zooming in then back out: **1 in 40**, a region name returning right as the zoom reversed.

JS tests pass (104).

author: wufengwind
body:
Adds [dm-ops](https://github.com/wufengwind/dsh-plugin-dm-ops), a DeepSeek Harness plugin for Dameng database inspection, security checks and recovery-condition assessment. This PR adds one catalog entry under `tools`.

The plugin reuses patched MIT-licensed engines from [DM-inspect](https://github.com/Shiyuedong-Jade/DM-inspect), [DM-security](https://github.com/Shiyuedong-Jade/DM-security) and [DM-recovery](https://github.com/Shiyuedong-Jade/DM-recovery). Their licenses and attribution are preserved in `vendor/` and `THIRD_PARTY.md`.

Its own implementation verifies target instance identity, scopes disk and log checks to that instance, distinguishes data-guard deployments from DMDSC, and separates missing evidence from verified recovery capability. Reports support deployment/status filters, structured evidence, root-cause grouping and shared evidence references.

Validation recorded in the source repository: 13 focused tests passed; a live run against one standalone instance and two same-host data-guard nodes completed 486 checks without execution failures on DM 8.1.5.60. Real DMDSC, cross-host failover, actual restore drills and browser performance remain unverified. The plugin assesses conditions; it does not perform remediation or recovery.

Draft: the public source repository was created on 2026-10-22 at 04:38 UTC, so it does not meet the catalog's one-day repository-age requirement until 2026-10-23 at 04:38 UTC. The source declares `dsh.bundle` and has the `dsh-plugin` topic. The entry YAML was parsed locally; catalog CI has not been verified.

Junta en un solo PR los cambios de #5, #7 y #8. Los commits siguen separados: se pueden revisar de a uno en la pestaña **Commits**.

**1. Fichas verificadas contra el Consulado de Córdoba** (antes #5)
- Criterio: la población es de Córdoba, así que el Consulado General de España en Córdoba tiene prioridad. Buenos Aires se usa solo donde Córdoba no publica el dato o lo tiene desactualizado.
- **Vacaciones y Trabajo:** no hace falta estar recibido/a (alcanzan 2 años aprobados de universidad; los de terciario no cuentan). Se suma «se hace una sola vez», la jurisdicción de Córdoba y el envío de la documentación por mail.
- **Trámites:** cuenta ajena, cuenta propia, prácticas, estudiante e investigador/a dicen Consulado General de España en Córdoba. Nómada digital: en persona en Bv. Chacabuco 875 (Buenos Aires usa BLS).
- **Familiar de español/a:** nota sobre la nacionalidad por opción para hijos de español/a de origen nacido/a en España.
- **Estudiante:** medios de 600 € por mes (100 % del IPREM) y seguro sin copagos.

**2. Dato puntual a verificar** (antes #7)

- Marcas aplicadas: fondos y envío por mail de Vacaciones y Trabajo; «3 años» de Investigador/a.

**3. Ahorros por tramos** (antes #8)

author: michaelyoussef396
body:
## What

The GA4 + Google Ads (gtag) and Clarity scripts now start loading **at first paint** instead of first thing in `<head>`. `gtag`/`dataLayer` and Clarity's queue are still set up immediately, so every config, event and conversion call queues exactly as before and is sent when the scripts arrive. Where the browser can't report paint, they start at the window `load` event.

## Why

The three scripts are about **365 KB compressed** (PageSpeed, 22 Oct) — more than the site's own JavaScript. Starting first thing, they competed with the page's own JavaScript on a phone, so the page became usable later, and Lighthouse charged their download to LCP.

**Correction on #11:** live PageSpeed on `/builders-licence-melbourne` (22 Oct, mobile): **performance 58, FCP 4.1 s, LCP 7.7 s** — barely changed from before #11. The "3.6 s → 0.9 s" lab numbers behind #11 were measured with the tag hosts unreachable, so they left these scripts out.

## Measured (independent review)

Lighthouse 12.8 mobile (simulated throttling), stand-in tag scripts at the real sizes, **n = 13**:

| Page | LCP before → after | Score before → after |
|---|---|---|
| `/builders-licence-melbourne` | 3.51 s → **2.05 s** | 78 → **83** |
| `/builder-registration-course-melbourne` | 3.50 s → **2.34 s** | 78 → **85** |

Honest reading: much of the score jump is how Lighthouse models LCP (it charges the tags' download to LCP when they start first). On a real throttled phone the visible page paints about 0.2 s sooner on slow 4G (no change on good 4G), but the page **becomes usable 1.7–1.9 s sooner on slow 4G** (0.25 s on good 4G), because the tags no longer compete with the app's own JavaScript — that's when the enquiry form starts working.

The first version of this PR waited for the `load` event. The review showed first paint gives the same PageSpeed result with about a third of the delay before the tags are ready (0.25–0.35 s later than today, instead of 0.8–1.35 s), so it now uses first paint.

## Trade-off — your call

- **Very short visits:** a visit that ends in that extra fraction of a second isn't recorded in GA4, Google Ads audiences or Clarity, and Clarity starts recording a little later. Expect GA4 paid sessions per Ads click to dip slightly and engagement rate to rise — a reporting change, not a traffic change. Annotate GA4 on the merge day.
- **Click attribution, rare:** queued hits go out with the URL at that moment. If someone taps an in-app link before the tags have loaded, the landing page's gclid/UTMs are gone by then, so a later lead would still convert but lose its link to the ad click. The tags are normally ready before the page is interactive, so this needs a very fast tap; `/builders-licence-melbourne` has no in-app links at all. CLAUDE.md now says nothing may change the URL before the tags load.
- **Not affected:** ad clicks and cost (Google Ads counts them itself); lead conversions firing; in-app page views, phone clicks and form events after the tags have loaded.

If you'd rather keep every bounce in GA4, don't merge this one; everything else stands alone.

## Checks

- `bun run build` passes; every prerendered page carries the new snippet. `bun test` 48 pass.
- Admin/dashboard guard unchanged: no tags, no `gtag` there (checked in Chromium for `/admin`, `/admin/dashboard`, `/admin/email-templates`, `/dashboard`, `/email-templates`).
- Live check on this PR's preview with the real tags: see the latest comment.

## Merge

Based on `main`; touches only `index.html` and one sentence of CLAUDE.md's Analytics section, so it merges cleanly with #14–#17, #19 and #20. Squash is fine. After merge: re-run PageSpeed on the two landing pages and compare GA4 sessions with Ads clicks for a week.

author: dylanpulver
body:
When a field sets `attribute`, a value rejected by a `@validates` hook stays in `ValidationError.valid_data`.

On current `dev`:

```python
class S1(Schema):
    s = fields.String(attribute="string_name")

    @validates("s")
    def validate_string(self, value, data_key):
        raise ValidationError("nope")

S1().load({"s": "foo"})
# messages:   {'s': ['nope']}
# valid_data: {'string_name': 'foo'}     <- the rejected value
```

With `many=True` every rejected value survives: `[{'string_name': 'foo'}, {'string_name': 'bar'}]`.

`_invoke_field_validators` reads the value under `field_obj.attribute or field_name`, which is where `_deserialize` stored it, but pops under `field_name` alone. With no `attribute` the two are the same key and the pop works, which is why this only shows up when `attribute` is set. The fix hoists `attr_key = field_obj.attribute or field_name` and uses it for both, in the single and the `many` branch.

Tests: `test_validates_with_attribute` now asserts `valid_data` on both branches, and its `many` case uses two items so the list is checked rather than just its length. `pytest tests/` is 1193 passed. Reverting only `schema.py` fails two tests in `tests/test_decorators.py` and nothing else.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5). The output above is from a local run against this branch's base.

author: asuresh8
body:
Based on `main`; #1510 (the binary watch) has merged. After this PR the kept swap code names nothing that is deleted with the update API, so a later deletion PR can remove `proxy/api/`, `handover.rs`, `orders.rs`, `root_orders.rs` and `stage.rs` without touching kept code.

**What it does** (`crates/kbf-installer/src/proxy/`)
- **Nodes step removed:** `Swap::nodes`, `ChildAdmin::post_desired`, `Admin::try_post_desired` and its retries, `DesiredError`, `Timing::desired_within` are gone; `Admin::new`/`child_admin` lose the operator token. `Phase::Nodes`, `Step::Nodes` and the intent's nodes fields stay so old `update.json` files still read.
- **Old API:** a POST with `nodes:true` (the body default) is refused with `400 nodes_retired` before the request id is saved, an order written, or the supervisor asked. Node rollout is retired; the `deploy` verb's default request is now refused too, and that verb is slated for deletion.
- **Moves:**
  - the supervisor types (`UpdateSpec`, `Supervisor`, `RestartPending`, ...) into `kinds.rs`;
  - the status-file reader (`StatusFile`, `installed_commit`, `staged_facts`) into `releases.rs`;
  - `HandoverConfig` into `handover_swap.rs`, without the operator token.

  The old modules re-export them, so `proxy/api` compiles unchanged.
- **Builder (`assemble.rs`):**
  - with `--kbf-binary`: a `Handover` over `LocalOrders` plus the binary watch's wiring, and `/v1/update/frontend*` answers **410** "the update API is retired; kbf is updated by its package";
  - without the flag: the old path through `handover::legacy`, the only call from kept code into old code.
- **Layering** (`kbf-integration-test/tests/layering.rs`): `the_swap_names_nothing_that_is_deleted_with_the_update_api` holds the kept non-test files to naming none of `proxy::api`, `handover::`, `orders::`, `root_orders::`, `stage::` (`assemble.rs` may name exactly `handover::legacy`); `the_scan_for_deleted_modules_sees_each_way_to_name_them` checks the scan itself.

**Not done, by design:**
- `Source` stays `pub use kbf_update::Source` in `model.rs`, the one place kept code names `kbf_update`. A proxy-local enum would change `UpdateRequest`, `OrderWriter` and about 15 test files.
- `MAX_AGE_SECS` is not used by kept code.
- `HandoverConfig` keeps three API-only fields, documented as such.

**Behaviour note:** with `--kbf-binary`, an update left in flight by a previous proxy resumes at the watch's first stable poll (5 to 10 s after start), not at the first API call.

## Tests

No local compile; CI is the check. Tests below are added or renamed by this PR; every other test is adapted to the field removals only.

**Nodes retired in the old API** (`api/router_tests.rs`, `api/tests.rs`)
- `a_post_that_asks_for_the_nodes_is_refused_and_one_that_does_not_is_taken`: a POST with `nodes` defaulted or `true` gets 400 `nodes_retired` and writes no order; `"nodes": false` is taken and `rollback` still defaults to false.
- `a_request_for_the_nodes_is_refused_and_nothing_is_saved_or_written`: the refusal happens before the request id is saved or an order written, so the same id is still free for a frontend-only request.

**Update route retired with the binary** (`assemble_tests.rs`)
- `with_copies_the_swap_is_wired_to_them_and_no_spool_or_api_is_made`: the wiring is over the given `Local` and its orders; no spool, request map or counter is opened.
- `without_copies_the_update_api_is_built_and_no_watch_is_wired`: without `local` there is no watch wiring and the API's order spool is opened where the config says.
- `a_spool_that_cannot_be_opened_is_a_usage_error_naming_it`: an unusable `orders/` is a usage error, not a failure that the unit would restart.
- `with_copies_every_call_on_the_update_route_is_answered_410_and_nothing_is_written`: any method, path and body on the route gets 410 with the retired text; nothing is written.
- `the_body_of_the_410_is_a_json_error_that_says_the_api_is_retired`: the 410 body parses as JSON and its `error` says the API is retired.
- `with_copies_the_note_says_the_api_is_retired_and_what_is_watched`: the start-up note says the API is retired and what is watched.

**Start-up wiring and errors** (`handover_tests.rs`, `proxy_verb_tests.rs`, `binary_watch_tests.rs`)
- `the_apis_start_up_errors_map_to_usage_and_failure_with_the_reason`: spool errors map to a usage error and binary errors to a failure, each with its reason.
- `the_start_up_line_says_what_the_update_api_will_do`: the legacy path has no watch and its start-up line names the files, the staging deadline and that a POST is refused.
- `the_seams_start_up_errors_map_to_exit_codes`: `AssembleError::Usage` and `Failed` map to the matching `VerbError`.
- `with_copies_the_verb_does_not_open_the_order_spool`: `serve` with copies builds the copies' seams, not the API's, so the spool's usage error does not come first.
- `the_real_handover_runs_the_swap_the_watch_starts_and_a_clone_sees_it`: a clone of the handover shares the swap supervisor, `busy` sees the running update, and the migration is asked for the schema the kbf printed.
- `the_wiring_assembled_from_a_config_waits_for_that_configs_gate`: the swap is built over the config's gate.

**Admin client without the token** (`admin_tests.rs`, `handover_swap_tests.rs`, `supervisor_tests.rs`)
- `the_admin_calls_use_the_admin_port_and_the_readiness_read_the_operator_port`: role and open-count calls go to the admin port, readiness to the operator port, the other slot untouched.
- `the_admin_client_is_bound_to_each_slots_ports_with_the_secret`: each slot's calls reach its own ports and carry the secret header.
- `the_child_admin_reaches_the_ports_of_its_slot`: admin and operator ports of a slot are not interchanged and every admin call carries the secret.

**Swap never tells the nodes** (`swap_tests.rs`, `supervisor_swap/tests.rs`)
- `the_bake_confirms_after_the_window_and_the_nodes_are_never_told`: with `nodes` true or false the bake confirms after the window, the nodes phase is never entered, `nodes_posted` stays false and no failure is recorded.
- `the_source_of_an_update_is_kept_in_its_record`: the update's source is kept in `update.json` and shown in the status, for staged and fetch.

**Old records still read** (`nodes_tests.rs`, `root_orders_tests.rs`)
- `a_record_at_the_retired_nodes_phase_goes_on_to_the_drain`: a proxy restarted on a record left at `nodes` sends nothing, drains, retires the old child and ends `done`.
- `a_failure_an_older_build_recorded_at_nodes_still_ends_the_update_failed`: a failure recorded at `nodes` survives the restart; the update ends `failed` at `nodes` with the staged release kept and the new child serving.
- `an_update_json_of_a_build_that_told_the_nodes_is_still_read`: the `nodes` phase, the `nodes` step and `nodes_posted` still parse.
- `a_wrong_type_in_a_key_the_swap_does_not_read_is_not_an_error`: the moved status reader reads only the three keys the swap uses; a wrong type elsewhere is not an error.

**Layering** (`kbf-integration-test/tests/layering.rs`)
- `the_swap_names_nothing_that_is_deleted_with_the_update_api`: no kept file imports `proxy::api`, `handover::`, the order spool or `stage::`, as a path or inside braces; the seam names only `handover::legacy`.
- `the_scan_for_deleted_modules_sees_each_way_to_name_them`: every needle and word is matched, `handover_swap::` and `LocalOrders` are not, a `use` statement is read across lines, and a comment or non-`use` line is not taken for one.

author: wboayue
body:
Second of three PRs for #342: a core maneuver runner and a script field that flies a roll, a loop, or a doublet on reaching a plane waypoint. PR 3 (eXplora gains, `explora_acro.csv`, flights) builds on it and `Closes #342`.

## Changes

**Core `commanders::maneuver`** (`no_std`, no allocation):
- `Maneuver`: up to `MAX_SEGMENTS` (16) segments, `Copy`, fixed size.
  - `#[non_exhaustive] enum Segment`:
    - `Rotate { axis, rate, end, thrust }`: a signed body rate about one axis until an angle has turned or a time has passed.
    - `Pause { duration_s, thrust }`: zero body rate for a time.
    - `Line` (Aresti lines, point-roll hesitations) can join later without breaking anything.
  - `RateLaw::Constant { radps }` or `RateLaw::Radius { radius_m }` (`V / R` each tick, V the airspeed, else the ground speed). Signed: negative roll is left, a negative radius an outside loop.
  - `Thrust::Maneuver` (`ManeuverConfig::thrust`, default 1.0) or `Thrust::Cruise` (`ManeuverConfig::cruise_thrust`). Doublets fly at cruise thrust (sim evidence below).
  - Catalog: `roll(rate)`, `loop_(radius)`, `doublet(axis, rate, half_s)` (`+rate`, `−rate`, then a `DOUBLET_PAUSE_S` 1 s pause).
  - `Maneuver::new` refuses with `ManeuverError` (`Empty`, `TooManySegments`, `InvalidSegment`).
- `ManeuverRunner`: `start`, `next(dt, state) -> Option<ControlInput>`, `abort`, `phase`.
  - Segments go out as `AbsoluteRate`, then a level `AbsoluteAttitude` recovery (`RecoveryConfig`: band, rate, settle, timeout), then `None` hands back to the caller.
- **Progress through an angle:** the twist of `start⁻¹ · q` about the segment's axis (new `math::twist_angle_rad`), unwrapped tick to tick with `wrap_angle`.
  - No Euler angles, which clamp at ±90° in a loop.
  - An angle segment times out at `timeout_factor` (2) × its expected time, so a non-finite attitude can't stall it. Durations and pauses end on time alone.
- **Shapes per ArduPilot's scripted aerobatics** (`libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/Aerobatics/FixedWing/plane_aerobatics.lua` at `3d24375`):
  - the loop is a vertical arc of a radius (`:1456-1462`);
  - the roll is whole turns along a straight (`:1465-1469`).
  - Unlike ArduPilot, the runner flies rates rather than tracking a path, and holds a fixed thrust where ArduPilot holds speed by throttle (`:54`, `:561`).

**sitl `ScriptCommander`:**
- `script/actions.rs` replaces `Holds`: one seam for a row's actions, its maneuver then its hold, started when the follower moves on from the row's waypoint, with the follower paused meanwhile.
- CSV field 8, on `plane` rows only: `roll:<deg/s>`, `loop:<m>` (negative: outside), and `doublet_roll`, `doublet_pitch`, `doublet_yaw` as `:<deg/s>[:<half s>]` (default half width 0.5 s).
- Parse errors: an unknown name, a wrong argument count, a malformed number, an unflyable maneuver, a maneuver on a copter row.
- `ScriptCommander::with_maneuver_config`.

## Sim evidence (`tests/maneuver.rs`)

All flown from the line at trim airspeed, on `airframes::plane()` and the sim tailsitter's plane side.

**Doublet thrust vs. the step it measures.** Peak roll rate for a 1 rad/s doublet, as a multiple of the command:

| Thrust | `plane()` | sim tailsitter |
|---|---|---|
| 0.4 | 0.97 | 1.01 |
| 0.6 | 0.98 | 1.21 |
| 1.0 | 1.02 | 2.20 |

- The propwash over the tailsitter's elevons grows their authority with thrust, so doublets fly at the cruise thrust.
- At cruise thrust, a doublet's first half peaks as a held 1 s step does (0.98 / 1.37) within 0.01 rad/s.
- Rolls need the maneuver thrust: at 0.6, the tailsitter's 180°/s roll reached only 1.9 rad/s and timed out.

**Bands** (measured + margin, each stated beside its test):

| Test | Rows | Measured | Band |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rolls_turn_a_full_turn_and_fly_on` | 180°/s both ways | plane 3.06 s / 23.4 m lost; tailsitter 1.81 s / 12.6 m | rotation ≤ 3.6 / 2.2 s, loss ≤ 28 / 15 m |
| `loops_fly_their_radius_and_fly_on` | 10 m, 25 m | radius 6–8% short; ≤ 2.0 m lower at exit | within 15%; ≤ 3 m |
| `doublets_measure_the_step_response` | roll, pitch at 1 rad/s | peak = step; final rate ≤ 0.48 rad/s | within 0.05 rad/s; ≤ 0.7 rad/s |
| all (`check_flies_on`) | | recovery ≤ 1.39 s; back on the line 0.0 m off, ≤ 1.1 m high/low | ≤ 2 s; ≤ 1 m cross track; `ALTITUDE_BAND_M` (ArduPilot ±1 m) |

**Roll height loss:** pure roll rate lets the lift tip over, so a roll sinks (plane 37 m at 90°/s). Keeping height through a roll is #481. PR 3's script flies its roll at 180°/s with height to spare.

## Tests

- **Core unit tests:**
  - out-of-range maneuvers refused (including 17 segments, zero and non-finite rates and radii);
  - catalog segments;
  - a full turn read from the attitude, ending at the commanded rate's tick: right, left, from a climb, loops inside, banked, and outside;
  - the phase order;
  - doublets on time, with and without an attitude;
  - timeouts without an attitude or a speed;
  - the recovery band (inverted, banked, nose down, still rolling, NaN);
  - `abort` and restart;
  - per-segment thrust;
  - config validation;
  - the loop rate from airspeed, else ground speed.
- **`math::twist_angle_rad`:** a table, including a quaternion's negation and NaN.
- **sitl:** field-8 parsing and its errors, the action seam (start on moving on, hold timing, maneuver then hold), and a `ScriptCommander` flying a row's doublet, recovery, hold, then the next leg.
- **Mutations** (fix staged first):
  - Ignoring the angle (timeout only) fails the unit turn test, and in the sim the roll's rotation-time band and the loop's height band.
  - Cruise thrust read as maneuver thrust fails `segments_fly_their_thrust` and `doublets_measure_the_step_response` (plane pitch: doublet 1.12 vs step 1.03).
  - Radius direction forced positive fails the outside-loop row (2095 ticks vs 1048).

## Checks

`cargo fmt --all`, `just lint`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (1407 passed), `just embedded`. `just fw-size`: 35,152 B text (the firmware wires no maneuvers).

No RealFlight check in this PR: no example flies a maneuver yet. PR 3 adds `explora_acro.csv` and its flights.

## What & why

The position tile is the signature component in `docs/WIREFRAME.md` §4. This PR renders it in four states — riding, pre-bank, entering, unsellable — plus the positions KPI band, filters, closed strip and state reference.

Closes #8

## Scope

body:
## Anlass

Der Betreiber hat am 22.10.2026 den Beitrag des Tages beanstandet und zu zwei Kacheln Folgendes gesagt:

- **UK-Inflation:** Statt eines Gebäudes, „das man nicht mal kennt“, gehört dort der Notenbankchef hin. Und zwar so, wie er „bestimmt mal gesprochen hat, mit Fahnen im Hintergrund“.
- **EQT übernimmt Qiagen:** „kennt kein Schwein.“ Auf Instagram soll nur stehen, was die breite Masse abholt. Auf der Website darf so eine Meldung stehen.

## Änderungen

- **Auswahl der Meldungen:** `ANWEISUNG_INSTAGRAM` steht in `lib/instagram-plan.ts` und wörtlich in `nachrichten-agent.yml`. Beide Fassungen verlangen jetzt Themen wie Zins, Inflation, Öl, Gold, DAX, Bitcoin und Weltkonzerne. Kaum bekannte Firmen sind ausgeschlossen. Fehlt eine fünfte passende Meldung, kommt sie aus den Quellen. Der Prompt hat damit 20.769 Bytes, die Grenze liegt bei 20.800.
- **Suche nach dem Notenbankchef:** `suchenFuer(titel, motiv, text)` erkennt Inflation und Zins in Überschrift oder Text. Dann sucht sie zuerst den Notenbankchef in dieser Reihenfolge: Pressekonferenz, Rede, dann jedes Foto.
  - Gesucht wird in seiner Commons-Kategorie (`deepcat:`, Tabelle `NOTENBANKCHEFS`), nicht nach seinem Namen.
  - Grund: Die Suche nach „Andrew Bailey“ lieferte als ersten Treffer einen Baseballspieler der Red Sox.
- **`taugt(…, person)`:** Bei Personensuchen schließen „conference“ und „meeting“ ein Foto nicht mehr aus. Auch der Commons-Hinweis auf Persönlichkeitsrechte blockiert dann nicht, denn er betrifft Werbung, nicht Nachrichten über ein Amt. Die Auswahl von Hand nutzt diesen Modus ebenfalls.
- **Dokumentation:** Tests ergänzt, AGENTS.md gekürzt und ergänzt (25.476 Zeichen), Nachtrag in ENTSCHEIDUNGEN.md, `wissen/` gespiegelt.

## Befund (Stand 22.10.2026, abgefragt über einen Läufer)

- **Andrew Bailey:** Auf Commons gibt es genau ein freies Querformat-Foto, mit Janet Yellen beim IWF 2021. Die Fotos der Bank of England selbst sind nicht frei.
- **Kevin Warsh:** gemeinfreie Fotos von der FOMC-Pressekonferenz.
- **Christine Lagarde und Kazuo Ueda:** jeweils viele freie Fotos.

## Prüfung

`npm test` 150/150, `tsc` ohne Fehler.

body:
## Summary

PR B of Connect Claude (SPEC §12, rollout step 1). It adds the three remaining tools that work on data Offing already has, on top of the OAuth MCP server from #45.

| Tool | Access needed | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `find` | Read | One broad lookup. You can combine `text`, `from`/`to` dates, `person_id`, `crew_id` and `chore_id`. Text searches people (names and notes), chores, chore lists and crews. A date range returns birthdays (including across new year) and chores due in it. `crew_id` gives the members with their member ids plus that crew's chores. `chore_id` gives the chore with its last 10 log entries and their entry ids. Results are capped at 50 lines per section, and a range can be at most 366 days. |
| `save_person` | Read and add new to add, Read, add and change to update | Works on the user's **own** address book only. Validation is the app's own (`PersonRequest::rulesFor` and `checkBirthday`, factored out so the two can't drift apart). An update changes only the fields passed, and `null` clears a field. It warns about a probable duplicate. Writes are audited as `person.created`/`person.updated` with `via: ai` and the OAuth client id. Deleting stays in the app. |
| `log_chore` | Read and add new to log, Read, add and change to undo | Ticks a chore off or skips it through Shipshape's `Logbook`, using the chore's current version and recording `via: 'ai'`. It can credit a crewmate who is aboard that crew. The same call repeated within 2 minutes is treated as a retry and not logged twice. Undo goes through `Logbook::void`. |

Other changes:
- **Write tools are hidden** from Read-only connections and from users without the matching feature (`shouldRegister`), so an assistant never sees a tool it can't use. If the level is too low for the action asked, the tool says which level is needed and where the user can change it.
- **Tool names are snake_case.** `get-briefing` is now `get_briefing`, which matches the SPEC and the server instructions that already said `get_briefing`.
- **Server instructions** now cover `find` and the write habits: only write what was asked, and ask when a name is ambiguous. The server version is now 0.2.0.
- **Shared code:** `App\Mcp\Text` holds the compact line format and `Concerns\ActsForGrant` holds grant, level and audit, both shared by all four tools.
- **Docs:** I updated the user guide (`docs/guide/AI-assistants.md`) and the CHANGELOG.

The scope is your own people only. Crew-owned people (passengers) are still managed on the crew page.

## Test plan

- [x] `vendor/bin/pint`
- [x] `vendor/bin/pest`: 335 passed. This includes the new `ToolsTest` (22 tests covering each tool, access levels, feature flags, other users' data, validation, duplicates, retries and undo) and an HTTP test that `tools/list` follows the grant level.
- [x] Larastan on the changed code: no errors.
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`: not run. There are no TS changes.
- [x] Boot-tested the real flow with `php artisan serve` and Chromium, as a guest:
  - magic link, then consent (`write-new` is the default), then token exchange
  - `tools/list` shows all four tools with their titles and hints
  - `find` by text and by range
  - `save_person`, including the duplicate warning
  - `log_chore`; a retry is not logged twice
  - undo is refused at write-new; I raised the grant level and the next undo worked without reconnecting
  - `find chore_id` shows the undone, "via an AI assistant" entry
  - the audit rows are there
- [x] Doc page updated (`docs/guide/AI-assistants.md`)

## Checklist

- [x] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`), see CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] No secrets, real personal data, or production tokens in this diff

author: lloyd-g-w
body:
## What

Removes the `job_wait` and `subagent_wait` tools. Models kept calling them to block on background work and lost time polling, even though prigh already wakes the agent with `[job <id> exited ...]` / `[subagent <id> finished]` when that work finishes, including after the agent has ended its turn.

- **Backend:** removes `job_wait`, `subagent_wait`, `Background_tasks.wait`/`wait_text`/`Wait_result` and `Tool_jobs.subagent_tools`. The tool descriptions (bash `background`, the job-started and moved-to-background messages, `subagent`) no longer mention them. `job_output`, `job_status`, `job_input`, `job_kill`, `subagent_status` and `subagent_cancel` stay.
- **Wake-ups in each context:**
  - **Main agent:** unchanged. A finished task starts a turn (`background_changed`).
  - **Subagent:** used to finish when it ended its turn, and its running jobs were killed. `Agent_loop.run` now takes `?wake`, which is called when the model ends a turn with no tool calls. It may block, and any messages it returns continue the run. `Tool_subagent` passes `Background_tasks.take_next`, which blocks until one of the subagent's jobs finishes. So a subagent is woken by its job reports and finishes only when it ends a turn with no jobs running. Jobs are still killed (and named in the report) if the subagent is cancelled or runs out of turns.
  - **Headless `prigh run`:** `Agent.wait_idle` already waits for background tasks and the turns their reports start. There is now a CLI test for this.
- **System prompt:** the "Background work" section now says: never block; keep working or end the turn; never sleep or poll; `job_output` shows a job's output without blocking. A subagent is told its job reports wake it and that it finishes only once its jobs have exited, so it should kill servers it no longer needs.
- **Frontends:** the special rendering of `job_wait`/`subagent_wait` in `tui/ui/tool_render.ml` and `tui/prigh-web/lib/tool_view.ml` is gone, along with the "still running" note parsing. Calls from old sessions render through the generic path, and there are tests for this in TUI and prigh-web.
- **Tmux test:** the "tools" scenario now ends the turn instead of calling `subagent_wait`, and the reports show as deliveries.
- **Docs:** README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md updated.

## Tests

New or rewritten Faux_provider expect tests:
- Main agent ends its turn with a subagent and a job running, and each report wakes it: `test_auto_background`.
- Background subagent ends its turn while its job runs, is woken by the report, and only then reports to the main agent: `test_background_jobs`.
- Subagent that ends its turn with a job running is woken by its report and finishes only then: `test_subagent`.
- Jobs are killed when a subagent runs out of turns, and when it is cancelled while waiting on its jobs: `test_subagent`.
- `prigh run`: a turn that ends with a job running is woken by its report: `test_cli`.
- `subagent_status` and `subagent_cancel` (rewritten without `subagent_wait`), plus `test_seen_files` and `test_background_jobs` adjusted.

Suites run:
- `nix develop .#backend -c bash -c 'cd backend && dune build && dune build @runtest'`: passes.
- `nix develop -c bash -c 'cd tui && dune build @runtest'` with `PRIGH_BACKEND` unset and the backend built first: passes. The tmux tests were run 3 times.
- pi-web does not reference these tools, so it was not run.

## Later

- A subagent that leaves a server running now waits until it is killed or the parent cancels it. The prompt and tool descriptions tell it to kill such jobs before finishing.

author: neonix-lab
body:
## live: O01 - append-only slices, nothing supersedes anything (ADR-0075 slice 9.1)

Refs #509. Parent: DG-O (`SCOPE.md` Part C, `O01`). Ends defect F1 of ADR-0075: a live day read as its last cycle.

### What changes

- **Planner** (`source_adapters/bybit_live_slices.py`, pure): the records of one acquisition become slices with half-open exchange-time windows. A slice closes at `slice_max_trades` (50 000), when the next trade is `slice_seconds` (300) or more after the slice's first trade, or at a UTC midnight (forced to the midnight instant). Trades of one millisecond are never split. Windows of an acquisition chain exactly; an empty window is not produced. Key `dt=<UTC day>/seg=<HHMMSS.mmm>` of the window start, parsed back strictly.
- **Publication** (`application/bybit_live.py`): both the live path and the restart reconciliation publish slices, each **revision 1 of its own partition** (`part-001.parquet`, `partition-manifest.json`, `coverage-manifest.json` in the window's directory, as the L2 slices do), through the same S13 / S14 / DataGateway read-back, and are never superseded. The wall-clock `part-HHMMSS` names are gone, so two publications in one second cannot collide.
- **Floor from the catalog**: the end of the latest durable partition of the dataset (live slice, day published before ADR-0075, or archive day). A trade before it is a replay (reconciliation: dropped and counted) or, on a live acquisition, an ordering violation (fail closed, `SLICE_ORDERING_VIOLATION`, nothing published). A reconciliation starts at the floor (continuity proven by the provider's recent window).
- **Profiles** (live and restart reconciliation): accept the key grammar and check the window: revision 1, start = key, end <= next UTC midnight, intent = window, no overlap with what is published, exact chain to the previous slice of the acquisition. The legacy `dt=<day>` key is accepted unchanged.
- **Checkpoint**: unchanged fields; it binds the last slice of the cycle.
- **Archive import** (T04): the CATALOG refusal now also covers a day that has live slices (`dt=<day>/seg=...`); without it the import could have been published over live coverage.
- Runbook: what the server publishes.

### Tests

- `tests/test_live_slices_v1.py` (35): planner invariants (also on random streams), ties, midnight, bounds, floor, key grammar, window checks of both profiles, wiring of the publication (floor, chain, mode, order, outcomes).
- `tests/integration_live_slices_postgres.py` (new CI job `live-slices-postgres`), real PostgreSQL, real `run_live_ingest_server`: six cycles leave six partitions, all revision 1 and `valid`, none `superseded`, **every published trade readable through the DataGateway** (before: the last cycle's trades); publications within one wall-clock second do not collide; the restart's reconciliation starts where the last slice ended and reads strictly with it; a replay publishes nothing; a late live trade fails closed; an acquisition across midnight is two chained slices; a slice that does not read back as published ends the loop (same count with other trades, and nothing back); the archive day and the live path never cover the same interval; the archive import refuses a day with live slices.
- `tests/integration_live_two_instruments_postgres.py` updated: it pinned the superseding behaviour; it now pins slices per instrument (and no longer needs to space publications by a second).
- Existing tests updated only where they referred to the removed `_next_revision` / `_record_intent_interval`.
- Mutation checks: 35 changes to the planner, the key grammar and the profiles, and 22 to the publication path and the archive guard, one at a time; all caught (the unit tests first, the PostgreSQL integration for the rest). Equivalent or redundant code found by the first round was removed instead of kept.

### Not claimed

- The pauses between cycles are not covered (`F2`, ended by `O02`): windows of two cycles do not chain and a strict read across them refuses; `allow-partial` returns every published trade. Until `O02` there are about 3 300 small partitions a day.
- Interpretation made explicit (not in the ADR text): at the end of an acquisition the last window closes one millisecond after the greatest `exchange_ts` (the session closes at a message boundary), so no acquired trade is dropped; a trade the provider might deliver for that same millisecond after the session is outside the claim.
- The first start after this change on a catalog that has pre-ADR-0075 `dt=<day>` partitions: the floor is the end of the latest declared window, so trades inside it that were not published are not republished. Existing partitions and their superseded revisions are left as they are; no repair.
- The state filter of the floor query (only durable states count) is not exercised against a catalog with superseded rows.
- No configuration surface (`O03`), no continuous session (`O02`), no deployment, no governance file changed.

### Checks

`python tools/run_tests.py` on Linux (WSL): 157 of 160 pass; the three that do not (`test_job_worker_runtime_v1`, `test_public_dependency_surface_v1`, `test_validation_transport_v1`) fail on the missing `QP_GIT_COMMIT` / non-editable install of that environment (the transport test passes with the variable set), not on this change. The three PostgreSQL integrations (`live_slices`, `live_two_instruments`, `bybit_archive_import`) pass against a disposable PostgreSQL 16. `workflow.py preflight --base implement/fid`, markdown links and `git diff --check` pass. I have not read this PR's CI.

author: uuriko
body:
Fixes #3778.

## Defect

An identity whose host registers a `wakeUrl` (via `POST /api/agent-heartbeats` mode `wakeable`, or the MCP `wake_register` tool whose entire contract is the wakeUrl) but which has NO agent-webhook subscription never received a single wake ping at that URL. In `server/agent-plugin-store.mjs`, `deliverWakePing` built subscription deliveries first and ran the wakeUrl fan-out only `if (deliveries.length > 0)`, journaling each wakeUrl row on the first subscription (signed with that subscription's secret). No subscription, no delivery — while `wakeStatusOf` still reported the agent wakeable.

## Fix (fix shape 1 from the issue: journal wakeUrl deliveries independently, with a signing story)

- When no subscription delivery exists but wakeable hosts registered wakeUrls, `deliverWakePing` now ensures a dedicated `agent.wake` **carrier subscription** for the identity and journals one signed delivery per distinct wakeUrl on it. The carrier is created through the existing `subscribeWebhook` path (server-generated signing secret — the same signing story as every other delivery; dedupe on identity+url+events reuses it on later wakes and re-enables it if disabled, matching subscribe-retry semantics). Its URL is the first registered wakeUrl and its event filter is exactly `[agent.wake]`, so room-event fan-out never matches it and no room body ever rides the carrier.
- The carrier is a normal subscription: it appears in `listWebhooks`, is disabled when the identity is revoked (and `deliverWakePing` still early-returns for revoked identities), and can be unsubscribed. Clearing the wakeUrl (`wake_clear` / pull-only heartbeat) stops it being re-ensured — that is the way to stop wakeUrl pushes for good.
- The adjunct loop now skips a wakeUrl that a delivery from the same call already targets (the carrier's own URL, or a subscription whose URL is the wakeUrl): one signal journals one ping per distinct URL. With-subscription behavior is otherwise unchanged — the pinned adjunct case (subscription URL + distinct wakeUrl = 2 deliveries) is preserved by specimen.
- No wakeUrl and no subscription still journals nothing; the heartbeat queue carries the wake, as before.

## Specimen (fail-first)

`tests/wake-url-only-delivery.test.js` (new):
- At pristine base `b7e63dbaa`: the two wakeUrl-only cases FAIL (0 deliveries journaled), the two controls pass.
