author: darshil9925
body:
## What this adds

An **Import** button on the Diamonds page for adding many stones at once from an Excel or CSV file, instead of one stone at a time through the Add Diamond form.

**Flow:** Upload → Map columns → Validate → Done

- **Upload:** `.xlsx`, `.xls` or `.csv`, first row = headers, up to 2000 stones. A CSV template can be downloaded.
- **Map columns:** headers are matched automatically (e.g. `CTS`, `RATE/CT`, `FLUOR`, `CERTIFICATE`); every match can be changed. 27 fields are supported, including prices, measurements, supplier and location.
- **Validate:** nothing is saved yet. Each problem row is listed by row number. Checks: required fields (shape, carats, color, clarity, cut), bad numbers, unknown shape/color/clarity, duplicate stock ID or certificate number within the file, and ones already in inventory.
- **Import:** valid rows are saved in a single transaction; rows with errors are skipped and reported.

Grade codes such as `EX`, `VG`, `NON`, `FNT` are converted to the values the Add Diamond form stores. If price per carat is missing it is calculated from rap rate and discount, using the same formula as the form.

## Files

- `app/api/diamonds/bulk/route.js`: `POST /api/diamonds/bulk`, requires a logged-in user; `commit: false` only validates
- `app/lib/utils/diamondImport.js`: field list, header matching and row normalising, shared by the modal and the API
- `app/components/DiamondImportModal.jsx`: the 4-step modal
- `app/diamonds/page.js`: Import button (hidden for loose-parcel accounts) and refresh after import

## How it was tested

Run locally against a MySQL schema inferred from the code, since the repo has no schema file. An 8-row Excel file with deliberate problems (non-numeric carats, missing cut, repeated stock ID, certificate already in inventory) imported 4 rows and rejected 4 with the right reasons. Re-importing the same file was rejected as duplicates, and the API returns 401 without a login. Imported stones appear in the list straight away.

Not covered: there are no automated tests (the repo has none), and I only tried a Gia-type account. Grade values are stored in the form's key format (e.g. `very_good`), which the stone list shows as `Very_good`.

author: guyberger
body: ## What this changes A long page is rarely heard in one sitting. Until now, coming back to one meant starting it again from the top: the listener lost their place, and the account paid for the characters a second time, since billing is per input character. A whole-page read now writes its playhead down as it goes, and the next read of that page continues from there. - The popup says how far in the page got — **Left off 52% through** — and the read button becomes **Continue page**, with **Start over** beside it for the top of the page. - `Alt+Shift+R` continues too, so the shortcut needs no extra key. - Continuing is the same move the extension already makes when a word is clicked: a chunk boundary is forced at the position, so the first request comes back *beginning* on the word about to be spoken rather than carrying the part of the page already heard. - A read that fails part-way through now keeps its position, so **Try again** carries on from the chunk that failed instead of re-synthesising the article from the top. **A position is remembered by the text, not the index.** An index is only true of the page as it was — a comment thread that grew, an advert that expanded, a sentence the author fixed, and the same number points into the middle of a different word. So a position carries the 80 characters that were about to be spoken; finding it again trusts the stored index when the text there still matches, and otherwise looks for those characters and takes the occurrence nearest where they used to be, falling back to shorter prefixes before giving up and starting from the top. **What keeps a position and what forgets one:** | | Position | | --- | --- | | Pause, close the tab, follow a link | Kept | | A request fails part-way through | Kept | | **Stop** (the panel goes back to Ready) | Forgotten | | **Start over** | Forgotten | | The page is heard to the end | Forgotten | Two thresholds keep the offer from being noise: the first 400 characters are not offered (quicker to hear again than to decide about) and the last 3% counts as a page that was finished. A selection read leaves no position at all — it is about text the user picked out, which may not be selected, or even there, next time. The store is one key in `browser.storage.local`, holding the 40 most recently read pages and nothing older than a month, keyed by URL with the fragment dropped. Every read and write of it swallows its own failures: nothing about a read should break because storage would not answer. Nothing new is sent to the API, and no new permission is needed. One related fix falls out of it: that store is written several times a minute, so the background worker and the reader now check *what* changed in storage before reacting. Treating a position as a settings change would have dropped the worker's warm settings copy — the one that keeps extension storage off the path of the next synthesis — and sent the reader on a round trip to the worker for a value that had not changed. ## How it was tested - `npm run verify` — 34 files checked, **118 unit tests pass** (99 before; 19 new in `tests/positions.test.js`), both builds written. The new tests cover relocating a position in a page edited above it, below it, at the position itself and beyond recognition; repeated anchors resolving to the nearest occurrence; which positions are worth offering; pruning by age and count; and that the store never touches a settings key or breaks when storage refuses. - **Headless-Chrome end-to-end suite against the mock API: 88/88 checks pass** (78 before; 9 new). The new section reloads the page between the two reads, so the content scripts, the chunk list and every byte of audio are gone and the second read has nothing to go on but what the first wrote down. It asserts the reload still knows the position, that the single request it makes begins in the paragraph the read was left in rather than at the top, that the highlight comes back there, that **Start over** asks for the same opening text a first read does, and that **Stop** forgets. - `tools/popup-paint.js` re-run: first contentful paint median 24 ms, unchanged — the new row ships hidden in the markup, so the popup still paints before it knows anything. - Screenshots of the flow, taken through the DevTools Protocol against the mock: ![The popup on a page left part-read: a Left off 52% through row with a Start over link, and the read button reading Continue page](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-4dc8ee9a-5266-4d7d-ab1c-b99a95295d60) ![The article after continuing: the highlight is back mid-article on the sentence the read was left in, not at the top of the page](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-ae8369e2-1f09-4228-9ec7-4c6efa23fd62)

author: aloysjehwin
body:
## Claude as the agents' model

The new provider, `server/src/adapters/claude.ts`, runs diagnosis and recommendations on Anthropic's SDK.

- **How it calls Claude:**
  - structured outputs constrained to each task's Zod schema (`betaZodOutputFormat`);
  - `effort: "low"`, so answers on the incident path stay short and fast;
  - Anthropic's server-side refusal fallbacks (`fallbacks: "default"`).
- **Timeout:** 25 s a call, so a diagnosis plus a recommendation fit in the 60 s function.
- **Safety net:** `GuardedLlm` still re-validates every answer and falls back to the offline reasoning on any failure.
- **How it's switched on:** with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set and `LLM_PROVIDER` unset or `claude`, the agents use Claude. The model is `claude-opus-5-5` unless `CLAUDE_MODEL` says otherwise.
- **Status:** the "ai" rail reads `claude:<model>`, and agent iNFTs record the model.
- **Tests:** 2 new tests against a stubbed Messages API. They check the request shape (schema, effort, fallbacks), parsing, and the fallback on a refusal or an off-schema answer.

## Pay on proof deployed (Hedera testnet)

The Hedera setup run on this branch (`stablecoin` and `payonproof`) created:

- **Ordo USD**, with Stablecoin Studio's SDK and factory: token [0.0.11123629](https://hashscan.io/testnet/token/0.0.11123629), proxy `0xacb8…8594`.
- **OrdoPayOnProof** at [`0xe9f1…a5e8`](https://hashscan.io/testnet/contract/0xe9f1bea75738434d45be5b92d2108b88d515a5e8).

The workflow wrote the addresses to Vercel, and the README lists them. Merging redeploys production, which turns the Pay on proof page on. The request file is empty again.

Payouts need one more step: settlement waits until OrdoTrust records the release on-chain. That needs the redeployed OrdoTrust, after which OrdoPayOnProof is redeployed bound to it.

Sesuai preview layar 2 (https://claude.ai/artifact/Wn4b627zs3Xu454xVPyKx8).

- **"Catat produksi" tidak terkunci lagi.** Sebelumnya tombol ini mati sampai kartu stok dimulai. Sekarang, kalau kartu stok belum dimulai, jumlah dan harga pokok di daftar barang hari itu otomatis menjadi stok awal. Selisihnya bisa dikoreksi lewat Stok opname.

  - **biaya lain** (tenaga harian, gas, ongkir);
  - total bahan, total biaya lain, sub total, dan **HPP / pcs** (perkiraan).
- **Server `POST /api/v1/stok/produksi/catat`.**
  - Biaya lain dicatat sebagai transaksi satu grup (dari Kas/Bank) dan ikut menjadi nilai produk jadi (`GerakStok.Biaya`).

author: trieloff
body:
Closes #873. **Test only.**

**Cause:** the takeover row starts a `playwright-cli eval` that never settles, then connects a second page's socket to `/cdp`. The takeover should close the eval's connection with `1011 … superseded-by-new-cdp-client`. Two waits made it race:
1. **A 2 s blind sleep.** It was supposed to let the eval get in flight before the takeover. Under load, playwright-cli takes longer than that to start and send its eval. The takeover then landed first, playwright-cli's own later connection took `/cdp` back, and the eval ran out its 30 s CDP timeout: `Runtime.evaluate timed out`.
2. **The second tab was opened and navigated after the eval started,** which also used up part of those 30 s.

**Fix:**
- The second tab is ready before the eval starts.
- The row waits (bounded, 60 s) until seven lists the eval as running, `model.browser.actions()` with `kind: 'eval'` and `status: 'running'`, instead of sleeping 2 s. Only the socket connect is left in the window.

**Proof:** CI under CPU load (twice nproc busy loops), cdp.test, 8×3, no retry. The name filter didn't isolate the row, so the whole file ran.

| Run | Takeover row failures |
|---|---|
| main's row | 2 of 48 rounds |
| second tab first, still with the 2 s sleep | 1 of 24 |
| this branch | **0 of 24** |

The other rows that failed in these runs are #848 (#872) and #874 (#875).

author: rohindh-r
body:
The second of three WebSocket PRs. #106 added the frame reader; this taps upgraded connections into it and keeps what they say. The screen and the HAR export follow in the next PR.

**What a socket says**
- `ProxyServer.upgrade` gives each direction of a connection upgraded to `websocket` a `FrameReader`, set up from the 101's `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions`. `bothWays`/`copyQuietly` take an optional tap that sees each chunk after it has been written on. A reader that throws anything is dropped for the rest of the connection: the record must never cost the connection. An upgrade to anything else stays bytes, as before.
- Messages reach the sink through a new `FlowSink.message(flowId, message)` (a default no-op), which `Owned` passes through.
- The flow is recorded as `started` with its `101` as soon as the upgrade happens, so an open socket is on record as one rather than as a request still waiting. `finished` comes when it closes.
- `SocketLog` (core/net/ws) keeps messages by flow, oldest first, bounded across every socket by count (5,000) and bytes (16 MiB). `TrafficProxy.messages` is the app's log; the recorder fills it, and Clear empties it.

**A hang-up at either end now reaches the other.** `bothWays` returned only once *both* directions had ended, while its comment said "either". When the app hung up, the server was never told, so the copy reading from the server waited. On a tunnel or a socket there is no read timeout, so that could be forever, holding a thread and both connections. A server hanging up didn't reach the app either. Now whichever direction ends first closes the other's input. Writing the WebSocket test is what found this: the flow never finished.

**Tests**
- A WebSocket through the proxy (a raw echo server doing the handshake): the app's masked message and the server's answer are both recorded under the flow's id, in order. The flow is recorded live with its 101 and finishes after the app hangs up.
- `aServerHangingUpHangsUpOnTheApp`: the app's next read is the end of the stream. Without the fix, that read times out after 5 s.
- An upgrade to something else records no messages.
- `SocketLogTest`: order per socket, the oldest dropped first whichever socket it came from, the byte bound, and clear.

On the emulator, https://echo.websocket.org/.ws ran through the proxy with Chrome reading it: it connected, and sent and echoed messages as before. The messages show up on screen in the next PR.

author: zzj3720
body:
Weak-network recovery for every client (the shared core), from the investigation in [this still.fail chat](https://app.still.fail/o/01M3HNG540559HJG7H4RCWW0TE/d70ccd1321eaa3aa3390df77fb901ff2774a7cc3da926c3cf25ca287a3ba5f22/ember%3Ac-786ae8f411).

Requested by: pengxiao <pengxiao@cue.surf>

## Problem

- **Regression from 3c8f7895a9**: brief streams back off 2 s → 60 s and a station answering no longer cuts the wait, so after a flaky period the station stays 正在重连 for up to 60 s once the link is good, and agent replies don't show. Its motive was real: each reopen read the whole station again (about a dozen reads) — on a quiet station the stream never got an event id, so it could never resume.
- After ~7 min unreachable a station is retried every 10 min; nothing tells the core the network is back when Wi‑Fi stayed joined.
- Messages that failed for lack of network are never resent; the new chat page turns into "no station" under the draft when the station goes down.

## Change

- **Station**: a stream read afresh gets an id-only SSE block (`id: <run>.<n>`, no data) with the log position, so the next stream resumes even if nothing was told. Older clients skip data-less blocks.
- **Core link** (`station/link.ts`): brief streams that resume wait 2 s → 8 s and the station answering or pings answering again cut it short; only brief streams that would read the whole station again (stations without the id) keep the 60 s backoff.
- **Pings as health** (`mesh.ts healthChange`): every way missing 3 pings in a row shows `reconnecting` at once while the stream is open; one answering again (or data on the stream) shows `online`.
- **Network back**: cloud socket opening after a failed try retries every station without a stream; the desktop shell also reports `net.isOnline()` flips as a network change.
- **Outbox**: messages failed with a network error (`host`/`mesh`/`timeout`, no status) are resent in order when the station's link turns `online`; idempotency key keeps them single. A new chat asked for while its station is `offline` is not sent and is asked once the station is back (POST /sessions is not idempotent, so ones that may have reached the station are not retried).
- **New chat page**: the kept station stays while down (`newChat.down`), with a notice and 重试 (web desktop + mobile web). Android/mbui UIs get the station instead of "no station" but no notice yet.

- **Station screen helper** (second commit, found while CI hung): its watching connection could be opened twice at once (revival and a request's `ensure`); the untracked one outlived `quit`, kept the test process alive (CI's 10-minute timeout) and triggered an extra revival. One shared opening now, let go if the station quits meanwhile. `HelperApp` takes a `Clock` (live by default); "the helper watched" runs on `testClock()`, advanced only while the station waits, and waits for the desktop's comeback work before each step. Stress, 4 at once: main 8 failures / 160 runs; now 0 / 400.

## Measured (core tests, fake clock; same scenario on main vs this branch)

| Scenario | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Stream cut every 10 s for 5 min, a chat open: station reads | 98 (350 before 3c8f7895a9) | 48 |
| After 6 brief streams, link good: back after | 60 s | 8 s; 1 s once the station answers |
| Station + cloud unreachable 7.3 / 9.7 / 14.2 min: back after | 586 / 442 / 172 s | 45 / 21 / 51 s |
| Unreachable 1.5 / 5.5 min | 34 / 34 s | 33 / 33 s (unchanged: bounded by the 60 s retry cap) |
| 3 messages failed while down | stay failed | sent in order once reached |

Stations not yet updated keep main's 60 s backoff for brief streams (they send no position).

## Validation

- `client/core-ts`: all 816 tests pass (after rebase); new regressions in `test/reconnect-recovery.test.ts` (resume within 8 s and no list re-reads, answered/pings cut the wait, pings show reconnecting/online, cloud back retries a long-down station, unreached messages resent in order and refused ones not, new chat kept while down and asked once back) and `test/mesh.test.ts` (`healthChange`, run on seeds 1–40, 0 failures). `reconnect-recovery` run 5× with 0 failures.
- `station`: `test/events.test.ts` and `event-log.test.ts` pass (new test for the id-only position block); full station suite (`pnpm test`): 998 tests, 985 pass, 0 fail (the rest skipped).
- Commit hook checks (typecheck web/desktop/core-ts) pass.
- Not done: a real device on a real weak network.

author: guolong123
body:
## 现象

`.omo/` 下有 1956 个文件被 git 跟踪，`.gitignore` 只忽略了 `.omo/evidence/` 下的 `*.png` 和 `*.sql` —— **`*.json` 没被忽略**。

而多个 jest 套件会**重写**这些 JSON（probe / matrix 产物）⇒ **跑一次测试工作区立刻变脏**：

```
$ (cd server && npx jest src/prisma)
$ git status --porcelain
 M .omo/evidence/plan-review-execution-gates/task-9/probe.json
 M .omo/evidence/server-gate-removal-tool-authority/task-9-matrix.json
```

危险在于 `git add -A` / `git commit -a` 会把这些测试产物扫进功能提交。

## 修法

1. `.gitignore` 增加 `.omo/evidence/**/*.json`（按现有规则的**同款 scope**：不加 blanket `*.json` / `*.sql`；`package.json` / chart values / e2e 证据仍须入库；`.txt`/`.md` 回执仍入库）
2. 已跟踪的 evidence JSON 取消跟踪（`git rm --cached`，**文件保留在磁盘**）

## 一个必须保留的例外（本次修正的由来）

第一版把 661 个 JSON **全部**取消跟踪，**过宽**。实测：在干净 checkout 的 worktree 里跑全量 → **7 个套件直接 ENOENT 失败**：

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../.omo/evidence/vteam-role-behavior-abstraction/before-agent-policies.json'
Test Suites: 7 failed, 179 passed, 186 total
```

原因是其中 3 个是「断言基线一致性」的 spec 读取的**冻结基线**（带字节身份闸门），不是可丢弃产物。仓库自己在 `server/src/execution-policies/__fixtures__/policy-fixtures.ts` 写明：

> 「BLOCKER-1 修复：基线文件必须**随仓库提交**（`git ls-files` 可见），否则干净检出下测试不可复现。缺失时抛错而不是静默跳过——断言基线一致性是这些 spec 的核心价值，跳过会让「证明」退化为空转。」

⇒ `.gitignore` 增加 3 条 `!` 反向规则，保留这 3 个基线入库：

```
!.omo/evidence/vteam-role-behavior-abstraction/before-agent-policies.json
!.omo/evidence/vteam-role-behavior-abstraction/before-boundary.json
!.omo/evidence/opencode-native-permissions-and-fixes/baseline-agent-policies.json
```

其余 658 个仍不入库。已核实**所有写点都先 `fs.mkdirSync(dirname, {recursive:true})`**（`seed.spec.ts:1618`、`platform-mcp.authority-matrix.spec.ts:671`）⇒ 目录按需创建，安全。

## 验证

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 干净 checkout（worktree）全量 `jest src` | **186/186 suites、4464/4464 tests 全绿**（修正前 7 套件红） |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `lint:check` | 68 problems / **0 errors**，与基线逐文件一致（未新增） |
| 跑测试后工作区 | `.omo/evidence/**` 无任何 dirty 项（实测 `git status --porcelain` 前后 IDENTICAL） |
| 磁盘文件 | 661 个全部**仍在磁盘**（`checked=661 missing=0`） |
| 基线字节身份 | 3 个冻结基线**逐字节未变**（只读夹具，测试不写它们） |

## 附带

同一 PR 收录 `.omo/plans/pm-coordination-hardening.md`（PM 协调机制化改造计划，7 批次 3 波）。

author: rakibulhaq
body:
## Summary

### Version: 0.1.6 → 0.2.0 (drops Python 3.9)
Snyk flagged 30 issues in locked dependencies (1 critical, 13 high, 15 medium, 1 low), already present on `main`. The fixed releases of aiohttp, multidict, urllib3 and yarl all require **Python ≥ 3.10**, so with `python = "^3.9"` the 3.9 resolution could only get the vulnerable versions. Python 3.9 has been EOL since October 2025, so this PR drops it:

- `python = "^3.10"`; `aiohttp` floor raised to `^3.14.4` so downstream installs can't resolve a vulnerable aiohttp
- Lock: aiohttp 3.14.5, certifi 2026.10.19, idna 3.20, multidict 7.1.0, urllib3 2.8.0, yarl 1.25.1 (everything else is unchanged apart from three 3.9-only duplicates being removed)
- CI matrix 3.10–3.13; Snyk job runs on 3.12; black/ruff target py310; README updated
- Minor bump to **0.2.0** to signal the dropped Python version (0.1.7 was bumped earlier in this PR but never tagged or published). 3.9 users stay on 0.1.6.

**Not tagged yet.** Tag after merging so `v0.2.0` points at the commit on `main`, then publish:
```
git checkout main && git pull
git tag -a v0.2.0 -m "Release 0.2.0" && git push origin v0.2.0
make publish
```

### Merge with main
Merged `main` (Copilot review commit `ead20ef`) into this branch. The `scripts/publish.sh` conflict was resolved in favour of this branch, which already passes repo args as an array and adds the release guards. Main's `"${REPO_ARGS[@]}"` fails with `unbound variable` under `set -u` on macOS bash 3.2 when no repository is set, so plain `make publish` would crash. `make check` passes on the merged tree (58 tests), and again after the dependency upgrade.

### Bug fix: alert intervals were ignored
`AlertDB.update_last_run` was never called, so every alert was evaluated on each ~1s scan tick regardless of its `interval` (an alert set to every 300s ran on 3 of 3 consecutive scans). The scanner now records each alert's last run after evaluation, **including on failure**, so a broken query waits for its interval instead of exhausting `max_errors` within seconds.

- SQLite path is configurable via `global.alert_db_path` (default unchanged: `alerts.db`)
- `AlertDB.close()` is called on `stop_async`
- CLI `--version` reads the installed package version instead of the hardcoded `0.1.0`, so version bumps show up there

### Test reliability
- Every test runs in its own tmp dir (autouse fixture), so `alerts.db` can't leak between tests or into the repo. This was a latent order-dependence that the interval fix would otherwise have exposed
- Two CLI tests mocked `asyncio.run` and dropped the coroutine; the resulting "never awaited" warning was blamed on whichever test triggered GC. They now close it
- `scanner_acknowledge_alert_async_returns_false_for_missing` was missing the `test_` prefix and never ran
- Removed the `event_loop` fixture (no-op under pytest-asyncio 1.x)
- New tests: interval is respected, re-runs after it elapses, failed queries still wait, configurable DB path, plus `AlertDB` round-trip/persistence tests. The interval tests fail without the fix

### Makefile / release tooling
| Target | What it does |
|---|---|
| `make release PART=minor [PUSH=1]` | Clean-tree check → `make check` → bump → `Release: X.Y.Z` commit → `vX.Y.Z` tag. Pushes only with `PUSH=1`; refuses if the tag exists |
| `make bump PART=patch\|minor\|major\|x.y.z`, `make version` | Version management via `poetry version` |
| `make publish` | Now refuses unless the tree is clean and HEAD is tagged `v<version>` (`SKIP_RELEASE_CHECK=1` to bypass) |
| `make publish-test` | Publish to TestPyPI |
| `make check` (aliases `ci`, `quality`) | Exactly what CI runs: black --check, ruff, mypy, pytest + coverage |
| `make doctor` | Diagnoses a broken Poetry/venv setup and prints the fix |
| `format-check`, `lint-fix`, `test-file`, `test-k`, `test-flaky`, `run`, `hooks` | Day-to-day helpers |
| `make clean` | Also removes coverage files, tool caches, `__pycache__`, `alerts.db` |

`DEVELOPMENT.md` documents the targets and the release flow.

### Config
- Explicit `[tool.ruff]` (`E4,E7,E9,F`, py39), `[tool.black]` and `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in `pyproject.toml`. Without a project ruff config, a contributor's user-level ruff config applied (146 errors locally)
- Pre-commit mypy hook scoped to `pysentinel/`, matching `make typecheck` and CI (it failed on missing `yaml` stubs in tests)

### CI
- Runs `make check`, so CI and local runs are identical
- Matrix: **3.10**, 3.11, **3.12, 3.13**, `fail-fast: false`
- Poetry installed before `setup-python` so `cache: poetry` actually caches (the old cache step ran after install)
- Removed duplicated pre-commit/ruff/mypy steps
- Fixed the Codecov condition: `secrets` can't be used in a step `if:`, so the token is exposed via `env`; uploads only from 3.11

## Test plan
- [x] `make check` passes locally (black, ruff, mypy, pytest)
- [x] New interval tests fail with the scanner fix reverted, pass with it
- [x] Suite passes 15× consecutively with unraisable-exception warnings as errors
- [x] `make release PART=minor PUSH=1` tested end to end in a throwaway clone against a local bare remote: bump 0.1.6 → 0.2.0, commit, tag, push; existing-tag and dirty-tree/untagged-HEAD guards refuse correctly
- [x] CI green on 3.10–3.13
- [x] Snyk green after dependency upgrade

## Not in this PR
Known issues from the review, left for follow-ups: `--async` CLI mode exits immediately; `threshold: {max: 0}` reports `threshold_value=None`; violation IDs collide within one second; `aioredis` 2.0.1 breaks on Python 3.11+ (now most supported versions); `asyncpg` isn't a declared dependency; Prometheus metric key is empty for nested queries.

author: jihoo12
body:
## Summary

Profiling `circle.hcs` (perf, user callchains) showed two costs unrelated to proof search:

- **Oracle round trip.** `horn cubical eval` encoded each derivation as an oracle (7.9 s) and decoded it again for the kernel (7.0 s), while the same kernel checks the same 963k steps from compact text in 1.0 s.
- **Interning.** ~40% of the time went to malloc/free and the term table: every lookup allocated a `Vec` even on a hit, and each node's children were stored twice (key and node).

### Changes

- `generate::Certificate::{Oracle, Direct}` chooses what `certify` hands the kernel. Without `--emit`, `eval` streams the derivation straight into the ground kernel (`oracle::check_text_with_rules`, which also collects `rules_used`). With `--emit`, the oracle path is unchanged, so the written certificate is exactly what was accepted. `script::run` keeps the oracle; `script::run_with` takes the choice.
- `Regenerated::oracle` is now `Option<Vec<u8>>`.
- Interner (`engine/term.rs`): probe with a reused buffer, the node's children are the key (one copy), atom lookup by address for literal names (confirmed by text), memoized unary numerals (`term::numeral`), and `keep_terms_until_exit` so the CLI doesn't spend ~7% freeing nodes at exit. Hash values are unchanged.
- In `eval` without `--emit`, the `ACCEPT` line no longer reports oracle bytes (none are built).

## Results (same machine, sequential runs)

| script | before | `eval` | `eval --emit` |
|---|---|---|---|
| circle | 55.4 s / 2.57 GB | 18.3 s / 1.83 GB | 29.9 s |
| poly | 15.3 s | 10.9 s | 13.3 s |
| binary | 4.1 s | 1.3 s | 3.2 s |
| bool | 1.9 s | 0.6 s | 1.4 s |

## Verification

- All ten `examples/cubical/script/*.hcs`: `--emit` output (theory, goals, oracle) and printed results are byte-identical to `main`; direct runs print the same results and step counts.
- `cargo test --release`: 145 passed. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.

author: cdalar
body:
## Problem

`onctl -p ac delete <TAB>` did not complete VM names. Cobra's completion path (`__complete`) parses flags but skips `PersistentPreRunE`, which was the only place `-p/--provider` was copied into `ONCTL_CLOUD`. So `ensureProvider` resolved the provider from the environment instead:

- `ONCTL_CLOUD` unset: exits with "No Cloud Provider Set", no completions.
- `ONCTL_CLOUD` set to another provider: completes *that* provider's VM names.

Exporting `ONCTL_CLOUD=ac` always worked, which made it look ac-specific.

## Fix

Move the `-p` validation and `ONCTL_CLOUD` assignment into `applyProviderFlag`, called from both `PersistentPreRunE` and `ensureProvider`. This covers every completion that lists VMs or sizes: destroy and its aliases, ssh, port-forward, images, and the `--type`/`--size` size completions.

## Verification

- New `TestEnsureProvider_HonorsProviderFlag`: `ONCTL_CLOUD=static` with `providerFlag = "ac"` must build the ac provider. Fails on the old code, passes now.
- End to end with a fake `container` CLI: `onctl -p ac __complete delete ""` returns the ac VM names with `ONCTL_CLOUD` unset and with it set to `static`; `-p bogus` returns the error directive.
- `go test ./cmd/` passes (one pre-existing, unrelated failure when run as root: `TestPopulateOnctlEnv_ErrorWritingFile` expects a read-only dir write to fail).

author: var1377
body: ## Root cause Not environmental. The bb2 tmpfs/xfs layout and inotify sysctls are fine: TMPDIR is xfs and no record is lost. Since #1204 (merged 2026-10-21 05:25Z), every Linux watch in a process shares one inotify hub and **two** service threads. `Shared::service` blocked on the watch's read-cursor mutex. When a fence, a stop or a paused test held that mutex, the pass parked a pool thread. Each record routed to the held watch after a pass called `begin_service` scheduled the watch again, so the held watch soon occupied both pool threads. No other watch in the process was then delivered until the cursor was released. `source_watch::tests::lost_changes_are_reported_as_everything` holds its watch's cursor while it writes 20000 files. Under gate load (load average around 95 to 150 on the 192-vCPU box), that takes longer than the 5 s deadline of the concurrent `linux_demand_watch_*` tests. Their records sat routed but undelivered, so they failed with `demand watcher timed out`. In both failing gate logs, the flood test is the last test to finish, just after the two failures. ## Fix - A service pass takes the cursor only if it is free (`Shared::service_reading`). If the cursor is held, the pass marks itself as owed. The holder's `ReadingGuard` reschedules the watch after unlocking, or force-services it when stopping. A second try-lock closes the window where the holder releases between the two attempts. - All cursor locks go through the guard: fences, stop, startup, retirement and the test-only `paused()`. No holder can skip the owed pass. - Retirement from a pass uses the cursor the pass already holds (`retire_in_service`) and only try-locks `retired`. The pass checks a new `retiring` flag instead of waiting on the `retired` mutex. A pass therefore never waits behind another thread. ## Evidence (bb2) - Stress with 48 parallel processes × 3 rounds, each running the two demand tests plus the flood test (load 90 to 160): - origin/main 59760fb41: 69, 70 and 69 timeouts per round. Only 20 of 144 runs were clean. - This branch: 0 timeouts. All 144 runs were clean. - New test `a_held_cursor_never_stalls_delivery_to_other_watches`. It pins a held watch to every pool thread, requires another watch to be delivered meanwhile, then requires the held watch to be delivered once released. It passes on this branch. The negative controls were run on bb2: - `service` locking with `self.reading()`: fails with `timed out waiting until the other watch was delivered`. - A guard that drops the owed pass: fails with `timed out waiting until the held watch was delivered`. - `cargo test -p acyclic-fs --lib` passed 3 times in about 5.2 s each, except one run that hit an unrelated failure in `native_mount::fence::destination::retry_tests` (a mount-registry assertion; no watch code involved). - Clippy (`--all-targets --all-features`) reports no findings in `source_watch/inotify`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents the shared Linux inotify service pool from parking behind one watch's read cursor, so a fence, stop, or paused test holding a watch no longer stalls delivery to every other watch in the process. - A service pass now takes the cursor only if it is free; otherwise it marks the pass as owed and the holder reschedules or force-services the watch on release. - Retirement from a pass uses the cursor the pass already holds and checks a `retiring` flag, so a pass never waits behind another thread. - Adds a test that holds a watch on every pool thread and verifies other watches keep delivering, then the held watch delivers on release. Written for commit 8a2973b1f9e4d126dbd9ab9a218356e61314625e. Summary will update on new commits.

author: mengyinghu-sys
body:
## Description

On Android, a test's press on a view that first has to be scrolled into view was lost whenever the scrolling reached the end of its list. Android 12's overscroll stretch was still relaxing when the tap landed, and a `ScrollView` catches a touch down during the stretch to stop it instead of passing it on. The stretch moves no view (it is a render effect), so the test agent's look for movement (`TestAgent.animating`) saw the app as quiet and pressed at once.

Reproduced by hand with `adb shell input`: a swipe that overscrolls the gallery's index followed at once by a tap on "System" does nothing; the same tap 1.5 s later opens the demo.

Each platform scroll view (`ScrollBox`'s `VScroll` / `HScroll`) now counts the frames it draws, which it does every frame while the stretch relaxes or the content glides, and `TestAgent.animating` counts them as movement, so the step waits until the scroll view is still. `docs/dev/tooling.md` says so.

## How to Test

`nsh test examples/gallery --target android` on a Galaxy Z Fold6 (SM-F9560, Android 16, unfolded):

- before: 23 passed, 22 failed: every test that opens a demo near the end of the index (System, Storage, Menus, Text, Gestures, ...) failed with the press lost or the view not found
- after: 35 passed, 10 failed. The rest are desktop-only steps (right click, hover ×2, keyboard shortcuts), the rotation test, which expects a 390 × 844 window, and the five Menus tests on a manual clock, a separate issue: on a real platform the manual clock does not move while a sheet's native slide-out runs or a long press holds, so the timers timed against them do not come due

`cargo xtask android --dev` builds the Java runtime.

author: bfaber-centaur
body:
Adds the c3 learned-correction lane: `research/composition-c3/correction/`. [NOTE.md](research/composition-c3/correction/NOTE.md) holds the summary and the reviewer handoff; README.md holds the tables.

**Order of commits.** Each design step was committed before the results it governs.

| commit | content |
|---|---|
| 3e3f73d | QUESTION.md |
| 4b70c74 | code and tests |
| 26c5590 | calibration choice, recorded after the reviewer's pin PASS and before any evaluation |
| 6fe4d74 | results and first figure |
| 95052f5 | F2 follow-up declaration and predictions, approved by the coordinator, before running |
| c3f03cd | F2 results, post-hoc V2 reference, NOTE |
| 897fa97 | the reviewer's wording fixes W1–W3 and C6, with no new runs (c3 REVIEW §2, PR #64) |

**Design.**
- **Bases.** Six frozen `ckpt-10000` runs: per-step readout and tied/final, seeds 51200–51202. SHA-256 is checked against c2 `recovered/RECOVERY.json`, the recipe through `c3train.check_source`, and the parameter hash before and after every fit.
- **Correction.** One correction to h_2, then the unchanged op 3 and readout.
- **Arms.**
  - A: identity.
  - B: a 128→64→128 ReLU map trained toward the centroid.
  - C: the same map, trained to reconstruct h_2. This is not a matched target-complexity control.
  - D: a linear decoder, then the decoded symbol's centroid.
  - E: the true-symbol centroid, an oracle reference that is not a guaranteed upper bound.
- **Evaluations.**
  - Main: seen states with a new op 3, the D2 overlap.
  - Grouped: prefixes split 8/4/4 per symbol with seed 71300. These are adapter-held-out prefixes, not globally unseen states.

**Results.**
- **Checks.** 18/18 reproductions are exact, and base hashes are unchanged.
- **Main.** D recovers the full E − A gain. B recovers 100% in per-step readout and 75–103% in tied/final. C is below A.
- **Grouped eval prefixes.**
  - B is never above A (−50% to 0% of the gain). D is above A in one base only (per-step 51201: 0.625 vs 0.562, 2 of 32 rows).
  - Learned arms drop training-program rows from 1.00 to 0.17–0.64.
  - The decoder reaches 0.53–0.66 (per-step) and 0.22–0.31 (tied/final). E, with the same fit centroids, reaches 0.83–1.00.
  - B is not purely decoder plus centroid. It is above D in 3 of 14 bases, and per the reviewer it answers 13–33% of the rows whose state it decodes to a wrong symbol correctly. It still stays below A.
- **F2** (eight c2 generalization tied/final bases on new task draws; recipe fixed). This replicates tied/final only:
  - main: B recovers 79–100%;
  - grouped: every learned arm is below A in all eight bases, and the decoder reaches 0.19–0.44.
- **Post-hoc reference.** The per-step bases' own V2 reads every prefix's h_2 at 1.00, but V2 was trained on all 128 prefixes.
- **Bound.** The grouped failure bounds this adapter (64 prefixes, 128-d state, unregularized) under this exposure. It does not bound linear availability of the symbol. Reviewer CX-C2 found that a val-tuned ridge decoder recovers at most 6%, which is within this bound.

**Correction to the first version of this description.** It said no learned arm beats A on grouped held rows. D does, in one base, as stated above.

**Compute.** About 0.8 of the 10-minute initial budget, plus 0.3 of the 5-minute follow-up budget.

Not to be merged by this lane.

body:
#### Why I did it

The liquid cooling check in `HardwareChecker` called `set_object_not_ok` for a leaking sensor only when the sensor was not yet in `leaking_sensors`. A sensor that keeps leaking is already in that list on every check after the first, so it was no longer reported Not OK on those checks while its `leak_status` was still `Yes`.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

In the liquid cooling check:

- `set_object_not_ok` is now called on every check in which the leak status is `Yes`. Only the leak event bookkeeping stays behind the `name not in self.leaking_sensors` check, so the "sensor report leaking event" is published once when the leak starts.
- The state is read from the `leaking` field with `leak_status` as the fallback. A value other than `Yes`, `No` or `N/A` is reported Not OK instead of being skipped, which would have let the sensor drop out of the report.

Add tests in `tests/test_system_health.py` for a held leak, recovery and a second leak, a leak that passes through `N/A`, two sensors leaking at once, an unexpected status, and the `leaking` field. Each asserts that a leaking sensor is Not OK on every check and that each event is published exactly once per change.

#### How to verify it

- From `src/system-health`, run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_system_health.py -k liquid_cooling`. The tests are expected to pass.
- On a platform where the liquid cooling check is enabled, hold one sensor at `Yes` for at least three polling intervals. The sensor should be reported Not OK after every interval, and the leaking event should be published only once.
- Set the sensor back to `No`. The sensor should be reported OK again and the recovered event should be published once.

author: vkpdeveloper
body:
## Summary

Starting a pull request watch on an already-green head woke the agent with old check results. A fresh watch now records its first known head, checks, and conflict state as its baseline without reporting them as news. Existing failures and conflicts are intentionally included in that baseline; comments and reviews newer than the watch start still wake the thread.

Issue: `pingdotgg/t3code#22184`

## Root cause

`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Orchestrator.ts:3388` initializes a fresh watch with a null head, empty check lists, and `passed: false`; only a re-armed watch inherits prior state. The evaluator treated the first observed head as a push and compared completed checks against that empty state (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.ts:40`, `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.ts:45`, `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.ts:64`). Any resulting change made the reactor persist a wake message (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/PullRequestWatchReactor.ts:543`).

## Changes

- `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.ts`: suppress initial check/conflict notifications while still recording the snapshot and processing new remarks. Re-armed watches keep their saved baseline. Hosts that omit the head SHA retain existing change detection instead of having every poll suppressed.
- `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.test.ts`: cover initial green, failed, cancelled, action-required, and conflicting states; subsequent failures, recovery, new heads, fresh remarks, and missing head SHAs.
- `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.test.ts`: verify that the baseline persists without messages, survives reactor restart, and still wakes on later check transitions and pushes. Preserve comment delivery through incomplete and paginated reads.
- `apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/pullRequests/tools.ts`: tell agents to handle existing check results before watching.
- `docs/user/source-control.md`: explain the initial baseline and handling of existing failures.

## Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Bug reproduced before the fix | `vp test run apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.test.ts apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.test.ts -t baselines` | 4 failed as expected: existing passed checks, failures, and conflicts were reported as news; the reactor persisted an unwanted checks-passed message. |
| Bug gone after the fix | `vp test run apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.test.ts apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/pullRequestWatch.forgejoComments.test.ts apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.test.ts apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/pullRequests/handlers.test.ts` | 124 passed, 0 failed, including all 4 baseline regressions and later-change delivery. |
| Tests | `vp run check:changed` | 106 passed, 0 failed across the 3 selected test files. |
| Typecheck / lint | `vp run check:changed` | All stages passed: format, lint, knip, generated GraphQL validation, and typechecks for both affected packages. |
| Server bundle | `vp run --filter t3 build:bundle` | Passed. |

Direct Node execution of `evaluatePullRequestWatch` also confirmed the transition sequence, serializing and reloading watch state between calls:

```text
Before fix, initial green snapshot: ["checks-passed"]
After fix, initial green snapshot: [], saved head=0410491, passed=true
Unchanged after saved-state reload: [], saved head=0410491, passed=true
Later failure on same head: ["checks-failed"], saved head=0410491, passed=false
Green checks on a new head: ["checks-passed"], saved head=bbbbbbb, passed=true
```

## Not verified

- Live GitHub polling and desktop/web/mobile UI were not exercised; host responses were supplied by the reactor integration fixture. This change uses the shared server evaluator.
- The repository-wide test suites and full application build are left to CI; targeted tests and the server bundle were run locally.

## Risk

low: check or conflict changes between starting a fresh watch and its first read become part of the baseline. This deliberately uses the first observed snapshot as the boundary; subsequent changes and timestamped new remarks remain actionable.

## Benchmark

- Arm: `claudeism`
- Model: `gpt-6-astra` (reasoning effort xhigh, service tier fast)
- Base: `ed9b7ca9c53843ea1e6b466bf7d52928d10e7db0`

author: isamu
body:
## Summary

psmux keeps spare shells in every server (`warm-pool-size`, default three) plus a hidden `__warm__` standby server. Per psmux's `docs/warm-sessions.md`, a spawn with `-e` skips that pool, and every cell's `new-session` carries `-e` (`tmuxNewSessionArgs`) — so no spare is ever claimed. They only held memory, and the reporter's `PSMUX_WARM_TRACE` shows every client resize restarting them.

- `server/infra/process/psmux.ts`: `psmuxGlobalOptions(version)` returns `warm off` for psmux 3.3.1+ (the release that added the option, psmux#120 — the issue said 3.3.4); nothing for an older or unreadable version, where an unknown option would print a config warning into the first pane.
- `server/infra/process/tmux.ts`:
  - `ensureConf` appends it to the conf on psmux only (real tmux has no `warm` option).
  - `applyLiveTmuxOptions` sends `set-option -t mt-<id> -g warm off` to every running session, asynchronously on every conf write (idempotent, best effort like the other live options), so an unresponsive server cannot hold startup. psmux runs one server per session and routes by `-t`, so a single bare `set -g` would reach only one. Setting it at runtime also kills the `__warm__` server (psmux `src/server/options.rs`). This is the difference from the fork's fix, which only covered new servers.
- Specs: the version gate, the conf content and the live per-session call; `set-option` registered in the `-t` target census.
- README's psmux section lists the new behaviour.

Closes #3166

## Items to Confirm / Review

- **Not run on Windows.** psmux behaviour rests on psmux's source (`-f` → `PSMUX_CONFIG_FILE`, read by `is_warm_disabled_by_config`; `parse_target` strips the `=`) and the reporter's trace of the fork's equivalent conf change. Worth a check on a Windows machine: after restart, no `pwsh` children under `tmux.exe server -s mt-…` and no `__warm__` server.
- `set-option` targets the bare `mt-<id>` through a new psmux-only builder, `tmuxPsmuxSessionTarget`, not `=mt-<id>`: psmux matches exactly anyway, and before 3.3.8 (psmux#558) it did not strip `=`. The census still bans a bare `tmuxSessionName` as a target. (`has-session`/`kill-session` with `=` have the same pre-3.3.8 gap; that is existing behaviour, and MulmoTerminal already asks for psmux 3.4.0+.)

## User Prompt

- issue #3166 を理解し、公式ドキュメントも見たうえで直す。
- PR を作る。

author: schmitch
body:
## Summary
Sets up `main-v26` as the Node.js 26 counterpart of `main`, which stays on Node 24.

- **Node version:** `NODE_VERSION` 24.22.1 → **26.12.1**. This is the latest Node 26 release (2026-10-21, a security release). The docs and the download-script example are updated to match.
- **Package IDs contain the major version:**
  - `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs` → `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26`
  - `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs.Native.<rid>` → `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26.Native.<rid>`

  `buildTransitive/Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs.props` is renamed to `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26.props`, because NuGet only imports `<package id>.props`. It now references the renamed native packages. The assembly and namespace stay `NodeJs.Embedded`, so moving between Node 24 and Node 26 only means changing the package ID.
- **Release tags:** `publish.yml` now runs on pushes to `main-v26` and on `node26-v*` tags. The package version is the tag without the prefix (`node26-v0.6.0` → `0.6.0`), and NuGet publishing runs only on those tags.

## Why main's releases are unaffected
- For a tag push, GitHub Actions runs the workflow file from the tagged commit. A `node26-v*` tag on a `main-v26` commit therefore runs this branch's workflow, and a `v*` tag on a `main` commit runs `main`'s workflow.
- The two tag filters can't overlap. `v*` only matches names that start with `v`, so it never matches `node26-v…`. This branch's `node26-v*` filter never matches a plain `vX.Y.Z` tag.

## Verification
- `./scripts/download-node.sh 26.12.1` stages all six RIDs, and the linux-x64 binary reports `v26.12.1`.
- I ran `dotnet build` + `dotnet pack` with .NET SDK 9.0.319, in the same order as CI, with `/p:Version=0.6.0`. It produces `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26.0.6.0.nupkg` (containing `buildTransitive/Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26.props` and `lib/netstandard2.0/NodeJs.Embedded.dll`) and all six `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26.Native.<rid>.0.6.0.nupkg`.

## Known issue (also on main, not fixed here)
The packed `.props` file sets the native package version to `0.1.0` when the consumer doesn't set `EmbeddedNodeJsNativeVersion`. `/p:EmbeddedNodeJsNativeVersion` has no effect, because the `.props` file is packed as a static file. NuGet then resolves the lowest available native version: for `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs.*` that is 0.3.0 (Node 22.21.1), and on this line it would stay on the first published `Envisia.EmbeddedNodeJs26.Native.*` version. This should be fixed on `main` and then merged into `main-v26`.

author: yousefed
body:
Closes #3079. This is an alternative to #3095.

## Problem

The label of a remote cursor was cut off:

- in a table, because the table's scroll container clips it,
- at the top and at the right edge of the screen.

## Solution

The label is `position: fixed`, so a scroll container does not clip it. CSS anchor positioning attaches the label to its caret, so the label follows the caret when the page scrolls or the text moves. The editor does not need code to position the label.

When the label opens, `showCursorLabel` picks its side:

- above the caret, or below it if there is no space at the top of the screen,
- from the caret to the right, or to the left if there is no space at the right edge.

CSS uses this side (`data-placement`) for the position, for the corner from which the label grows, and for its square corner at the caret. The browser does not flip the label (`position-try-fallbacks`): it keeps a flipped side after the caret moves away from the edge, and CSS cannot tell which side the browser picked.

The closed label is the marker at the top of the caret, as before. It opens and closes with an animation, as before.

Browsers without anchor positioning show the label as before (`@supports`). The table and the edges of the screen can still clip it in these browsers.

## Other changes

- `showCursorLabels: "always"` did not show the labels. Now it shows them.
- A label now opens while the collaborator types. Before, it opened only when the collaborator moved the cursor. Typing does not change a cursor in Yjs, because the position is relative to the text. The plugins now also find the authors of remote edits in the Yjs document.
- The Yjs 14 cursor plugin now removes its listeners when the editor unmounts.

## Compared with #3095

#3095 also uses CSS anchor positioning, but it moves the labels into the portal element. This PR keeps each label in its cursor. Thus, it does not need to sync labels with the awareness state, and it does not change the structure of the two cursor plugins. Also, it does not use `@container anchored`, which only Chromium supports.

## Known limitations

- When a label is open, the editor does not pick its side again after a scroll, a resize, or a change of the layout. The label can go off the screen until the cursor moves or the collaborator types again. This mostly affects `showCursorLabels: "always"`.
- Backspace does not open the label. The cursor position does not change, because it is relative to the next character. Also, Yjs does not record who deleted content. The Delete key opens the label, because it changes the cursor position.

## Tests

- New browser tests for Yjs 13 (`cursorLabel.browser.test.ts`): a label in a table, at the top and at the right edge of the screen, after the cursor moves away from the right edge, while a collaborator types, and with `showCursorLabels: "always"`.
- New browser tests for Yjs 14 (`YCursorPlugin.browser.test.ts`): a label after a cursor move, while a collaborator types, with `showCursorLabels: "always"`, and the removal of the listeners.
- The new tests pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. The tests for the fixed behavior fail on `main`.
- An editor in a shadow root works without other changes.
- Performance in Chromium: each cursor move adds approximately 0.1 ms of layout, and each remote edit adds approximately 0.06 ms of script. Scrolling with 20 open labels needs no layout and no style recalculation.

## What
The required job `v2-bootstrap` (`witnesses.yml`, emitted by `gunbc.witness.compiler_gate_workflow`) now checks out `github.sha` (the pull request MERGE REF) instead of `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`. One row changed (`compiler_gate_checkout_ref`); `witnesses.yml` regenerated by `generated_artifact_gate main_wet` (one-line diff, contract stamp unchanged; extra host-drift files the remote touched were NOT taken).

## Why
main has no merge queue, so a head checkout means nothing ever builds head merged with the base. That is how #14539 and #14675 went green and then broke main. The head pin dated from the merge_group premise, which no longer holds. A merge-ref checkout also pairs the workflow text and the tree by construction (third specimen of `instruction_and_subject_resolved_from_different_revisions`).

## Condition (5): consumers keyed on the head
Read before editing: the emitted workflow and the seed hosts. `census_head_commit` already reads `GITHUB_SHA`; `behavioral_receipt_plan` uses `rev-parse HEAD`, which in a merge-ref checkout IS the merge sha, so receipts name the composed tree (correct). The heal job has its own head checkout and stays on the head (it pushes back); fork PRs get no run.

## Trade-off (stated plainly)
MITIGATABLE, not closed. The merge ref is fixed when the PR event fires; commits landing on main afterwards do not retrigger the run. The window narrows from "never composed" to "event to landing". Row `verdict_stale_at_the_merge_instant` is now read at Mitigatable, ceiling StructurallyGuaranteed, trigger = a composed-tree verdict at/after landing (queue or required up-to-date check).

author: utkarshdalal
body:
## What
A40 runs every child gamescope spawns through `/system/bin/linker64`, because the modern host variant (targetSdk >= 29) may not exec a binary out of its own data directory. The legacy variant may, and does for everything it starts itself; under gamescope it still got the linker route, and wine does not survive that without help: its loader derives the library directory from `/proc/self/exe`, which is then the linker's path, so every gamescope session on a legacy build died at wine startup with

    wine: could not load ntdll.so: dlopen failed: library "/apex/com.android.runtime/bin/../lib/wine/aarch64-unix/ntdll.so" not found

The modern host hides this by redirecting `/proc/self/exe` for wine (`REDIRECT_EXEC__PROC_SELF_EXE`); the legacy host never needed to.

A42: exec the child directly first, exactly as before A40, and go through the linker only when the kernel answers EACCES. The modern variant's behaviour is unchanged; the legacy variant gets its direct exec back. `Process.cpp` is compiled into both `gamescope` and `gamescopereaper`, so both binaries change.

## Verified
- Retroid Pocket 6 (Android 13, Adreno 740), legacy app build: before, Blazing Chrome / Balatro / Celeste containers all died at wine startup as above on Proton 9 and Proton 10 (X11 on the same build was fine). With A42: Blazing Chrome under gamescope runs, override surface bound, game-window reported, splash cleared, game on screen.
- Odin 3 (modern build): sessions still start through the linker (EACCES path), unchanged.

Built with `android/build-gamescope.sh` against the build-20260218 termuxfs; the resulting `gamescope`/`gamescopereaper` have the same NEEDED set as the 20261022 payload binaries. The wlroots W4 patch still starts Xwayland through the linker unconditionally; Xwayland has no exe-path dependency, so it is left as is.

author: idanmuallem
body:
## Summary

Gated pipeline from spec #25: lint, Staging (Dry run, no wallet key) in front of Production, a 24h + Approve gate, and one failure email for any job.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  test["test (pytest + ruff)"] --> build
  changes["changes (runtime files?)"] --> build
  build["build :sha"] --> ds["deploy-staging :8502"]
  ds --> vs["verify-staging (meta-harness, no wipe check, records baseline)"]
  vs --> ap["approve-production (env: production, 24h + Approve, supersedes older pending)"]
  ap --> dp["deploy-production (Staging history check, same :sha, WAL checkpoint)"]
  dp --> mh["meta-harness (unchanged checks)"]
  all["any job fails (push runs)"] -.-> nf["notify-failure email"]
```

```diff
 config/
-├── requirements.txt          # runtime + test
+├── requirements.txt          # runtime only (image)
+├── requirements-dev.txt      # runtime + pytest, ruff, pre-commit (CI)
 ├── ci/
+│   ├── deploy_staging.sh     # fresh db + paper dir, polybot-staging, refuses a key
+│   ├── check_staging_history.sh  # Production gate: count >= baseline, same SHA
+│   └── ensure_ec2_running.sh
+ruff.toml                      # shared by CI and pre-commit
+.pre-commit-config.yaml        # conflict markers, large files, private keys, ruff
+.github/workflows/meta-harness.yml   # reusable, Staging or Production
```

Startup: `DEPLOYMENT_ENV` (unset = production). Dry run starts without a wallet key; Live run still requires it; Staging + Live run raises `StagingLockError`.

Done outside the diff: `main` protected (PR required, `test` check, 0 approvals, admins may bypass); `production` environment (owner reviewer, 1440-min timer, admin bypass).

## Evidence

- **Before:** `validate_runtime_env` requires a wallet key in Dry run.
  **After:** `tests/unit/test_runtime_env.py`, 10 tests: Dry run keyless starts; Live run keyless raises the missing-variables error; Staging + Live run raises the Staging lock; unset marker = Production.
- Local Docker run as Staging (no key, `DEPLOYMENT_ENV=staging`): dashboard 200, engine fresh, readback `deployment_env=staging`, no error lines in logs, history survived `docker restart`, `TRADING_MODE=live_run` raised `StagingLockError`.
- Each pre-commit hook rejected its bad case locally; ruff passes; actionlint passes on both workflows.
- `test_account_budget_tick::test_the_first_tick_of_a_new_utc_day_resets_the_budget` already fails on `main` (date-dependent). Not caused by this branch.
- Real-run gate checks from the spec (docs-only push skips deploy, deliberate failures email, shrunk Staging history blocks Production, second merge supersedes, 24h + Approve) still to do after merge.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert the merge to restore the old workflow. Staging's container and files on the instance stay until removed by hand.

**Blast Radius:** Production

Before merging: add the `GMAIL_USERNAME` / `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` repo secrets (none exist, so no email has ever sent), open 8502 to your IP, and create `/home/ec2-user/.env.staging` without a wallet key. Otherwise `deploy-staging` fails and Production never deploys.

## 변경 내용
API 한도 2단계: cap-ok(하루 Claude 실행 상한 확인)를 1회 약 158건에서 3건으로 줄인다.

**원인**
- 기존 cap-ok는 8개 워크플로 × 2레포 = 16번 run 목록을 읽고, **오늘 실행된 run마다 jobs를 한 번씩** 더 읽었다.
- 측정 시점의 오늘 run 수가 142라서 1회 약 158건이고, 하루가 지날수록 늘어난다.
- 이 확인이 **리뷰어 잡마다, 작성 prep마다** 돌아서 시간당 약 9,000건이 됐다. GITHUB_TOKEN 한도는 레포당 시간당 1,000건이다.

**방법**
1. Claude 잡이 있는 워크플로가 `run-name`(= run 목록의 `display_title`)에 부서를 남긴다.

   | 워크플로 | run 제목 | 세는 법 |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | `_claude-write` (수동 실행) | `claude:<부서>:<모드> #<이슈>` | 그 부서 토큰 주인 1 |
   | `claude-request` | `claude-request to:<부서> by <라벨 붙인 사람>` | 그 부서 토큰 주인 1 (봇이 붙인 라벨은 route가 실행 안 하므로 0) |
   | `claude-review` | `claude-review <PR 브랜치> by <PR 작성자>` | 브랜치 부서와 작성자로 `reviewers_for` 계산 → 리뷰 부서마다 토큰 주인 1 |

2. cap-ok는 이 3개 워크플로의 **오늘 run 목록만** 읽는다(파일당 1페이지, 하루 100개를 넘으면 다음 페이지). jobs는 읽지 않는다.
3. claude-review는 **prep에서 한 번만** 계산하고 `cap_ok`·`cap_reason`을 matrix로 넘긴다. 리뷰어 잡에서는 다시 조회하지 않는다.
4. **fail-closed 유지**
   - run 목록 조회가 실패하면 모두 ok=false다.
   - 작성 prep은 "cap을 확인하지 못해 실행하지 않음"으로 멈춘다.
   - 리뷰어 잡은 Claude를 돌리지 않고 `agent-review/<부서>`를 `quota — <이유>`(error)로 남긴다.

**알려진 한계**
- 수동 실행 리뷰(`dispatch #N`)는 제목에 브랜치가 없어 세지 않는다. 수동 실행이라 드물다.
- 사람 PR이 부서 여러 개를 바꾼 경우 브랜치 부서 하나 기준으로 센다.
- 이 PR이 머지되기 전의 run은 제목 형식이 달라서, **오늘만** 앞선 사용량이 빠진다.

## 측정 (시간당 GITHUB_TOKEN 추정, 전 → 후)
기준: 최근 1시간 실행 수(작성 11, 리뷰 run 24, 리뷰어 잡 46). 오늘 Claude run 142.

| 항목 | 1회당 (전 → 후) | 시간당 (전 → 후) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cap: 작성 prep (×11) | ~158 → **3** | ~1,740 → 33 |
| cap: 리뷰어 잡 (×46) | ~158 → **0** (prep 값 사용) | ~7,270 → 0 |
| cap: 리뷰 prep (×24) | 0 → **3** | 0 → 72 |
| 그 외 GITHUB_TOKEN (guards·리뷰 prep·route·team-guard·작성 prep 기본·action 내부) | 변화 없음 | ~245 → ~245 |
| **합계** | | **~9,250 → ~350** |

→ 한도(1,000/시간) 안으로 들어온다. 1단계(#107, PR 정보를 페이로드로) 효과까지 합친 값이다.

author: helebest
body:
Fixes #573.

## What changes

This PR changes only documentation. It records a decision taken on 2026-10-22: the 64-byte ceiling on a composed MCP tool name stays.

- A tool whose `mcp__{server}__{tool}` name is longer than 64 bytes is not offered to the model, and the brain logs it (`internal/brain/mcptools.go` `mcpNameFits`, `maxModelToolName`). This is unchanged.
- The reference was recorded with no such ceiling. Composed names of 69, 75 and 76 characters were offered and echoed back intact (managed-agents-wire-recordings 2026-09-03 batch2, `session.events.list.long`).
- So a session here can lack tools that the same agent has on the reference. The registry now argues that as a deliberate divergence, instead of listing it as an open question.

```
the two names share 57 bytes:   mcp__ (5) + server + __ (2) + tool  <= 64
a 50-byte server, 5-byte tool   -> 62 bytes, offered
a  5-byte server, 50-byte tool  -> 62 bytes, offered
any server,  57-byte tool       -> at least 65 bytes, never offered
```

**docs/DIVERGENCES.md:**
- **A new CONFIRMED entry**, *An MCP tool's model-facing name — one longer than 64 bytes is not offered (decided 2026-10-22, #573)*. The file's rule is that a recorded difference kept by choice "moves up to the divergences". The entry argues the choice. The alternative was a shortened name, declined for three reasons:
  1. No recording shows the reference using one.
  2. Its rule would become a permanent contract. The model sees the name, a cut-off call's `agent.tool_use` and a denial's text carry it, and replay derives it again on every turn. A later change to the rule would rename a tool in the middle of a session.
  3. The case is narrow.
- **The INFERRED entry** *Offering an MCP tool to the model*: "The ceiling is #573." becomes a pointer to the new entry. `*Tracked:*` drops #573 and keeps #78, which still asks what the reference does with a name it cannot offer.

**changelog.d/573-mcp-prefix.fixed.md** (unreleased, from #968): its last sentence said "#573 stays open for it". It now says the ceiling stays by decision.

**STATE.md:** Active work is now just "**None.**". The narrative of the 2026-10-17 triage queue and its backlog pointer are gone, since STATE.md holds only work in flight.

There is no new changelog fragment, because no behavior changes.

## #573's scope, item by item

1. The `mcp__` prefix reservation on custom tool names: merged in #968 (844e725).
2. The "the name it shows the model is bare" sentence: removed from `mcptools.go` in #805 (0aa1dbc).
3. The cap decision: this PR.
4. A test of the compose/decompose round trip, already on main:
   - the outbound composed name, and the inbound `agent.mcp_tool_use` with the bare `name` and `mcp_server_name`: `internal/brain/mcpturn_test.go` `TestAListedMCPToolIsOfferedAndGated`;
   - replay reassembling the composed name: `internal/brain/replay_test.go` `TestBuildRequestReplaysTheLog`.

## Verification

**The model was substituted.** The verifier ran on claude-opus-5-5 (from its transcript). Its frontmatter pins claude-fable-5-1, and the session set no override.

**First run, at a3ebd74: FAIL.** The blocker was the stale fragment above, which would have gone into the release notes word for word. Two notes:
- The decision's citation pointed at an issue thread that does not record it. A comment on #573 now records it.
- "a shortened name the reference never shows" reached past the recording.

**Second run, at 2cebfd2: PASS WITH FINDINGS.**
- `tools/registrycheck` passes, and so does `go run ./tools/registrycheck -issues`. In a scratch copy, with #573 forced closed, the registry stays clean, with 30 issues referenced.
- The `tools/sdkref` corpus tests pass. Three fixture tests fail on this host only, because the module-cache path has a space.
- The tests the new entry cites, and those its reasons rest on, pass: `TestAComposedMCPNameMatchesTheDocumentedRule`, `TestAnOverlongMCPToolNameCostsOnlyItsOwnTool`, `TestACutMCPCallIsAnsweredUnderItsPrefixedName`, `TestBuildRequestReplaysTheLog` and `TestDenial*`.
- Each claim checks against the code: the 5 + 2 + 57 arithmetic, the drop and its log line, and the denial, cut-off and replay paths. The recordings hold six distinct composed names, none shortened.
- The "above" and "below" pointers between the two entries resolve.
- The verifier did not run the full `make verify`, since the change is markdown only. CI runs it.

Its one note, **fixed in 3b03666**, a text-only commit: "a short server name does not save a long tool name" was too strong, since the two names share the bound. The entry now says that a tool name longer than 56 bytes is never offered, whatever its server is called.

## Review

This diff is documentation markdown only, so the repo's tiering allows a single reviewer.

**Claude** (`/code-review`, xhigh, which inherits the session model, claude-opus-5-5) reviewed a3ebd74 and found 11 items. Every one is fixed in 2cebfd2 except the last two:
1. The stale fragment.
2. The "never shows" overclaim.
3. A deliberate divergence filed under INFERRED. Fixed by the new CONFIRMED entry.
4. The scope was understated: a long tool name under a short server is dropped too.
5. The decision was not argued.
6. Nothing closed #573. This body carries "Fixes #573".
7. The issue thread did not record the decision. Now commented on #573.
8. STATE.md's "one PR each" was false for #573.
9. STATE.md carried backlog under "None".
10. **Not changed:** a pointer comment beside `maxModelToolName` in `mcptools.go`. The registry entry already cites the code. A Go comment would take this PR out of the docs-only tier for a pointer the registry carries.
11. **Partly changed:** a long sentence. The new entry is written in short sentences, and the sentence it replaced is gone.

author: apontzen
body:
tangos keeps its tutorial and CI data in its own R2 bucket and wants the same `index.html` listing as pynbody's. Rather than tangos carrying a copy of the script, this makes pynbody's `bucket-index` workflow callable from other repositories in the organisation.

- **`.github/workflows/bucket-index.yaml`** gains a `workflow_call` trigger with `title`, `description` (HTML) and `pynbody-ref` inputs, plus the four R2 secrets. A caller passes its own secrets with `secrets: inherit`. A called workflow's checkout would otherwise fetch the caller's repository, so the job checks out `pynbody/pynbody` explicitly: at `pynbody-ref` (default `master`) when called, or at the triggering commit when run here. The concurrency group is now per repository, so pynbody's and tangos' runs don't queue behind each other. Edits to the workflow file itself now also trigger a run.
- **`pynbody/test_utils/make_bucket_index.py`** gains `--title` and `--description`. They default to the existing pynbody text, and I checked that the default page is byte-identical to before (apart from its timestamp).

The caller is pynbody/tangos#307.

Tested:
- pynbody's own run on this branch ([run 39740216763](https://github.com/pynbody/pynbody/actions/runs/39740216763)) regenerated the pynbody page.
- tangos calling this branch ([run 39740246082](https://github.com/pynbody/tangos/actions/runs/39740246082)) listed the 17 objects in the tangos bucket and uploaded its page, using tangos' own secrets.

Once this merges, the tangos caller switches from this branch to `@master`.

body:
Part of #1933 (VQ5-PERSONA, after VQ5-CAPTURE-GENERIC, PR 1941).

PR 1941 asked whether capture should stop setting the console fixture's `swarm_qa_persona` cookie (`PERSONA_COOKIE`) when it captures someone else's app. BGD answered on 2026-10-22 at 07:07Z:

> "Skip it when no route names a persona and --settle generic"

## What now holds

`images/agent-runtime-browser/swarm_qa.py`:
* New `sets_persona(routes, settle)`. It is True under the console's settle. Under `--settle generic` it is True only when some route in the route list (any group) names a `persona`. `capture()` works it out once and passes it to `_capture_route` as `persona_cookie`.
* When `persona_cookie` is False, `_capture_route` makes no `add_cookies` call, and the route's manifest entry records `"persona": null` instead of `member`, because no cookie carried an identity. **This manifest change goes slightly beyond the brief.** Nothing in the repository reads `entry["persona"]` except these tests.
* Every console capture is unchanged: the cookie is set on every route, `member` included. A generic route list that names a persona keeps today's behaviour, and `load_routes` still refuses an unknown persona against `PERSONAS`.

`docs/design/visual-qa-any-app.md` §4.2: one new row in the list of console-specific parts.

* `test_a_generic_capture_with_no_persona_route_sets_no_persona_cookie`: failed before the fix (the cookie was set as `member` on both routes) and passes after it.
* `test_a_console_capture_still_sets_the_persona_cookie_on_every_route` and `test_a_generic_capture_whose_route_names_a_persona_keeps_the_cookie`: guards on today's behaviour. First partial PR toward #7: add a persisted automatic-suggestions toggle and reorganize settings using native Obsidian controls. This intentionally leaves #7 open for subsequent daily-use polish.

- Signed-out status-bar clicks still sign in; signed-in clicks toggle automatic suggestions, showing off or the current Copilot health status (normal when ready).

author: mouse-blink
body:
## Summary
The mutation workflow pulled `ghcr.io/gooze-dev/goozels/gooze-reports:main` for the cache, but nothing ever pushed it, so every PR re-tested every file.

- **Triggers:** pull requests, plus `push` to `main` and `workflow_dispatch`. A manual run on `main` can seed the baseline once.
- **Publishing:** the merge job runs `gooze report push "$REPORTS_REF"` after `gooze report merge`, only for a run on `main` that isn't a pull request. Shards never push; they hand reports to the merge job as artifacts, as before.
- **Permissions:** the workflow stays `packages: read`. Only the merge job gets `packages: write`, and fork PRs get a read-only token anyway.
- **Pins:** `checkout`, `upload-artifact` and `download-artifact` are pinned to the same commits as #11.

This follows the shared-baseline pattern in the gooze docs (https://gooze.dev/docs/ci/github/). `gooze report push` is in the released v1.2.0, which the workflow installs.

body:
## The Maker's guest strip draws the chosen designs

**Owner, 22 Oct (live Maker › Mood Board & Dress Code › Guests):** ticked Suit and tie → 4 designs; the Wear ▾ said "Suit and tie · 4 designs", but the figure strip drew the Classic two-button suit four times, once per colour — *"they did not show still just 1 design showed"*. Same across styles ("Suit and tie +2 · 5 designs" → four Classic suits), and four of one long dress for the women.

**Cause:** the strip drew every colour option in the column's hero drawing (`heroArt`, the first allowed design). The allowed designs only reached the Wear ▾ and the line under it.

**Fix:** the strip wears the colours in turn along every allowed design, across styles in tick order (`stripLooks`, `lib/attire-design-picks.ts`). Design 1 gets colour 1, design 2 gets colour 2, and so on. With more colours than designs, the designs repeat; with more designs than colours, the colours repeat. Each figure uses its own design's drawing, tinted by its own zones (suit: the colour on the tie, over black · barong: its body, pants charcoal · smart casual: its top, chinos khaki · women: the whole dress). It is labelled with the design name and what its colour colours, and its dot edits the colour it wears. Men and women both.

**Unchanged:** a column with one design (every dress code before 21 Oct) keeps the shipped strip byte for byte. The guest page's "Dress with us" board already drew the chosen designs (#6749): re-walked, not changed.

**Guard:** `lib/guests-pick-styles-and-designs.test.ts` § 8 renders the real `MoodBoardStudio` and checks, per column:
- the owner's four suits give 4 distinct designs, each in colour 1–4, colour on the tie, coat black;
- the owner's mixed five (3 suits + Jusi barong + Blazer over tee) with 4 colours: the 5 designs in tick order, the colours repeating, the barong's body and the smart-casual top tinted, no tie on the barong, each named;
- women: every allowed dress, all distinct;
- 2 designs × 4 colours: the designs repeat and every colour is worn;
- a 40-seed fuzz;
- a legacy single `style` gets one figure per colour, all in the shipped design, with no new attributes.

Adds one point to the Guide chapter "Which AI model? Settings that matter", the README and the user guide: keep the Context Size at or a little below the model's limit at the provider.

Esolite trims the prompt to Context Size minus Max Output, but it only estimates the prompt's length (characters per token, `klite.embd`). author: jchumtong
body:
## What

- Moves the next-page query forwarding (`parse_qsl(next_page_token.query)`) from `SurveyResponsesStream` into the `SurvicateStream` base class, so `SurveysStream` paginates too.
- `SurveyResponsesStream` still sends `attributes[]` on the first page and defers to the base class after that.

## Why

`SurveysStream` used the SDK's default `get_url_params`, which ignores the page token. Its page-2 request went to `/surveys` with no `start` cursor, got page 1 back, and `SurvivatePaginator`'s loop guard ended the stream without an error. So only the 20 newest surveys ever synced.

On 2026-09-14 two new surveys ("Listing Published - Apps/Web") were created, which pushed "CSAT - Delighted" (`472f11b83a067afc`) onto page 2. CSAT responses have not loaded into the warehouse since. "NPS - Delighted" is now the 20th survey on page 1, so the next new survey would drop it as well.

## Test plan

- [x] Live API, surveys stream: `main` returns 40 records (page 1 twice, 20 unique, no CSAT); this branch returns all 21 surveys, CSAT included.
- [x] Live API, CSAT responses: 3,576 responses, all unique; 3,574 carry `CaseId` (attributes are still forwarded on later pages), and 563 were collected since 2026-09-14.
- [x] `ruff check`: no new findings (D102, S105 and TC002 are already on `main`, and this branch fixes `main`'s TC003); `mypy` clean.

author: ti-chi-bot
body:
This is an automated cherry-pick of #72141

<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #69534

Problem Summary: `DROP DATABASE` on a schema with tens or hundreds of thousands of tables repeatedly materialized every `TableInfo` in DDL state transitions and InfoSchema v2 handling. The resulting memory spike could OOM TiDB before the DDL step committed, leaving the job stuck in `queueing` and repeatedly retried by new DDL owners.

### What changed and how does it work?

The drop-schema state transitions now use `metaMut.IterTables` so only one full `TableInfo` is decoded at a time. The public-to-write-only transition collects only TTL and label-rule information. The delete-only transition collects compact notifier metadata, affinity group IDs, materialized-view and materialized-view-log IDs, and the physical table IDs required for cleanup and GC.

The notifier accepts pre-extracted mini table metadata, while TTL and affinity cleanup consume compact summaries instead of retaining complete table metadata. The streaming path and existing `getIDs` path share the same table-plus-partition ID semantics through `getPartitionIDs`. Notifier chunking and the persisted event format remain unchanged.

InfoSchema v2 now streams table metadata when applying a dropped schema and collects only physical table IDs instead of first building a `TableInfo` slice. Schema table iteration is context-cancelable, and errors from the v2 drop-schema path propagate through `ApplyDiff`. Table metadata reads share a cancellable helper that retries temporary flashback-in-progress errors with a fresh read and context-aware backoff.

Peak memory is substantially lower, although the DDL job still retains the physical IDs required for deletion-range GC.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)

On a 3c 4812Mi pod, the PR build drops 400,000 tables and stays near 2 GiB. Auto analyze also uses `ListTables`, so it was disabled for the benchmark to ensure the test ran. Master is OOM-killed during `DROP DATABASE`.

|                 |                 PR                  |                     Master                     |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Base            | PR 72141                            | master `13544e9b14`                            |
| Tables          | 400,000                             | 400,000                                        |
| Peak RSS        | 1.92 GiB (1969Mi)                   | 4.69 GiB (4801Mi) (from sample)                             |
| `oom_kill`      | 0                                   | 1                                              |
| Drop result     | `synced`                            | process OOM killed                             |
| TiDB after drop | same process still running          | `tidb-server` gone; client lost the connection |

The table shape used by the benchmark is:

```sql
CREATE TABLE user_account (
  id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  user_id BIGINT,
  org_id INT,
  status TINYINT,
  name VARCHAR(64),
  email VARCHAR(128),
  created_at DATETIME,
  amount DECIMAL(18,2),
  score DOUBLE,
  note VARCHAR(255),
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  KEY idx_user_id (user_id),
  KEY idx_org_status (org_id, status),
  KEY idx_email (email),
  KEY idx_created_at (created_at),
  UNIQUE KEY idx_name (name)
);
```

New unit coverage includes physical table ID collection, drop-schema mini metadata, InfoSchema table iteration and cancellation, drop-schema ID collection, and flashback retry behavior.

  > <!-- Or your custom  "No need to test" reasons -->

```text
make bazel_prepare

./tools/check/failpoint-go-test.sh pkg/ddl -run '^TestSchema$' -count=1

```

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory

Documentation

- [ ] Contains syntax changes
