author: amiriqbalmcs
body:
## Fix: Connection wizard sends ChatGPT users to a menu that no longer exists

### Problem

Codex became part of the ChatGPT desktop app on July 9, 2026. Its MCP settings moved from **File → Settings → Plugins → MCPs** to **Settings → MCP servers**, and the app now needs a **Restart** after a server is saved before **Authenticate** appears.

The Connection wizard (ChatGPT App) still told users to open the old Plugins menu and the "Connect to a custom MCP" form, so they could not find where to add the server.

### Fix

`includes/admin/trait-admin-connection.php`, text only:

- **OAuth steps:** Settings → MCP servers → Add server, choose Streamable HTTP, enter the name and URL, then Save, Restart, Authenticate and Approve.
- **Application password guide:** same path, and "Save and Restart" after filling in the form.
- The code comment describing the flow is updated as well.

No behaviour changes. The OAuth flow itself is unchanged.

### Sources

- [ChatGPT & Codex changelog](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog): "Codex joins the ChatGPT desktop app" (2026-07-09), plugin management moved into Settings
- [Model Context Protocol, ChatGPT app](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=app): "Open Settings, then select MCP servers. Select Add server. ... Save the server, then select Restart." and "select Authenticate"

### Not changed, worth checking

The Application password method also shows the command `codex mcp add %NAME% --transport http --url ... --header "Authorization=Basic ..."`. OpenAI's current CLI docs list only `--url`, `--env`, `--oauth-client-id` and `--oauth-client-secret` for `codex mcp add`, and say headers belong in `config.toml` (`http_headers`). I could not verify this without the Codex CLI, so it is left as is. Someone with the CLI should check it.

### Testing

PHP lint. The change is limited to translatable strings and one comment.

author: mcanouil
body:
With `facet-wrap()` or `facet-grid()` and free x or y scales, a discrete axis moved by `position-beeswarm()`, `position-jitter()`, or `position-nudge()` came out as a continuous axis in each panel.
You got ticks at 0.8, 1, 1.2 where the level names should be.

These positions move points on a synthetic numeric column, and only the mapping ref marked that column as discrete.
The renderer strips the refs from panel layers before it trains the scales for each panel again, so that training read the numbers and picked continuous.
Now `_scale-type-from-cache` treats a column with recorded levels as discrete.
Only that rewrite records levels, so the result no longer depends on whether the ref is still there.

There is a unit test on `train()` with a stripped mapping, and an eyeball plot in `tests/visual/facet-free-offset-discrete.typ` that covers beeswarm, jitter, and nudge under `facet-wrap`, plus beeswarm under `facet-grid`.

![Five faceted point plots. Each panel shows a discrete x axis with only its own level names: a in panel p, b and c in panel q.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/512275b0-974c-4bad-ac30-d837bc41a79c)

Option 2 of #1511: a one-command helper, no bot. A pull request opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger CI, and the repository has no credential that can push branches and open PRs here, so this keeps a person in the loop and needs no new secret.

`tools/bump-docs.sh [--sha X] [--issue N] [--skip-checks] [--no-pr] [--dry-run]`: resolves metel-docs `main` (no submodule checkout needed), stops if the pin already points there, branches `chore/bump-docs-<sha>` from `origin/develop`, moves the gitlink with `git update-index --cacheinfo` (never `git commit -- docs`), runs `rfc.py check` and the architecture check on the new commit, pushes, and opens the PR with the docs commits listed. It never merges.

- `tools/test_bump_docs.sh`: real git repositories in a temp directory (no network, no gh): usage error, dry run changes nothing, a real run (branch, gitlink moved, title, pushed, only `docs` changed), an existing branch refused, a dirty tree refused, up-to-date reported. Runs in a new CI job `tools self-tests`.
- `AGENTS.md` and `PROCESSES.md` describe the flow and list both tools (the inventory check passes).

Closes #1511.

author: mehdidotesk73
body:
## What
Replaces the days / weeks / months `<select>` dropdowns in the Price Explorer metric configs (Moving average, Bollinger bands, Bollinger score) with an iOS-style vertical **wheel picker**.

- New `src/components/WheelPicker.vue`: a generic `v-model` component.
  - Native scrolling + CSS `scroll-snap` gives momentum and snapping. The row in the centre is committed once scrolling settles.
  - **Closed:** one row tall. Its height is stretched to the number input beside it and measured with `ResizeObserver`.
  - **Held or scrolling:** bulges 12px each way as an overlay, so the layout doesn't move. Only a `clip-path` animates, which keeps the scroll geometry fixed mid-gesture.
  - Neighbouring rows tilt, narrow and fade (a per-row `perspective()` + `rotateX`). There are no selection lines.
  - Scrolling is y-only (`overflow-x: hidden`, `touch-action: pan-y`).
  - `click.prevent` stops the surrounding `<label>` from focusing the number input, which would pop the keyboard on mobile.
- `UNIT_OPTIONS` is added to `src/lib/period.ts`.
- Docs: a version-history entry in `experience.md`; the `WheelPicker` component and `UNIT_OPTIONS` in `system-design.md`; a Done entry in `TODO.md`.

No new dependencies.

## Why
Dropdowns are clunky on a phone. A wheel is quicker to flick and fits the mobile-first UI.

## Testing
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run test:run` and `npm run build` pass locally, and CI `build` is green.
- Headless Chromium at phone size: closed height matches the input (28.2px), it opens on hold or scroll and closes after it settles, there's no horizontal scroll, and tapping a row selects it.
- Tuned on iPhone via the Deploy Preview over several rounds of feedback.

author: sjoon21
body:
## 요약
변환이 끝난 녹음 노트에서 AI가 잘못 들은 말이 있는 문장(타임스탬프 단위)의 고친 문장을 **제안**하고, 사용자가 줄마다 수락·거절합니다. 설계·측정: `docs/design/transcript-polish.md`.

## 화면 (소유자와 정한 것)
- 이름은 **스마트 교정**(영어 Smart fix, `스마트 검색`과 짝). 코드·CLI는 `polish`. 대화 내용 툴바에 있습니다(양옆 패널이 아님). 요약 탭에서 고른 AI 서비스를 씁니다.
- 도는 동안 대화 내용 영역 가장자리에 빛 한 줄기가 돌고(폭 1180px 이상), AI가 아직 보지 않은 줄이 위에서부터 물결처럼 빛나고, 구간(5천 자)이 끝날 때마다 그 구간의 빛이 꺼지며 제안이 나타납니다.
- 제안은 그 줄 바로 아래에 낱말 diff(지운 말 줄 긋기 → 새 말)와 `수락`·`거절`.
- 막대: `교정 제안 {n}개 · 확인할 것 {m}개`, `모두 수락`(숫자 확인·다시 쓴 문장 표시가 있는 것은 빼고) · `모두 거절`.
- 받은 줄은 `스마트 교정됨`(파랑, 사람이 고친 `수정됨`과 구분). 원문은 남고 ⌘Z로 되돌립니다. 하나만 받으면 자주 쓰는 단어를 제안합니다.

## 코어
- `polish.suggest`: 고칠 범위 5천 자 + 앞뒤 30문장 문맥, 4개 동시. 정답 후보는 회의록과 같은 블록(자주 쓰는 단어·확인한 참석자·메모). 사용자가 고친 줄은 고치지 않습니다.
- 버림: 문장부호·띄어쓰기만 다름, 크게 짧아짐, 문장 경계 옮기기(앞뒤 문장의 말을 끌어오거나 넘김). 표시: `number`(짐작한 숫자), `rewrite`(여러 낱말 다시 쓰기).
- `tractus polish <노트> run|show|accept|reject`, `<노트>/polish.json`, 받기는 `apply_text_edits`의 `by: "ai"` → 선택 키 `corrected_by: "ai"`(사람이 다시 고치면 지움).
- Rust `polish_start`(요약과 같은 키·busy 처리, 이벤트 `kind: "polish"`), `polish_resolve`. `load_meeting`이 `polish`와 `corrected_by`를 싣습니다.

## 측정 (gemini-3.8-flash-high, 앱 기본 경로)
| | 결과 |

author: masked-kunsiquat
body:
Closes #232. Part 3 of #220, completing ROADMAP Task 10. No schema change.

## What it does
- **Your ratings** on each Stats tab (Books, Films, Shows): the average, the top five, and a half-star spread chart that opens larger. Each title counts once, at its score for the period.
- **Only the period's own ratings count.** A rating takes the date of what it is on:
  - a read: its finish, else its last session (a Did-not-finish read has no finish), else its start;
  - a film viewing: the day it was watched;
  - a watch-through: its latest episode viewing.
  Undated ones count under All time only.
- **Ties** go to the most recent, then A to Z.
- **A top row prints the exact score** ("4.3") only when its stars can't show it.
- **Year in review** ends with **Your favourites of <year>**: the top-rated book, film and show of that year, by that year's ratings only.

## How it's built
- **Data:** one DAO query, `StatsDao.observeRatedItems`. The type is a filter on it (one engine, #126).
- **Rules:** all of them live in pure `ratingStats()` / `favourites()` in `features/stats/data/RatingStats.kt`.
- **Screens:** one shared `RatingsCard`; a new `YearPage.FAVOURITES`.

## Checks
- **Full gate green:** `:shared:jvmTest :shared:testDebugUnitTest :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:verifyRoborazziDebug ktlintCheck :app:lintDebug` + `:app:assembleDebug`, 2,920 tests.
- **Device:** `connectedDebugAndroidTest` 47/47 on SM-G975U1, on the final head.
- **Hand check on seeded data:** I rated Arrival's Nov 2025 viewing 5★ and its May 2026 viewing 3★.
  - Films → Year: "Average 3.0 · 1 film rated".
  - All time: "Average 4.0", Mostly 4★; the spread dialog opens.
  - Year in review 2026 ends with Favourites: Film, Arrival, 3★.
- **Sabotage, each guard seen failing:**
  - the DNF session fallback;
  - the year bounds on favourites (this test was strengthened when the plan's version survived the sabotage);
  - the exact-score rule;
  - the long-title weight;
  - the favourites page in the page list;
  - the Books wiring.
- **New goldens**, looked at: `stats-films-ratings.png` and `year-review-favourites.png`. No existing golden changed.
- **Review:** a fresh whole-branch review found 0 Critical and 2 Important. Both are fixed test-first in 587d6c0:
  - the favourites page crushed its last title on a small phone at the largest font, so titles are now capped at two lines;
  - the Books-tab wiring had no test that could fail.

## Decisions for the owner
- **Card position:** the card is last on every tab, including Books (after Formats).
- **Spread caption:** "Mostly 4.5★", using the app's existing number style.
- **Quiet years:** a quiet year (nothing logged) shows no favourites page, per the spec. A read rated with only a start date, in an otherwise empty year, is therefore not shown there.
- **Session dating:** a rating dated by a session uses the session's *end*, while the rest of Stats buckets sessions by their *start*. A session across midnight on the 31st can put the session in one month and its rating in the next.

## Deferred minors
- **Star alignment:** a row that prints "4.3" sits its stars slightly left of the other rows' stars.
- **TalkBack wording:**
  - the card's stars read "Your rating, X of 5", though they are a score or an average;
  - each row's parts are separate stops;
  - the ★ glyph is read as "black star".
- **Threading:** on Films/Shows, `ratingStats` isn't moved to `Dispatchers.Default` like its sibling computation. The cost is negligible.

author: mmornati
body:
## Summary

Implements [docs/phase-1/step-4-guard-detection.md](docs/phase-1/step-4-guard-detection.md). The guard watches the default branch, finds the PR that turned a check red from CI results that already exist, and opens nothing, in every mode.

- **History:** a `push` to the default branch triggers an API walk of first parents into `main_commits` (`seq`, chain breaks). Each commit is mapped to its merged PR through `changes`, or through `commits/{sha}/pulls` for rebase merges.
- **CI results** go into `ci_results`: check runs from every app and commit statuses, stored as `green` / `red` / `ignored` with name and source only. `cancelled` is ignored.
- **Detection** (pure `src/guard/detect.ts`): `culprit_found` / `ambiguous` / `no_culprit`, with confirmation (the next commit is red, or the check is still red after 2 h; otherwise `flaky`). A per-repository advisory lock prevents duplicate events.
- **Report:** for `culprit_found` only, one marker-deduplicated comment on the culprit PR, through an existing Phase 0 route. No `guard` feature client and no Phase 1 route. `graft guard list` lists the events.
- **Permissions:** `statuses: read` plus the `check_suite` and `status` events, in both manifests. No `actions: read`.
- Migration **0011_guard**, plus `guard.checks` in `graft.yaml`, `mode show` notes and two `pilot doctor` warnings.

## Testing (developer agent)

- lint, typecheck and build pass. `pnpm test` passes **1068** tests in 96 files. `eval:ci` passes with the baseline unchanged.
- migrate → rollback → migrate: only 0011 rolls back.
- All 11 spec mutation checks are caught, plus 2 extra variants. U-DET-14's generator was fixed so that it catches "two PRs blamed on the last one". "No advisory lock" fails I-GRD-10 in 3 runs out of 3.

## Deviations (recorded in `docs/decisions.md`)

- **D17 (from a security review during the build):** `guard.checks` is read from the **last green commit**, not the failing one, so a candidate cannot filter out its own failure. A missing or invalid file there means every check counts. Covered by **I-GRD-12b**.
- **T1(a):** per GitHub's docs, an App with `checks` permission receives other apps' `check_run` / `check_suite` `completed` events, so the +5/+30 min re-check fallback is not built. This is not verified on real GitHub yet (HUMAN-TODO).
- **D12:** the observe key window equals the observe delay, so the 7-day completed-job deduplication cannot swallow a later trigger.
- Simplest options where the spec was silent: detection follows parent links, an open event moves to an earlier commit when its red result arrives later (I-GRD-10b), more than 50 candidates count as ambiguous, and the neutral suite uses an observe delay of 0.

## Merge order

**Merge after mmornati/graft#25 (step 3, migration 0010).** Then rebase this PR and check:
- the migration order, and the step-down tests (I-DB-2, I-MODE-1, I-ENF-1, the pilot-ops "one migration behind" test, I-GRD-1);
- conflicts in the shared files: schema, migrations index, registry, crons, purge, doctor (15 checks), the graft-ops groups and `decisions.md`.

## For a human (HUMAN-TODO)

- Accept `statuses: read` and the new events on every installation.
- Check T1(a) and the whole flow on a sandbox repository.
- Run the manual smoke test.
- Brief the pilot teams.

body:
Implements the repository tasks of `platform-broker` (1.1–4.4). The MQTT broker, the shared Docker network and the host's nginx configuration move from `legacy/` into `leoiot-platform/`, and the broker gains the browser endpoint that `platform/data-contract` requires: MQTT over WebSocket at `/mqtt`, anonymous and read-only on `leoiot/room-climate/#`.

**Nothing on vm23 changes until the manual cutover (tasks 5.1–5.4, design D8).** Do not promote this to `release` before the cutover has been done.

## What changes

- **`leoiot-platform/compose.yaml`:** new deploy unit, deployed before `legacy` and the other units. It runs `mosquitto` (`eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.22`) and creates the network `2526-4ahitm-leoiot-dashboard_leoiot` under its existing name, so `leoiot-pv` changes nothing.
- **`leoiot-platform/broker/`:**
  - `mosquitto.conf`: per-listener settings. Port 1883 needs an account (`pwfile`, `acl`). Port 9001 (WebSocket, bound to `127.0.0.1` only) is anonymous and limited by `acl-websocket`. Persistence is on.
  - `acl-websocket`: in Git, no account names.
  - `acl.example`: shows the shape of the host-local `acl`.
  - `pwfile` and `acl` are ignored by Git.
- **`legacy/`, removals only:** the `mosquitto` service, the `depends_on: mosquitto` entries, the `mosquitto_data` volume declaration, and `config/`. The network is now declared external.
- **Proxy config:** `legacy/deploy/nginx.conf` moves to `leoiot-platform/proxy/nginx.conf` with its history (unchanged move in its own commit), then gains `location = /mqtt` with a per-client connection limit.
- **`.github/ci/`:** the `legacy/config/ → mosquitto` line is gone from `legacy-services.map`, and `affected.test.sh` expects `leoiot-platform` as the first unit. This is an exception to "`.github/` in its own PR": the test requires the map and `legacy/docker-compose.yaml` to match in both directions, so the two can only land together (task 2.2). CI runs every check.
- **Signposts for other teams' agents:**
  - `legacy/README.md`: a "Removed parts" entry, the start order, and the rewritten pwfile note.
  - `leoiot-platform/README.md`: status, what runs from the folder, and the host-local files.
  - Docs pages, DE and EN: setup, interfaces, architecture and operations, including the `/mqtt` row in the nginx routing table.

## Checks run locally

- **Compose:** `docker compose config -q` passes for `leoiot-platform/compose.yaml` and `legacy/docker-compose.yaml`.
- **CI script test:** `bash .github/ci/affected.test.sh` passes all 44 checks (run in a container with bash 5, GNU coreutils and the Compose plugin).
- **Broker scenarios (task 1.3):** all nine passed against a throwaway Compose project with throwaway accounts, removed afterwards:
  - 1883 rejects connections without credentials;
  - an existing account publishes and subscribes on any topic;
  - the collector account publishes on `leoiot/room-climate/105`;
  - the collector account can't publish on `co2/threshold/high` or the PV topic;
  - an anonymous WebSocket client receives retained and new room messages;
  - an anonymous publish is not delivered and leaves the retained message unchanged;
  - an anonymous client subscribed to `#` or `nili3/#` gets nothing outside `leoiot/room-climate/#`;
  - retained messages survive a broker restart;
  - 9001 is bound to `127.0.0.1` only.
- **nginx:** `nginx -t` passes for `leoiot-platform/proxy/nginx.conf` (nginx 1.27, stub certificates). The diff against the old file is only the new block.
- **Docs:** `npm run build` passes.
- **Spec:** `openspec validate platform-broker --strict` passes.

## Reviewer notes

- **Network takeover:** Compose 2.40 only warns when a project uses a network another project created, while older versions refuse. The cutover therefore removes and recreates the network once (D8), which works with any version. This is recorded in design D2.
- **File permissions:** `chmod 644` for `pwfile` and `acl` (platform README) couldn't be checked on macOS. Cutover task 5.2 checks it on vm23.
- **Leftover in CI:** `.github/ci/affected.sh` still matches the now-missing `legacy/deploy/nginx.conf`. That's harmless and left for a later cleanup.

author: rahma530
body:
## Root cause of "the same log line shows up twice"

Confirmed: not a report-pulling bug. A task's delivery auto-creates its own `daily_logs` row
(`source='auto_task'`, using the task's own title/description as the summary — see
`20261120000000_auto_daily_log_from_delivered_task.sql`). If the same employee also logs that same
task manually on the same day, both rows are individually legitimate, different database rows —
but when both land in one report, they read as the exact same line repeated.

## Fix

Added `dedupeIdenticalWorkLogs` (`src/lib/reportDraftSources.ts`): collapses rows with the same
user, same client, same day, and byte-identical summary text (trimmed) — content-based, not just
id-based (the existing `dedupeReportSourceReferences` only ever caught the exact same id appearing
twice, e.g. via two different evidence paths). Only an exact match collapses; a merely-similar line
is left untouched, since this project never silently merges two entries that might carry different
details.

Wired into:
- `collectClientReportSources`/`collectEmployeeReportSources` — the brand-new-draft preview, also
  what feeds the "N visible work logs" count badge.
- `ReportDraftWorkspace`'s `composeManifestContent` — an already-open report's Pull sources
  again/Group similar entries/AI Summary/Revert to original sources, which all route through it.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — passes.
- New test case in `scripts/checkReportDraftSources.ts`: two different ids, same user/client/day,
  byte-identical text (even with extra whitespace) collapse to one; a merely-similar line and a
  same-text-different-day line both stay; plus a direct unit test of the generic helper. All pass,
  alongside every existing assertion in that script.
- Full `lint` chain — passes (the one `checkPdfLinkAnnotations.ts` failure is pre-existing and
  unrelated, confirmed on a clean `origin/main` checkout with no changes, same as prior PRs).
- `npm run build` — passes.

Pure client-side change — no Edge Function or SQL/schema change (the frontend doesn't currently
read the `source`/`task_id` columns at all, so this dedupes by content instead of by that flag —
noted in the code comment in case a future change wants to prefer keeping the manual row
specifically). Never merged by me.

body:
Full modular rewrite of GhostSignal, replacing the single-file v1 monolith (`ghostsignal.py`) with a tested package.

## What's new in v2
- **Pure, Qt-free core** (`ghostsignal/core`, `backends`, `sdr`, `headless`) — unit-tested without a display; a test enforces no PyQt6 imports in those packages. Thin Qt layer in `ghostsignal/ui` + `workers`.
- **Continuous moving-fix playback** via `gps-sdr-sim` user-motion files (v1 only transmitted a single static point). Plus **speed profiles** (constant + trapezoidal accel/decel) and **NMEA track replay**.
- **Real SDR execution** (HackRF / LimeSDR) with a **mandatory authorization gate** before transmit, and a **planner-only** mode that just generates the script.
- **Pluggable multi-constellation backends**: GPS (`gps-sdr-sim`) and Galileo (`harshadms/galileo-sdr-sim`) are real; GLONASS/BeiDou are plugins that require a configurable external multi-GNSS tool and are experimental (greyed out until configured). Honest framing — no out-of-the-box multi-constellation claims.
- **RINEX ephemeris downloader** (BKG/IGS mirrors; CDDIS needs an Earthdata login), **session save/load with v1 migration**, a **headless `ghostsignal-cli`**, and a generation-only **Docker** image.
- Command-injection fix in the generated shell script (every arg is `shlex.quote`d).

## Setup
Python 3.12 venv (`pip install -e .`), PyQt6 + WebEngine. The C simulators are built via `scripts/build-gps-sdr-sim.ps1` / `build-galileo-sdr-sim.ps1` and require a mingw/MSYS2 gcc toolchain (not bundled). 71 tests pass.

## ⚠️ Merge note — divergence with current `master`
`master` has 3 commits made after this branch forked (`796e0a4`, `9378651`, `ea80bad`) that add **v1-only** features to `ghostsignal.py` — a **speed/movement randomiser** and a **right-click waypoint context menu**. v2 **deletes** `ghostsignal.py`, so:
- Merging as-is produces a modify/delete conflict on `ghostsignal.py` (resolved by keeping v2's deletion), and
- those two v1 features are **not yet ported into v2** (they remain in git history).

Decide before merging whether to retire v1 as-is or port those features into v2 first.

Design spec and implementation plan are included under `docs/superpowers/`.

author: polo-nyan
body:
Operator decision (Telegram q-d72d): test `minute`, with random 30-60 s intervals and no fixed cadence.

## Why

In a read-only check on 2026-10-22, 06:53→07:16Z, no drop progress moved while the miner's minute-watched events got 204 from Twitch (23× for twitchplayspokemon, about 45× for streamdatabase/Witchspire). The minute-watched loop only sends a HEAD request for the newest segment. Upstream #846 reports that progress now needs real HLS segment downloads.

## Change

New `classes/HLSFetcher.py`. `TCPM_HLS_SEGMENT_FETCH=off|minute|continuous`, default `off`. `continuous` logs a warning and stays off.

- `minute`: for each drop-relevant stream the miner watches (at most 2), it GETs the newest 160p segment and discards the body. The interval is random, 30-60 s, drawn fresh for each fetch and for each stream.
- The fetches run in their own thread. Random 0.3-2.5 s delays separate the playlist and segment requests. The master playlist is re-read at a random 8-15 min. The requests therefore do not line up with the minute-watched events. The minute-watched events do not change.
- Drop-relevant means `drops_condition()`, or a channel with an unfinished reward-choice campaign. `TCPM_HLS_SEGMENT_CHANNELS` limits the set further, for example to `twitchplayspokemon` for the test.
- Budget: `TCPM_HLS_DAILY_BUDGET_MB` (default 300) per UTC day. Byte totals are logged every hour and for each day, and one line is logged when the budget is reached.
- The three env vars are passed through `test-docker-compose.yml`.

## Verification

- 76 tests pass, locally and in the python:3.12 image. The new tests cover: intervals stay within 30-60 s and are not constant; streams are independent; off makes no fetches; continuous makes no fetches; the budget stops fetching and resets the next UTC day; at most 2 streams; the channel allowlist; a dropped target stops being fetched.
- Smoke test against the real public twitchplayspokemon stream: 1 segment per tick, about 85-93 KB per fetch, next fetch scheduled 42-45 s later. That is about 160 MB per day for one stream at the mean interval.

author: enriquej67
body:
## Qué cambia

La ayuda de enfoque del Sol y la Luna en vivo deja de oscilar: el número es el percentil 25 de los últimos 2,5 s con histéresis (antes, la mediana de 5 fotogramas), debajo del recorte va la gráfica del último minuto con el mejor de la sesión, el recorte lleva su nombre («limbo» o «terminador»: el número es siempre el limbo) y el PC dice por voz «mejora», «empeora» o «igual» al girar el enfocador. Arreglado un valor falso: con la Luna cortada por el borde de la imagen el círculo se ajustaba al terminador y el limbo salía más fino que el real, contaminando el «mejor» de la sesión; ahora se exigen 30 ángulos, el radio de la sesión y el disco quieto.

## Cómo lo he probado

- Banco con los cuatro vídeos SER reales de la Luna del 21-oct-2026 (Saturn-C, 20 fotogramas/s): el limbo por fotograma varía un 6-7 % con el mismo foco (seeing); la nitidez del disco entero o del terminador no es más estable. Mediana de 5 → saltos del 8 %; percentil 25 de 2,5 s → 1-2 %.
- Reproducción del vivo sobre el tramo del primer vídeo en que la Luna se sale del encuadre: el número desaparece en vez de dar 2,0-2,9 px falsos, el «mejor» se queda en 3,0, y mientras la montura se mueve con el pad se avisa «la imagen se mueve».
- Tramo con desenfoque sintético (sigma 2 px) sobre otro vídeo real: «empeora» 5 s después de empezar, «igual» una vez, «mejora» 2 s después de recuperar el foco, sin falsas alarmas.
- `herramientas/probar_enfoque_dia.py` (nueva, sintética), `probar_apilado_video.py`, `probar_servidor.py` y `probar_traducciones.py` en verde. Sin equipo real todavía: pendiente probarlo con la cámara en la próxima Luna.

## Lista

- [x] `python -m compileall -q .` y pyflakes sin nombres sin definir
- [x] Si añade una clave de configuración: está en `config.example.ini` con comentario (no añade ninguna)
- [x] Si cambia la interfaz: captura de pantalla (imagen compuesta del vivo adjunta en la conversación: recorte etiquetado, número y gráfica)
- [x] Si merece aparecer en el historial: línea en `CHANGELOG.md`

author: peterstreamland
body:
Phase 3 task 4: the filters for the fingering search (SPEC 5). All are off by default.

- **Inversion:** a numbered inversion, or "any". Each shape now reports its inversion, which is undefined for a bass outside the chord (F/G).
- **String set:** any set of strings may sound; the rest are muted.
- **Maximum span:** 3–6 frets (already there).
- **Open strings off:** with a capo, the capo's fret is off too.
- **Omit the 5th:** removes the perfect 5th where a shape could already drop it. It doesn't apply to power chords, nor to diminished or augmented chords. A 5th asked for in the bass stays only in the bass. A deliberately omitted 5th costs no playability points.

**Tests:** 11 new filter tests, each checked against hand-written shapes (032010 and 332010 for C's inversions, 1x0001 for G7/F, x35553 for C without open strings, x32x1x for C without its 5th). All 2,616 tests, lint, typecheck and build pass locally.

PLAN.md ticks task 4. DECISIONS.md records the choices. Nothing changes on screen yet: the chord boxes are task 8.

author: kmrh47
body:
Explorer forgot every view choice when it closed, and qol panels could not be resized by the user.
This pull request gives Explorer a settings page and window memory, and lets users resize qol's gpui windows and keep the size they pick.

## What changes for the user

Explorer:
- Row or icon size (Ctrl+1 to 5, Ctrl+wheel, the slider) and hidden entries (Ctrl+H) are remembered and follow the profile to other machines.
- A new settings page holds the same two values, with a card blurb and pictures for the view size, and `explorer settings` opens it.
- The window has an OS title bar, can be resized down to 640 by 400, and reopens at its last size and place; maximized sizes are not remembered.
- The sidebar, the Name column, the crumbs and the scrollbar fit any window size.
- A plain click on a row drops the current picks.
- Explorer's window shows its own icon (a compass needle on the qol nut, in a folder) in the panel and window list instead of the desktop's grey gear; on X11 the window sets `_NET_WM_ICON`, ported from Zed upstream (zed-industries/zed#40096), and other platforms ignore it for now.

Resizable qol windows:
- Panels and overlay panels get eight invisible resize zones on their edges and a minimum size; a window the user resized reopens at that size.
- The settings panel keeps the user's size on every page once they resize it, and fits its width to the screen.
- The launcher resizes from its edges down to 680 by 370 and shows as many Apps and Files rows as fit; flows keep their designed size.
- CLI Sessions keeps the user's panel size across folds, resizes only its width while folded, and can shrink to three rows.
- The shot editor reopens where it was left, can shrink to fit a 700 px screen, and scales the screenshot to fill it with strokes kept on the same image pixels.
- Remove app reopens where it was left, can shrink to 460 by 290, shows as many rows as fit and says so when a search matches nothing.
- The first emoji in a new text weight no longer freezes the first frame of a maximized Explorer, because each weight's fallback font loads in the background after startup.

## How

Explorer settings:
- `plugins/explorer/qol-config.toml` declares `view_size` and `show_hidden`, both `core` scope.
- Each change saves only its own key through `PUT /api/plugins/<id>/config`, which merges keys, checks the schema and reloads the plugin; a background saver coalesces slider drags and finishes its last save before the window closes.
- The new shared helper `qol_plugin_api::host_exec::save_plugin_config_keys` lets any plugin save some keys without replacing its whole config.
- The doctor's `config_readable` check validates the saved settings.

Resizing in `libs/gpui`:
- `resize_frame` drives edge drags from the client at about 120 Hz, starts each drag at the press position, and lands it at the release size.
- A size counts as the user's only while a drag or an OS live resize is in progress, so window-manager clamps, maximize and tiling moves never pin a size; a resize the window manager takes over counts for up to five seconds or until its release is seen.
- Window memory writes each move or resize to the pending save at once, so a quit inside the save delay keeps the last bounds, and the CLI Sessions fold holds the unfolded bounds in window memory instead of a second file.
- Undecorated windows stop one pixel short of a panel-less monitor, because Muffin and Metacity treat a monitor-sized one as fullscreen and refuse to shrink it.
- The launcher resizes itself from the client, because Muffin drops `_NET_WM_MOVERESIZE` for dock windows; Explorer, which has an OS frame, draws no in-content resize zones.

Vendor gpui (each change is listed in `vendor/gpui/MODIFICATIONS.md`):
- On X11 a window with a minimum size renders into a child window sized to its content in 256 px steps, which grows once to the largest monitor when a live resize starts, so resize steps no longer rebuild the Vulkan swapchain (about 18 ms per step on NVIDIA) and a window that is never resized holds no monitor-sized swapchain (about 100 MB on a 4K monitor).
- The `_NET_WM_SYNC_REQUEST` counter is acked on the refresh after the frame drawn at the new size, so the window manager no longer shows a black strip on the trailing edges.
- `Window::set_window_min_size` sets the minimum on every platform, which keeps the window gravity Explorer's title bar needs and drops the Windows window-procedure subclass.
- `Window::is_live_resizing` reports an OS resize on X11, Wayland, Windows and macOS, and `Window::expect_live_resize` grows the X11 render child before a client-driven resize starts.
- `_NET_WM_MOVERESIZE` starts at the press position, so a quick drag on a resize edge no longer jumps.

## Fixes from the guest tests

- A remembered panel restored on a smaller screen keeps its size and only its position is clamped; before, the fixed-size reveal never confirmed and Explorer reopened blank and quit.
- The settings panel fits its width to the work area; before, with every plugin loaded it asked for 1296 px and never showed on a 1280 px screen.
- A panel opens even when no compositor is running; before, Explorer started before the desktop's compositor (or on a desktop without one) quit with "surface could not prepare a fresh frame", because the hidden-until-drawn reveal needs a compositor.
- The second review board's fixes (a1370b707) size the render child lazily, claim sizes only on evidence of a user resize, and report a drag end once per drag instead of polling it.

## Known leftovers

- A frame slower than 1 s during a window-manager resize makes Muffin drop resize sync for that window, so later resizes of it are no longer synced with its frames.
- A SIGKILL from outside the tray inside the save debounce loses the last bounds, because the pending save never runs.

Design context: the state audit and the architecture page at https://claude.ai/artifact/1L9saqA4uMAVYJWCzUtgLZ.
Tests run in CI.

Draft because it adds a settings page and changes how windows look and resize (UI).

author: bluefishforsale
body:
Fixes the `session::tests::every_state_the_driver_enters_is_redrawn_in_order` flake on Windows (run 39736174737, `left: "linking"`, `right: "choose_access"`).

Cause: a real ordering bug, not just a test problem. `Session`'s redraw called `on_change` (which emits to the window) before storing the new view, so anything reading the current screen right after hearing of a redraw could get the previous one. That includes the test's final `session.view()` and the page's `current` call. On a multi-thread runtime the test thread sometimes won that race. The fix stores the view first, then notifies.

Tests: a new regression test, `a_redraw_stores_the_new_screen_before_anyone_is_told_it_changed`, checks, inside the redraw callback, that the stored screen already equals the one being announced. It failed deterministically before the fix (`redraw of linking went out before it was stored`). The session tests now run on a current-thread runtime with a paused tokio clock (`tokio` `test-util` as a dev-dependency) and an async channel, so there are no real-time waits. The 5 s timeout only fires if the driver task stalls.

Verified locally with `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 ALL_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost,::1 cargo test --offline -p relay-app`: the full relay-app suite (20 tests) passed 200/200 runs in a loop, and clippy (default and all features) and fmt pass.

body: ## 관련 이슈 LAN-739 ## 무엇을, 왜 친구 초대 같은 이벤트를 사용자가 바로 알 수 있게, 홈에 들어오면 이벤트 공지를 가장 먼저 바텀시트로 띄웁니다. **화면** - 시트 위쪽을 꽉 채운 가로 4:3 이미지 한 장과 「자세히 보기」·「닫기」로 구성합니다. 문구는 이미지에 들어 있습니다. - 「자세히 보기」나 이미지를 누르면 링크로 갑니다. 앱 안 경로면 화면을 옮기고, https 주소면 앱 밖 브라우저로 엽니다. 링크가 없는 공지는 「닫기」만 둡니다. - 시안: 피그마 ✅ Screens 페이지 「LAN-739 이벤트 공지 팝업」 섹션 B안. 캡처의 이미지는 예시입니다. **누구에게, 몇 번** - 기존 정기 구독자(월간·연간 등)에게는 보이지 않습니다. 100일 이용권·무료·대시보드로 기간을 받은 사용자에게는 보입니다. 구독 상태를 알 수 없으면 띄우지 않습니다. - 같은 공지는 기기마다 한 번입니다. 「자세히 보기」든 「닫기」든 한 번 반응하면 다시 띄우지 않고, 새 공지를 등록하면 다시 한 번 뜹니다. **어떤 공지를** - 백엔드 `GET /api/v1/popups/active`(Aragornnnnnn/landit-be#319, LAN-740)가 고른 공지 하나를 띄웁니다. 어드민에서 이미지·링크·기간·켜고 끄기를 바꾸면 배포 없이 반영됩니다. - 백엔드 배포 전이라 API가 404를 주면 공지 없이 지나가므로, 이 PR을 먼저 머지해도 됩니다. **계측** - `Event Popup Viewed`·`Tapped`·`Dismissed`(popup_id)로 노출·탭·닫기를 남깁니다. ## 리뷰 포인트 - 홈 순서 — 강제 업데이트 → 이벤트 공지 → 램프 래디·소감·알림 동의·프리미엄 프리뷰 순입니다. 공지 응답을 기다리는 동안과 공지가 열려 있는 동안 뒤의 것들이 기다리고, 램프는 공지를 닫은 뒤 그날 처음처럼 나옵니다. 판단은 `_model/event-popup-order.ts`에 모았습니다. - 강제 업데이트는 확인 중일 때도 1순위로 봅니다. 그동안 홈과 스몰톡 탭의 자동 안내(공지·램프·소감·스몰톡 첫 안내·코치마크)가 모두 나서지 않습니다(`useForceUpdateFirst`). - develop에 들어온 #400(프리뷰 끝까지 소감 보류)과 합쳤습니다. 소감·리뷰 시트는 강제 업데이트·공지·프리뷰를 모두 기다립니다. - 페이월 이탈 할인 시트와 대화 직후 동전 연출은 방금 한 행동의 응답이라 공지가 그 뒤를 기다립니다. - 선택 업데이트 시트(SOFT)는 공지와 함께 뜰 수 있습니다. 그 시트를 닫았는지는 업데이트 게이트 안에만 있어 이번에는 다루지 않았습니다. - 지난 방문의 응답이 캐시에 남아 있어도 이번 방문의 응답이 올 때까지 공지를 정하지 않습니다. ## 체크리스트 - [ ] 코드 추가 500줄 이하 (5~10분 리뷰 가능한 볼륨) — 테스트 포함 815줄, 테스트를 빼면 369줄입니다. 공지 순서(강제 업데이트·램프·시트)가 한 흐름이라 나누지 않았습니다. - [x] 브랜치 이름에 이슈 번호 포함 (`feat/LAN-739`) - [x] 커밋 메시지가 컨벤션(`{type}({scope}): 메시지`)을 따름 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mininet-labs
body:
Desktop packages could install/verify successfully while missing the application core needed for identity and signing. Client manifests now require exactly one nonempty hashed sibling mininet-app-service.exe, including nested/mixed-case Windows paths. Checks run at construction/parsing, container writing, install planning/install and installed verification, including mutated manifests. Generic non-desktop packages remain supported; existing release scripts already stage the core.

A visible Retry application core action recovers initial spawn/status failure while preserving drafts and operation IDs. It does not replay mutations, create/unlock identities or change network grants. Failed status clears stale signing state. Unix host-package layouts support the explicit sibling .exe fallback with native precedence; no PATH/current-directory search is added. Action diagnostics now name only the action, omitting captured private disabled fields, source paths, unpublished drafts, photo bytes and unexpected reply bodies.

Validation: 142 targeted passing tests (132 setup engine/wizard/CLI-fixture, 9 desktop IPC/client, 1 diagnostic redaction), targeted Clippy warnings denied and formatting/diff checks. Production mini CLI built without the Wasmtime test runner; two packaging smoke cases accept a complete bundle and reject a missing core before writing output. Tests use temporary fixtures and recording shells; no real Windows installation, launch of packaged applications or release activation was performed.

Stacked on #392. Composition/hashes do not establish executable authenticity; existing approval/release evidence remains separate. Native Windows/vault/upgrade acceptance, raw-media import and broader beta journeys remain open. No merges or governance activation.

author: futrime
body:
P2-13: Sophisticated Backpacks' world systems, admin commands and server/common config, matched to SB / SophisticatedCore 1.21.x.

## What's in it

### Commands (`src/feature/admin/SbpCommands.cpp`, `Sbp.h`)
- New root `/sbp`, alias `/sophisticatedbackpacks`. It needs operator rights: SB's op level 2 maps to Bedrock operators (`GameDirectors`).
  - `list [playerName]`: newest first, with SB's header `Backpack Name, Colors, Last Open By, Last Open On`. Cloth/Trim words are drawn in the nearest text colour, and the date uses Java's `SimpleDateFormat()` ("M/d/yy, h:mm AM").
  - `give <targets> <backpackUuid>`: gives to every target, as SB does.
  - `removeNonPlayer <onlyWithEmptyInventory>`.
- The same overloads also work as `/backpack list|give|removeNonPlayer`.
- Other units can add sub-commands with `ABP_REGISTER_SBP_SUBCOMMAND` (P2-2 templates). `getOrCreateCommand("sbp")` is idempotent, so a second root registration is harmless.
- Phase-1 `/backpack list` and `/backpack give <player> <uuid>` became the `/sbp` versions. `/backpack info <uuid>|stats|remove|cleanup|openfor` stay as admin extras.

### Access log (`AccessLog.{h,cpp}`)
- Implements SB's `BackpackAccessLogger`. Every backpack GUI open records the item id, uuid, player name, display name, both colours, epoch-ms time and `columnsTaken`.
- Saved data lives in LevelDB `abp:accesslog`. The per-player cache is kept for 30 s.
- `list`, `give` and `removeNonPlayer` all work from the log.
- Phase-1 holder records are migrated once, so existing backpacks count as player-owned.

### Config parity (`SbConfig.{h,cpp}`, `Connections.cpp`)
Three new files with SB's key names, defaults and ranges (clamped where they are read):

**`config/sophisticatedbackpacks-server.json`**:
- `disallowedItems` (globs allowed too), `containerItemsDisallowed`.
- `noInteractionBlocks`, `noConnectionBlocks`, `allBlockConnectionsDisallowed`.
- `<tier>Backpack.inventorySlotCount` / `upgradeSlotCount`. Storage grows to the setting, and shrinks only when the cut slots are empty.
- `entityBackpackAdditions.*` (all 20 keys) and `nerfs.*`.
- `maxUpgradesPerStorage`, using SC's "Only %dx %s can be used in %s".
- `itemFluidHandlerEnabled`, `allowOpeningOtherPlayerBackpacks`, `itemDisplayDisabled`, `tickDedupeLogicDisabled`, `canBePlacedInContainerItems` (shulker box screen and hoppers).

**`config/sophisticatedbackpacks-common.json`**: `chestLootEnabled`.

**`config/sophisticatedcore-common.json`**: `enabledItems`. On world start it is filled with every mod item as `|true`; crafting a `|false` item is refused.

### Linked storage and the Ender Linker (`src/feature/linked/**`, `core/LinkedGroups`)
- New item `alleviatedbackpacks:ender_linker`. Original art comes from `tools/textures/linked.ps1`. Recipes are SB's `OEO/BOB/OEO` and the shapeless clear.
- Groups are saved data (LevelDB `abp:linked`). Each endpoint item carries its group, endpoint id, PRIMARY flag and the group's storage uuid, so:
  - contents, upgrades, ticking, render info and the jukebox all resolve to the one shared (primary) storage;
  - only the primary can tier-upgrade it, through a Storage tier-growth gate.
- SC's link rules are covered:
  - create primary;
  - add an empty secondary (failure: "Storage has contents");
  - bind a linker to an existing endpoint;
  - "Storage is already linked";
  - a stack of linkers splits one linker off.
- Feedback follows SC: enderman teleport sound at 0.5/1.15 plus witch particles on success; a bass note plus an action-bar status on failure.
- Bedrock interactions:
  - right-click a backpack slot with the linker on the cursor, or the linker slot with a backpack on the cursor, in the native screen;
  - use the linker on a placed backpack.
- Placing an endpoint in creative places a new secondary copy and the hand keeps its item.
- Several endpoints of one group can stand placed; their shared storage ticks once.
- Tooltips (client hook): the linker's blank/bound/"Linked to:" lines, and the endpoint role header "Main Linked" / "Linked" with the group name.

### UUID dedup (`src/feature/dedup/**`)
- Implements SB's `UUIDDeduplicator`. It runs:
  - on backpack item entity spawn, against other item entities within 10 blocks;
  - every 40 ticks per dimension over player inventories, offhand and chest slot, unless `tickDedupeLogicDisabled`;
  - on GUI open.
- The copy with more slots keeps the uuid, and the first one wins a tie. Linked endpoints are skipped.

### Nerfs (`src/feature/nerf/**`)
- `tooManyBackpacksSlowness` (default off): every 40 ticks per dimension it applies `nerfEffect` (slowness fallback) for 80 ticks at `ceil((n - max) * ratio)` levels, capped at 10, with no particles.
- `onlyWornBackpackTriggersUpgrades` goes through the new PlayerScan carried-upgrade gate.

### Opening another player's backpack (`src/feature/access/**`)
- The client mod right-click sends key action `openOtherPlayer` with the target runtime id and hit position. The client pre-checks like SB.
- The server re-checks everything:
  - `allowOpeningOtherPlayerBackpacks`;
  - the hit's local y is in [0.9, 1.6);
  - the hit is from behind (dot > 0, using the body yaw);
  - the target's `anotherPlayerCanOpen` (backpack override, else the player's own setting, default on);
  - the chest slot only.
- The viewer's screen closes when the target takes the backpack off or walks away.
- A backpack settings entry toggles `anotherPlayerCanOpen`.

### Mob backpacks and chest loot (`src/feature/wearable/**`)
SB's `EntityBackpackAdditionHandler`, exactly:
- Eligibility: `entityLootTableList` (Bedrock ids/tables), empty chest slot, `1/(int)(1/chance)`, no raiders of a raid. This is decided one tick after the spawn.
- Tier weights 625/250/125/25/5/1. Vanilla local difficulty gives index `floor(3/6.75*eff-0.1)` → pools from minMid / minHigh.
- Spawn egg colours; lazy loot (partial rolls `minD..minD+2`, `LOOT_FACTOR = rolls/3`, backpacks removed from the loot, random empty slots, overflow voided).
- 1/4 jukebox, of which 25% advanced, with random non-blocked discs. These mobs play through the jukebox service at the mob's position.
- `difficulty+2` potion buffs from SB's pool for 30 min; health `base * minDifficulty`; tier-weighted helmet/leggings/boots, enchanted 1 in (6 − minD) at level 5 + special·18 + minD·6.
- Drops only to a player kill (`dropToFakePlayers` → simulated players), with chance `(0.5 + looting·0.15)·tierMult` (1/1.25/1.5/3/4.5/6).
- Otherwise the storage goes away. A dropped jukebox backpack carries its upgrades as extra items.
- A mob leaving the level loses its backpack's storage unless it converted.

Chest loot uses SB's inject tables exactly (single roll, empty weights), mapped to the Bedrock tables (`shipwrecktreasure`, ...) and gated by `chestLootEnabled`.

## Phase-1 extras (removed or neutralised)
| Extra | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `admin.maxNestingDepth` | default 0 = unlimited (SB has no limit) |
| `admin.keepBackpacksOnDeath`, `admin.disabledUpgrades` | kept, off / empty by default |
| `admin.disallowedItems` | deprecated, still read (merged with SB's list) so existing deny-lists keep working |
| `wearable.worn.doubleSneakToOpen` | default off (the client mod's B key opens the worn backpack) |
| `wearable.mobs.*` (tier weights per dimension, difficulty multipliers, per-tier effects, loot rolls, `includeSpawnerMobs`, `dropChanceNotKilledByPlayer`) | replaced by SB's `entityBackpackAdditions`; random upgrades kept as `wearable.mobs.addRandomUpgrades`, default off |
| `wearable.chestLoot.*` (per-table chance + items) | replaced by SB's inject tables |
| `general.allowShulkerBoxes` default `false` | now `true` (SB lets shulker boxes in; `containerItemsDisallowed` refuses them) |
| `/backpack list` (holder-based) | is now SB's `/sbp list` (access log) |

## Shared-contract changes (all additive; please note when merging)
- `game/Storage.h`: `setTierGrowthGate`.
- `game/PlayerScan.h`: `setCarriedUpgradeGate`, applied to every `carriedBackpacks` list.

author: kerthans
body:
Fixes #1422.

RFC 7591 §2 defines the `jwks` client metadata as a JSON object, but `ClientRegistrationMetadata.JWKS` is a `string`. `RegisterClient` therefore failed on any registration response that included `jwks` (Ory Hydra returns `"jwks": {}` on every registration), and a JWK Set passed by value was sent as a JSON string.

As suggested in the issue, the custom `MarshalJSON` and `UnmarshalJSON` are on `ClientRegistrationMetadata`, so both the request and the response are covered. `JWKS` keeps its type and now holds the JWK Set as JSON text:

- Encoding: a value that is a JSON object is sent as an object. Any other non-empty value is still sent as a JSON string, as before.
- Decoding: an object is stored as its JSON text, a JSON string is stored as its contents (the previous behavior), and `null` leaves it empty. Other JSON types are an error.

`ClientRegistrationResponse` embeds `ClientRegistrationMetadata`, so its existing methods could no longer embed an alias of itself: the metadata methods would be promoted through the alias and encode only the metadata. They now use a struct that lists the response fields next to the metadata.

Tests cover both types in both directions (`{}`, a key set, the string form, `null`, a non-object, and the string fallback on encode), plus a `RegisterClient` round trip with the response from the issue. The new object cases fail on main. `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: iamphduc
body:
Door: two-way

Two review changes the human chose on 2026-10-22.

## What changes

1. **The engine's best move is never graded.** When the move played is Stockfish's best in that position (`evals[ply].best === move.uci`), it gets drop 0, accuracy 100 and no grade, and it's never a key moment, even when the next position's search scores it lower. Before, search noise at 500 ms could make the key-moment card read "You played X · Stockfish: X". This applies to both sides.
2. **His moves are marked too.** `reviewPly` (`src/game/review/build-review.ts`) now grades his moves with `gradeMove` at the same 10/20/30 levels. The review's move list shows his marks with the same chips and colors as yours. This supersedes "The review marks only your moves" (2026-10-18).

## Defaults the human didn't pick

- His moves while he's still in his book (plies before you leave it, `ply < bookPlies`) are never graded. They stay `drop`, `accuracy` and `grade` `null`.
- The summary's counts, your accuracy and the key moments are about your moves only. `counts` and the key-moment candidates skip `!byHuman` moves, so they mean what they meant before.
- The graph is unchanged. It draws points for your graded moves only, and its cursor tip shows only the label for his moves.
- Tapping one of his marked moves moves the cursor but doesn't reopen the phone's key-moment sheet. Your marked moves still reopen it.
- Without his books (they failed to load), there's no book end, so his moves are graded from his first move.

## Notes

- The game accuracy (Lichess's formula over the win % series) still counts a best move's noise drop. Only the per-move accuracy and grade ignore it.
- Docs: `post-game-review.md` (How it works, Why, Watch out, History), the `features.md` review row, the idea's Status line, and the stale Watch out line in `his-moves-after-his-book.md`.

## Verify

```bash
npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/game/review src/features/review
npm run build && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2
```

author: jasondwhyte
body:

_Requested by **Jason** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01A5yQtY5a3RzSQuJ4aTm2sL?thread=cmsg_01A5yQtY5a3RzSQuJ4aTm2sLBsePDf75AfXwahzd4X1tjU)_

## What changes

The "Mark as production" switch becomes a **Session label** menu. A label is a coloured bar across a session (and the tab's border and tag on desktop) with words on it, the same way production worked.

- Each label has a **name**, a **colour** (one of the eight named colours, or a hex code like `#1F6FEB`) and an optional **warning sign**.
- **Production** comes as the first label: red, with the warning sign. It can be edited or deleted like any other.
- Labels are managed in **Settings → Hosts → Session labels**, or made straight from the host form's **New label…** menu item.
- A host can still set its own **Words on the bar**; blank shows the label's name.
- Deleting a label asks first (saying how many hosts use it) and takes it off those hosts.

## Storage and compatibility

- Labels are a synced setting, `session_labels` (added to `SYNCED_SETTINGS`), so every device draws them the same. No saved list means the Production preset.
- Host records gain `session_label` (the label id). A record with `production: true` and no `session_label` reads as the Production label, so existing production hosts keep their bar without any migration step.
- `production_label` stays the host's own words, and `production` is still written (true only for the Production label) so older app versions keep showing the bar for production hosts.

## Tests

- Model tests for the legacy read, the round trip and how a host's mark is worked out.
- Widget tests: picking Production in the host form, making and editing labels in Settings (hex validation included), a host carrying a custom label with its colour, and deleting a label.
- Engine: a `session_label` round-trip test. `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`, `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check` pass locally.

Docs: GUIDE.md section is now "Session labels"; DESIGN.md and VAULT.md mention the new fields.

body:
CODECOPY, CALLDATACOPY and RETURNDATACOPY took the generic path: three indirect calls per op (memory size, dynamic gas, execute). They now get MCOPY's inline fast path in the cold switch, used when the destination memory is already allocated and gas covers the copy; otherwise the op falls back to the generic path.

EEST 150M-gas blocks: codecopy x1.27-1.37, calldatacopy x1.31-1.34, returndatacopy x1.23-1.24 (no BAL / BAL), above noise; mcopy and extcodecopy unchanged; an ADD loop does not change (instructions/op +0.00%).

author: zoltan118
body:
The validator set took about 9s to load. The page HTML arrived in 0.6s. The rest was spent waiting on chain reads.

**Cause.** Every browser read through `lcdGet` or `fetchWithTimeout` called `freshestFirst()`, which probed `blocks/latest` on every host in the LCD pool and waited for all of them. coreum-rest.publicnode.com stopped answering today (8s timeouts from curl as well), so every read waited out its 5s probe timeout. Verdicts were cached only after a probe finished, so the reads a page fires at load each started their own round of probes.

**Change** (`src/lib/chain-config.ts` only):
- the probe promise is cached, so concurrent reads share one probe per host
- probes still run in parallel, but the order settles as soon as the highest ranked host proves fresh. A host already known to be behind tip still goes last, so the proposal 45 protection holds
- probe timeout 5s to 2s
- publicnode moved below cosmos.directory

**Measured on /validators** (production before, local dev after):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| blocks/latest probes | 54 | 6 |
| first chain read starts | ~6.6s | ~1.0s |
| last chain read done | ~8.4s | ~3.1s |
| validator rows | 52 | 52 |

Every page reading through these helpers benefits, not only /validators.

Not in this PR: /validators still makes 29 sequential-batch `delegations` reads for the PSE-excluded addresses, plus repeated `validators`, `annual_provisions` and `distribution/params` reads from separate components. Moving those behind one cached server route is the next step.

author: thisisjun786
body:
Fix terminal input wrappers that expose `Fd()` staying in canonical mode, and stop reporting caller cancellation as a successful quit. Wrapped input now uses raw mode and the cancellable decoder while preserving the caller's reader and file ownership. Signals and quit keys still exit cleanly; caller cancellation retains its error. The TUI design contract documents these rules. Full verification also exposed an existing startup race: submitting before history discovery supplied a conversation ID terminated the client. The client now holds that initial pending input until discovery succeeds, restoring it to the draft on refusal or connection loss. A change of conversation focus invalidates the deferred send.

Validation:
- New Linux PTY regressions failed before the fix and pass afterward: raw mode and immediate quit through a `Read`/`Fd` wrapper, caller cancellation during negotiation, terminal restoration, and retained input ownership.
- `go test -race ./internal/tui/...` — passed.
- `go test ./e2e -run '^TestTUITerminalLifecycle$' -count=1` — passed, including signal shutdown during negotiation and after welcome.
- `go test ./e2e -run '^(TestM1ConversationHistoryOrder|TestM1ReplyShapeLONGQA)$' -count=1 -v` — passed after fixing the startup race; both tests also failed on the unmodified base during diagnosis.

body: ## What changed Pillow was a transitive lockfile pin at **12.3.0** (via matplotlib and streamlit in the `dev` group). There was no `requirements*.txt`, Space `requirements`, Dockerfile, or CI pin. This PR: - Adds an explicit `pillow>=13.0.0` floor to the `dev` group in `pyproject.toml`. - Regenerates `uv.lock` with `uv lock` (not hand-edited). Locked version is **13.0.0**. - Raises `streamlit` from `>=1.65.0` to `>=1.66.0` (lock: **1.66.1**). Streamlit 1.65.0 declares `pillow<13,>=7.1.0`, which is why Dependabot’s own security update never produced a PR. 1.66.1 allows `pillow<14,>=9.2.0`. - Adds `tests/test_image_loading.py`: - generates a small JPEG in-process with Pillow and decodes it (`Image.load()`, the `ImagingJpegDecode` path). - writes PNGs through `scripts/plot_matrix.py` `write_figures` (matplotlib/Agg `savefig`) and decodes each file. No other Pillow pins existed. No application code called removed Pillow 12→13 APIs (`Image.ANTIALIAS`, `textsize`, `Image._show`, I-mode PNG save, `fromarray` mode changes, etc.). ## Alerts closed - **Dependabot alert #5** — critical heap overflow in `ImagingJpegDecode` (`GHSA-8g5g-8vmr-9782` / `GHSA-5x8w-8jj5-q52h`). - **The 6 high-severity Pillow alerts** shipped in 13.0.0 (WMF/EMF OOB read, SPIDER bomb bypass, Exif header loop, JPEG comment write overflow, TIFF tile/YCbCr OOB, PDF stack exhaustion, and the rest of the 13.0.0 high set). Pillow 13.0.0 also includes two critical fixes (stale native storage after mode transitions; JPEG decoder buffer overflow). ## Python versions Pillow 13 requires **Python ≥3.11** and drops 3.10. This repo already has `requires-python = ">=3.12"` and CI is a single job on **3.12**. No supported Python is dropped; the CI matrix was not changed. ## Test evidence (local, this VM) ``` uv run ruff check src tests evals # All checks passed uv run pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_times_inspect.py # 95 passed in 6.65s ``` `tests/test_times_inspect.py` stays ignored in CI (needs Docker). Installed/locked Pillow is 13.0.0. No benchmark numbers are claimed.

author: jotitadev
body:
### What

`tools/pr_overlap.py --branch <branch>` gives a different report when it runs from a subdirectory of the checkout, for example `cd tools && python3 pr_overlap.py --branch my-branch`:

- **Same exports** is always empty. `scan()` diffs with the pathspec `core/libs/prx/*.cpp`, which git reads relative to the current directory, so from `tools/` the export diff is empty. On a real open PR (#9452), `scan()` finds 11 exports from the root and 0 from `tools/`. Two PRs that implement the same export pass silently.
- Conflicting files are printed relative to the current directory (`../core/...`), because `git merge-tree --name-only` prints them that way. Their GitHub links then point to the wrong path.
- The conflict line ranges are dropped. `hunks()` gets that relative path, or the root-relative path from `--name-status` with a pathspec read from the current directory, and finds no hunks either way.

The script now switches to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` before running any git command, so every path is read and printed from the top of the repository. A relative `--out` is resolved before the switch, so it still lands where the caller meant. CI runs from the repository root, where the output does not change.

### Tested

macOS 27.2 arm64 (M2 Max), git 2.55, `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9.6 and Python 3.14.7, main ab347d144, then rebased onto d6eafa54d with the tests and `check_conventions.py` run again:

- New `test_branch_report_from_a_subdirectory_matches_the_root` runs the script end to end. A shell `gh` returns one open PR, and `url.<repo>.insteadOf` serves the fetch locally. The open PR and the branch both change line 1 of a library file and both add `sceExample`. From the root the report lists the file with `[L1]` and `sceExample`. With main, the run from `tools/` reports `../core/libs/prx/libSceExample/Export.cpp` with no line and no shared export. With this change the output from `tools/` and `core/libs/prx/` is the same as from the root. A run with `--out reports` from `tools/` writes `tools/reports/7.md`, and the test fails without the `--out` resolve. It is skipped on Windows, like the other test in the file that needs a shell.
- All seven `test_pr_overlap*.py` files pass on 3.9, and `test_pr_overlap.py` passes on 3.14. With the new test and without the change, it fails on both.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes. `python3 tools/pr_overlap.py --branch fix/pr-overlap-from-subdirectory` lists only #988, which conflicts with main and touches the same file. #8970 and #9539 also change `tools/pr_overlap.py`: both merge cleanly with this change, and with both merged on top all eight `test_pr_overlap*.py` files pass on 3.14.

- [x] Based on current `main`; no other open PR implements the same functions
- [x] One topic per PR; follow-ups go in a new PR

author: thomast8
body:
## Why
On 22 Oct the Mac froze and needed a forced reboot. WindowServer was starved while agent workers (pytest -n 4, xcodebuild, repowise) ran at full priority. The guards that fixed it only existed as live files on this machine, so a new Mac wouldn't get them.

## What
New `guards/` folder: `ui-guard` (runs every 15 s), `disk-guard.sh` (weekly cleanup), their launch agents, and `guards/install VALUES`, which copies the scripts to `~/.local/bin`, renders the plists with `@@HOME@@` and reloads them. ui-guard renices any worker above 15% CPU to +10. It pauses workers for 30 s when WindowServer stays above 60% for two ticks while the CPU is under 10% idle, memory pressure goes critical, or free disk drops under 5 GB. It never touches the agents themselves (codex, claude), and it never kills anything.

## How
Compared with the live copy from this morning there are four changes. The WindowServer trigger now also needs the CPU under 10% idle: WindowServer sat at 62-82% during normal use and the old check paused workers 6 times in 16 minutes with CPU to spare, which can't help it. The load-average trigger is gone, replaced by `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level >= 4`: a Simulator booting on its own pushed load past 150 with 28% CPU idle, and the old trigger paused real workers about a dozen times for nothing. ui-guard no longer quits Lunar, because Lunar wasn't causing the brightness churn. A pause now writes a deadline and sets an EXIT trap, and the next tick resumes anything a SIGKILLed pause left stopped. The plist labels are now `local.*`, so there's no identity in the repo. `install` also waits for `bootout` to finish before calling `bootstrap`, because calling it straight away failed with error 5.

## Verification
From this branch, with a values file that only has `HOME=$HOME` in it:
`guards/install <values>` run three times in a row: exit 0 each time. `launchctl list | grep guard` shows `local.ui-guard` running and `local.disk-guard` loaded. `plutil -lint ~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.*guard.plist` gives OK, and `grep -c @@` on them gives 0.
For the crash path, start `python3 -c 'while 1: pass' &`, run `ui-guard pause 6 &`, then `kill -9` the pause. The worker stays in state `TN`. Once the deadline passes, the next `ui-guard tick` puts it back in `RN`.
`ui-guard status` now prints `WindowServer 50%   CPU 14% idle   memory pressure 1` in place of the load average. With a stand-in `top` on PATH reporting WindowServer at 75% twice, a tick at 35% idle doesn't pause, while one at 4% idle logs `WindowServer 75% twice, CPU 4% idle`, pauses for 30 s and resumes.

## Notes / deferred
`disk-guard.sh` still skips `~/Library/Caches/Nadir` by name. That's a personal project name in a public repo, so decide whether to keep it or move it to a values token. The WindowServer trigger hasn't fired under real starvation yet, so the renice is what's doing the work all the time. The orchestrator change that calls `guards/install` is in thomast8/warp-dev-environment#7, and this PR should merge first.

author: dihuangdh
body:
## What changed

- The existing `app-builder-lib` patch now also reads `build/messages.yml` when electron-builder generates installer messages, adding our messages and replacing bundled ones with the same name.
- `nsis.installerLanguages` is set to `en_US` and `zh_CN`, the app's UI languages. Other systems get the English installer.
- Removed the Vietnamese `appProcessCheckFailed` text added in #375, and the test that required it.
- `test/desktop-installer-contract.test.ts` runs electron-builder's own message generation with our config and checks that every `$(...)` used in `build/installer.nsh` is compiled for both installer languages, and that no other language is compiled.
- `docs/desktop-releases.md` describes where installer messages live and how they reach the installer.

## Why it changed

The v0.0.0-beta.4.12 and v0.0.0-beta.4.13 release runs failed in "Build Windows package":

```
warning 6040: LangString "appProcessCheckFailed" is not set in language table of language Vietnamese
Error: warning treated as error
```

electron-builder only reads its bundled `templates/nsis/messages.yml`; nothing in the build read `build/messages.yml`. Up to beta.4.11 the installer only used bundled messages (`appRunning`, `appClosing`, `appCannotBeClosed`), so the build passed, though our `appCannotBeClosed` wording never shipped. #352 (`omg*` progress messages) and #369 (`appProcessCheckFailed`) were the first to rely on our own messages, so none of them existed in the installer. Without `installerLanguages`, electron-builder builds all 30 bundled languages; Vietnamese is the last, which is why NSIS reported it first. Adding a `vi` entry (#375) could not help because the file was still not read, and beta.4.13 failed with the same warning.

The PR checks did not catch this: the progress smoke test compiles a hand-written fixture that defines its own LangStrings, the contract tests only read the YAML, and the real electron-builder Windows build only runs on a release tag.

## How it was checked

- The new contract test passes, and fails when the merge in the patched `nsisLang.js` is disabled.
- After `rm -rf node_modules/app-builder-lib && bun install --frozen-lockfile`, both the new `nsisLang.js` change and the existing extraction hooks are applied.
- `bun run prepare:preinstalled-plugins`, `bun run changelog:check`, `bun run typecheck` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `bun run test` on macOS: 3483 passed, 6 failed. The same 3 `test/publish.test.ts` failures occur on unmodified `main` here (my sibling cloud checkout is on an old branch); the `preview`, `preview-lifecycle` and `local-debug` failures only occur under full-suite load and pass when those files run alone, with and without this change.

Not checked yet: a real electron-builder Windows build and installing it. The release workflow can only build on a tag today; a separate PR adds a build-only manual run so this branch can be packaged and installed before the next tag.

Installer behavior change: Windows users whose system language is neither English nor Simplified Chinese now see the English installer instead of electron-builder's bundled translation.

author: reliant-01
body:
Friction from reliant's P7a lanes (C0, L2, L3, L4, L5) with `forge fix connect-errors` (#1114, #1137).

## What changes

1. **`--scope <path>` (repeatable/comma-separated)**, like `forge lint --scope`, on every *Scoped* codemod (`connect-errors`, `operatorkit`, `tx-isolation`; `composition-graph` is one whole-tree decision and refuses the flag). Only files under the paths are rewritten and reported on. The reader analysis still reads the whole module. A test outside the scope that would switch to `svcerr.Code` is listed, not rewritten. When that test is the package's *own* test (it calls the package directly), the package stays on `ToConnect` and the test is named. The `--allow-dirty` clean-tree check now looks only inside the scope (git pathspecs). `codemod.Codemod.Run` takes `codemod.Options{Write, Scope}`.
2. **The report names every reader and how it reaches the package**: file:line, the enclosing function, the kind of read, and the reach (`in the package` / `in its own tests` / `<pkg> imports it` / `<pkg> calls it through the interface X.M at …, which *T implements and <site> hands it`). It does this on **every run**. Before, a re-run with nothing left to rewrite said nothing about why the wrappers stayed (L4), and only the first reader was named (L2: `worktree_test.go:322` was never listed).
   - **New edge (L4):** a reader that reaches a handler through a consumer-declared interface counts, but only when production code actually hands the handler's type to that interface. Reliant now reports `triggertools.unwrapConnect … through triggertools.TriggerAPI.ListTriggers … which *trigger.Service implements and internal/app/providers_worker.go:449 hands it`. An interface that is only ever given a generated client (cmd's `triggerDaemonLister`) is not an edge: the client has the handler's method set, but its calls go over the wire.
   - **Dropped edge (L3, and L5's token):** an import from test files alone no longer counts. `chat`'s tests importing `run`/`message`/`streaming`, and `cmd/reliant/cmd`'s test importing `token`, no longer keep those packages wrapped.
3. **Errors read off the wire are not in-process readers.** This covers `*connect.Client` and `*ForClient` stream methods, plus the generated `<svc>connect` client interface and struct. It also follows functions of the module whose every error is one of those (or `nil`, or a fresh `errors.New`/`fmt.Errorf` that wraps only such values), up to 3 calls deep. A `connect.NewError` built inside a test is also not a reader.
4. **After a real run, every file:line is the rewritten file's line.** Positions go through a line diff of each rewritten file, before against after.

The `migrations/v0.1.47/connect-errors` skill is updated to match.

## Corpus fixtures (testdata/connecterrors)
- `viaiface` + `lister` + `compose`: a reader reached through an interface, wired in production → kept, and the report names the reader, the interface call and the wiring site.
- `pingsvc` + `cliapp`: an interface with the handler's method set that is only ever given a generated client → bare.
- `testonly` + `reader_test.go`: a test-only import → bare. The importer's test `CodeOf` becomes `svcerr.Code`.
- `wired` + `wireclient/pingv1connect`: direct `*connect.Client` reads, and reads of a generated client through a `%w`-wrapping helper → bare.
- `asserted_test.go`: a second reader in one package → both are listed.
- The wire test now covers each new handler, plus lister's in-process read (`%T %v`). Output is identical before and after the rewrite.
- New tests: `TestConnectErrors_ScopeRewritesOnlyItsSlice` (a file scope with its own tests out of scope; a package scope with an importer test out of scope), `TestParseScope`, `TestLineMapper`, `TestFix_CodemodScope`. `assertSitesOnDisk` checks every file:line in dry and real reports against the file on disk. Re-runs stay no-ops (idempotence), and they still name every kept package.

## Verified on reliant (main 6cefea67, a scratch worktree, since removed)
- Dry run: the 17 packages C0 kept on `ToConnect` drop to **13**. `inbox`, `run`, `message` and `streaming` were only ever held by test-only imports, so their wrappers now drop. `daemon_registry` and `project` get no false edges from `cmd/reliant/cmd`.
- Real run: **523/523** reported file:line sites match the file on disk. The re-run gives 0 rewrites and still names all 13 kept packages. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/handlers/...` pass. `go test -short` passes for inbox, run, message, streaming, chat, trigger and triggertools (the DB-backed tests are skipped under -short).

## Local gate (forge)
- `task test -- ./internal/codemod/... ./internal/cli/fix/...` (race, count=1): ok.
- `go test -short -run 'Codemod|Upgrade|Pin' ./internal/cli/`: ok.
- New fast tests run 3x: ok.
- `forge lint --quiet --scope internal/codemod --scope internal/cli/fix --scope internal/cli/upgrade_codemod.go --scope internal/cli/generate_forge_pin.go`: 14 gating linters passed.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connection still renders host-read pending and failure feedback directly from imperative request fields.

## User Impact

Connection keeps the loaded host and activity history visible during refresh, keeps the failure message visible through a held retry, and recovers when that retry succeeds. Editing connection and session settings remains responsive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing plain owner now exposes a completion receipt for each system-info read. A deferred Solid read consumes the accepted result; `latest()` retains that result while the next read is pending. Narrow Loading/Errored boundaries present feedback without holding connection changes or replacing the host, history, or draft controls.

The shared system-info cache, ten-second poll cadence, cancellation and capability checks remain authoritative. Ping remains a separate rolling measurement and creates no readiness promise. The lazy route, host tags, CSS classes and selectors are unchanged.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI and UI-pages test typechecks | Passed |
| Connection page tests | 25/25 passed on pinned Bun; held retry retains failure, host DOM, session draft and focus |
| Connection rendering tests | 13/13 passed |
| Targeted lint/format and whitespace | Passed |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Paired production builds / strict performance | Passed; startup 316,537 → 316,504 B gzip (-33 B, within 64 B build variance), 7 JS requests; CSS 40,894 B / 1 request unchanged |
| Production Knip | Exact base/head logs byte-identical: two pre-existing unused heartbeat files; no new findings or ignores |
| Visual states | All five before/after captures passed and were inspected: initial host loading, ready, refresh pending, failure, retry pending; synthetic fixtures, no browser errors |

Production LOC: 971 → 1,034 (+63 across three files). The added code carries accepted completion through cancellation/retry and scopes native feedback to the existing host/activity sections.

<details>
<summary>Solid 2 checklist in the touched production files</summary>

| Item | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Conditional intrinsic handler binding | 0 → 0 |
| 2. Component cleanup | 0 → 0 |
| 3. Manual read presentation | 1 → 0; deferred reads 0 → 1; Loading 0 → 2; Errored 0 → 1 |
| 4. Mutation feedback | 0 → 0 |
| 5. Manual component loaders | 0 → 0 |
| 6. Copied collection signals | 0 → 0 |
| 7. Hand-written component creation | 0 → 0 |
| 8. Throw-only context wrappers | 0 → 0 |
| 9. Sibling loading groups | 0 → 0 |
| 10. Component owner APIs | 0 → 0 |

Accepted owner facts: `statusFailed` records the accepted result, while its completion drives native presentation. Ping is telemetry whose payload is discarded, with bounded samples and a latest-failure marker. Host and activity share one system-info read, so no Reveal group applies. Connection/session edits keep their synchronous Gateway owner operations.
</details>

Before is on the left and after on the right. Full frames were inspected; only local test port, measured ping and build-hash footer differ.

## Summary

The published ElizaOS plugin (0.11.1) can add paid items the user did not ask for:

- **Premium Plan from substrings.** Registration intents used `text.includes('pro')`, so "Quote promptbot.xyz" or any message with "provide" or "professional" quoted and paid for the **Pro** plan. "starter" and "enterprise" inside other words behaved the same way.

author: gracedeternalkingcabbageman
body:
Ambra's user composer led both pickers with BTC but offered no BTC trade: the app gave the engine no Bitcoin Lightning wallet. This is the web wallet's BTC leg (web wallet #199/#200), ported.

- `user_trade_btc.dart`: `user-trade-btc.js` in Dart. The BTC receiver makes the hash, the asset's giver locks first, and BTC is paid only once the leaf received under the hash is held for good. A payment is held to its route's whole lock (`payRoute`), and the leaf's `need_seconds` is sized from that lock.
- `btc_lightning.dart`: the wallet's own hosted Bitcoin node, over the LSP. A sale's hold is under a hash whose preimage the phone draws and stores before asking the node for anything. The phone settles only when the whole amount is held with blocks to spare, never for a cancelled trade, and registers the hold again if the node forgot it. A payment's routing fee is capped at the ticket's, and a payment is called failed only on a refusal or when nothing is in flight. The first BTC trade brings the node up. A sale for more than the node can receive is not offered.
- `user_trade.dart`: the smallest seam, a nullable `btc` dependency read at each use, and `btc-gateway` entries only when it is set. The phone also asks the BTC maker at `/leafmaker-btc` (testnet-ops #36).

Tests: `btc_lightning_test.dart` and `user_trade_btc_test.dart`, 13 between them, including a two-hop route case (fee on the ticket, delay 52 → `needSeconds(52)` and maxDelay 58). Whole suite `flutter test` 423/0 on this branch rebased on main; analyze clean on every touched file. No Rust touched. The service calls it uses need the LSP at web wallet main ≥ 71ddb449, restarted. The emulator run against the regtest stack follows.

author: jbookout
body:
## Summary

Delete the once-per-minute control-plane tick and generic ledger execution stack. Native schedulers retain recurrence.

```diff
- launchd → control-plane tick → database queue → generic dispatcher
+ launchd → existing job command
```

Joe approved these deletions on 2026-10-22: "God yes, please get rid of the crap like this that prevents progress and slows down everything".

The supplied background-jobs audit measured 21,193 ticks, 3 successful runs, and 7,538 overlapping wakes. The patch removes the adapter, plist, runner, collectors, provider dispatch, production sync wrapper, overlap watchdog check, obsolete tests, and schedule-board ledger projection.

## Decisions

author: jaheba
body:
Builds on [pydantic/monty#1089](https://github.com/pydantic/monty/pull/1089) and implements the method-call preparation proposed in [pydantic/monty#1107](https://github.com/pydantic/monty/issues/1107).

Resolve `q.m` before evaluating arguments, then call the prepared callable with its optional receiver. Missing attributes now fail before argument side effects, and argument evaluation cannot replace the selected method. Builtin methods can also be saved and called bound or unbound.

Retain the legacy `CallAttr`, `CallAttrKw`, `CallAttrExtended`, and `MethodDictMerge` encodings and dispatch paths. New dumps use version 14; the loader still accepts version 13. Preserve the existing identity and hash behavior of `chain.from_iterable`.

Regression tests cover argument evaluation order, native binding, saved method keys, and genuine #1089 dumps with suspended legacy calls. Each suspended legacy call is dumped again using version 14 before resuming.

Validation:
- Compatibility, method lookup, and REPL tests: 110 passed.
