author: gabewillen
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gabewillen"} -->
_Requested by **Gabe** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Co4kW44AMpRkba9egtneRp?thread=cmsg_01Co4kW44AMpRkba9egtneRp7tKnApwGMVpo9AomWhTP2k)_

**Stacked on `claude/project-thread-a9rb2x` at `9b2ccaae`.** This PR targets main, so its diff also includes that branch's commits until that branch merges. Review from `ca8fc5d3` onward.

This is workstream 4 (body and room) of the parity plan. It closes gaps B1 to B7. Its decisions are D155 to D160.

## What changes

- **B1 and B2, focus (D155).**
  - `bot.clear_focus` is removed, with no alias.
  - Focus stays on a device until the bot focuses another one.
  - An unfocused body focuses the device of the input that starts a turn.
  - At a turn's end, the reflex floor focuses the first held percept's device.
- **B3, percepts (D156).**
  - A busy body now holds what arrives instead of deferring it (`floppy.held`).
  - The next turn takes the longest arrival-order prefix that fits within 8 percepts, 65536 bytes and 32 participants. A single percept is passed as itself; several become one `bot.perceived {percepts}`.
  - When the bot is deactivated, rebooted or degraded, that transition logs whatever is still held as `floppy.released {count, reason}`. Released percepts are never replayed.
  - Each turn's environment counts `held_percepts`.
  - Attention bias and autonomy match each percept on its own. Autonomy's unhandled `acted` is the reference's `{percepts, acts}`.
  - In a batch that is only partly handled, selections that name no target are dispatched only after the cognition carries `acted.acts` into the turn's output. That is the cognition tiers' change C9, on `claude/project-thread-qn1yop`.
- **B4, participants (D157).**
  - `bot.input` carries `participants`.
  - Every schema inlines the original's one `Participant`, because scxml.rs refuses a cross-file `$ref`. `contracts.rs` checks that every inlined copy is the same.
  - Host `bot.input` is still accepted.
- **B7, supervision (D158).**
  - The room's `present` state is a parallel. `keeping` holds membership and delivery, and each bot runs in its own `supervising.<bot>` region.
  - A bot that degrades, fails, or fails to activate is restarted, with the original's budget and doubling backoff. Once the budget is spent, it is left down.
  - `stable_after_ms` is counted once, from the bot's first `bot.activated` (`starting.<bot>` → `serving.<bot>`). When it elapses, the bot's attempts reset.
  - A `bot.deactivate` stops the bot for good, including one that arrives during backoff.
- **B5, objects (D159).** The room's `objects` let a device sit on an object (`placed_on`), rendered as `<device ... on="desk">`.
- **B6, firmware (D160).**
  - Once every ability is ready, the body invokes `firmware` by `srcexpr`, under a 30 s start bound.
  - The default firmware, `bots/floppy/firmware/firmware.scx`, offers nothing.
  - An owner's firmware is handled like an ability: its choices are offered, its reports take turns, and it is read each turn and rendered as `<firmware ref id state>`.
  - A test that lays out the body must also copy `bots/floppy/firmware/`.
- **Fixes from review.**
  - A batched turn could overflow scxml.rs's 64 KiB event bound and leave the body stuck in `processing`. The turn timer is now armed before the send, and `error.execution` fails the turn.
  - The release reason no longer depends on `_event.name`.
  - The stability timer is no longer re-armed on every reboot.

Edits to shared files are in their own commits. The bless commits say what drove each trace change. Most of the trace changes in `fdc714a3` come from four things: the ignore description no longer names `bot.clear_focus`, the firmware start step, `held_percepts`, and the restart after a failed activation (see `90124d1f`).

## Testing

- `cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and the `floppy-cognition` unit tests pass.
- These integration suites pass: `body`, `environment`, `contracts`, `defaults`, `communication`, `identity` and `cognition`.
- The `document_irp` suites for the documents this PR changes pass: `autonomy`, `floppy`, `cognition` and `reasoning`. The full run was cut off at the 2 h limit, so it was run per suite.
- Traces were re-blessed with `FLOPPY_TRACE_BLESS=1` for this intended change.
- Known gaps:
  - Nothing tests a restart after `error.communication.<bot>`. I found no way to make a child session fail without fault injection in the engine.
  - Nothing tests `floppy.released` with reason `rebooted`. The cognition double can't reboot while percepts are held without a race.
- Pre-existing flake: `deactivate_while_activating_is_answered_and_cancels_the_abilities` failed once under 4-thread load. It sends `bot.deactivate` before the bot has joined the room, and it passes when run alone.

author: tchughesiv
body:
## NO-ISSUE: retry NetworkClass cleanup while child VirtualNetworks are active

**Summary**

The ComputeInstance fixture cleanup (`cleanupComputeInstanceFixture`) deletes
the suite-created NetworkClass after waiting for its child VirtualNetwork to
disappear. The server can still count the deleted VirtualNetwork as active
when the class delete arrives, rejecting it with `FailedPrecondition` and
failing the cleanup. Because the failed cleanup leaves the NetworkClass
behind, the next spec's `BeforeEach` (which requires the deployment's single
NetworkClass slot) fails too, cascading two spec failures.

Observed in the `Integration test (fulfillment-service) / it-fulfillment-service`
required CI job:

```
[FAIL] ComputeInstance with Subnet attachment [AfterEach]
  uses tenant defaults when network_attachments is omitted
  fixture cleanup delete failed: rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc =
  cannot delete NetworkClass 'cudn-subnet-...': 1 active VirtualNetwork resource
[FAIL] ComputeInstance with Subnet attachment [BeforeEach]
  rejects ComputeInstance without attachments when the tenant has no default subnet
  NetworkClasses/Create -> FailedPrecondition
```

**Fix**

Retry the NetworkClass delete with a bounded `Eventually` (1 minute, 1s poll)
that treats `NotFound` as success, until the server-side active count clears,
then keep the existing wait-for-NotFound. This matches the retry conventions
used by the neighboring fixture helpers.

**Testing**

- `go vet ./it/`, `gofmt`, and `go test -c ./it` compile checks pass.
- CI exercises the full `SUITE=fulfillment` suite on this PR; the retried
  cleanup path runs in every spec of the `ComputeInstance with Subnet
  attachment` Describe.

**Scope note**

The other NetworkClass delete sites were checked: `createCatalogItemNetworkClassFixture`
creates a standalone class with no child VirtualNetwork (no exposure), and the
tenant-default fixture cleanup runs after the caller's default-networking
cleanup, so its ordering differs. Only the observed failing path is changed.

author: andtii
body:
`collect` walked a module's `export *` chains again for every name imported from it (`namespace_exports` rebuilt the target's whole export list per imported name, and `export_names` followed every path through a diamond of barrels down to depth 32) and found each import specifier by a linear scan of the module's imports. Importing a package through barrels, as sigx's packages are, was quadratic or worse in the names: on sigx-core, `collect` was 87% of `velt check` (1.1 s of 1.3 s per round, four rounds).

Each module's export names and export table are now built once, in one pass with the precedence `export_at` gives (own `export`ed declarations, then export lists in order, then each `export *` in order; the first one naming a name decides it). Lookups are binary searches, and namespace members (`N.x`) are a range of the sorted names. An import that binds namespace members which a module's export list names (`export { ns }`) drops what was computed, as those change what the module exports. A cycle of `export *` falls back to the name-by-name walk. Import specifiers resolve through an index built once per check.

`VELT_SEMA_TIMINGS=1` prints the time of each pass in each round of the checker (docs/internals/README.md), which is how this was found.

Measured (release, Apple M-series, best of 5, CPU time; signalxjs/core at `021c056` with the server shim of #379):

| `velt check` | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| SSR entry (`renderToString`: reactivity, runtime-core, server-renderer, serialize) | 1.96 s | 1.08 s |
| every sigx-core package | 13.2 s | 2.2 s |
| `bench/compile/all_std.vlt` | 0.145 s | 0.143 s |
| a generated app of 2,715 files | 1.00 s | 1.01 s |

(The machine was loaded during this table; on an idle machine every sigx-core package went from 5.2 s to 0.8 s.) Diagnostics are byte-identical before and after on all three sigx entries and on the generated app.

Tests: `imports_through_barrels_grow_linearly` in `crates/velt_sema/tests/scaling.rs` checks a package of N modules behind a diamond of barrels whose every name the root imports by name, at N = 100, 400, 1600, and requires the cost per module to stay flat. It passes in 2 s; on `main` it did not finish in 10 minutes.

Refs #379, #1370.

author: ionutneicu
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ionutneicu"} -->
_Requested by **Ionut** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AjDsovfVBDU2xDV6EvWxnG?thread=cmsg_01AjDsovfVBDU2xDV6EvWxnGQLhePLZ7C7rSu3rwFoACup)_

Step 1 of the plan (the measurement core), plus the first memory-hierarchy benchmark and its graphs.

## What changes

- **HAL (plain C headers)**
  - `olt/hal/arch.h` + `arch/x86_64.h`, `arch/aarch64.h`, `arch/generic.h`: cycle counter (`rdtsc` with lfence / `cntvct_el0`), prefetch read L1/L2/L3/NTA + write, barriers, cpu_relax, cache line flush (`clflush` / `dc civac`), cache line size (CPUID / `CTR_EL0`).
  - `olt/hal/os.h` + `src/hal/linux/os_linux.c`: monotonic clock, affinity, SCHED_FIFO, mlockall, pre-faulted buffers with THP control, cache topology from sysfs, CPU/board/kernel/preempt model, governor, isolated CPUs, THP policy, RAM.
  - `olt/hal/perf.h`: optional counters. `perf_event_open` backend (generic HW/cache + software events, each probed separately, multiplex-scaled) or stub, chosen with **`-DOLT_WITH_PERF=AUTO|ON|OFF`**.
- **Harness (C++17)**: tick calibration, timer overhead, `OLT_BENCHMARK(...)` self-registration, warm-up, stats (min/max/mean/stddev/MAD, p50/p90/p99/p99.9/p99.99 with type-7 interpolation, percentiles flagged unreliable when < ~10 samples are in the tail).
- **Output**: console table, `results.json` (platform + config + summaries), raw per-sample CSV.
- **Benchmarks**
  - Ported: `thread.create_to_start`, `thread.exit_to_join`, `sync.mutex_wakeup`, `sync.condvar_wakeup`, `alloc.malloc`/`alloc.free`. The wake-up tests now use a persistent worker. The old mutex test unlocked a `std::mutex` from a thread that didn't own it, which is UB; that's fixed.
  - New `mem.cache_sweep`: random pointer-chase latency (`mem.latency_random`) and sequential read/write cost (`mem.read_seq`, `mem.write_seq`) over one pre-faulted buffer, for buffer sizes from 1 KiB up to 4x the LLC, 4 sizes per doubling.
- **`tools/olt-report.py`** (stdlib only, installed as `olt-report`): self-contained HTML report. It graphs latency and bandwidth against working-set size with the L1/L2/L3 sizes drawn as bands, and adds a hover readout, a per-level summary, design hints, and a percentile table for the other benchmarks.
- **CLI**: `--test` globs, `--samples`, `--warmup`, `--affinity`, `--cpus`, `--rt-prio`, `--mlock`, `--park-us`, `--mem-min/--mem-max`, `--sweep-steps`, `--sweep-samples`, `--hugepages`, `--out`.
- **Tooling**: unit tests + smoke run + report in ctest, `cmake/toolchains/aarch64-linux-gnu.cmake` (ctest runs under qemu), GitHub Actions CI (gcc, clang, generic/no-perf, aarch64 cross, .deb), `debian/` packaging, README with build dependencies and porting guide.

## Testing

- x86-64 gcc 13, clang, and the generic-HAL/no-perf variant: all ctest tests pass, no warnings.
- aarch64 cross-build: all tests pass under qemu-user. The code hasn't run on real ARM hardware yet.
- `dpkg-buildpackage -b` produces an amd64 .deb with `os-latency-tests` and `olt-report`.
- Cache sweep on an x86-64 VM shows clear steps at L1 (48 KiB), L2 (2 MiB) and towards DRAM. Report checked in light and dark mode.

## Open items

- `debian/copyright` says `License: TODO` until a LICENSE is chosen.
- Maintainer email in `debian/` is taken from the git history; change it if needed.

Lib fix: `TestAdapter#filtered_time?` (`activejob/lib/active_job/queue_adapters/test_adapter.rb:61-63`, `job.scheduled_at > at`) called Comparable's `greaterThan` on a `Time`. `Time` spells `<=>` as `compare`, not `compareTo`, so the call crashed with `this.compareTo is not a function` whenever a block-form `perform_enqueued_jobs(at:)` enqueued a scheduled job. It now uses `rbCmpint(cmp(a, b), a, b) > 0`, which is `cmp_gt` (`vendor/ruby/v3.3.11/compar.c`).

author: psaab
body:
Refs #16153

## Why

W2.4 narrowed survivor (validated-by:research, Codex C binding on P8):

- **P3:** the retained-snapshot partial publishers (route-overlay, capture-authority, link-refresh, policy-scheduler, deferred worker-arm) each hand-rolled `clone -> bump -> hash -> dedup -> publish -> adopt` over `next := *m.lastSnapshot`; the copies drifted (the #15955 triple hash was one drift) and the route-vs-capture dedup predicates differ in ways only one copy documented.
- **P4:** `stampCaptureAuthorityWithRoutesMode` (builder.go) and `refreshCaptureAuthorityLocked` assigned the same four capture fields field-by-field and could drift.
- **P2-narrowed:** `PolicyRuleSnapshot.Action` / `DefaultPolicy` were stringly typed; the send gate checked counts only, so an empty/malformed/future action token shipped to the helper relying solely on the Rust reader.
- **P8-narrowed (canary-aware):** no standalone `binding_plan.go` move — `snapshotBindingPlanKey` et al. stay in `maps_sync.go` where `binding_plan_key_crossplane_8901_test.go`'s source-text canaries read them.

## What

- New `manager_partial_publish.go`: `cloneRetainedSnapshotLocked` (single-use strip under the pending-full latch), `bumpRetainedGenerationLocked`, `preparePrehashedPublish` (single #15955 hash), `dedupHit` (hash match + #9520/#9684 unknown-outcome stand-downs), `adoptPublishedSnapshotLocked`, and `copyPreparedSectionsBack`/`adoptPreparedPublishLocked` (#15043) for the non-prehashed scheduler/worker-arm senders. Publishers keep their prep, protocol/disarm gates, error wrapping, and their own dedup predicate: capture ANDs `publishedSnapshot != 0`, link-refresh ANDs `resampled == 0` — characterized, not unified. `syncSnapshotLocked` deliberately not extracted (distinct retained-publish shape, no clone twin).
- P4: both capture stamps go through `captureAuthorityFields.applyTo` — the single detached writer of the four fields. Per-publisher detach only; no blanket deep clone.
- P2: typed `policyAction` vocabulary (`permit`/`deny`/`reject`, deliberately not unified with the filter `accept`/`discard` set) + `typedPolicyAction`; `validateSnapshotForSend` refuses unknown/empty rule actions and non-empty garbage defaults as known-unsent (`errSnapshotPolicyAction`, matched by `isKnownUnsentFailure` — no retry debt). `policyActionString` lowers through the typed tokens, deny fail-closed default. Rust enum remains the enforcement backstop, does not gate.
- #15955 hash leg reused, not re-fixed (coordination note in the issue).

## Validation

- New `partial_publish_16153_test.go`: capture dedup characterization (**RED** when the `publishedSnapshot` arm is dropped: unpublished capture republish returns `(false, nil)`), capture stamp detach+parity, send-gate differential table (known tokens + empty default admitted; empty/future/malformed/filter-vocab refused known-unsent), typed vocabulary + lowerer defaults, binding-plan helper reachability (P8 non-vacuity).
- Existing pins intact: `TestPublishHashDedup*15955` (overlay exactly-1-hash), route-overlay/capture/link-refresh/scheduler/worker-arm republish suites.
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` run: only pre-existing failures, base-attributed on `974028945c` (lab socket-path length, WG degenerate-key and unit/vlan config gates, owner-key parity) — identical on clean `origin/master`.
- `go vet` / `gofmt` clean.

## Risk

Behavior preserved by construction (same dedup predicates, one hash per publish, ACK-then-retained-cache). Link-refresh saved pub.snap before the send, so a #9520 content-conflict retry that republished at generation 9 was adopted as stale 8 (helper held 9; manager/retained/published/applied stayed 8). Fix: pub.snap = publishSnap after successful send in RefreshInterfaceRowsForLink, matching route-overlay/capture callers, so adoptPublishedSnapshotLocked commits the generation actually carried (also repairs postPublishHash preSendClear snapshot and binding-plan key inputs). New call-site regression TestInterfaceLinkRefreshAdoptsConflictRetryGeneration16153 (manager_link_refresh_test.go): conflict at 8 then ACK at 9, asserts sent [8 9] and generation/last/published/applied all 9 — RED without fix (all 8), GREEN with it. Reviewer-command suite passes (5 tests incl. preserved 9520 scheduler/overlay/worker-arm pins); go vet/gofmt clean.

## Fold 2 (heartbeat fixtures + honest full-run attribution, head 1523054735)

Rebased onto master 26003e3408. TestScheduledSnapshotSeedsBestEffortHeartbeat11285 and TestScheduledReintroductionSendsHeartbeatBeforeApply15093 built PolicyRuleSnapshot with empty Action, so the new send gate refused before any heartbeat was reached; fixtures now carry Action "permit" plus Summary.PolicyCount=1 (the #15742 count arm — both tests also fail on clean current master for the count reason alone). Honest full comparison (pkg/dataplane/userspace, -count=1 -json, top-level names, same TMPDIR/GOCACHE method): PR head 119 failing, clean master 26003e3408 125 failing, PR set is a strict subset of base — zero PR-only failures. Delta: the 2 heartbeat tests fixed here + 4 flaky/env-sensitive base-only names (TestDisabledInterfaceNoPendingOrVIPLeak13149, TestPartialRepublishRefusesQuarantineOnlySkew12247, TestStalledSyslogDoesNotParkEventReader11697, TestTrunkWithNoUnitZeroPutsNoUnitRowOnTheParentIfindex_7509) that flip independently on both trees. body:
## 변경 요약
- **기본 LLM 모델 변경:** `gpt-5-mini` → `gpt-6-luna` (추론 강도 `low`). 메뉴 계획, 채팅 설명에 적용
- **리뷰 한 줄 요약은 `gpt-5-mini` (추론 강도 `medium`) 유지:** `zelo.llm.review-summary.model`, `zelo.llm.review-summary.reasoning-effort` 설정 추가. `SpringAiLlmGateway.summarizeReviews`만 요청 옵션으로 이 모델을 보냄
- **LLM 시간 제한 `zelo.llm.timeout`:** `5s` → `12s`
- **실패 로그 모델명:** `ResilientLlmGateway`가 실패 로그에 요청별 모델을 남김 (리뷰 요약 실패 시 `gpt-5-mini`로 기록)
- **리뷰 요약 프롬프트에 식품 안전 규칙 추가:** 맛·취향·배송 소수 의견은 빼고, 상함·곰팡이·이물질·유통기한·먹고 탈이 남 같은 식품 안전 의견은 1건이라도 "일부 ~라는 의견도 있어요"로 포함

## 근거 (실측)
### 메뉴 계획: gpt-6-luna low가 더 정확하고, 빠르고, 싸다
| 모델 | 정확도 | p95 | 5초 초과 | 가격 (입력/출력, 1M 토큰) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-5-mini (기존) | 93.3% | 15.3s | 85% | $0.25 / $2.00 |
| **gpt-6-luna low** | **98.3%** | **7.5s** | 68% | **$0.10 / $0.50** |

- 정확도: 인원·예산·조건 키워드·목록 안 재료를 맞힌 비율 (조합당 60번)
- 같은 입력으로 다시 잰 속도: 평균 10.0s → **4.4s**

### 리뷰 요약: 지금 프롬프트는 gpt-5-mini가 더 잘 지킨다
- 리뷰 요약 실험(300번)의 요약 원문을 다시 읽고 채점: "한두 명 의견은 빼라" 규칙을 **gpt-5-mini 88% vs gpt-6-luna 68%**. luna는 "~평이 많지만 짜게 느낀 분도 있어요"처럼 소수 의견을 덧붙이는 습관이 있었음
- 식품 안전 규칙 실험(조합당 18번, 원문 재채점): **gpt-5-mini 18/18**, gpt-6-luna 17/18. 두 모델 모두 안전 의견은 12/12 포함, 부풀림("의견이 갈려요") 0번
- 요약은 사용자가 기다리는 호출이 아니라 상품마다 미리 만들어 저장하므로, 속도(mini 평균 7.1s)보다 품질을 우선

## 팀 확인 필요
- [ ] 기본 모델 `gpt-6-luna` low 변경과 timeout `12s`에 동의하는지
- [ ] Day 6 툴 호출 경로: gpt-6-luna는 Chat Completions에서 툴 호출을 **추론 none일 때만** 지원함. 툴 경로의 모델은 따로 측정해서 정해야 함
- [ ] 리뷰 요약에 식품 안전 의견을 소수라도 넣는 정책에 동의하는지

## 테스트 방법
- `./gradlew test --tests 'com.server.zelo.ai.llm.*'`
  - `SpringAiLlmGatewayTimeoutTest`: 일반 요청 본문에 `"model":"gpt-6-luna","reasoning_effort":"low"`
  - `ReviewSummaryHttpTest`: 리뷰 요약 요청 본문에 `"model":"gpt-5-mini","reasoning_effort":"medium"`
  - `SpringAiLlmGatewayMockTest`: 리뷰 요약 요청 옵션에 리뷰용 모델·추론 강도·timeout
  - `ResilientLlmGatewayTest`: 리뷰 요약 실패 로그에 리뷰용 모델명
  - `ReviewSummaryPromptTest`: 프롬프트에 식품 안전 규칙 포함
- 로컬: real 모드로 앱 실행 후 메뉴 계획·리뷰 요약 호출 → 로그의 `model=` 값 확인

## 참고
- 이 브랜치는 `feat/review-seed` 위에 쌓여 있음. 리뷰 시드 PR이 먼저 머지돼야 이 PR에 커밋 2개만 보임

人不在键盘前时（离开工位、在另一个房间）没法给本机 Claude Code / Codex 会话派活。

- 新增 `satellite/` 离线收音端（sherpa-onnx，不进 App 安装包）：说「小卡拉米」→ 叮 → 说一句话 → 本地转文字 → 交给 App 走与输入框相同的路由 → 用 `say` 播报结果。一口气连着唤醒词说，开头也不丢（唤醒后从唤醒词结尾补回缓冲音频）。

- 路由拿不准时不发送、不弹窗抢焦点：这句放进空输入框，回到电脑按快捷键确认；框里已有没发出去的话就不拼接（两件事拼成一句会送错），播报"回到电脑再说一次"。

author: roboaholic
body:
## 背景
用户要求把之前删掉的手机连接（二维码配对）页面加回来，放进「实验性」设置菜单。这个页面原来是在 #70 里删掉的。#70 同时让桌面端彻底停用 Anchor Relay：不建、不启动 RelayConnector，删掉 `remote:*` IPC 和 preload API，去掉 `qrcode` 依赖。

## 改动
1. **Settings 新增 `Experimental` 分组**：导航现在是 Appearance / Agent / Updates / Experimental。设置界面原来就是英文，所以分组名也用英文。样式和其他分组一致。`openSettings("experimental")` 可以直接打开这一页。
2. **Experimental 页放回 Mobile access**（新文件 `SettingsExperimentalSection.tsx`）：
   - 页面最上面有一条提示，用现有的 `--warn-bg / --warn-border / --warn` 颜色。内容是：这是实验功能，以后可能会改或删；启动时默认关闭；重启后会自动关掉。
   - 恢复了原来的内容：Relay 状态胶囊（disabled / connecting / online / offline）、Encrypted relay 卡片、Devices（已配对设备和待批准请求，可以 Approve / Reject / Revoke）、Quick pairing 二维码。
   - 原来手写的 checkbox 开关换成了共享的 `Switch` 控件。原来的 Apply / Disable 两个按钮去掉了，拨动开关就直接生效。
   - 颜色全部用现有主题变量（去掉了原 CSS 里的 hex 兜底色）。唯一例外是二维码出现时底色是白色，因为二维码必须黑码白底才扫得出来；没有二维码时占位区用 `--bg-muted`。另外修了原来的一个小 bug：状态类名 `is-connected` 和实际状态 `online` 对不上，导致 online 时不变绿。
   - 没有原生 `title` tooltip，有测试保证。
3. **重新加回 `qrcode` / `@types/qrcode` 依赖**。

## Relay 行为（重点）
- **启动时永远不连 Relay**：`main.ts` 只创建一个轻量的 `RemoteAccessController`，不创建 `RelayConnector` 和 `RemoteRequestHandler`，也不读旧配置去调用 start。旧 settings.json 里就算还有 `remoteAccess.relay.enabled: true`，`loadSettings()` 照样当作关闭（保留 #70 的逻辑）。
- **只有用户在 Experimental 页拨开开关才会连接**：开关通过 `remote:update({ enabled: true })` 调到 controller。controller 这时才懒加载创建 RelayConnector 和请求处理器，再用持久化的 relay 身份（roomId / hostPeerId / ticket / secret）启动。
- **开关状态只在本次运行有效、不写盘**：settings.json 里的 `enabled` 一直是 `false`。重启 App 后 Relay 一定是关的，要用就再拨一次开关。relay 身份会持久化，这样已配对的手机在下次打开时还认得这台电脑。
- 关掉开关会立刻 `stop()`；App 退出时 `dispose()` 会释放 Relay 和请求处理器。
- 只打开 Experimental 页不会启动 Relay：页面只调 `remote:getInfo`，而且只在开关打开时才每秒轮询一次。

## 测试
- 新增 `electron/remote/remoteAccessController.test.ts`：不拨开关时不会创建也不会启动 relay；拨开后才 start，带 `enabled: true`；关掉会 stop；第二次打开复用同一个 relay；关闭状态下 approve / revoke 会报错；dispose 会释放。
- `electron/settings.relay.test.ts`：旧配置里 relay 开着，读出来仍是关闭；新增 `getRemoteRelayIdentity()` 用例，身份保持稳定、返回和写盘的 `enabled` 都是 false。
- `architectureBoundaries.test.ts`：把“桌面端永远不接 Relay”改成“启动时不启动 Relay”。main 里不调 `relay.start(` 和 `setEnabled(`，也不在顶层 `new RelayConnector`；IPC 里唯一调用 `setEnabled` 的地方是 `remote:update`。
- `SettingsPanel.test.tsx`：导航是 `Appearance / Agent / Updates / Experimental`；默认页看不到 Mobile access；Experimental 页有实验提示，开关默认关、状态显示 disabled、没有二维码，打开页面不会调用 `update`；点开关会调用 `update({ enabled: true })`，开关变成打开；页面里没有 `[title]`。
- `npm run typecheck` 通过；`npm run lint` 0 errors（25 条 warning，和 main 一样）。
- `vitest`：792 passed / 4 skipped。失败的 6 个文件都是本地已知问题：box 上没有 g++，node-pty 跑不起来（localHost ×2、terminalService）；另外 sshConfig ×2、terminalStore 'shares concurrent resets'、mobile/web 的 App.agent 和 sessionCrypto，main 上一样失败。以 CI 为准。

## 实机验证（Linux 打包，Xvfb 1920×1200）
- 用一份旧的 settings.json（`remoteAccess.enabled` 和 `relay.enabled` 都是 true）启动：Experimental 页显示 **Disabled**，开关是关的，没有二维码。
- 拨开开关后，几秒内状态变成 **Online**，显示二维码（Dark Modern 和 Light Modern 都试过）。退出后 settings.json 里两个 `enabled` 都还是 `false`。
- 截图（Dark / Light × 关 / 开）已经单独发给用户确认。**UI 改动，确认前不要合并。**

author: pgermosen
body:
## Summary

Part of #6046 (part 10). A Task can now use the seven optimized Amazon EMR integrations the Step Functions guide lists, which failed with `Unsupported resource` before: `createCluster`, `setClusterTerminationProtection`, `terminateCluster`, `addStep`, `cancelStep`, `modifyInstanceFleetByName` and `modifyInstanceGroupByName`, with `.sync` for `createCluster`, `terminateCluster` and `addStep`.

- **Calls:** a new `EmrTaskInvoker` calls Floci's EMR in the state machine's Region, under the guide's field names: `ClusterId` where EMR takes `JobFlowIds` or `JobFlowId`, a single `Step` or `StepId`, and the fleet or group found by name through `ListInstanceFleets` or `ListInstanceGroups`.
- **`.sync`:** records `TaskSubmitted` with the call's result, then polls `DescribeCluster` or `DescribeStep` under the Task's `TimeoutSeconds` and the execution's budget, as `ecs:runTask.sync` does. The result is the describe response with the call's result after it.
- **Failures:** a step that ends `FAILED`, `CANCELLED` or `INTERRUPTED`, or a cluster that terminates before `WAITING`, fails the Task with `States.TaskFailed` and the describe response as the cause. When the wait ends early (a timeout or `StopExecution`), an `addStep.sync` cancels its step; a cluster is left running.
- **EMR errors** fail the Task under the SDK exception class: `EMR.InvalidRequestException` and `EMR.InternalServerException` for the two errors EMR models, `EMR.AmazonElasticMapReduceException` for anything else.
- **Refusals:** a `createCluster` whose `Instances.KeepJobFlowAliveWhenNoSteps` isn't `true`, or that carries `Steps`, an `addStep` without a `Step`, an id in a ByName request, and a name matching no group or fleet, or more than one. A Task without the `ClusterId` its API acts on, a `cancelStep` without a `StepId`, or a ByName request without its name fails too, before EMR sees it. `.waitForTaskToken` and `.sync` on the other four APIs are unsupported resources.

Changes to EMR on the integrations' path:
- `AddJobFlowSteps` on an unknown cluster, or one in another Region, is `ValidationException` "Specified job flow ID does not exist." It answered `DescribeCluster`'s `InvalidRequestException`.
- On a terminated cluster, `ModifyInstanceGroups` is `ValidationException` "An instance group may only be modified when the cluster is running or waiting." and `ModifyInstanceFleet` is `InvalidRequestException` "A job flow that is shutting down, terminated, or finished may not be modified." with `ErrorCode` `INVALID_JOB_SHUT_DOWN`. Before, both answered "Cluster <id> is terminated." `EmrHandler` now sends an error's extra members, such as that `ErrorCode`. `AddInstanceGroups` and `AddInstanceFleet` keep their message, since no source shows AWS's.
- `TerminateJobFlows`, the four `Set*` cluster setters and `CancelSteps` refuse a request without a member their model requires (`JobFlowIds` and the setting, or `StepIds`) with `ValidationException` "1 validation error detected: Value null at 'jobFlowIds' failed to satisfy constraint: Member must not be null", as `RunJobFlow` does for `Name`. They read a missing list as empty and a missing setting as its default (`TerminationProtected` as false) and answered success, which `terminateCluster` and `setClusterTerminationProtection` reached. The not-null violation is now one `SmithyValidationErrors.notNull` helper.

Not here: AWS's polling cadence ("a hard-coded 60 seconds job polling frequency for the first 10 minutes and 300 seconds after that"; Floci polls every 100 ms, as it does for ECS), IAM checks on the EMR calls (none, as for ECS), and the `emr-serverless:` integrations, which are part 11.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [x] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [ ] Docs / chore

## AWS Compatibility

The sources:
- **The integrations:** the Step Functions Developer Guide's "Optimized Amazon EMR APIs" table gives the seven APIs, which of them take `.sync`, the renamed fields, and the `createCluster` rules ("The field Instances.KeepJobFlowAliveWhenNoSteps is mandatory, and must have the Boolean value TRUE." and "The field Steps is not allowed."). The guide also says "Step Functions does not terminate an Amazon EMR cluster automatically if execution is stopped", and that for Run a Job (.sync) it makes "a best-effort attempt to cancel the task", which is why `addStep.sync` cancels its step and a cluster is left alone.
- **`.sync` results:** the `createCluster.sync` output recorded on AWS, a console screenshot in [corvuslee/public](https://github.com/corvuslee/public/tree/master/howto/vscode-stepfunctions_emr), is `Cluster`, the SDK metadata, then `ClusterId`. Floci leaves the SDK metadata out, as it does for every task. AWS's own [sample-emr-transient-cluster-step-functions-eventbridge](https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-emr-transient-cluster-step-functions-eventbridge) reads an `addStep.sync` result's `Step.Status.State`.
- **A failed step:** [anorth848/aws-data-analytics](https://github.com/anorth848/aws-data-analytics) parses a failed `addStep.sync`'s cause with `States.StringToJson` and reads `Step.Status.FailureDetails`, so the cause is the describe response as JSON text.
- **Error names:** the AWS re:Post question [AWS Step Function does not recognize job flow ID](https://repost.aws/questions/QUSo4YGQwtRsqBKcpLJkucWQ/aws-step-function-does-not-recognize-job-flow-id) (2020) shows an `addStep.sync` failing with `EMR.AmazonElasticMapReduceException` for a `ValidationException`, the same rule as the `StepFunctions.AWSStepFunctionsException` Floci already uses. Its CloudTrail record and a botocore error in [raster-foundry/raster-foundry#352](https://github.com/raster-foundry/raster-foundry/issues/352) give `AddJobFlowSteps`' "Specified job flow ID does not exist.".
- **Terminated-cluster modifies:** real responses in hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#1355 and hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#9400 (instance groups) and hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#31375 (instance fleets, with the `ErrorCode`).
- **Not sourced:** the results of `addStep.sync` (its `StepId`) and `terminateCluster.sync` follow the same rule without a recording; the timestamps inside stay EMR's epoch seconds; the error name for a failed step or cluster is not recorded, so it is `States.TaskFailed`; no source shows what AWS answers for a refused request, so the refusals are `States.TaskFailed` too, the `createCluster` ones worded as the guide's rules; and no EMR recording shows the error for a missing required member, so the setters and `CancelSteps` use AWS's framework validation message, as #1731 did for `RunJobFlow`'s `Name`. `docs/services/step-functions.md` says so.

Incorrect behavior fixed: these resources failed with `States.TaskFailed` "Unsupported resource"; `AddJobFlowSteps` and the two modify operations answered with codes and messages no AWS response shows.

## Checklist

- [ ] `./mvnw test` passes locally
- [x] New or updated integration test added
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [ ] I have no more than 2 open, non-draft pull requests and no more than 4 open pull requests in total (drafts included) in this repository (maintainers and dependency bots are exempt).

On the unchecked boxes: I ran the 67 tests of all 8 EMR classes and the two Step Functions EMR ones on the final change, not the whole suite. `./mvnw checkstyle:check` is clean, and `make docs-check` and `make partition-check` are clean on the final branch; CI covers the rest. #6250 and #6251 are open as well.

The tests:
- New `StepFunctionsEmrIntegrationTest` (7), from a state machine outside the default Region: the full flow (`createCluster.sync`, `addStep.sync`, `addStep`, `cancelStep`, `modifyInstanceGroupByName`, `terminateCluster.sync`) with each result and the `TaskSubmitted` details, a fleet resized by name, the `createCluster` refusals, the fields each API needs, the error names, a resize

author: sopika2
body:
Makes Mementos (her Zipline at `mementos.niijimasisters.com`) **the Archive's storage**. Without `ZIPLINE_URL` + `ZIPLINE_TOKEN` the app behaves exactly as before: both modes sit behind one `Storage` interface (`src/lib/server/media/storage.ts`).

## What changes with Zipline set up

- **Every save goes to Zipline:** uploads, share-target files, tweet photos/GIFs/videos and `/api/save`. The media row keeps the Zipline file id, name and public link. Only a WebP thumbnail stays local, now in `data/thumbs/`. Existing thumbnails are moved there on start. Uploads go into a Zipline folder called **Archive**, which is created if missing. `x-zipline-deletes-at: never` is sent so a default expiry can't eat her saves; if her Zipline has a maximum expiry and refuses that header, the upload is retried without it.
- **Nothing is lost.** If Zipline is down or refuses a save, the original is kept on disk and the migration moves it later. If Zipline stores a *changed* copy (it can strip GPS data or compress pictures), the original stays on disk for good (`keep_local`), and the Mementos page counts these.
- **Mementos link right away:** every file has `mirrorUrl` from the moment it is saved. **Copy Mementos link** in the lightbox just copies it. The old upload-on-demand endpoint is kept only for files the migration hasn't reached yet.
- **Viewing streams through the Archive** (`/file/<id>`, `src/lib/server/media/proxy.ts`) with Range/206/416 passed through, plus an ETag. Why proxy rather than redirect:
  - the token stays on the server, and password-protected Zipline files still work;
  - the browser talks to one origin: same CSP and sandbox headers, and it keeps working behind Cloudflare Access;
  - Safari gets proper ranges for video;
  - the traffic between the containers stays on `zipline_default` through `ZIPLINE_INTERNAL_URL` (default `http://zipline:3000`), while links shown to her use `ZIPLINE_URL`.
- **Exports (.zip)** stream each file from Zipline, one after another, so memory stays flat. A file that can't be fetched is listed under `missing_files` in `captions.json`.
- **Delete** asks whether to also delete on Mementos (checkbox, off by default) on the item page and in bulk select. Kept files go into a `zipline_ignored` table, so the sync never brings them back.
- **Sync** (`src/lib/server/mementos.ts`) runs on start, every `zipline.sync_minutes` (5) and on **Sync now**:
  - it pages through her files and imports new pictures and videos as items in a shared **Inbox** collection, with thumbnails (made from the picture, or from Zipline's own video thumbnail), dated by their Zipline `createdAt`;
  - it never duplicates the Archive's own uploads: it knows their ids, matches links from the old "Copy Mementos link" button by name, and waits for in-flight uploads before comparing;
  - items whose Zipline file was deleted get a **Gone** tag, which is cleared if the file comes back. Nothing is marked when the list couldn't be read completely.
- **Migration:** on start, every original in `data/media` is uploaded, oldest first. The job resumes where it stopped: the Zipline id is recorded right after the upload, so a crash never uploads twice. The local copy is removed only after Zipline reports the same size **and** sends back the same SHA-256. It waits out 429s. Progress, kept and failed counts, a **Retry** button and the sync status are on the new **Mementos** tab (`/mementos`). `/healthz` reports `storage` and the Mementos connection state, but doesn't fail on a Zipline outage.

## Zipline API targeted

**Zipline v4**, read from the source of v4.8.0 (`github.com/diced/zipline`, with v4.0–v4.5 checked for route differences):
- upload: `POST /api/upload` (multipart `file`, with headers `authorization: <token>`, `x-zipline-folder: <folder id>` and `x-zipline-deletes-at`). Answers `{files:[{id,name,type,url}]}`.
- list files: `GET /api/user/files?page&perpage&sortBy=createdAt&order=asc&filter=all`. Answers `{page,total,pages}`.
- one file: `GET` / `DELETE /api/user/files/:idOrName`.
- folders: `GET /api/user/folders?noincl=true` and `POST /api/user/folders`.
- raw bytes: `GET /api/user/files/:id/raw` (signed in, v4.3+), falling back to `/raw/:name` on older v4.
- errors: `{error:"E2001: …",code,statusCode}`.

Upload links are rebased onto `ZIPLINE_URL`, because Zipline builds them from the Host it was called on (`zipline:3000`). **v3 is detected and refused** with a clear message on the Mementos page. v3 returns bare arrays and string links and its upload has no file id, so supporting it wasn't cheap.

## Deploy

`git pull && docker compose up -d --build`, then in `.env`:
- `ZIPLINE_TOKEN`: in Zipline, click your name (top right) → **Copy token**, or Settings → User → Token.
- `ZIPLINE_URL=https://mementos.niijimasisters.com` (already the example value).
- `ZIPLINE_INTERNAL_URL=http://zipline:3000` (the default).

The Archive is already on `zipline_default` (the `TRAEFIK_NETWORK` default). If her Zipline service isn't named `zipline`, set the internal URL to the right one. Open **Mementos** to watch the move. New settings under `zipline:` in `config.example.yml` (`sync_minutes`, `folder`, `inbox_collection`). DB migration `0002_zipline` runs on start.

## Tested

- `pnpm verify` passes (81 tests, svelte-check with no warnings, lint, build).
- `src/lib/server/zipline.test.ts`: client tests against recorded v4/v3 answers (`tests/fixtures/zipline/`, shaped from Zipline's source). Covers headers, the expiry retry, the 401 hint, 429 retry-after, v3 detection, paging, the raw fallback, folders and delete.
- `src/lib/server/mementos.test.ts`: tests against `tests/fake-zipline.ts`, a small fake Zipline v4, run both in-process and over a real HTTP socket:
  - saving: a save goes to Zipline with only the thumbnail left local; a save while Zipline is down is kept on disk and then migrated; a changed copy keeps the original; local mode is unchanged;
  - migration: checked byte for byte, the old Copy-Mementos link adopted, resumed after a crash with no double upload, waits out a 429;
  - sync: imports into the Inbox, no duplicates, non-media skipped, Gone marking set and cleared, no marking on a failed list, the Inbox recreated if she deleted it;
  - delete with keep and with delete; proxy Range, 304 and 404; export from Zipline; v3 refusal.
- I ran the production build with `ACCESS_MODE=off` against the fake server (`node scripts/fake-zipline.ts`):
  - 4 local items migrated (local originals removed), old thumbnails moved to `data/thumbs`, and 2 "phone" uploads imported into the Inbox (the `.txt` was skipped);
  - a curl upload straight to the fake showed up after **Sync now**, and a file deleted there got the Gone tag;
  - copy link wrote the public URL to the clipboard; delete with and without "Also delete on Mementos" did what it says;
  - `/file/<id>` returned 206 with `content-range`;
  - with Zipline unreachable, pages still render, a save falls back to disk, and the Mementos page shows the error;
  - with no Zipline configured, files stay on disk as before.
- Screenshots at 390px and 1280px (Den, lightbox, item page, Collections, Mementos, Inbox): no horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth` 390/1280). The tabs were tightened on phones so the fourth fits, and tile badges no longer overlap the owner tag.

## Not tested

- A real Zipline instance (none reachable from the sandbox), her Google Drive datasource, or Zipline's real rate limiter. The fake mirrors the API from the source.
- A real browser playing a long video through the proxy. Range handling was checked with curl and unit tests.

body:
## Waarom

Rik vond de installatie op de VPS te ingewikkeld (script plakken, sleutel in GitHub zetten, vragen beantwoorden). Hij heeft de repo openbaar gemaakt; daardoor kan het veel korter.

## Wat verandert

- **Eén regel op de VPS:** `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rheijmen/alternatievengids/main/deploy/setup-vps-gids.sh | bash`. Het script stelt geen vragen meer en haalt de site via https op, dus er is geen sleutel of inlog nodig.
- **Privé-repo blijft mogelijk** met `USE_KEY=1` (dan weer met een deploy key), voor als de repo ooit weer privé moet.
- **`docs/HOSTING.md`** is teruggebracht tot drie stappen: twee DNS-records, een regel plakken, controleren.
- **Interne notities** uit `docs/OVERDRACHT.md` gehaald nu de repo openbaar is (Baserow-id's, opmerkingen over andere overzichtssites). Er stonden geen sleutels of wachtwoorden in de repo; dat is gecontroleerd. De geschiedenis is wel openbaar en bevat dezelfde interne notities.
- Gevonden en gerepareerd: de systemd-eenheid kon het pad van het bijwerkscript letterlijk als `$BIN_DIR` bevatten.

## Gecontroleerd

- `npm test`: 33 tests, waarvan 4 nieuw: het **hele script van begin tot eind** tegen een lokale nagemaakte repo met een branch `site` (clone, tweede run verandert niets, een nieuwe bouw komt aan via het bijwerkscript), een run **via een pipe** (`cat script | bash`, zoals `curl | bash`), een duidelijke fout als de branch ontbreekt, en de privé-modus.
- Bouw en controle: 414 pagina's, 0 fouten.
- Openbaar bevestigd: `raw.githubusercontent.com` geeft 200 voor het script en voor `site/index.html`; de privé scan-repo geeft 404.

## Niet gecontroleerd

Het script is niet op de echte VPS gedraaid; alleen met nagebootste `caddy`, `systemctl` en `curl`. Het eerste echte gebruik is door Rik.

## Geschiedenis

De remote branch bevatte nog de commits van PR #5; die zijn met een "ours"-merge aangesloten. Het diff met `main` is alleen deze wijziging.

author: prathamesh-sonpatki
body:
## What
Local checks for logjson/tracejson pipelines, before any API call:
- A function allowlist with argument counts taken from the query engine, including the `_over_time` suffix.
- A function object must have exactly one key.
- `as` must be a plain name (letters, digits, underscore; may start with a digit, matching the engine, but not be all digits).
- Field-argument shape checks (malformed field references are rejected).
- `$gt`/`$gte`/`$lt`/`$lte` require a numeric value.
- `$quantile_exact` gets the same checks as `$quantile`, including the numeric-guard dataflow rule.

Shared rules live in `internal/telemetry/pipeline_rules.go` (renamed from `quantile_validate.go`).

## Why
Model-built pipelines failed with an opaque upstream 400 instead of a local error that shows the right example.

## Tests
- Logs: `TestPrepareLogJSONQueryAcceptsEveryAggregateFunction`, `TestPrepareLogJSONQueryRejectsInvalidAggregateFunctions` (includes malformed field references), `TestPrepareLogJSONQueryRejectsInvalidAggregateAlias`, `TestPrepareLogJSONQueryQuantileExactNeedsNumericGuard`, `TestPrepareLogJSONQueryRequiresNumericComparisonValues`
- Traces: `TestSanitizeTraceJSONQuery_AcceptsEveryAggregateFunction`, `_RejectsInvalidAggregateFunctions`, `_RejectsInvalidAggregateAlias`, `_RequiresNumericComparisonValues`
- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green; existing tests unchanged.

Known simplifications: trace field args are checked by shape only, with no tracking of aliases from earlier stages; `groupby` alias values are a follow-up.

author: recrwplay
body:
## What

Adds a generated `nav/docsets.json` to the `@neo4j-antora/tabbed-nav` extension (0.3.9 to 0.4.0), alongside `nav/tabs.json`. It feeds the "All Neo4j documentation" modal in docs-ui (`docs-restructure` branch), which now reads it instead of `tabs.json`.

Shape, one entry per Antora component:

```json
[{ "name": "cypher-manual", "title": "Cypher Manual", "group": "Query",
   "versions": [{ "version": "25", "latest": true, "url": "/cypher-manual/25/intro/",
                  "pdf": "/cypher-manual/25/neo4j-cypher-manual-25.pdf" }] }]
```

- `url` is the first linkable internal page of that version.
- `pdf` is only set when the PDF exists: in the build output for the in-build stage, in the bucket listing for the S3 aggregator. Stored at `<component>/<version>/_exports/neo4j-<component>[-<version>].pdf`, public URL without `_exports`. The version segment is omitted for unversioned docsets.
- `group` comes from the docset's `page-docset-display-group` attribute (antora.yml or playbook); empty when unset.

## How

- New `docsets.js` builds the file from the aggregated `tabs.json`, shared by `index.js` (in-build aggregate stage) and `aggregate.js` (post-publish S3 aggregator).
- `tabs.json` only keeps a component's latest version (plus all versions of version-grouped docsets), so each component's latest entry now also carries `docsetVersions`: every version with its first page. The nav code ignores the new field, and components not yet rebuilt fall back to what `tabs.json` already has.
- New `docsetsFile` option (default `nav/docsets.json`, `false` to skip).

## Attribute names

- `page-docset-version-group` is now the preferred name for the existing `page-tabs-group` (version matching across docsets). Both work; the new one wins if both are set. It is copied onto pages as `page-tabs-group`, which the UI layouts and nav helpers still read, so docs-ui needs no change for it.
- `page-docset-display-group` is new and sets the group shown in the modal.

## Testing

- The `docsets.js` merge logic was checked on sample data and against the live dev `tabs.json` (44 docsets) with a local script.
- Not yet run: a full Antora build with the extension, or `aggregate.js` against S3 (needs AWS credentials). Hence draft.

## Follow-ups

- Document `docsets.json`, `docsetsFile` and the two attributes in docs-playbook (`reference/pages/antora/extensions/tabbed-nav.adoc`, `docs-restructure/pages/set-up-docset.adoc`), from `main`.
- Docsets need `page-docset-display-group` set before real groups appear; the modal currently uses a temporary placeholder mapping.

author: jangtrinh
body:
Closes #862

## Problem
On a slow frame (a software GPU, a big file) egui batches several pointer events into one frame and reports only the last pointer position. `on_drag` never runs on the frame of the release, so:
- A move, resize or rotate whose press, moves and release shared one frame ended as a click, or left the layer short of the release position.
- When a release and the next press shared a frame, `on_press` replaced the open Move, Resize or Rotate before it ended. Its edits stayed on the canvas, but the transaction was dropped, so undo could not remove them (also in v0.6.0).

#857 fixed this for Draw only.

## Change
All in `canvas/interact.rs`:
- `on_release` takes the position where the pointer let go. A pending click, move, resize or rotate is first brought there with the same update code `on_drag` uses, so snapping behaves as it does for a slow drag. The drop container for a move is chosen at that position too.
- A new press ends a Pending, Move, Resize, Rotate or Draw that is still open. A release before the press ends it at the release position; it commits as one undo step before the new press starts. This holds when the press lands on a panel, not only on the canvas.
- A press and release at one spot in one frame stays a click: it never resizes or rotates by the pixels between the pointer and the handle centre, and never adds an undo step.
- A primary press with no release before it (a lost release) ends the gesture as it was last drawn, with no reparent.
- Every release step uses the modifiers stamped on the release event, not the state at the end of the frame. Shift going up with the button keeps the axis lock, the aspect lock and the 15 degree snap; a Shift-click right after the release does not lock the finished move; Alt after a flick makes no copy. The draw arm uses them too.
- A middle press over a pending click drops the click, so the selection stays; a pointer that went past the drag threshold in that frame still makes the move.
- `on_drag` and `on_release` share `follow_pointer`; the rotate update moved into `update_rotate` unchanged.

Not changed: CornerRadius, AutoLayoutDrag, SmartSelectionDrag and ShapeControl still drop their transaction when a release and a press share a frame. Follow-up.

## Tests
New `shell/tests/fast_drag_transform.rs` (17 tests; 10 gestures: move, move of an unselected layer, corner, edge and snapping resizes, single and group rotate). Each gesture is compared with the same gesture spread over many frames, delivered three ways: press, moves and release in one frame; last move sharing the frame of the release; pointer far away at the press.

Red first on the unchanged `interact.rs`: 8 of the first 10 fail; the one-frame resize click and the sub-threshold jitter are regression guards. Review round: 6 of the 7 added tests fail on the first PR head (modifiers, Alt copy, draw square, middle press over a pending click); each guard fails when its guard is removed (resize click: width 366 instead of 360; jitter: lower the drag threshold).

Green: all 10, plus the 23 `fast_drag_draw` tests unchanged.

Gates: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked`, `cargo test -p designos-app --locked --no-fail-fast` (two wall-clock budget tests in `terminal::tests::bootstrap` fail under load and pass alone), `scripts/zero_fake_ui_gate.py` (17/17).

author: seenark
body:
## Why

There is no record of which skills get used, so deciding which ones to delete is a guess. Some skills are used only when the agent reads them on its own. This records every Skill Use and shows the counts.

## What changed

- New `skill-stats` feature. It records each Skill Use with its source (user, agent, subagent) in a global store, or in a Git-ignored `.omp/skill-stats/` store for Project Skills.
- `/skill-stats` and `/skill-stats project` show 7-day, 30-day and since-Reset-Point counts, unused skills, and a copyable `npx skills remove` command for delete candidates. `reset` moves a Reset Point and deletes nothing. `import` reads past session files once, with no model calls.
- Ponytail helper commands emit a new shared `codesook/skill-use/v1` event (shared-display `./skill-use`), so their uses count too.

## Scope

- Delete candidates are skills with no use in 60 days that were installed at least 60 days ago. Only `npx skills` installs join the command. Others show their path.
- Skills whose `SKILL.md` is gone are hidden. Records are never deleted.

## Blast Radius

The feature is off by default. Ponytail only adds one event emit. shared-display gains one export and goes to 1.5.0, and the settings plugin goes to 1.4.0 for the new feature entry.

## Verification

- `bun run verify` passes, including 29 skill-stats tests.
- Real TUI run (`verify-omp-plugins`): `/ponytail-review` recorded a user use, the dashboard showed it, reset zeroed only the since-reset count, and import filled a project store whose `.gitignore` keeps it out of Git. The project dashboard listed it, and a second import was refused.
- Not verified live: `/skill:x` and the agent's own `skill://` reads, because the scratch profile has no model. Unit tests and the import run cover the same signals.

author: hraiservices
body:
## Summary
The purple flash the user reported (screenshot: login page briefly plain black/white, then swaps to violet) wasn't a bug in the sense of corruption — "Violet" is actually the app's default accent color (`DEFAULT_COLOR_THEME` in `src/lib/color-themes.ts`). But the *flash itself* was a real, fixable issue: `ColorThemeLoader` applies the `theme-<id>` class in a `useEffect`, which only fires after the shop's `colorTheme` setting comes back from Supabase — so every load (not just the first) briefly painted the plain default theme before swapping to the shop's actual color.

## Fix
Mirrors the existing fix for the font flash (`FontLoader` + the blocking `<script>` in `layout.tsx`'s `<head>`):
- `ColorThemeLoader` now also caches the resolved `colorTheme`/`sidebarStyle`/`cornerStyle` to `localStorage` (`shop-color-config`) once all three have loaded.
- A new blocking inline script in `layout.tsx`'s `<head>` reads that cache and re-applies the theme class/sidebar class/`--radius` var before React hydrates.

A genuinely first-ever visit (nothing cached yet) still shows one unavoidable flash — same tradeoff the font fix already accepts — but every repeat visit, which is what was actually being reported, no longer flashes.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` — clean
- `npx eslint` on both changed files — clean
- `npm test` — 468/468 passing

The topology takes files over HTTP, mail and FTP as well as print jobs now, so the engine is renamed **BDF Docflow**.

## What moved

- Pages, `WWW-Authenticate` realms, `printer-make-and-model`, IPP `requesting-user-name`

body:
## Cosa fa
L'accesso **Cliente** passa da una pagina a tre, tutte del proprio cliente:
1. **I miei risultati** (invariata).
2. **Piano editoriale (PED)**: i contenuti che il team gli ha mandato, in schede (Da approvare / In lavorazione / Programmati / Pubblicati / Tutti), con anteprima di testo, media, hashtag, menzioni, data e ora. **Approva** oppure **Chiedi modifiche** (commento obbligatorio): con le modifiche il contenuto torna in *Bozza* col suo commento.
3. **Brief**: modulo di richiesta lavorazione (titolo, cosa serve, scadenza e riferimenti facoltativi) e stato delle richieste gia inviate. Il brief nasce *Inviato* e compare nella pagina Brief del team.

Avvisi in app: al cliente quando c'e qualcosa da approvare; al team (responsabili del cliente + chi ha chiesto l'approvazione) quando il cliente risponde o invia un brief.

## Sicurezza
- `editorialContents` e `briefs` restano **solo staff** nelle regole Firestore: il cliente passa da percorsi server che filtrano per il **suo** cliente.
- Lista bianca dei campi del PED (`lib/client-ped.ts`): niente task, progetto, campi personalizzati, errori di pubblicazione, id degli account. Le **bozze del team non si vedono**, tranne quelle tornate per le sue modifiche.
- Rispondere (approva / modifiche) e inviare un brief e consentito **solo** a un utente Cliente di quel cliente; lo staff non risponde al posto suo (per approvare senza cliente resta "Approva senza cliente", solo amministratori). Risposta in transazione, solo su contenuti *in attesa*.
- La pagina `/clients/[id]/editorial-plan` per il ruolo Cliente non monta l'editor dello staff.

## Verifica
`tsc` pulito, 398 test (nuovi: client-ped, client-brief). **Non provata con un login Cliente reale**: da provare dopo il deploy con un utente Cliente di prova (serve un utente con ruolo Cliente e clientId).

author: vaipakam
body:
## What

**Before:** when the indexer withdraws a loan record the chain has no loan for (#2197), it clears the shared alert memory for that loan id. The keeper's own health-band memory (`hf_band_state`, keeper-private database) was pruned only for ids whose `loans` row still exists with a terminal status. A withdrawn id has no row, so its marker stayed forever. If the chain later issued the same id to a real loan, with the same holder and the same band, the keeper read it as an unchanged observation and suppressed that loan's first warning.

**After:** the keeper's prune (`apps/keeper/src/hfBandNotifications.ts`) also drops a marker when `loan_orphans` holds an entry it had not yet seen, for this chain, this chain's Diamond and that id. The marker's write and the inbox row are fenced by the same causal token.

**How:**
- **Causal token.** Each marker records `orphan_seq` (new additive keeper migration `0006_hf_band_orphan_seq.sql`). This is the newest `loan_orphans.id`, read in the same statement as the loan's holder, so both come from one snapshot (Codex r4).
  - A marker is written only while a `loans` row exists; an unresolved holder defers the write. So a withdrawal with a higher id is the move of the very row the marker came from, and the marker goes.
  - A withdrawal the marker had already seen came before it, so the marker is kept.
  - The ordering uses the table's own AUTOINCREMENT ids, never the two machines' clocks (Codex r1).
- **Fenced inbox rows.** The inbox insert carries the same token as an in-statement guard, next to the epoch guard. A withdrawal landing after the holder read therefore cannot recreate the withdrawn loan's alert, or take the dedup key of a same-day reissue (Codex r4).
- **Pre-upgrade markers.** A marker from before `0006` is judged by whether its `loans` row is still there, then stamped (Codex r2).
- **Old Diamonds.** Entries from an earlier Diamond are ignored, because `loan_orphans` outlives a fresh Diamond.
- **Bind limits (Codex r5).** Every list-taking statement in the module now binds its list as one JSON parameter read with `json_each`, the shape the indexer's `insertNotificationRows` uses. A statement's bind count is therefore fixed by its text, and a wide pass can no longer exceed D1's bind limits and stall on every tick.

Two test-only fixes ride along because `main` is red on them:
- `apps/agent/test/schemaGateEntry.test.ts`: #2653's fix, ported unchanged.
- `contracts/test/GovernorDayPoolTest.t.sol` `testTrailingAverageIncludesMirrorDayCredits`: it now finalizes day 4 before day 5 averages its mirror credit (#2645 made finalization the single writer).

**Deploy note:** `0006` is additive. A merge is a deploy on the keeper machine, so its update timer is paused before the merge and the migration is applied right after, as for #2596.

## Why

Codex found this on #2636; it was deferred to #2638 because the indexer has no binding to the keeper's private database.

## What's deferred (intentional)

The case where the chain reissues the id before the indexer withdraws the old record is out of scope: at a settled block the id then exists, so no withdrawal is ever recorded. A pre-upgrade marker on an id both withdrawn and reissued before this deploy cannot be recovered, because nothing records which loan it was written from (stated in the code).

## Verification

- `apps/keeper`: `vitest run` 748 passed. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean. New tests cover:
  - the withdrawal landing between the holder read and the insert (fails with the guard removed);
  - another Diamond's withdrawal and an older one;
  - a 2,600-edge, 2,600-marker pass with no statement over 10 binds.
- `apps/agent`: `test/schemaGateEntry.test.ts` 3/3.
- `contracts` (default profile, targeted): `GovernorDayPoolTest` 48/48, `GovernorDualAccumulatorTest` 19/19, and the six other suites that read mirror credit all pass.

## Closes

Closes #2638

author: daniel-ospina
body:
Closes #9572

Seventh round. Each round was driven by a fresh-context review that found the
same fabrication still alive one layer further out. Thirteen sites so far: SDK
doors, EventAPI lane, hosted REST models AND handlers, the seed surfaces, the
extractor document stage, the conversation-mining lane, the private capture
door, the production `/v1/sessions/commit` door, the `uses[]` stub fold, the
v1 BYOK summary seam, the session-index issue-linking door, and the LongMemEval
ingest lane in `tools/`. The sweep is now repo-wide, not `tortoise/`-scoped —
the last one lived outside the package the first six rounds read.
All findings are fixed here; none are deferred as "out of scope". The
exhaustiveness claim is scoped honestly: this is every site FOUND, and the
class is swept by grep (`kind="…"` defaults, `SET …objectKind=`) rather than
asserted to be empty.

## The defect

The identity-upsert doors fabricated the discriminator's default, so "the
caller named no kind" and "the caller named `other`" were the same string on
the wire. The fold then did exactly what it was told:

    ON MATCH SET s.subjectKind = coalesce($sk, s.subjectKind)

— which preserves a stored kind ONLY if "not supplied" arrives as NULL. It did
not: `create_subject`/`create_object` defaulted the argument to `"other"` and
`create_entity` popped `props.pop(kindKey, "other")`, so

    create_subject("Probe Subject Z", "team")   # team
    create_subject("Probe Subject Z")           # -> 'other'  (silent reset)

Direction matters, and an earlier draft of this message had it backwards (the
reviewer measured it): a canonical re-create is probe-gated (#2295), so the
journal kept the FIRST write's real kind while the LIVE node was reset —
`live == replay` was **False** pre-fix, and replay was the honest copy. The
EventAPI lane journals every mention, so there the fabricated value did reach
the record.

## Every fabrication site FOUND, all fixed

| Site | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk.create_subject` / `create_object` | `subjectKind: str = "other"`, always forwarded | `str \| None = None`, forwarded only when named |
| `sdk.create_entity` | `props.pop(kindKey, "other")` | `_entity_door_props` **omits** an unsupplied discriminator |
| `projection._upsert_subject` | `ev.get("subject_kind", "other")`, `ON CREATE … s.subjectKind=$sk` | `ev.get("subject_kind")` (NULL), `ON CREATE … coalesce($sk,'other')` — the Object arm already worked this way |
| `api.add_subject` / `add_object` (EventAPI lane) | emitted `subject_kind="other"` | key absent when none named |
| `hosted_api` `POST /v1/subjects` + `/v1/objects` | request models defaulted `"other"` **and the endpoints forwarded it** | `str \| None = None`, forwarded only when named; `_require_approved_kind` gated on the same condition |
| `hosted_api._OrgSeedSurface` / `onboarding.selfhost._SdkSeedSurface` | `subject_kind="other"` default | same treatment |
| `extractor._SemanticStage` + `extract_entities` | invented `"other"` for a model that named none | `_named_kind` omits the key — **the default document-ingest path** |
| **`extractor._normalize_entity` + `mining.ConversationMiner`** | normalized an absent kind to `'other'`, then always forwarded it to `api.add_object` | new `objectKind_named` provenance bit; `_kind_kwargs` forwards the kind only when the model named one — **the default conversation-mining path** (`mine_corpus(extract_entities=True)`) |
| **`sdk` capture/v2 door (`payload["entities"]`)** | `str(e.get("kind", "core:other"))`, i.e. the classifier's family fallback written as a kind | `tortoise/kind_fallbacks.py` — ONE predicate: the fallback sentinel is a REPAIR, not a discriminator, so it is omitted. A payload always names a kind, so an absent-key guard alone would never fire |
| **`/v1/sessions/commit` (`_execute_commit_writes` §6)** | forwarded `er.entity.kind` unconditionally — and `extractor_v2` repairs to `core:other`, so **the production capture door** (`TortoiseSDK.commit_session` POSTs here) reset a stored kind | same shared `writable_kind` predicate; the pin is at the ROUTE, because a helper-level pin is exactly how this twin survived four rounds |
| **`projection` `uses[]` stub fold** | bare-string `uses` defaulted `'other'` and wrote it with a hard `ON MATCH SET o.objectKind=$kind` | absent stays absent; `ON MATCH o.objectKind=coalesce($kind, o.objectKind)` — the Subject arm's shape |
| **`sdk._summary_to_payload`** (v1 BYOK commit seam) | invented `kind="core:concept"` for a summary entry naming none — never a §5 object kind, and never written by product code, so never a caller's classification | names the DECLARED family fallback (the payload schema requires the key), which the door's shared predicate drops |
| **`tools/longmem_eval/ingest_v2._write_payload`** | `objectKind=str(e.get("kind", "core:other"))` — the eval twin of `_payload_entity_kind`, in a re-entrant per-session lane, so re-ingest re-typed a stored Object (measured: `capability` → `core:other`) | imports the same `writable_kind`; the kind rides the kwargs only when writable |
| **`sdk._connect_issue_objects`** (the session-index door) | synthesised `"issue"`/`"pr"` from a session file's frontmatter key and wrote it with a hard `MERGE … SET o.objectKind=$okind` — so on MATCH it re-typed the stored Object (measured through the public `index_sessions()`: a connector's `pm:issue` and a user's `capability` both became `issue`) | the kind moves to the fold's `ON CREATE` arm; a re-index refreshes `name`/`repo`/`issue_number`/`url` and touches nothing else |

Three subtleties the fixes needed, all now pinned by tests:

- `_normalize_entity` runs **twice** on the conversation lane (the stage normalizes, then `extract_conversation_entities` normalizes the stage's output), and the second pass sees the already-normalized `objectKind: "other"` — a real string. The provenance bit is therefore carried when the input states it, or double-normalization would flip "the model named none" back to "named".
- A kind the closed vocab **repaired** is our guess, not the caller's value, so it is not "named"; an explicit `"other"` is.
- `FAMILY_FALLBACK_KINDS` is the **namespaced** sentinel only: the bare `other` is a real core kind a caller may name, including to re-classify back to `other`, so it stays writable — adding it would contradict `_normalize_entity`'s deliberate "an explicit `other` is NAMED" and is pinned against.
- The fallback rule lives in **one** leaf module (`tortoise/kind_fallbacks.py`) that both the private SDK door and the hosted commit door import. The fifth fabricator was a twin that imported nothing from the SDK's private surface — one shared predicate is what keeps a sixth from appearing under a second spelling.

**Not changed, deliberately:**

- A caller who *does* name a kind still updates it on a re-create, and caller-supplied props still apply ON MATCH — that identity-upsert contract is unchanged, and it is what the three doors' `destructive` risk tier now rests on. `tool_registry.py` justified that tier with the fabricated default; that claim became false, so it now states the true one (props ON MATCH). Re-deriving the tier from #4122's axis is a classification question of its own — a bug fix must not silently settle it.
- The two **MCP alias** tools (`tortoise_create_subject`, `tortoise_create_object`) still take the kind as a REQUIRED parameter, so an MCP client cannot omit it. That is a surface shape, and changing it is an MCP-surface change that needs Daniel's approval — so it is stated here rather than made. `tortoise_create_entity` (the door actually in use) takes the kind through `props` and is fixed.
- **A stored VALUE moves on purpose:** a first create from a v2 payload whose kind was repaired used to store `objectKind='core:other'` and now stores `other` — the same kind in the SDK/REST spelling, so one graph stops carrying two. Only a consumer filtering the exact string `'core:other'` sees the move; it is stated in `sdk._payloa

author: tomerbar44
body:
## Summary
The homepage becomes the new brain film site, replacing the "Parry · private beta" page. It ships with a working booking form, a cookie banner with consent-gated analytics, and up-to-date search and AI metadata.

## Why
The new site was built and reviewed on preview links. Tomer asked to publish it on www.parry-io.com, with maximum visibility to search engines and AI assistants.

## What changed
- `public/home.html` is the self-contained page (three.js r170 from jsdelivr, brain model `public/brain.glb`, logos and brand assets). `next.config.ts` serves it at `/` with a beforeFiles rewrite. `app/page.tsx` stays in place but is no longer reached.
- `/api/contact` and `/api/e` rewrite to the `parry-site-contact` Cloud Run service (project rising-ocean-484208-i7, europe-west3). It emails booking requests to the team through the existing SMTP account and writes analytics events to Cloud Logging.
- Cookie banner: nothing measures or stores until the visitor accepts, Decline is as easy as Accept, and there is a "Cookie settings" link in the footer. Google Consent Mode defaults to denied.
- SEO / GEO:
  - New `robots.txt` names the search and AI crawlers explicitly, allows them everywhere, and disallows `/data-room`.
  - `sitemap.xml` lists every page.
  - `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` match the current copy.
  - New `favicon.ico` (16/32/48), a 192px icon, `site.webmanifest`, and a 1200×630 OG image (124 KB).
  - JSON-LD for Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication and FAQPage.
- Site-wide metadata in `app/layout.tsx` no longer says private beta. Subpage titles use "·" instead of the long dash.
- Long cache (1 day, stale-while-revalidate 7 days) for the brain model, logos and brand assets.

## How it works
`/` → beforeFiles rewrite → `/home.html` (a static file). The page talks only to its own origin for the form and analytics, so it needs no CORS, and the service URL never appears in the browser. Existing routes (`/privacy`, `/terms`, `/trust`, `/status`, `/sla`, `/careers`, `/changelog`, `/google-data`, `/data-room`) are unchanged.

## Risks
- three.js loads from jsdelivr, pinned to 0.170.0. If the CDN is down, the copy and the form still work but the brain does not render.
- `brain.glb` is 13 MB and loads progressively. It is cached for a day after the first visit.
- The booking form depends on the Cloud Run service. If it fails, the visitor sees an error and nothing is lost silently.
- `npm ci` fails on main already (lockfile drift: @emnapi/*). This PR does not touch the lockfile.

## Test plan
- `next build` passes, then `next start` checked locally:
  - Every route returns 200 with the right content type, including `/`, `/privacy`, `/robots.txt`, `/favicon.ico`, `/brain.glb` and `/og.jpg`.
  - `/api/contact` and `/api/e` reach the service through the rewrite.
  - The security headers are present.
- Headless Chrome on the production build:
  - The banner shows, and zero analytics requests go out before consent.
  - After Accept, the queued events are sent and the choice is remembered.
  - The page renders with no console errors.
- The booking form sent a real test email end to end through the preview link.
- Mobile sweep at 390×844, 375×667 and 360×740, plus 125/150/200% zoom, with automatic checks for clipped and overlapping text.

## Security impact
- No secrets in the repo. The Cloud Run service reads SMTP credentials from Secret Manager under a dedicated service account that can read only those two secrets.
- The contact endpoint always sends to one fixed recipient. It validates the email, blocks header injection, has a honeypot, and is rate limited to 5 per IP per hour and 60 overall.
- The analytics endpoint logs no IP addresses and caps event size and rate.

## Rollback plan
Revert this PR. Removing the `/` rewrite alone also brings back the previous homepage (`app/page.tsx` is untouched).

## Linked issue / ticket
Jira was unavailable at the time; Tomer asked to proceed without a ticket.

author: mrousavy
body:
Stacked on #1968.

Nitrogen now writes Apple output to `nitrogen/generated/apple`, next to `shared` and `android`. `addNitrogenTargets` defaults `swiftSources` to `["apple"]`, so a library keeps its Swift and Objective-C++ sources in `apple/`. The template, the React Native and standalone test libraries and the Hermes test glue move from `ios/` to `apple/`, with regenerated bindings. Nitrogen's own `autolinking/ios` sources move to `autolinking/apple`. The unused `tests/standalone/hermes/Package.swift` is removed, since the root package defines the Hermes target. The fallback Swift module file, written when a library has no Swift specs, also moves to `generated/apple/swift`, where SwiftPM looks for it.

`Package.swift` stays at each package root. React Native 0.88's SwiftPM autolinking only finds a library manifest at the root or in `ios/`, and SwiftPM rejects targets outside the package root, so an `apple/Package.swift` could not reach `cpp/` or `nitrogen/generated/shared`. react/react-native#59361 adds `apple/` to that lookup for libraries without shared C++.

The `ios` platform key in `nitro.json` and specs keeps its name, as do generated file names such as `HybridBaseSpecCxx.ios.cpp`, the React Native apps' `ios/` projects and the iOS test runner.

Existing libraries move `ios/` to `apple/` and update `files` in `package.json`, or keep their folder with `addNitrogenTargets(to: package, swiftSources: ["ios"])`.

Validated with the workspace build, typecheck, lint, Prettier and swift-format, and `bun specs` with no drift; every moved generated file is byte-identical. The example app resolves its Swift packages and builds for the iOS simulator from the new paths. The standalone iOS build and runtime suite pass on the iOS 27 simulator (24 passed, 1 skipped).

## Scope

Harden the already private/owner-deferred F7 screenshot collector against unwanted **outbound browser requests** from the isolated synthetic staging browser. This is a code-only safety increment, not browser execution or F7/F8 acceptance.

## Changes

- Block cross-origin HTTP(S) and WebSocket requests using `BrowserContext.route` and `routeWebSocket`, before creating pages, with service workers disabled.
- Allow only the **exact attested staging origin** and its matching WSS (or loopback WS) companion. No CDNs, off-origin APIs, alternate ports, production destinations, host suffix bypass or HTTP downgrade.
- Keep a non-identifying `blockedCrossOriginNetworkCount` per case; no URLs, request bodies, patient names, cookies or response content in audit JSON. Mark attempted off-origin access `REVIEW_REQUIRED`.
- F7 independent integrity validator now rejects a falsely green finding with missing/nonzero blocked-request count.
- Add independent unit regressions for origin policy and forged false-green counts; reinforce source checks and document infrastructure limitation.

Playwright's `routeWebSocket` / `WebSocketRoute.connectToServer()` are supported since v1.48; private workflow pins Playwright 1.56.1.

## Required boundaries
- Repo is currently **PUBLIC**: private-only browser workflow stays SKIPPED, no screenshots or real data.
- Product owner requested no human/manual QA until **all** engineering work is completed.
- F7 0/486 actual screenshot case signoffs; owner visual/interactive `NOT_EXECUTED`, F8 qualified 88-case operational release `NO_GO`, Hostinger verification not implied.
- All original Master Scope 88 sections unchanged. Does not close #265, #327 or #250.

author: focafunk
body:
## Qué cambia

Un script nuevo: `_backend/database/scripts/geo-paises-registracion.sql`. **No modifica código** — es
un script que corre el PM contra la base de cada ambiente.

## Por qué

El combo de países de la registración sale de `core.tablas` con `tabla='paises_registracion'`, que
guarda el **código ISO** en `valor` (`AR`) y el **nombre** en `descripcion` (`Argentina`). Pero los
estados no se buscan por el código: `getEstados` de `COREDataService` concatena el **nombre**:

```sql
where t.tabla = concat('estados_paises', :pais)   -- :pais es la descripcion
```

Así que si la `descripcion` no coincide **carácter por carácter** con el `valor` de `tabla='paises'`,
el combo de estados vuelve vacío y **no hay ningún error en ningún log**: la query no encuentra filas.

`paises_registracion` tiene **`Peru`** y `geo-paises-hispanohablantes.sql` carga **`Perú`**. Quien se
registra eligiendo Perú no ve ninguna provincia.

## Qué hace, y por qué es seguro

Corrige **solo `descripcion`**, y solo en las filas que tienen equivalente en `paises` ignorando
acentos y mayúsculas. Usa `translate()` y no la extensión `unaccent`, que puede no estar instalada.

**No toca `tabl_id` ni `valor`.** Lo que las otras tablas guardan como referencia es el `tabl_id`
(`seg.users.reg_pais_id`, `core.empresas.pais_id`, `prd.establecimientos.pais`), y el trigger lo arma
como `tabla||valor`. Como ninguno de los dos cambia, el `tabl_id` queda igual y ninguna referencia se
rompe. No inserta países ni da de baja nada.

Trae además el **diagnóstico** (partes 1 y 3, solo `SELECT`), que dice la verdad en cualquier
ambiente en vez de depender de un log viejo: por país, si su descripción existe en `paises`, cuántos
estados resuelve, y cuántos usuarios ya se registraron con él.

## Lo que deja para que decidas (comentado a propósito)

- **Parte 4 — qué países ofrecer.** Hoy hay 7; el geo tiene 21 con estados y localidades. Es decisión
  de producto, así que va comentada. Toma la `descripcion` del propio `paises`, así que por
  construcción no pueden volver a desalinearse.
- **Parte 5 — `Alemania` (DE).** No está en el geo, que es solo de países hispanohablantes, así que su
  combo siempre va a venir vacío. Incluye la consulta para ver si hay usuarios registrados con ella y
  los tres caminos: dejarla, baja **lógica** (nunca borrado real), o cargarle estados de otra fuente.

## Cómo lo verifiqué

No me conecté a ninguna base del proyecto. Levanté un PostgreSQL 16 descartable en otro puerto, armé
una réplica de `core.tablas` con el trigger y **las 7 filas reales** de `paises_registracion` —las que
devolvió el CORE en `logs/log-2025-10-14.php`—, y le cargué el **geo real** (`INSERT` de 21 países,
530 divisiones y 25.505 localidades, sin un error).

| | |
|---|---|
| Diagnóstico antes | Reproduce el problema: `Peru` y `Alemania` con **0 estados**; los otros 5 OK |
| Corrida 1 | `UPDATE 1` — solo Perú. Después: **`Perú` → 26 estados, OK** |
| Corrida 2 (idempotencia) | **`UPDATE 0`** — no vuelve a tocar nada |
| `tabl_id` y `valor` después | **Intactos** en las 7 filas |
| Referencia del usuario | `seg.users.reg_pais_id = 'paises_registracionDE'` sigue resolviendo |
| Parte 4 con el filtro actual | `INSERT 0 6`, y el total **sigue en 7**: los 6 conflictúan y solo normalizan |
| Parte 4 sin filtro | `INSERT 0 21` → 22 filas, **21 con estados**; la única sin estados es Alemania |

El Postgres descartable quedó apagado y borrado.
