body:
## Incident
Engineering recovery for #167 — differing calories across physical menu, app, and delivery platforms. This draft does **not** change production nutritional numbers.

## Included
- `MenuOption`: unreviewed nutrition no longer defaults to verified.
- `CatalogItem` and standalone `MenuOption`: explicit nutrition source, serving basis/grams, reviewer ID and verification timestamp; ordinary live nutrition edits rejected until reviewed.
- Authenticated admin/superadmin approval:
  - `POST /api/dashboard/catalog-items/:id/nutrition/approve`
  - `POST /api/dashboard/menu/options/:id/nutrition/approve` (unlinked only)
- For ordinary draft nutrition edits: prior approval cleared. Linked options use CatalogItem as sole nutrition authority.
- Read-only `GET /api/dashboard/menu/nutrition-audit` scanning published products and **actually attached** menu options, reporting unapproved, missing/zero-default, wrong basis and macro-kcal anomalies.
- **Opt-in** `MENU_NUTRITION_APPROVAL_GATE=true`: new product/option authoring remains draft; explicit menu publish checks all eligible active/draft nutritional data **before** any release write and blocks incomplete records.
- Public menu item/option + V2 projection expose `nutritionDataStatus`, `nutritionVerified`, source/serving info while keeping legacy numeric fields compatible with installed Flutter versions.
- Unit contract tests, isolated Mongo lifecycle test, focused GitHub Actions.
- Staged rollout instructions: `docs/menu-nutrition-rollout.md`.

## Release blockers
- Never merge or deploy until all relevant CI is evaluated, and staging end-to-end menu validation is complete.
- Perform read-only live DB/menu audit, verify actual recipes, portions, allergens and owner/kitchen sign-off; do not invent calories or bulk-upgrade old `verified` records.
- Third-party platforms (HungerStation/Keeta) require separate merchant data corrections and screen-by-screen confirmation.
- Flutter repo currently read-only via this connection; its UI may display numerical legacy values without checking `nutritionVerified`. Upgrade/test Flutter and dashboard before shipping strict handling or any `null` semantics.
- Audit all other admin, bootstrap and migration publish paths before enabling strict flag on production.
- No production writes, deployments, or numeric menu changes have occurred.

Issue #167 tracks full multi-platform closure.

author: piotrchabros
body:
**Problem.** A user could not send a second notetaker for the rest of the hour, even after a 41-second meeting whose bot had already finished. An ad-hoc booking counted as active until its scheduled end (start + chosen duration), and only one active meeting was allowed.

**Changes**
- **Live meetings only.** A meeting now counts as active only while it is live: a live session, waiting for dispatch or retry, re-armed, or just created. Finished meetings (READY, ENDED_EARLY, FAILED) no longer block. The repository returns the choice flags and the latest session status, and `isAdHocMeetingActive` in the service decides.
- **Same link.** It is reused only while that meeting is live. After it finishes, the same Meet link gets a new booking and a new bot, since Meet links recur.
- **Configurable limits.**
  - `NOTETAKER_AD_HOC_MAX_ACTIVE_MEETINGS`, default 10, was 1.
  - `NOTETAKER_AD_HOC_MAX_MEETINGS_PER_DAY`, default 50, was 10.
  - The daily cap still counts every dispatched attempt, because each one cost a bot.

Tests: 2961 pass; type-check:ci clean, including the integration test files; Biome no errors. Integration tests were updated but not run, because this checkout is live production.

author: ggarber1
body:
## Problem
No worker code has ever run in AWS:
- The worker Lambdas held a Terraform placeholder ZIP (`raise Exception('placeholder…')`) and **no workflow deploys Lambda code**.
- The reminder worker was a forever-loop (5-min scheduler + SQS poller) that **nothing starts — not even locally** (no `__main__`, not in docker-compose). Reminders were never sent end-to-end.
- The Lambdas only got `ENV` + `SSM_PARAMETER_PATH`, so `get_settings()` couldn't even build (no `DATABASE_URL`).
- Eligibility/ERA Lambdas had no code behind them at all.

## Design (agreed)
Two **scheduled Lambdas from the API container image** — scale to zero, cost grows with practices.
- **reminders** — every 15 min. One pass: claim ≤200 due rows straight from `appointment_reminders` (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, no SQS), deliver, record outcome.
- **risk-scoring** — nightly. Extra 4h high-risk reminder **removed** (48h + 24h are enough).

## Changes
**API / workers**
- `reminder_worker.send_due_reminders()`: atomic claim (`enqueued` + `claimed_at`); claims older than 15 min reclaimed after a crash; rows with a Twilio SID marked sent (never resent); outcome written only `WHERE status='enqueued'` so a mid-send cancel wins; cancelled / no-show / already-started appointments → reminder cancelled. Delivery functions unchanged.
- `risk_scoring_worker.score_upcoming_appointments()`: 4h reminder removed; scores written in one bulk UPDATE (was one UPDATE per appointment).
- `lambda_handlers.reminders / risk_scoring`: fresh DB engine per invocation (`asyncio.run` = new loop per call; a pooled engine would be bound to a closed loop on warm starts).
- `core/lambda_config.load_settings_from_ssm()`: cold-start load of SSM secrets under the **same env names ECS injects**; paginated, decryption, timeouts; existing env wins. Placeholders are loaded as-is (staging SMS → honest `failed`).
- Migration **0041**: `sqs_message_id` → `claimed_at` (status `enqueued` kept = "claimed", so UI/webhooks are unchanged).
- Deleted `app/core/sqs.py` + `sqs_queue_*` settings; `awslambdaric` dependency.
- `python -m app.workers.reminder_worker` / `risk_scoring_worker` run one pass locally (DEV.md).

**Infra**
- `lambda-workers`: two image Lambdas (`awslambdaric` entry point, `image_config.command` per handler), EventBridge schedules, non-secret env only (`API_ENV`, buckets, `SSM_PARAMETER_PATH`); IAM = SSM path + KMS decrypt + `ses:SendEmail` (S3/SQS removed). Placeholder ZIP, eligibility/ERA Lambdas and SQS triggers deleted.
- `ecr`: repo policy so this account's `dental-*` Lambdas can pull the API image.
- `github-oidc`: deploy role may `UpdateFunctionCode` on the two workers.
- `deploy-staging` / `deploy-production`: update both Lambdas to the new image after migrations.
- `cloudwatch`: alarm on **any** failed worker run (old ">5 errors / 10 min" could never fire at one run per 15 min).

**Docs**: OPEN_QUESTIONS worker decision; 4.2A note; backlog item fixed; new items — remove unused SQS queues, 🔴 SES not configured (no identity / sender / API-task permission / sandbox), failed reminders have no retry.

## Tests
- `test_reminder_job.py` (10, real Postgres): sent once; not-yet-due untouched; cancelled/no-show/started appointments → cancelled; **two concurrent runs send each reminder exactly once**; stale claim recovered (fresh claim left alone); Twilio SID present → not resent; failure recorded; batch limit spans runs.
- `test_risk_scoring_job.py` (2) + updated `test_scheduling` scoring test (approved: kept "scores high", replaced 4h assertions with "no reminder rows").
- `test_lambda_config.py` (4), `test_lambda_handlers.py` (4).
- Removed `tests/workers/test_risk_scoring_worker.py` (only covered the removed 4h reminder).
- Local: ruff, mypy, 492 unit + 321 integration; migration 0041 up/down/up; API image builds for linux/amd64 and imports both handlers; `terraform validate` both envs; staging plan (lambda/ecr/oidc/cloudwatch): 0 destroy, 1 in-place (deploy role policy).

## ⚠️ One-time apply before the next staging deploy
`staging-up` applies `module.lambda_workers` but **not** `module.ecr`, `module.github_oidc`, `module.cloudwatch`. Apply those once (targeted) so Lambda can pull the image and the deploy can update the functions. Then: deploy → `aws lambda invoke` both functions → check CloudWatch logs.

body:
## Qué cambia

El proyecto estaba entregado como un **panel de análisis**: la simulación corría por dentro y el usuario solo miraba el resultado. La asignatura pide un **videojuego de simulación**, y el formato de los cuatro documentos que pidió el profesor (nombre y objetivo, procesos del negocio, parte visual, alcance) es el de un documento de diseño de juego.

Esta rama lo reformula como un **videojuego de simulación en primera persona**.

## Lo que hay ahora

- **Juego 3D en primera persona** (React + Three.js/R3F + Tailwind): el jugador ocupa los seis puestos del taller —recibe, diagnostica, cotiza, toma refacciones, repara y entrega— y camina por el local con WASD.
- **Contratación de personal** con IA por puesto: cada empleado ocupa su puesto y hace el trabajo por su cuenta.
- **Economía completa**: precios, nómina, alquiler, refacciones (lote normal y urgente), saldo y flujo de caja.
- **Cuota diaria y reputación** con condiciones reales de victoria y derrota: sobrevivir 30 días cumpliendo la cuota, sin quebrar y sin perder la fama.
- **Parte del día** al cerrar cada jornada y **pantalla final** con el resumen de la partida.
- **Panel de análisis** conservado como segunda vista: es lo que valida el modelo contra la teoría y alimenta el reporte.

El motor de eventos discretos en C es **autoritativo**: el navegador no simula nada, sólo manda acciones y dibuja el estado. La misma semilla y las mismas acciones reproducen la partida bit a bit.

## Verificación

- **8 suites, 485 904 comprobaciones**, todas en verde.
- **Validación contra M/M/c: error relativo del 0.20 %** en la permanencia media.
- El juego es **ganable y perdible**: con el equipo completo se ganan los 30 días; sin contratar a nadie se pierde en el día 3.
- 60 fps estables, sin errores de consola.

## Fallos que aparecieron al construirlo

Documentados en `notas/06-bitacora-y-decisiones.md` y cubiertos con pruebas:

1. La fórmula de `Lq` del módulo analítico estaba mal (le faltaba el factor `(c·ρ)^c`): daba 0.1050 donde Erlang-C da 0.1751. Lo detectó la comparación con la solución analítica.
2. El reparto del trabajo de los mecánicos causaba inanición de cola: los dos se iban siempre al diagnóstico y la reparación no recibía a nadie.
3. El día se cerraba dos veces y la nómina se cobraba por duplicado: el taller quebraba el primer día.
4. La partida se serializaba sin candado y el polling del cliente lo corrompía.

## Notas

Las notas 01–04 se reescribieron como documento de diseño del juego, y la 03 documenta por qué el juego usa una escala de tiempos más corta que el modelo analítico.

body:
Backport of #21754 to `4.13.x`, rebuilt by hand on the branch rather than from the conflicting cherry-picks: the dependency bumps first, then the APIM commits as merged on 4.12.x.

## Issue

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/APIM-15561

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/APIM-15566

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/CJ-5412

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/CJ-5411

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/AIAM-1340

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/APIM-15572

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/APIM-15569

https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/AUTHZ-373

## Description

Same leak as APIM-15203 and APIM-14921, more call sites: Vert.x 5 keeps every client it creates in the close future of its owner until Vert.x itself closes, so a client created per call accumulates even when it is closed.

- `fix(rest-api)`: the Kafka console proxy (`ProxyKafkaConsoleResource`) created one `HttpClient` per proxied request. The clients now live in a `KafkaConsoleClient` Spring bean, one per Kafbat address, closed with the context. Since its pool is shared by every user of the node, each proxied request has an idle timeout (`kafka.console.server.timeout`, ms, default 30000), the whole exchange is bounded to twice that (on that timeout the Kafbat request is reset, so a response still trickling in or a request still waiting for a connection gives its pooled connection back), the wait queue is bounded, and the browser's hop-by-hop and framing headers and the APIM `Cookie` are no longer relayed to Kafbat (the body length is set by Vert.x).
- `fix(gateway)`: debug mode (`DebugReactorEventListener`) created one `HttpClient` per debug run. The listener now builds a single client on first use, and resets the request of a run that hits the global timeout so that it frees its pooled connection.
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-fetcher-http` to 3.0.2, which reuses one client across page fetches instead of one per fetch (gravitee-io/gravitee-fetcher-http#66).
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-fetcher-github` to 3.0.2, `gravitee-fetcher-gitlab` to 3.0.2 and `gravitee-fetcher-bitbucket` to 3.0.3, which reuse one client across fetches (and GitHub / GitLab tree listings) and free the pooled connection of a non-200 response (gravitee-io/gravitee-fetcher-github#60, gravitee-io/gravitee-fetcher-gitlab#66, gravitee-io/gravitee-fetcher-bitbucket#61).
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-alert-engine-connectors-ws` to 3.0.1, which reuses one WebSocket client per Alert Engine endpoint instead of one per connection attempt (gravitee-io/gravitee-ae-connectors#59).
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-exchange` to 3.0.1 and `gravitee-cockpit-connectors-ws` to 6.0.1. The Cockpit connector plugin bundles `gravitee-exchange-connector-websocket`, which now reuses one WebSocket client per endpoint instead of one per reconnection or failed attempt (gravitee-io/gravitee-exchange#107, gravitee-io/gravitee-cockpit-connectors#416).
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-gamma-module-aim` to 5.0.10, whose AM SDK client factory shares one `WebClient` instead of building one per AM call (gravitee-io/gravitee-gamma-module-aim#1218).

Clients built once per API deployment (APIM-15572): on Vert.x 5.0.x a closed client stays registered on the close future of the context that created it, so every redeploy leaves the previous clients in memory until the node stops. HTTP and WebSocket clients are created as Vert.x shared clients under a unique name (a shared client is registered through a nested close future that unregisters itself on close; the unique name means no pool is ever shared); `NetClient` has no shared mode, so it is unregistered right after creation, as `NetClientUtils` does in native-kafka.

- `fix(healthcheck)`: the v2 health check (`EndpointRuleHandler`) client.
- `fix(service-discovery)`: the v4 Consul service discovery client (`ConsulServiceDiscoveryService`).
- `fix(tcp-proxy)`: the TCP proxy endpoint client (`TcpClientFactory`), now closed when the endpoint stops (`TcpProxyEndpointConnector.doStop`, through the shared `LazyCloseable` above).
- `fix(repository-redis)`: the Redis repository (rate limit and distributed sync) built a new Redis client, hence a new `NetClient`, on every connection attempt; it now reuses one client per event loop across reconnects. Limit: in sentinel and cluster mode a discarded connection (failover, READONLY node) does not expose its socket and is dropped with its client, so each lost connection there still costs one client; failed connect attempts no longer do.
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-node` to 9.14.2 (HTTP and WebSocket client factories, which also fixes the HTTP proxy endpoint, the v4 health check, the v4 HTTP dynamic properties and the MCP, LLM, A2A and agent-to-agent endpoints, gravitee-io/gravitee-node#630), `gravitee-connector-http` to 6.0.5 (v2 APIs, gravitee-io/gravitee-connector-http#133), `gravitee-resource-auth-provider-http` to 2.0.1 (gravitee-io/gravitee-resource-auth-provider-http#37), `gravitee-reactor-llm-proxy` to 5.0.1 (GCP token client and upstream client now closed and released), `gravitee-service-discovery-consul` from 1.3.0 to 3.0.0 (built against Vert.x 5: 1.x embeds a Vert.x 4 Consul client that cannot run on 4.13, plus the same leak fix, gravitee-io/gravitee-service-discovery-consul#22).
- `fix(deps)` (gravitee-node): the Hazelcast cache and cluster plugin URLs in `helm/values.yaml` follow the 9.14.2 bump, with a chart CHANGELOG entry.
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-entrypoint-webhook` to 8.0.4, which reuses one client per callback origin across subscriptions (APIM-15569, gravitee-io/gravitee-entrypoint-webhook#183).
- `refactor(common)` + `fix(http-proxy)` + `fix(tcp-proxy)`: the HTTP, WebSocket and TCP client factories of the proxy endpoints hold their client in a shared `LazyCloseable` (`gravitee-apim-common`): built on an event loop by the first request, closed by the thread that stops the endpoint, with build and close serialised so that close never misses a client being built, and a closed holder fails instead of building a client nobody would close.
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-reactor-a2a-proxy` to 2.1.3, whose endpoint connector now closes its upstream HTTP client when it stops (it never did, so the gravitee-node fix alone could not release it, gravitee-io/gravitee-reactor-a2a-proxy#29).
- `fix(deps)`: bump `gravitee-gamma-module-authz` to 3.6.5, whose AM SDK directory client factory shares one `WebClient` instead of building one per AM user sync run (AUTHZ-373, gravitee-io/gravitee-gamma-module-authz#288).

## Additional context

- Kafka console pool: 20 HTTP/1 connections instead of the default 5, since the console page loads its assets in parallel (before, each request had its own client).
- The Kafka console and debug mode clients are no longer closed per call; they are released when Vert.x stops.
- The bumps go to `gravitee-apim-distribution/pom.xml`; `gravitee-node` and `gravitee-connector-http` are also bumped in the root `pom.xml`, which declares them too (Danger checks `gravitee-node`).
- Retention tests for the new fixes open real connections before stopping the component (a shared client only unregisters once its connections are closed) and fail without the fix: 20 clients left for the v2 health check and the TCP proxy, 10 for Consul v4, 8 for the Redis repository. The health check (HTTP client), TCP proxy (`NetClient`) and Redis tests carry a canary that fails once Vert.x no longer leaks closed clients (5.2).
- Every workaround tied to that Vert.x 5.0 behaviour, and every canary, is tagged `vertx-5.0-close-future-leak`, so removing them with Vert.x 5.2 is a single search. The client reuse in the Kafka console, debug mode and Redis repository is not a workaround and stays.
- Tests: `ProxyKafkaConsoleResourceTest` counts the clients held by Vert.x after 20 proxied requests (1); `should_reuse_one_http_client_across_debug_runs` checks a single client across two debug runs.
- Follow-up of the static scan of Vert.x client creatio

author: jonasyr
body:
Agents rarely used Serena and codebase-memory, and subagents used them even less. This PR finds out why (14 days of transcripts) and fixes the causes in every setup loadout supports. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-serena-cbm-usage-design.md`; decision: ADR 0039.

## Why

| 14 days, Claude Code 2.1.305 | Sessions | Serena used in | codebase-memory used in | Symbol-like greps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main sessions | 592 | 5 | 6 | 1375 |
| Subagents | 590 | 17 | 17 | 3146 |

- **Tools loaded on demand.** Subagents had to call ToolSearch before using Serena or the graph. Only 27 of 585 ever did.
- **Hints that never block were ignored.** loadout's search hint was followed 3 times out of 109.
- **No Grep or Glob tools.** Claude Code on Linux, macOS and WSL has neither; agents search through Bash. So the old `Grep|Glob` hooks never fired.
- **codebase-memory's own `hook-augment` prints nothing.** In 0.12.1 every call takes about 6 s against its own 2 s deadline (upstream #2683, #2441).

## What changes

- **Serena's documented Claude Code hooks, `remind` included.** Each runs through `hooks/mcp_guard.py`, which stays silent in three cases:
  - Serena is not installed;
  - Serena is switched off for the folder;
  - you already run the same hook yourself.
- **`alwaysLoad` for both plugin servers.** Their tools are called directly, also in subagents. Cost: about 12-13k tokens per context.
- **loadout's search hint is removed.** The Context7 / Microsoft Learn hint for docs lookups stays.
- **Subagents get the exact tool names**, and Codex gets its own "search first" card.
- **The codebase-memory project of the folder is named** at session and subagent start. This is a file check; no daemon is involved.
- **`cbm_auto_index` preference**, default on, can be undone. codebase-memory then indexes a new git repo on its own.
- **`hooks/refresh.py` re-indexes in the background** an indexed repo that codebase-memory's watcher does not watch. It runs at the end of a turn, after a git command that rewrites the tree, or after 20 changed files.
- **Serena needs no refresh.** Verified in Python and TypeScript.
- **New check rows:**
  - your own Serena hooks;
  - a second Serena or codebase-memory server;
  - codebase-memory's own hooks;
  - `auto_index`;
  - a failed refresh.
- **`loadout usage` counts better.** A better parser counts searches with several patterns and every search in a chained command, and Serena's reminders are counted.
- **The codex-reviewer agent** can read with Serena and the graph.

## Validation

- **Full suite:** 3388 passed.
- **Live, against real Serena 2.1.0 and codebase-memory 0.12.1:**
  - `remind` blocks the 3rd grep, end to end through `run.sh` and the guard.
  - The refresh makes a new function visible in an unwatched repo: 0 hits before, 1 after. This check caught two bugs that the stub tests missed: a tree output instead of JSON, and collapsed dashes in project names.
  - The project pointer is right for default and custom project names.
- **Live, a headless Claude Code session on this branch's plugin:**
  - The main agent and an unprompted subagent called `trace_path`, `search_graph` and `find_symbol` first, with no ToolSearch.
  - Serena's reminder fired in the subagent, which then switched to `trace_path`.

Codex users approve the changed plugin hooks again in `/hooks` (or the extension's hook review). `loadout check` lists that.

author: allpro244
body:
Region growth, part 2 (after #448). The region's land developers now carry balance sheets, like the commercial rivals and the homebuilders (#427), and they compete with the player for farms.

## Before
The named developers were counts with an unlimited purse. They bought every farm whose read cleared. One whose streets did not pay held the land indefinitely at no cost. They never competed with the player: a farm in the player's talks was off their market.

## Now (`growth.ts`, `homes.ts`)
- **Founding and finance.** Each developer starts with its own money (the homebuilders' purse) and a construction desk. The desk advances 65% against the land and 75% against the streets (12 CFR 34 App. A interagency LTV limits). Interest is paid out of cash monthly at index + 2.4. Fees and closing costs are paid in cash.
- **Revenue.** The developer is paid lot by lot as the builders take its lots (`landDevSold`). Each sale releases 120% of the per-lot loan to the desk.
- **Underwriting.** A developer signs only a deal it can carry to the end: the land, the fees and the streets, net of what it has already promised its other farms.
- **Refused rezoning.** The farm is sold back at its farm-use value.
- **Banked land** pays the interest every month it sits. A developer that cannot pay its way for three months fails. Its desk sells the farms, and a farm already zoned for houses reads with no board. Its plats' lots go to the builders through the market, and the shortfall is the desk's loss.
- **Competition with the player.** A farm the player is negotiating for, but has not yet signed, stays on the developers' market. The seller's price becomes the player's offer when that is higher. A developer that values the farm more buys it out from under the player, and the news says so (`voidContract`).

## Measured
- **Competition probe (seed 3).** Talks were opened on every listed farm at farm-use value. In three years, 5 farms were bought out from under the player, and no developer ever held a farm while the player was still in talks for it.
- **10 years.** Seed 1: plats 7 → 6, houses 228 → 226. Seed 3: unchanged at 17 plats and 492 houses; the developers there are profitable and the books never bind. Developer cash at year 10 is $0.04-3.0M, and debt is retired as lots sell.

## Checks
`BW_CITY=region` conserve (2 seeds × 120 months) reconciled to $0. Also passed: landdev, homebuild, platdesign, region-growth (it now prints each developer's cash, debt and lots sold, and checks its debt against its loans), rng-audit, tsc.

body:
## Summary

`GroupedTaskRow` (`packages/ui/src/project-sidebar/grouped/task-row.tsx`) returned early with `if (dragOverlay) return taskRow;` before about 15 hooks: `useState`, `useRef`, `useEffect`, `useFeedbackStore`, `useTaskListItemContextActions`, `useDraggable` and `useDroppable`. That breaks the rules of hooks. Today `TaskGroupedView` mounts the overlay as its own `GroupedTaskItem` that always has `dragOverlay`, so the path is never hit. But any instance that flipped the prop would throw "Rendered fewer hooks than expected".

The component is now split, so each part has a fixed hook order:

- **`GroupedTaskRow`** is a thin memoized wrapper. It picks between the two views below.
- **`GroupedTaskDragOverlayRow`** is the presentation-only overlay. It calls only `useZCodeIntl`, so it still avoids the drag/drop, context-menu and task-path hooks, as the existing comment requires.
- **`GroupedTaskInteractiveRow`** is the full row. The `dragOverlay` branches that could never be reached are gone.
- **`deriveGroupedTaskRowPresentation`** is a plain function (not a hook) that both views share: title, attention badge, leading indicator, cron/off-peak flags, time label and active state.

Overlay markup and classes are unchanged:
- no `role`, `tabIndex` or `title`;
- `pointer-events-none cursor-grabbing … shadow-lg`, plus `bg-selected` when the row is active;
- the interaction badge has no snooze action;
- no workflow run lines and no hover actions.

## Tests

- New `packages/ui/test/groupedTaskRowDragOverlay.test.ts`. It renders the overlay and the normal row, then switches `dragOverlay` back and forth on one instance. The toggle test failed on `integration` with "Rendered fewer hooks than expected" and passes now.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` on 10 related files: 47/47 passed.
  - `groupedTaskRowDragOverlay`, `groupedTaskRowArchiveConfirm`, `groupedTaskRowTooltip`, `workspaceGroupedTaskPermissionTag`, `taskWorkbenchDragPreview`
  - `taskListItemHoverActions`, `taskRowActionButton`, `remoteConnectionPresentationComponents`, `webRemoteControlTaskIndexRowHoverActions`, `groupedOffPeakSystemGroup`
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
  - The first run failed in `components/ai-elements/message.tsx` (shiki `BundledLanguage` mismatch), a file this PR doesn't touch. The cause was a stale local `node_modules`.
  - After `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, typecheck passes.
  - That install's `prepare` step (`install-git-hooks.mjs && build:cua`) exited 1. This is unrelated to this change.
- `pnpm lint`: 0 errors and 96 warnings, the same total as on `integration`. None are in `task-row.tsx`.
  - The repo's oxlint config doesn't enable `react/rules-of-hooks`.
  - With that rule enabled explicitly, `task-row.tsx` goes from **16 warnings to 0**.
- `pnpm fmt:check`: ok.
- `pnpm architecture:check --changed`: 0 violations.
- Not run: E2E and a manual drag in the app. The overlay markup is unchanged, and the overlay is still mounted the same way from `TaskGroupedView`.

## Summary by Sourcery

Split grouped task rows into dedicated overlay and interactive views to preserve stable hook usage across drag states.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent React hook-order errors when grouped task rows switch between interactive and drag-overlay modes.

Enhancements:
- Separate grouped task overlay presentation from the full interactive row while sharing their display state.
- Keep drag overlays free of interaction controls, workflow content, and task-path side effects.

Tests:
- Add coverage for overlay presentation, interactive-row behavior, and toggling between both modes without rendering errors.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Drag overlays now display tasks without interactive controls, while regular task rows retain their usual interactions.
  * Changing a task row between overlay and regular display no longer causes an error.
* **Tests**

author: cayden-design
body: ## Why cards posted as unclassified Mia Rene Davies and Doug Pace were not missing a client, a voice prompt, or a campaign map. The SalesGlider webhook (`5d7ab500-3881-4e39-9ec1-2436b7a2c597`, campaign `4161324`) ran classification and then stored the reply as `OTHER`. The same thing hit Nutter LinkedIn (`#nutter-ai-replies`): Charles King, Christopher McCoy, and Faith Thomas (Oct 20–22). LinkedIn never has a SmartLead category, so every client’s HeyReach replies go through Jev, then Gemini. Railway logs at the unclassified posts: - Jev: `401 {"error":{"message":"User not found."}}` - Gemini classify (and the OOO / not-interested second passes): `402 Payment Required` (prepay credits depleted) - The handler then logged `suppressed from Slack { classification: 'OTHER' }` and `[OtherAlert] Posted` That `OTHER` is the unclassified Slack line (`Not auto-drafted`). It is not a model decision. Email clients that already have a SmartLead category skip Jev, which is why their email channels still got draft cards. Two follow-on bugs made the miss stick: - SmartLead thread history is `{ history: [{ type: 'SENT', email_body }] }`. Jev only read `role: 'us'`, so `last_outbound_from_us` was "they may have written first" and the prompt prefers OTHER. - Claude drafts call Gemini embeddings first. The same 402 aborted Claude and fell through to a Gemini draft that also 402s, so even a positive label produced no model draft. Mia's real cards showed up later. Doug Pace and the three Nutter rows were recorded suppressed and never got a card. This PR does not rewrite those rows. ## Fix The fallback is not SalesGlider-specific. `classifyReply` calls `classifyDuringOutage` with no client id and no platform check, for SmartLead and HeyReach webhooks and pollers. When Jev fails and Gemini classify is unavailable, label the reply instead of storing OTHER: - info / "what do you do" / "can you send" → `QUESTION` - a thread we already wrote on, or any other short non-pitch reply → `INTERESTED` - clear no, OOO, unsubscribe, wrong person, and recruiter-style pitches stay out of the draft set - "Good luck with the search" / "best of luck" is a polite no (`NOT_INTERESTED`, not drafted), including Charles King - "will speak internally to our board" and "I was with AITP board for a few years" stay `INTERESTED` and draft A real Gemini `OTHER` is still kept. `CLASSIFIER_FALLBACK_GEMINI=0` still returns `jev_failed` / OTHER. SmartLead `SENT` history (and the webhook `sent_message` when history is missing) is now the last outbound passed to Jev. Claude still drafts when the embedding lookup throws. Pollers stay Gemini-only. If Gemini billing is empty they use the existing template draft, which is still a draft card rather than the unclassified line. This branch includes the follow-up card dedupe from PR #119, which is already on `claude/prospect-reply-automation-q2jei`. The two changes do not touch the same files, and both stay. ## Config to change (not done here) 1. `JEV_API_KEY` is rejected with `401 User not found`. Restore that Jev user or replace the key (`JEV_API_URL` is still set; the call reached the API). 2. The Gemini project behind `GEMINI_API_KEY` is out of prepay credits (`402` on `gemini-3.8-flash`, including embeddings). Top up AI Studio billing so classification and drafts use the models again. Until then, new email and LinkedIn replies on every client get a heuristic label and a Claude draft (webhooks) or the template draft (pollers). No client row, campaign map, or voice prompt change is required. Already-suppressed rows are left as they are. Production config and data were not changed. ## Tests `npm test` after merging in the deploy branch — 507 passed, 0 failed. Cases cover Mia, Doug, and the three Nutter LinkedIn replies, plus a source check that the outage helper names no client. The PR #119 follow-up idempotency tests still pass.

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific rule for the cookie notice on rejestr.io. The notice is a plain paragraph in the page footer with a single "OK" button that acknowledges it (the text tells users to change browser settings if they don't consent). Because the footer is not fixed or sticky, the heuristic flow never detects it. The rule finds the notice's OK button in `#footer`, clicks it to dismiss the notice, and the self-test checks that the button is no longer visible. The site stores the choice in localStorage, so the rule does not match again on later loads.

- `npx playwright test tests/rejestr-io.spec.ts --project=chrome`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

body:
## Real consistency bug
Phase 8K improved the HTTP 401 text to `Your signed-in session is missing or expired`. But `IdentityBetaApp.runAction()` still decided to discard stale auth using the old regex `/session expired|unauthorized/i`, which no longer matches that string. A protected Friends 401 could therefore leave stale signed-in identity state visible.

## Fix
- Introduce `VeyraSessionExpiredError` for **bearer-protected requests only** that returned HTTP 401.
- Detect the concrete error type in React and atomically clear in-memory session, friends and pagination.
- First-time registration/login cryptographic 401 remains a **signature error**, not a fabricated expired session.
- Regression tests simulate `AUTH_REQUIRED` from Friends and `INVALID_SIGNATURE` from registration.
- No persistence, signing, payment or Mainnet changes.

CI PASS required before merge/deploy. Port to the isolated Identity Beta hosting release; no financial production changes.

author: pauliano22
body:
## Summary
- **dashboard**: bump `next` 16.2.2 → 16.4.2 and `eslint-config-next` to match. This resolves multiple critical Next.js advisories on the installed version range, including unauthenticated RCE in the Image Optimization API (AVIF) and in `next/og`'s `ImageResponse`, SSRF in Server Actions/rewrites, and several middleware/proxy bypasses. Also updates `@clerk/nextjs`, `@clerk/backend`, `@clerk/react`, `@clerk/shared` within their existing `^7.x` semver range, which resolves critical advisories in `@clerk/nextjs` and `@clerk/shared`.
- **dashboard**: the `next`/`eslint-config-next` bump enables a new `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule that flags the existing fetch-on-mount effect in `src/app/page.tsx` (it calls `setLoading`/`setFetchError` before the first `await`, which is the standard pattern for this kind of effect). Added a scoped `eslint-disable-next-line` with a comment explaining why, rather than restructuring the data-fetching logic, to keep this PR focused on the security fix.
- **mcp-server**: ran `npm audit fix` to resolve `proxy-addr` (critical — IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet), plus `hono`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `ip-address`, `qs`, and other transitive advisories. `package.json` is unchanged — all fixes landed within existing semver ranges.

## Not fixed
`npm audit` still reports 5 high-severity advisories in `braces` (ReDoS), pulled in transitively through `eslint-config-next`'s own lint tooling (`@next/eslint-plugin-next` → `fast-glob` → `micromatch` → `braces`). The only available fix is `npm audit fix --force`, which would **downgrade** `eslint-config-next` to `14.2.35` — the wrong direction, and not compatible with Next 16. This is dev-tooling only (runs during `eslint`, not shipped to users or the production bundle) with no attacker-controlled input path, so it's left as accepted residual risk.

## Test plan
- [x] `cd dashboard && npm run build` — succeeds (Next 16.4.2, Turbopack)
- [x] `cd dashboard && npm run lint` — passes with 0 errors
- [x] `cd mcp-server && npm run build` (tsc) — succeeds
- [x] `npm audit` re-run on both packages post-fix (dashboard: 0 critical/moderate, 5 high residual as noted above; mcp-server: 0 vulnerabilities)

author: sei-ahouseholder
body:
- Closes #5039
<!-- ⚠️  THIS LINE MUST BE FIRST — before any ## header. Moving it breaks the GitHub sidebar. -->

## Summary

The Case Manager's abandonment of an open embargo proposal, its honour of a late `Accept` and its re-invite of a late accepter now carry the semantic type of their AS2 shape, as ADR-0152 rulings 1 and 2 require. A Case Manager that has a stake in an embargo now records its own consent change as its `Update(EmbargoConsent)`, never as a `Reject`, so a replica can tell the Case Manager's abandonment from a participant's refusal by the payload's `actor`.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0

## Changes

- **New `UNDO_INVITE_TO_EMBARGO_ON_CASE`** (`vultron/core/models/events/base.py`, `events/embargo.py`, `wire/as2/vocab/activities/embargo.py`, `wire/as2/extractor/_instances.py`, `wire/as2/factories/embargo.py`, `core/ports/trigger_activity.py`, `adapters/driven/trigger_activity_adapter/embargo.py`, `semantic_registry/embargo.py`, example `undo_embargo_invite`): `Undo(Invite(EmbargoEvent))` gets a pattern, a factory, a port method and a registry entry with `use_case_class=None`. A copy that arrives is reported "no use case found" (#5037's path). `("Undo", "Invite")` is added to the canonical and CASE_MANAGER-authored signatures (`sync/nodes/canonical_entry.py`).
- **Abandonment** (`core/behaviors/embargo/nodes/abandon.py`): for each open proposal, the Case Manager commits the activity that cancels it, carrying the `CANCEL`: its `Reject` of a proposal it received, or its `Undo` of one it sent itself. It then commits an `Undo` of each Invite it relayed for that proposal (`relayed_invite_ids`, read from the ledger). All of it runs in one transaction. A proposal never relayed is cancelled all the same. `_abandoned` is removed.
- **Replica split** (`sync/nodes/embargo_event_conditions.py`, `announce_tree.py`): `reject_invite_to_embargo_on_case` is split by `sent_by_case_manager`. The Case Manager's `Reject` goes to the abandonment slot, which cancels the proposal; a participant's goes to the rejection slot, which records `DECLINED`. A new `EmbargoInviteWithdrawal` slot copies the `Undo`'s `CANCEL`, which a relay's `Undo` finds already in place. The replica code that applies the cancel moved to `embargo/nodes/abandon_effect.py`.
- **The Case Manager's own consent** (`embargo/nodes/manager_commit.py` `CommitOwnConsentDecisionNode`, `trigger_tree.py` `reject_embargo_trigger_bt`, `use_cases/triggers/embargo/reject.py`): when the Case Manager rejects by trigger, it commits only its `Update(EmbargoConsent)` of the row and builds no `Reject`. The trigger response reports that `Update` as its `activity` (TRIG-04-001). The `reject-embargo` route description now says this, and `test/adapters/driving/fastapi/openapi_trigger_snapshot.json` is regenerated for that description-only change (TRIG-12-003).
- **Honoured late `Accept`** (`expiry_tree.py`, `answer_trees.py`, `nodes/expiry_commit.py`): the honour is no longer a diversion. The new `on_time_or_honoured_accept` backstop lets a late `Accept` of the embargo in force take the on-time path, so the received `Accept` is committed verbatim and no `Update(EmbargoConsent)` follows. `CommitAndApplyHonourLateAcceptNode` and `create_commit_and_honour_late_accept_tree` are removed.
- **Re-invite** (`nodes/reinvite.py`, new `embargo/proposer.py`): the re-invite of a late accepter, and the Invite sent to a reinstated participant, is now a relay committed as `invite_to_embargo_on_case`. Its `attributedTo` is the embargo's proposer, read from the ledger by `embargo_proposer_id`, or the Case Manager when no Invite proposed the embargo. `is_relayed_embargo_invite` now also reads a self-attributed Case Manager Invite as a relay when the replica's register already holds the embargo it names, decided. On the proposer's replica, the relay slot indexes only an embargo that is still an open proposal, so a re-invite to the embargo in force leaves the index as the Case Manager's store has it (EP-08-003). `RelayOpenProposalsToJoinerNode` reuses the same helper. `EMBARGO_REINVITE_SEMANTIC_TYPE` and its replica slot are removed.
- **Module splits** (BTND-07-004): `sync/nodes/event_conditions.py` is split into `_event_condition_base.py` and `embargo_event_conditions.py`, and `embargo/nodes/abandon.py` into `abandon_effect.py`. Both old modules re-export the moved names.
- **Specs**: EMB-16-001, EMB-17-002, EMB-17-003, EMB-17-009 and MSM-07-004 are amended, VAM-05-013 is added, and EMB-17-011 is retired with `spec-retire` (`plan/retired-specs/EMB-17-011.md`). ADR-0140 item 4's honour bullet now points to ADR-0152.
- **Docs and notes**: `docs/topics/behavior_logic/use-cases/embargo-lifecycle.md`, `docs/reference/vultron-spec/_pec-state-machine.md`, `docs/reference/messages/em.md` (with the regenerated occasion fragments and `lookup*`), `notes/embargo-lifecycle.md`, `notes/participant-embargo-consent.md`, `notes/case-communication-model.md` and `vultron/core/behaviors/embargo/AGENTS.md`.
- **Test fix**: `test_sender_entitlement_ratchet.py` built its parametrize ids from every registry entry, so it broke at collection once one entry had no use case (latent since #5037). The ids now come from the same generator as the parameters.

### How AC-3 is met under the decision on #5039

The user chose option A: a Case Manager with an embargo stake (EP-09-002) records its own consent change as its `Update(EmbargoConsent)` and never as a `Reject(Invite(EmbargoEvent))` (amended MSM-07-004). After this change, every `Reject(Invite(EmbargoEvent))` the Case Manager sends in the ledger is an abandonment. So the replica's split on the payload's `actor` is sound: the Case Manager's `Reject` cancels the proposal, and a participant's records `DECLINED`. Tests cover both: `test_a_reject_is_the_abandonment_only_from_the_case_manager`, `test_the_managers_reject_and_a_participants_take_different_slots` and `test_the_managers_own_reject_is_its_update_of_the_row`.

### Behaviour change to note: the honoured late `Accept` no longer re-issues stale stub Invites

The old honour diversion ran `embargo_admission_backfill_nodes`, which is the backfill followed by `ReissueStubInvitesNode`. The honour now runs the on-time `Accept` path, whose effects are the record and the backfill only, so AC-4 holds: replica state is the same as after an on-time `Accept`. The stub re-issue (CM-11-016) exists to replace stub Invites whose terms are stale because the embargo in force changed. An `Accept`, late or on time, never changes the embargo in force; it only moves the accepter's own row. So the honour had nothing to make stale. Any stub that was already stale is re-issued by the act that changed the embargo, which still runs the re-issue (the owner's activation, termination, `Add` and `Remove(EmbargoEvent)`). The backfill (CM-10-006), which the honour does need because it can admit the accepter, still runs.

## Spec amended

### EMB-16-001

- Before: A Participant in EM Proposed (q^em ∈ P) that detects a CS transition into a public (q^cs ∈ ···P··), exploit-available (q^cs ∈ ····X·), or attacks-observed (q^cs ∈ ·····A) state MUST abandon the proposed embargo by cancelling each open proposal in the case's embargo register, so EM derives None (q^em P → N), and MUST emit ER to notify other Participants.
- After: A Participant in EM Proposed (q^em ∈ P) that detects a CS transition into a public (q^cs ∈ ···P··), exploit-available (q^cs ∈ ····X·), or attacks-observed (q^cs ∈ ·····A) state MUST abandon the proposed embargo by cancelling each open proposal in the case's embargo register, so EM derives None (q^em P → N), and MUST notify the other Participants. The CASE_MANAGER cancels each proposal with the activity its AS2 shape names: its ER, `Reject(Invite(EmbargoEvent))`, of a proposal it received, committed as `reject_invite_to_embargo_on_case`, or its `Undo(Invite(EmbargoEvent))` of a proposal it made itself, committed as `undo_invite_to_embargo_on_case`, followed by its `Undo(Invi

author: houfu
body:
Security audit follow-up (2026-10-22).

The eMudhra/emSign intermediate-CA key compromise requires removing the emSign root CA from trust stores; certifi < 2026.10.19 ships a bundle trusting it (MITM risk on outbound TLS). Prod images (zeeker-datasette + zeeker-frontend, currently certifi 2025.4.26 inside the running containers) are built from this repo — after merge, CI publishes a new sha image tagged with the merge commit SHA, and a separate compose tag-bump PR rolls prod forward (docker compose pull && up -d, never --build).

Refs: https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576 (certifi GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2)

Change: `uv lock --upgrade-package certifi` — uv.lock only, certifi 2025.4.26 bumped to 2026.10.19 (>= 2026.10.19). No code changes.

author: cptnope
body:
## Why
The current workflow runs 6 OS/Python combinations plus MCP integration on both every feature-branch push and the PR, unnecessarily multiplying billed Actions time.

## Changes
- Stop triggering CI on feature-branch pushes. PRs and main receive only Ubuntu/Python 3.12 core tests + a Linux MCP integration test.
- Keep the full 3-OS x 2-Python cross-platform matrix available through **Actions → Python security baseline (lean) → Run workflow**.
- Add a 5-minute timeout per job to prevent stalled tests consuming Actions minutes.
- Add concurrency cancellation for superseded runs and pip caching for faster setup.

No production application code changes. Review the new PR's quick checks; merge to activate savings for future runs.

author: nawaaaaaaaar
body:
## Summary

Fixes #570.

Reject MultiIndex level names containing whitespace before serializing the CF `compress` attribute. Its level names are space-separated, so encoding a level such as `"lat lon"` currently succeeds but decoding then looks for nonexistent `"lat"` and `"lon"` coordinates.

The error names the offending level and tells the caller to rename it. Ordinary Unicode names remain supported; no arbitrary restriction to ASCII or Python identifiers is introduced.

## Reproduction

Reproduced on unchanged upstream `ee13cb860717299ca8f66d35461e5e50910f3d47`: encode a MultiIndex with a `"lat lon"` level and decode it. Encoding succeeds and decoding raises `KeyError: 'lat'`. The initial regression matrix failed in all 15 cases before the production change.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest cf_xarray/tests/test_coding.py -q`: **35 passed** on current head.
- New coverage: spaces, tabs, newlines, leading/trailing whitespace, Unicode whitespace, all three index-selection forms, unchanged input after rejection, and a valid Unicode-name round trip.
- `ruff check cf_xarray/coding.py cf_xarray/tests/test_coding.py`: passed.
- `ruff format --check cf_xarray/coding.py cf_xarray/tests/test_coding.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

This deliberately validates an unrepresentable input instead of silently renaming user coordinates or changing CF's attribute grammar.

## Coverage follow-up

The current head also tests that unrelated spaced variable names remain allowed and that unselected MultiIndexes are not validated, and documents the restriction in the coding guide.

A local coverage run confirms all newly added executable statements are covered. The only uncovered lines in `coding.py` are pre-existing lines 50, 113, 116, 133, 134, 138, and 139. This run passed all 35 coding tests.

Codecov currently reports 75% aggregate patch coverage while its `unittests` flag reports 100% patch coverage, and warns that the report is 132 commits behind main. The aggregate patch gate remains unresolved; no threshold or configuration has been weakened to bypass it.

author: nawaaaaaaaar
body:
## Summary

Fixes #398.

Allow a list or tuple of field names as the row-key argument to `pivot()`. Each key field becomes a separate leading output column. Scalar field-name calls keep their existing output shape.

The sorting key is flattened to the compound row fields plus the pivot-column field, and grouping uses a tuple of all row-key values. The existing aggregation, missing-value, and disk-backed sorting machinery is reused.

## Reproduction

Reproduced on unchanged upstream `364957617961c338657b202c169a461b935d1c32`:

```python
table = [
    ("city", "year", "kind", "value"),
    ("A", 2025, "x", 1),
    ("A", 2025, "y", 2),
    ("A", 2026, "x", 3),
]
list(etl.pivot(table, ["city", "year"], "kind", "value", sum))
# Before: ArgumentError: invalid field selection: ['city', 'year']
```

All ten added regression cases fail before changing production code.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest petl/test/transform/test_reshape.py --doctest-modules petl/transform/reshape.py -q`: **88 passed**.
- `python -m pytest petl/test/transform petl/test/util -q`: **592 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Regression coverage: list/tuple keys, aggregation of repeated keys, missing pivot cells, pre-sorted input, reversed input, two-row buffers forcing disk-backed sorting, repeated iteration, one-element key sequences, and header-only tables.
- `python -m compileall -q petl/transform/reshape.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Includes a docstring example and changelog entry. This adds compound row keys only; compound pivot-column keys and other reshape API redesigns are intentionally outside scope.

## Review follow-up

Reproduced Qodo's duplicate-header finding with two additional failing tests, then replaced independent name lookups with `asindices()` and the existing tuple-preserving `rowgetter()`. Compound grouping now resolves repeated header names consistently with sorting, for both presorted and automatically sorted input. Qodo now marks the finding resolved.

author: nawaaaaaaaar
body:
## Summary

Close XLSX workbooks in `finally` using openpyxl's public `Workbook.close()` API.

The existing cleanup runs only after the row loop has been exhausted. If a consumer closes the generator early, throws an exception into it, or selects a missing worksheet, the read-only workbook's ZIP archive remains open. This is a newly reproduced resource-management defect, rather than a duplicate of an existing issue or PR.

## Reproduction

Reproduced on unchanged upstream `364957617961c338657b202c169a461b935d1c32`:

1. Open an XLSX table with `read_only=True`.
2. Read one row.
3. Call `.close()` on the iterator.
4. The loaded workbook's `_archive.fp` is still open.

The regression matrix also reproduces the leak on `.throw()` and a missing sheet. These three cases fail before the fix; normal exhaustion is a passing compatibility control.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest petl/test/io/test_xlsx.py --doctest-modules petl/io/xlsx.py -q`: **52 passed**.
- Regression tests track actual openpyxl workbooks rather than replacing the workbook with a fake.
- Each test closes any leaked archive in its own `finally`, so the pre-fix reproduction does not leak descriptors into the rest of the suite.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Includes a changelog entry. Sheet selection, range handling, and row conversion are unchanged.

body:
Fixes #271. Implements the code and doc parts of the #272 prevention plan.

## What changed

- **Reminder battery** (`scripts/reminder-thread-battery.js`): always creates a fresh `mkdtemp` data dir, even when `SLEUTH_DATA_DIR` is already set; checks the runtime root actually moved before writing; no longer deletes anything before the run (the tree is fresh); removes only its own tree; restores the caller's `SLEUTH_DATA_DIR`. `RunScenarioAsync` returns `{ RuntimeRoot }`.
- **Jest setup** (`tests/runtime-setup.js`): always creates the per-worker temp dir; an inherited value is ignored.
- **Live-root refusal**: `Workspaces.AssertNotLiveRuntimeDir(caller)` throws when the runtime root contains a `.live-data` marker. `scripts/lists-harness.js` and `scripts/slack-harness-file-upload.js` call it before starting any module. The running app never calls it.
- **Loud missing state**: a missing enabled-channels file logs WARN ("auto-scheduling is OFF in every channel"); `RemindersModule.StartAsync` logs ERROR when that happens while the workspace has reminders.
- **Backups**: `backup-sleuth-data-fixed.sh` backs up the service's effective data dir (env, then the service's `SLEUTH_DATA_DIR`, then the install dir) and now includes `events/*.jsonl`.
- **AGENTS.md**: deployed servers are read-only for agents; names the allowed read-only tools and the forbidden ones.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 145 suites + 1 existing skip, 2,887 Jest tests; 116/116 Node. Build, `validate:commands`, `validate:fsm`, `validate:ai`, `validate:reminder-pipeline`, `validate:changelog-tone`, sanitize-scan: pass.
- Regression test `GH-271: never touches the caller's data dir` seeds all five live files, runs the battery, and requires them byte-identical. Both GH-271 battery tests **fail against the previous script** (2 failed).
- With `SLEUTH_DATA_DIR` set to a marked scratch dir, the battery and isolation suites pass and write **0** files into it.
- Backup: scratch tree with workspace/reminder/completion/stats/events files → zip → restore is byte-identical (JSON and JSONL).

## Not in this PR (ops, need operator approval)

- [ ] Create the `.live-data` marker in `/var/lib/aegis-sleuth` on prod and dev.
- [ ] After deploy, point the nightly backup cron at the deployed `backup-sleuth-data-fixed.sh` (the cron currently runs the stale copy in `/root/sleuth-app`).
- [ ] Add the read-only server rule to the operator's user-level agent instructions, so sessions in other repos see it.
- Skipped: the startup Slack notice does not show the channel count; the ERROR log covers detection. Revisit if a log-only signal is missed again.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: arvicco
body:
Linear A joins the library, the Old Uyghur dictionary lands on last week's segmenter, the sidecar harvest closes its genuine residue, and two research rails gate every future paid-model and parallels lane. Library: **2,474,515 documents / 117,467,688 passages across 251 corpus sources**. Wall time, adoption to gate handover: **2h52m of orchestration** (11:38Z–14:30Z spanned ~6h52m wall; the window also carried two owner-commissioned audits — the agent-outreach channel survey and an 81-survey yield audit — whose work ran interleaved with the gate batches).

## The new scripts

- **sigla** — the SigLA palaeographic database of Linear A (CC BY-NC-SA, read verbatim from the site footer): **787 inscriptions / 3,097 sign-group passages**, every attestation classified and rendered (syllabograms by phonetic value with homophone subscripts, logograms by Latin name, erasures as ⟦…⟧), 15 attestation-less inscriptions skipped by rule. The data ships as OCaml Marshal payloads inside a JS file; the new `ocaml-marshal` parser family decodes them natively and proves itself by re-encoding both upstream payloads byte-identically. Mined per the aggressive-mining rule: Minoan ceramic phases → dating through thirteen new researched Aegean band rows (**760 of 787 dated**, the Thera high/low chronology dispute declared in the table), find-sites → places (787), typology → the kind fold (tablets/nodules/roundels as administrative), CMS seal references as metadata. First sync verified: +787/0 errored, exactly the lane census.
- **wilkens-oui** — Wilkens's *Handwörterbuch des Altuigurischen* (Göttingen 2021, CC BY-SA 4.0 with the share-alike rider recorded): **49,619 dictionary entries** on the layout-aware segmenter shipped last phase — sub-entries as their own records under their main entry, 10,194 cross-reference pointers (~88.5% resolving), rejected readings kept as `false-reading`, printed-page citations. The class comment reconciles 49,619 accepted + 2 named skips against the measured 49,621 segmenter records and declares the residue (1,355 entries with U+FFFD where the PDF's Chinese font has no Unicode mapping — an enrichment, not a parse fix; typos as printed; collation residue upstream's own). First sync verified: +49,619/0 errored, sha-pinned single GET.

## The harvest and the rails

- **The sidecar harvest** (bhsa/dss/rem/ren): the brief's main items proved already shipped — the board entry was stale and is corrected — so the lane harvested the verified residue: every bhsa clause/phrase-grain feature + the `mother` dependency edge now ride the spans (all 88,131 clauses / 253,203 phrases covered); the DSS→BHSA lexeme crosswalk censused at 99.98% plain-string resolution (no table warranted; the silver etcbc decoder row rejected with its census); ReM's lost true-normalization lane restored plus six more; ReN's sentence/heading boundaries and annotator comments joined with loud two-way censuses; and a real CorA parser seam bug fixed (ReN inter-token comments were overwriting token comments). Parse-only passes verified: bhsa ~39, rem ~406, ren ~234 updated, zero errors.
- **The model-output shelf convention**, built before any producer exists: content-addressed cache keys (sha256 of urn|tool|prompt_version|model), versioned prompt files whose bump orphans rows without deleting, per-run sidecar provenance with an append-only fsynced cost ledger that survives kills, and a monthly budget table that fails closed — 17 seam tests, a seventh local shelf with its own write gateway.
- **The parallels recall@K harness** (`rake bench:parallels`): six gold ground-truth sets censused (inscription edition pairs 10,420 · cuneiform composite witnesses 46,775 · Trismegistos same-text 488 · SuttaCentral parallels 4,320 · passage-grain reuse alignments 96 · book-grain reuse 931,847), deterministic seeded sampling, precision reported honestly as a lower bound. Baselines ran at this gate and their sidecars are pinned under db/bench/ — every future scoring technique must now show a measured recall gain. The in-suite baseline already isolates a real blind spot: one-to-three-token inscriptions produce no 4-gram and score zero.
- **The smalls**: the plain slavic-wikisource family fetches all-or-nothing (the clobber fix ported from the indexed family); ONE dated MCP contract bump (findspot attribution, sense fields on show/search, fuzzy + translations search params, `nabu clarify` and `parallels --explain` CLI parity — pinned hashes updated deliberately); the eebo prose-imprint reader widened (+31 documents gain or fix an imprint place, verified by a full before/after diff over every distinct raw string; 32 strings remain honestly unreadable); rejected-grain skip assertions pinned for the remaining wikisource cones; and the person card lists catalogue mentions (rulers, authors, eponyms — a 3–16 ms prefix-range over existing facets, no new table: Esarhaddon → ruler: oracc 2,266 · cdli 576).

## The registry-merge rider (landed after the PR opened)

The lect registry's new package merged mid-gate and its follow-ups ride here: canonical synced (+8 anchors / +3 stages / +11 codemap rows), the five Wikisource cone postures retired to their machine grains — Telugu's whole cone stages **Classical Telugu** by a source override (all 453 documents, the cone is composition-bounded), Welsh stages **Early Modern Welsh** by print-year band inference (95 in-band; the 185 post-1800 modernized editions deliberately bare), Javanese/Sundanese/Breton resolve through the new aliases — and the **Jyotsnikā admits** (+1 document / 1,026 passages: the Malayalam anchor landed, the sii precedent executed; its era row honestly bandless, the dating proposals span the 15th–17th c.). The fixture registry re-cut (267/142/27/180, census pins swept), the etym honest-miss exemplar moved to Northern Sami now that Finnish is minted, and the four new scripts (Balinese, Javanese, Rejang, Sundanese) wire through the byte-check, collation and dossier tables with researched dossier rows. Lect staging re-materialized live: 2,025,525 facet rows.

## Verification

Combined suite at pick-sequence end: 14,602 runs / 317,893 assertions / 0F 0E 0S. Final suite on the gate tree, rider included: **14,602 runs / 317,917 assertions / 0F 0E 0S** (107 s parallel); lint 1,845 files clean. author: jasonmcintosh
body:
## Problem
Reports of a CA trust issue with eMudhra's emSign hierarchy. Service images keep trusting `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` (the root for the EM DV/OV/EV TLS CA - G3B/G3C and EM OV CS CA - G3B/G3C intermediates). I confirmed this in the published `orca:2026.3.1`, `2026.2.4` and `2026.1.3` images.

The JVM `cacerts` is generated from the distro `ca-certificates` package, so the fix is a rebuild against current packages. The JDK version doesn't matter for this.

## Change
Each `Dockerfile.slim` / `Dockerfile.ubuntu` (and `kayenta/Dockerfile`) gets one `RUN` right after the JVM install that:
- upgrades the CA packages (`apk upgrade`, or `apt-get install --only-upgrade ca-certificates ca-certificates-java`)
- fails the build if `keytool -list -cacerts` still lists emSign ECC Root CA - G3

Fixed package versions: Alpine `ca-certificates` 20261020-r0 (3.20 and 3.24), Ubuntu 20260816ubuntu0.22.04.1 (jammy) / 20260816ubuntu0.26.04.1 (resolute).

## Validation
Built orca `slim` and `ubuntu` from this branch and inspected the trust store:
- Alpine: only `emSign Root CA - G1` remains
- Ubuntu: `emSign ECC Root CA - C3`, `emSign Root CA - C1` and `emSign Root CA - G1` remain; G3 is gone
- The guard exits non-zero against the currently published `orca:2026.2.4` image, so it does fail on a vulnerable image

Not built locally: the other services (same pattern, same line), and `deck` / `spin` (no JVM, untouched). 2025.x branches are not covered.
Local Alpine builds needed `http://` apk mirrors because of TLS interception on my machine. The committed Dockerfiles are unchanged in that respect.

## After merge
Cut new patch releases from the branch so the rebuilt images are published.

author: houfu
body:
## Summary

The OpenWebUI rebase runbook told maintainers to `git fetch upstream --tags`. That puts OpenWebUI's version tags in the same `v*` namespace as LQ.AI's releases. Both projects have a `v0.9.0`, and git does not overwrite an existing tag on fetch, so in a clone that fetched upstream first, `v0.9.0` points at OpenWebUI's commit. The docs-site changelog (`git tag --merged HEAD` in `site/scripts/lib/git.mjs`) then silently left out our v0.9.0 release. GitHub's LegalQuants repo is unaffected; this is a local-clone problem the runbook caused.

Changes, all in `docs/openwebui-rebase-runbook.md`:

- §0 adds the remote with `--no-tags` (or sets `remote.upstream.tagOpt --no-tags` on an existing one) and fetches upstream tags into `refs/tags/owui/*`, with a paragraph on why.
- Every upstream tag in a command now uses the `owui/` form: the tag listing, `merge`/`merge-base`, the §3 `read-tree` grafts, `git show`, the `git grep` checks and the §9 `git log` range. Version names in prose stay as plain version numbers; LQ.AI's own tags stay bare.
- A new note covers clones that already have the bare tags: `git config remote.upstream.tagOpt --no-tags` then `git fetch legalquants --tags --force`, which repoints a colliding tag at the project's release.

`git grep` found no other doc or script that fetches upstream tags. ADR 0001 mentions "the latest upstream stable tag" only in prose, so it needs no change.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 docs/audits/check_doc_links.py docs/openwebui-rebase-runbook.md`: 0 dangling links
- [ ] Reviewer: run the new §0 fetch in a clone and confirm `git tag -l 'owui/v0.11*'` lists upstream tags and `git rev-parse v0.9.0` is the LQ.AI release (`91973fd80`)

author: nickmele
body:
A false claim reminder could clear a job's done and take the owner's end panel away. Neither reminder is now sent while `all_done` stands.

- **How it happened:** a reminder goes through `told_by_fleet`. The turn it starts isn't one of Fleet's own notices, so `hearing.rs` clears the done when it begins. On the job that built these reminders (#2694, #2695, #2704), the closing summary after `all_done` was read as asking the owner to walk something, and the reminder's turn removed his end panel.
- **The change:** `unbacked` returns nothing when a done stands. An agent that called `all_done` has said nothing is left.
- **Tests:** two new ones failed before the change, with `assertion left == right failed: all_done stands` and the rig test. After it: `21 tests run: 21 passed` across `reply_claims` and `session_done`.
- **Still open:** with no done standing, a reply that only describes a walk request still gets one false reminder. Rules can't tell description from request; #2692 is the model reader.

author: tommybarvaag
body:
## Problem

`BrandLogo` puts the caller's `className` on an inline span, so `size-*` on it does nothing. The mark's svg carries no class, so the `[&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4` rule in menu rows, select options and buttons draws it at 16px whatever size the caller asks for. A `size-3` mark in a `DropdownMenu.Item` paints a 16px svg in a 12px span, 2px off-centre. Outside a row a `size-6` mark keeps its 242×286 artwork size. Consumers had to reach through the span with `*:size-full!`.

Fixes #392.

## Scope

`BrandLogo` is a Fuse component, and the row and button recipes that override it are Fuse recipes, so the fix belongs here. Every consumer that shows a brand mark in a menu row, select option or button hits it. In Fuse that includes the `DataTableFilter` add menu and option lists.

Left out: sizing a full logo through `className`. A full logo keeps its inline span, because a sizing box collapses the viewBox-only Fjordkraft, Nordic Green Energy and Telinet full logos to 0×0 when nothing sizes them. A wordmark has no place in a 16px row slot.

## Change

- When `BrandLogo` draws a mark, its span gets `inline-flex shrink-0` ahead of the caller's `className`. The svg is clamped to the span with `min-w-full max-w-full min-h-full max-h-full`, so a size class on `BrandLogo` sizes the artwork, up or down.
- The clamp holds no `size-` class, so the row and button rule still gives an unsized mark its 16px. The issue's `size-full` would opt the svg out of that rule: an unsized mark in a menu row or button would then grow from 16px to its artwork size, about 240px, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- `shrink-0` stops Firefox and WebKit from shrinking the span to 0px wide in a cramped row. Chromium doesn't shrink it, so the Chromium-only browser suite can't catch its loss. The code comment records this.
- The drawn-mark span keeps the `hidden` guard Card, Attachment and Item use, because `inline-flex` beats the user agent's `[hidden]` rule without preflight.
- The Nordic Green Energy and Telinet mark svgs have only a viewBox, so the clamp would collapse an unsized mark to 0×0. `BrandLogo` passes them their viewBox extent as `width`/`height`. The bespoke mark components don't change, so direct callers that size one dimension keep their aspect-ratio sizing.
- JSDoc on `BrandLogo` and `BrandLogoProps`, a menu-row example and a sizing paragraph on the icons handbook page, and a patch changeset.

## Verification

New browser tests in `brand-logo.browser.test.tsx`. Each is checked against a hand-written size, except the artwork-size test, which reads each mark's own viewBox:

- A `size-3` mark in an open `DropdownMenu.Item` renders a 12×12 svg filling its 12×12 span. Red before the fix: 16×16.
- A `size-6` mark renders a 24px svg in a `Button` and outside any row. Red before: 16px in the Button, 242×286 outside.
- An unsized mark keeps 16px in a menu item and a `Button`. Green before and after: it guards the row rule.
- A hidden drawn mark computes `display: none`. Red before the guard: `inline-flex`.
- Every drawn brand's unsized mark renders at its artwork size, the extent of the bespoke svg's viewBox. `BrandLogo` doesn't set that viewBox, so a re-cropped mark fails the test until its fallback size is updated. Changing the `fkse` fallback width to 80 turns it red. Red before the fix for `ngfi` and `fkse`, which stretched to the container width.

Commands, all passing:

- `vitest run --project browser src/icons/` (12 tests)
- `vitest related` on the touched files, and the full Fuse unit project (2627 tests)
- `turbo run check --affected` (21 of 21 tasks, including size-limit, pack and the docs build)
- `pnpm check`
- After `01a4225b`: `turbo run check --affected` (21 of 21) and `pnpm check` (25 of 25)

Before choosing the clamp, I measured `size-full`, `inline-flex` plus `size-full`, and the clamp with and without `shrink-0`, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, using a scratch page. The other candidates either grow an unsized row mark to its artwork size or collapse it to 0px in Firefox and WebKit.

Review: two fresh-context Codex passes, one for bugs and one for maintainability, over two rounds. Round 1 raised the `hidden` override and a regression for one-dimension direct callers of the two marks. Both are fixed above. Round 2 found nothing.

A second review loop on the pushed branch ran Codex bugs and maintainability passes and one Opus simplify pass. The Codex passes found nothing. Simplify raised four nits, all fixed in `01a4225b`: `BrandLogo` renders one `<Mark>` instead of a nested ternary, the artwork-size test reads its expected size from the viewBox instead of a hand-copied table, two centre assertions that couldn't fail on their own are gone, and the drawn-brand loops share one `DRAWN_BRANDS` constant. The second round found nothing. Two notes describe behaviour that already exists on `main` and is left for separate PRs: a pending `Button` hides only its direct-child svgs, so a `BrandLogo` mark stays visible beside the spinner; and `InputGroup.Addon` sizes only direct-child svgs, so an unsized mark there keeps its artwork size.

Not checked: the browser suite runs Chromium only, so Firefox and WebKit were checked only on the scratch page. I didn't run the docs e2e tier, because no docs-app behaviour changed.

Screenshots: a temporary browser test with the shipped `styles.css` and `themes.css`, in Chromium, scaled 4×. It has no docs fonts. The scene is a `Button` with a `size-6` Nordic Green Energy mark, and an open menu with the issue's `size-3` Fjordkraft mark in a dark chip, an unsized TrøndelagKraft mark and a `size-6` Gudbrandsdal Energi mark.

author: g1obalworlds
body:
**What was wrong:** `Session::grouped` (used by `command.batch` and `plugin.run`) promises that a failed group leaves the documents at their start state, but it only restored fields of tabs still open. A tab closed (or reordered) inside the group stayed that way, with its unsaved edits, and `self.active` could point past the end of `docs`, so every later command returned `NoDocument`.

**Trigger:** two tabs open (`file.new`), then `command.batch` with `file.close {index:1, force:true}` followed by `node.set` on a missing id.

**Fix:** snapshot the tab list at group start and rebuild `docs` from it on failure (tabs opened inside are still dropped; the existing per-tab restore then runs).

**Tests:** new `failed_group_reopens_documents_closed_inside_it` (fails before, passes after); full `cargo test -p figcraft-engine` (1091 passed), fmt and clippy clean. `cargo xtask ci` stopped at the wasm step because the wasm target isn't installed locally. Note: the snapshot clones `DocState`s (Arc-backed) on every group, unmeasured.

author: xunholy
body:
## What and why

A follow-up to #1712 (DIST-E1-T02, merged as `ee9875d`) for review-1474's two non-blocking findings (https://github.com/syntropyai-hq/syntropy/pull/1712#issuecomment-6342627360). Refs #93.

**N1. Mixed access sizes.** `spsc::shared`'s `copy_in` and `copy_out` moved 8-byte words, then single bytes, and each end split the record by its own length. Two ends that disagree about a length, say after a garbled length word, could touch the same bytes as a `u64` on one side and as `u8`s on the other. std's atomic model also forbids that for non-synchronised accesses: "every pair of non-synchronized atomic accesses must be either disjoint, access the exact same memory (including using the same access size), or both be reads".

- **The fix.** Both helpers now move `len.div_ceil(8)` whole words. `copy_in` zero-pads the last word, and `copy_out` loads it whole and keeps only the bytes `len` covers.
- **Every access is the same size at the same place.** Every access to a record's bytes, on either end, is a `u64` at an 8-aligned offset from the slot's record area, and the length word is a `u32`. That holds whatever the two ends think the length is.
- **It stays inside the slot.** Every stride is `8 + slot_bytes.next_multiple_of(8)`, so `len.next_multiple_of(8)` bytes always fit a slot. The SAFETY comments of `push`, `pop` and both helpers now state that bound.

**N2. An unmeasured claim.** The module doc's "costs about what a `memcpy` of the same words would" sentence is removed: no benchmark backs it. The doc now says what's true: every slot access is atomic, and always the same size at the same place.

## Tests

- **New: `every_length_round_trips_through_whole_words`.** A one-slot ring of 21-byte slots, a size that isn't a multiple of 8, so the last word is partial for most lengths. Every length from 0 to 21 goes through it, long and short in turn through the same slot, and each must round-trip exactly. The pop must also leave the caller's buffer untouched past the record. It runs in `model()`, so under loom too.
- **Kept passing:** the hostile-peer tests (garbage over the whole ring; a concurrent scribbler of indices, close flags and length words), the length-guard test, the loom shadow cells, and `ipc`'s cross-process test, which carries 10⁶ records each way through this copy path.

## Verification

Run at `1d39295` (on `main` `a91fa014`), x86-64 Linux (WSL2), toolchain 1.99.1. Under the fleet rule these are crate-scoped runs only; hosted CI runs the rest.
```text
$ cargo clippy -p syntropy-spsc -p syntropy-ipc --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings    (clean)
$ RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo clippy -p syntropy-spsc --lib --tests --locked -- -D warnings   (clean)
$ cargo test -p syntropy-spsc -p syntropy-ipc --locked    (every suite ok: spsc 27 unit, 3 + 2 (+1 ignored) + 7 integration; ipc 14 unit + 3 cross-process)
$ LOOM_MAX_PREEMPTIONS=3 RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p syntropy-spsc --lib --locked
test shared::tests::every_length_round_trips_through_whole_words ... ok
test result: ok. 27 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
$ D5 over the changed files / commit message / this body    (exit 123 / 1 / 1: clean)
```

Not run locally: the full lint and the workspace tests, which hosted CI runs (fleet rule). There's no `xtask`, `ci/`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` change, and no plan change.
