author: theconnman
body:
## Summary

Adds the Pod-local shared connector resolver under ADR 0239, checkpoint 2 of the shared connectors epic. The resolver lives in `curie_connector_proxy.resolver` and serves `POST /v1/resolve` on a Unix socket through a strict HTTP/1.1 parser. It refuses chunked or compressed bodies and oversized heads before reading any body byte, and never echoes received bytes in an error. Each caller session gets request-scoped invocation handles (`crh1.` plus 32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 digest, bounded at 1024 invocations and 4096 sessions). Every provider call is admitted again against the database, and authorization is never cached. Admission connects as the application's own role from the sealed or raw DSN file and reads membership, binding and status rows under the cp1 role-derived row policies with FOR SHARE locks on `lock_guard`. It revalidates the handle after every database wait and again before commit and release. At startup the resolver verifies its role has exactly the privileges it needs. It refuses a role that holds foreign authority, refuses to start if the snapshot sealing Secret or the caller signing key is present, and never reads `DATABASE_URL`.

Credential material comes through a source seam: a registry of named sources with a static envelope source and a connector identity source today. Refresh-capable sources plug into a coordinator built on the cp1 compare-and-set functions: begin, provider call, seal to the current recipient, commit. Any uncertain outcome marks the binding `recovery_required` and is never replayed. A later OAuth source registers against the same seam with no `server.py` edit and no migration. `apps/worker/src/curie_connector_proxy/server.py` is unchanged; cp4 wires shared proxy mode into it. A stdlib-only Python 3.12 reference SDK and a 53-case wire corpus ship beside the resolver, and the corpus runner drives the real resolver over its socket as an external process.

The API `check` route now persists `source_stale` on a mismatch, and the flag stays set until an explicit reimport clears it. Expand migration 0124 adds the column. It also replaces the cp1 functions `shared_connector_refresh_begin` and `shared_connector_refresh_mark_recovery` so both lock the binding `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` before the refresh intent. Every move into `recovery_required` therefore waits for resolves already holding the binding `FOR SHARE`, and a later resolve sees the recovery, so no credential is released after recovery commits. The lock order stays application, binding, intent, recipient last, the application role gains no grant, and the downgrade restores the cp1 definitions exactly.

## End-to-end verification

| Tier | Required / n/a | Reason | Mode (fake / live) | Command and observed outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| skill | n/a | No runner, ACI or plugin-format source changes | n/a | n/a |
| local | required | New expand migration 0124 and a changed API store path; new worker resolver package | live | On `f54993717`, built the API image with `docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile .` and ran `python -m curie_api.schema_compat upgrade` from it against a throwaway Postgres 16. It applied 0001 through 0124 (`outcome: applied`, `target_head: 0124`), the column read back as `source_stale boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, both replaced refresh functions read back as SECURITY DEFINER with their original owner, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in their definitions and no PUBLIC EXECUTE, and a second `schema_compat plan` returned `already_at_head`. The resolver is not reachable from the compose stack until cp4 wires it into `server.py`, so its nearest boundary is its own Unix socket. `test_resolver_sdk_corpus.py` starts the real resolver against real Postgres 16 and Valkey 8.1.10 and drives it from the reference SDK in a separate Python 3.12 process: all 53 corpus cases matched their expected status, refusal code and per-call credential digest (5 tests, 0 skips). |
| local-release | n/a | No lockfile, image recipe or released schema window change | n/a | n/a |
| cluster | n/a | No chart template, values or sandbox changes; `charts/curie/files/schema-compat.json` only records the new expand revision | n/a | n/a |
| live provider | n/a | No model provider calls | n/a | n/a |
| external integration | n/a | Shared mode activates nowhere yet; provider calls in tests go to a local fake that replays recorded response shapes | n/a | n/a |
| factory | n/a | No factory runtime, publication or work item paths change | n/a | n/a |

1. [x] Every proved required tier above names its exact command, the commit it ran against, the mode it ran in, and the literal outcome observed.
2. [x] Each meaningful acceptance criterion has positive proof plus a falsifiable negative or a second independent path.
3. [x] Every unproved required tier names its blocker in the table and has a visible Discovery waiver naming an open issue. Any follow up in the table includes its issue number.

Each checkpoint criterion passed a fresh receipt on `eab5945b1` with `CI_REQUIRE_POSTGRES_TESTS=1 CI_REQUIRE_VALKEY_TESTS=1`, and every JUnit report was nonempty with zero skips:

1. Wire contract: `test_shared_source_contract.py -k wire`, 17 passed.
2. Handle registry: `-k handle`, 16 passed.
3. Per-call admission, revalidation and role isolation: `-k admission`, 28 passed.
4. Source seam and refresh coordinator: `-k seam`, 15 passed.
5. Reference SDK against the corpus: `test_resolver_sdk_corpus.py`, 5 passed.
6. Acceptance pair plus an empty `server.py` diff against the epic base: 116 passed.
7. Migration 0124 and the schema pins: the 0124 and 0123 migration tests, `test_schema_compat.py`, `test_shared_connector_admin.py`, `test_schema_serving.py`, `cargo test --lib schema_window` and `cargo test --test integration cluster_rollback_schema` all passed.
8. Static gates: Ruff check and format on the owned files, strict mypy and import-linter (15 contracts kept, including the rule that `curie_connector_proxy` imports no curie_worker, kubernetes, sqlalchemy, redis or boto3 module).

Each refusal and fail-closed branch has a liveness test next to it. Two admission tests pause a resolve inside its source, then run `shared_connector_refresh_mark_recovery`, or a refresh begin on a lapsed lease, from a second application role connection. The transition must wait as a lock waiter blocked by the resolver's backend until the resolve commits, and the next resolve must be refused `recovery_required`. Both failed on the previous functions with "mark_recovery completed while a resolve held the binding" and "refresh_begin completed while a resolve held the binding". The migration test checks owner, grants and the exact cp1 definitions after downgrade. `apps/worker/tests/binding` passed 253 tests with zero skips on a migrated database at `eab5945b1`. The image check in the local row ran on `f54993717`; the only later change is the merge commit `eab5945b1`, which touches one test file. Concurrency tests use separate real connections and lock waiter barriers.

Persisting `source_stale` needed a column, so this checkpoint adds expand migration 0124. A check that only reports staleness forgets it as soon as the source matches again, and a stale binding must stay refused until an operator reimports it. Moving the expand head to 0124 required the same pin updates cp1 made: `cli/src/application_schema_windows.json` and the tests that pin it (`cli/src/schema_window.rs`, `cli/tests/cluster_rollback_schema.rs`), `charts/curie/files/schema-compat.json`, `packages/protected-hooks/src/curie_protected_hooks/schema_serving.json`, `apps/api/src/curie_api/schema_compat.json`, `revision_kinds.json`, the existing API tests that pin the head and the relational database interface document. author: uilian-c
body:
## O que muda
**Livro**
1. **Modo escuro**: o leitor usa as cores do tema (texto claro em fundo escuro); o PDF/impressão usa sempre "papel claro" (`.tt-claro`), legível com o celular no modo escuro.
2. **Leitor como e-book**: página inteira sem moldura nem cantos arredondados, cabeçalho fino (fechar, capítulo, **sumário**), rodapé com barra de progresso do livro todo, "Semana 21 · página 4 de 5" e setas; deslizar só folheia quando o gesto é horizontal (rolar não vira página); "Virar a página" no fim; **continuar de onde parou**. Tocar num registro abre o registro.
3. **Imprimir** virou um botão secundário ("Imprimir para o fichário", com bolinha quando há páginas novas).
4. **Data e hora** em cada registro do livro ("Momento · 22/10/2026 às 14:32"; a hora quando foi postado no próprio dia).
5. **Fotos**: no livro e no PDF, inteiras (sem corte), uma por página quando grandes, sem quebrar entre páginas; o PDF espera as fotos carregarem. No detalhe do registro, a foto única fica do tamanho dela (sem as faixas cinzas dos lados).
7. **Humor no livro**: cada página mostra como cada um estava (carinha e palavra) e uma frase sobre a variação ("O coração ficou mais leve do que na semana passada", "O cansaço apareceu: o corpo está trabalhando por dois…"); sem registro, o convite para contar. A abertura do capítulo traz o arco do mês ("Um mês que começou mais pesado e terminou mais leve").

**Fichário (6)**: "Últimos registros" recolhe (lembrado); cada pasta tem "Ver por: Mês / Semana / Trimestre", com o grupo mais novo aberto e os outros recolhidos (com as fotinhas).

**Nome do bebê como jornada (8)** — migração 026
- Enquanto não há nome: cartão "Escolhendo o nome · Qual vai ser o nome?" logo abaixo do bebê no Início, com os favoritos.
- Cada um sugere nomes e curte os favoritos (quem sugeriu já curte); **a família também sugere e curte** no app dela (não escolhe nem tira ideia dos outros). O parceiro e o casal recebem aviso das sugestões.
- O casal escolhe ("É esse!") → festa com o bebê e o nome → "Guardar este momento no Mural" (vira um Momento, e entra no livro).
- Depois de escolhido, o cartão some e o nome vive no app (Início, jornada, livro); as ideias ficam guardadas como parte da história, e dá para trocar.

## Migração
`db/migrations/026_nomes_do_bebe.sql` (tabelas `baby_name_ideas` e `baby_name_likes`).

## Testes
- `api-nomes.mjs` (novo): sugerir, não repetir, curtir, família sugere/curte mas não escolhe nem apaga dos outros, casal escolhe.
- `e2e-livro`: nome em destaque no Início, sugerir/escolher/festa/Mural, leitor (data, hora, humor, página X de Y, sumário, continuar), papel claro no modo escuro.
- `e2e-fichario`: ver por semana/trimestre, recolher grupo e últimos registros.
- Unidade: humor no capítulo, agrupamento por semana/trimestre.
- tsc, eslint, vitest (167) e integração passaram (exceto `api-notificacoes`, `api-marcar`, `e2e-notificacoes`, que só falham no container local por causa do proxy).

author: getlitlabs
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"rkgirdhari"} -->
_Requested by **The Righteous Writer** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FEVuAwkLYzhq5h8NTKcr5D?thread=cmsg_01FEVuAwkLYzhq5h8NTKcr5D4Um6oxW7WuCkdEkqdCg2op)_

## Why

Any charter edit means a new version and a new seal. Before this PR, booting the new charter against the existing vault failed with `GenesisMismatch`, so a bump to v1.0.1 cost the whole stele.

## What

- **`Stele::record_charter_version(charter, royal, "X.Y.Z")`** appends one `HCC-CHARTER-VERSION-v1` row (from/to version, byte length, digest) in the reserved namespace `genesis.charter.version`. The row's `royal_seal_sig` is the operator's Ed25519 signature over the new charter digest. The call is refused in four cases:
  - the seal does not verify;
  - the key is not the genesis operator key;
  - the vault is already on this charter;
  - the version does not rise.
- **`Stele::lineage()`** returns the genesis charter plus one epoch per version row. Each row must be canonical, continue from the previous tip, carry a higher version, use the same key, and have a signature that verifies.
- **Boot** (`ensure_genesis`) accepts a vault only when the lineage tip is the booting charter, so a retired charter can no longer boot.
- **Reserved namespace**: `append` and `append_in` refuse `genesis.charter.version`, so `scribe.stele.append` cannot forge or brick the lineage.
- **BATON** gets `replay_lineage`: each trace must match one charter in the lineage, never an older one than the trace before it. `replay(d)` is the single-charter case. The daemon now replays across the lineage and logs `charter vX (N version(s) in lineage)`.
- **Operator command**: `cargo run -p hcc-xtask -- charter-version <charter> --to-version X.Y.Z --vault <eduba_vault.db>`.
- `chare.provenance.tag` (67/30/3) stays TYPED until its meaning is confirmed. Vanguard keeps three live jobs. No new crates.

## Proof (cloud)

New tests:
- stele: forward path, wrong key and forged seal, reserved namespace, an unsigned well-linked row breaking the lineage, version compare;
- BATON: lineage replay forward-only;
- daemon: boot after a bump keeps the vault and refuses the retired charter.

Results:
- fmt and clippy are clean.
- `scripts/nine_gates_audit.sh` gives **11/11 PASS**, gate 4 at 122 tests.
- `xtask charter-version` against a vault booted under the baked v1.0.0 seal correctly refuses with "already on this charter".

## Unverified on the operator machine

`cargo +1.99.0 test --workspace` and the audit on Windows have not been run. A real bump has not been done: there is no v1.0.1 charter or seal yet, and that ceremony is the operator's call.

author: cody-seibert-gsa
body:
## Problem

The validator's "Fetch from URL" rejects sources like https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FuhuXia/TestFiles/refs/heads/master/warning_example.json with **"URL did not return JSON."**, even though the harvester harvests them fine.

GitHub raw (and S3, and plenty of agency servers) serve `data.json` as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` or `application/octet-stream`. `fetch_json_from_url` only accepted `application/json` / `application/*+json` and refused everything else before reading the body. The harvester's `download_file` never checks `Content-Type`; it just parses the body.

## Change

- Remove the `Content-Type` check (and `_is_json_media_type`) from `dcatus_validation/fetch.py`, so the validator behaves like the harvester. The body is still capped at `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, and `parse_json_document` still rejects non-JSON with a line/column error.
- Tests: replace the media-type unit tests with a parametrized test showing `application/json`, `text/plain`, `application/octet-stream` and a missing header all parse. The "rejections raise InvalidCatalogSource" test now checks that an HTML body is reported as invalid JSON.

## Testing

`poetry run python -m pytest tests/unit/dcatus_validation` passes (83 tests).

author: coatless
body:
Each Bioconductor release publishes a `PACKAGES` file per repository with an `MD5sum` for every package, and the catalog had no checksum for any package. This adds `bioc_package_checksums` (release, repository, package, version, md5sum, keyed by release, repository and package), read from `https://bioconductor.org/packages/<release>/<repository>/src/contrib/PACKAGES` for `bioc`, `data/annotation`, `data/experiment` and `workflows`. Only entries with `Package`, `Version` and `MD5sum` are kept, and a package listed twice keeps its first entry.

Every release in `bioc_releases` is read, plus devel under its version number from `config.yaml`. A frozen release is read once and kept: the manifest's `checksums.frozen` lists its repositories and later runs do not ask for them again. The current release and devel are read on every run and their rows replaced. A repository a release does not have (HTTP 404) is skipped and listed under `checksums.missing`. With the 49 releases in `bioc_releases` today plus devel, the first run reads 50 releases and 200 release repositories. After that each run reads the current release and devel, 8 repositories.

The checksums never stop or hold up the catalog, which the merger waits on daily:

- Each file gets the per-item retry budget (5, 15 and 30 s) and a 60 second timeout.
- A failed read keeps that repository's rows and is tried again on the next run.
- Reading stops for the run after three failures in a row or ten minutes, and the rest waits for the next run.
- An error anywhere in the step, or a prior checksum table that cannot be read, keeps the run going with the prior rows. A prior table holding fewer rows than its manifest counts makes the run read every release again.

The run log and the manifest's `checksums` block count the releases and repositories read, the rows, and the repositories missing, failed and deferred. The publish gate includes a fingerprint of the rows and the frozen list, and the schema version is 4, so the first run after merging publishes.

The existing run tests use a stub with no checksum fetch, so every checksum read in them fails, and they pass unchanged apart from the schema number.

Not run against bioconductor.org: the tests use a hand-written `PACKAGES` fixture and a fake fetch.

Tested with `Rscript tests/testthat.R` (1153 passing, 0 failures), the same command the Test workflow runs.

- Cliente en `ue1` con dos enlaces: `lte` (`tun_srsue`, hacia 172.16.0.1, `type = cellular`) y `fijo` (veth al netns raíz con netem: 15 ms, 10 Mb/s, 1 %, ~110 ms de cola; `FIJO_NETEM`). Resumen: el bonding saca al LTE del reparto en 1,2–1,7 s y el TCP queda en 8–11 Mb/s (2× la redundancia, 4–6× menos retransmisiones). La redundancia no silencia el LTE con BLER 5 % y 1–4 s de cola; el TCP cae a 3,5–4,6 Mb/s (Mathis para 1 % a 30 ms: la copia tardía del LTE no repara la pérdida del fijo). El estimador de capacidad sigue al SNR pero se congela con el enlace silenciado. El teléfono nunca se desconectó. No toca `engine/`.

author: guibeira
body:
## What

The worker environment and command no longer reach libkrun VMs through places that cannot carry them:

1. **Host → guest: a virtio-console port instead of the kernel command line.** `__vm-boot` sends the worker env, and the worker command (`III_WORKER_CMD`), as one length-prefixed JSON frame over a new `iii.env` port. iii-init reads it right after `mount_filesystems()` and exports it, so the worker, supervisor restarts and `iii worker exec` inherit it as before. Only iii-init's own plumbing stays on the command line, and all of it is validated before boot.
2. **Launcher → `__vm-boot`: stdin instead of argv.** `run_dev`, the OCI adapter, the sandbox daemon and compose (through a new `stdin` field in the prepare plan) pass `--env-stdin` and write the env to the child's stdin. `__vm-boot` drains it before anything else.

Shared codec: `crates/iii-supervisor/src/env_channel.rs`. Guest side: `crates/iii-init/src/worker_env.rs`.

Linear: MOT-5493 (boot panic), MOT-5492 (secrets in `ps`).

## Why

**MOT-5493.** The env rode the kernel command line as `KRUN_ENV`. msb_krun writes each pair as ` KEY="VALUE"` without escaping (`msb_krun-0.1.16/src/api/builder.rs:503`), then unwraps the insert (`msb_krun_vmm-0.1.16/src/builder.rs:599-600`), which only accepts printable ASCII. One env value with an accent, an emoji, a newline or a tab panicked the boot:

```
thread 'iii-worker-vm-boot' panicked at .../msb_krun_vmm-0.1.16/src/builder.rs:600:53:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: InvalidAscii
```

Compose forwards the whole machine environment into the VM (`crates/iii-compose/src/spawn.rs:164`), so one odd variable in the user's shell was enough (reported on macOS with the quickstart). Values containing `"` were also silently split, and every value was readable in the guest's `/proc/cmdline`. The worker command had the same problem: a non-ASCII OCI entrypoint or `--arg` panicked too.

**MOT-5492.** Launchers passed the env to `__vm-boot` as `--env KEY=value`. Credentials from `env_file` and the machine env were readable by every local user through `ps` for as long as the VM ran.

## Notes

**Design decisions**
- The port is used only with an embedded init (`iii_filesystem::init::has_init()`, which is every release build), because only then is iii-init guaranteed to be the same build. An on-disk init may predate the port, so that path keeps the command line, but now rejects what it cannot carry with an error naming the key instead of panicking.
- No fallback for mismatched compose / iii-worker versions: they ship in the same release. An older compose spawns the plan with a null stdin, and `__vm-boot` then fails with *"no worker environment on stdin ... Install iii and iii-worker from the same release"*, matching compose's existing message for an unknown prepare subcommand. A newer compose with an older iii-worker keeps working (the old plan has no `stdin`).
- Errors never include env values.
- `III_WORKER_CMD` and `III_ENV_PORT` coming from the worker env are dropped, so a stray one in the forwarded machine env cannot replace the real command.
- The codec enforces execve's limits (128 KiB per variable, 1 MiB in total) and names the offending variable, instead of letting the worker spawn fail with an anonymous E2BIG.

**Behaviour changes worth knowing**
- `__vm-boot` gains `--env-stdin`; `--env` stays for manual runs and tests.
- The prepare plan (`__local-prepare` / `__bundle-prepare`) always carries `stdin` and no env in `args`.
- iii-init's `root_pivot` runs before `/sys` exists, so it still sees only plumbing; every later boot step sees the worker env, as before.

**Testing**
- New unit tests: codec (round trip with non-ASCII, quotes and newlines; limits; no value in errors), guest frame reader (split reads, transient EOF, timeout, oversized header, missing port), host writer thread (300 KiB, more than a socketpair), `split_vm_env` (port path, legacy order, PATH fallback), `feed_env_stdin`, compose plan stdin (piped and closed vs `/dev/null`), the bundle command test, plus `tests/vm_boot_env_stdin.rs` (a real `__vm-boot --env-stdin` subprocess; no KVM needed).
- Manual, on Linux/KVM with `docker.io/iiidev/python:latest`:
  - the installed 0.24.6 reproduces the exact `InvalidAscii` panic;
  - with this branch, `Olá, São Paulo 💖`, `say "hi"` and `line1\nline2` reach the worker byte-for-byte, and a non-ASCII `--arg` boots;
  - nothing secret is in the guest `/proc/cmdline` or in the host `ps`;
  - a simulated compose (`__local-prepare` + spawning the plan) shows the same, and the old-compose case gets the same-release error.
- Three independent review rounds; the final verdict was *ready for PR*.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: 3 tests in `crates/iii-worker/tests/worker_list_discovery_integration.rs` fail identically on `main` on the test machine.

**Not done yet (why this is a draft)**
- **Not tested on macOS / Apple Silicon (HVF)**, where the crash was reported. Needs one smoke boot with a non-ASCII env value before merge.
- Left on purpose: a space in `KRUN_WORKDIR` is accepted (msb_krun writes it unquoted; nothing in the guest reads it, and rejecting it would refuse workdirs that boot today). The `website` blog post `why-agent-sandboxes-are-converging-on-libkrun-not-firecracker.md` still shows the old builder call; it is a point-in-time article.
- Open product question, not addressed here: whether compose should forward the whole machine environment into VMs.

author: marcnnn
body:
Closes #7. Bottom of a stack: #1 Cube.js, #2 OData, #3 generator, #4 overrides, #5 token auth and #6 docs build on it.

## What changes
- `AshJsonApiWrapper.QueryDialect` behaviour: `can?/2`, `filter/3`, `sort/3`, `paginate/2`, `build_requests/2`, `unwrap_response/4`, plus optional `opts_schema/0` (options are validated at compile time).
- `json_api_wrapper do dialect X end` (or `{X, opts}`) picks the dialect. The default is the new `AshJsonApiWrapper.Dialect.Simple`.
- The data layer is now a generic loop: it builds requests, follows `next`, and reads records into the resource. Whatever the dialect leaves in `runtime_filter`, `sort`, `offset` and `limit` is applied afterwards. Page counts work through `run_aggregate_query` for dialects that report a total.
- `can?/2` delegates to the dialect, so unsupported operators are rejected before any request. Ash does not ask `can?` about `and`/`or`, so dialects reject unsupported boolean shapes in `filter/3`, which still happens before the request is sent.

## Behaviour changes in Simple
The existing tests pass unchanged. A second commit fixes pre-existing bugs that the new offline tests surfaced:
- an `and` whose handled side became `nil` turned the rest of the filter into `false`;
- `and` with a get endpoint lost the endpoint, and without one skipped the filter_handler params entirely;
- the first value placed in a list or CSV list was added twice;
- an `or` was half moved into a list.

Also: headers from the query context and paginators are now actually sent, and a `false` filter returns `{:ok, ...}`. Runtime filter, sort and limit now run in that order; before, the limit was applied before filtering.

## Tests
`test/query_dialect_test.exs` (a test dialect) and `test/simple_dialect_test.exs` (Mox, offline).

author: ap-lukebradford
body:
#80 — Server: a merged PR's minor findings become one tech-debt issue in Backlog

## What changed

When the engine ends a run whose PR merged, it now files that PR's minor findings as one tech-debt issue in Backlog.

What changed:
- core `review.ts`: `parseMinorFindings` reads the list lines under `MINOR_HEADING`, in the format the PR-body writer produces. New helpers `minorIssueTitle`, `minorIssueBody`, `minorIssueNoteKey`, `minorIssueFailedText` and `minorIssueFiledText`. `RunLoop` gains `minorIssue` (a number once filed, null once tried with nothing filed, absent if not tried).
- server `publish.ts`: `Publisher.fileMinorFindings` runs `gh pr view --json body,labels`, then, if there are findings, `gh issue create --repo --title --label <area>,chore --body-file <tmp>`. It uses argv with no shell and a mode-0600 temp file that is removed afterwards. The area label comes from the PR's `area:*` labels, falling back to the ticket's.
- server `github-board.ts`: new `addCard` looks up the issue's node id, runs `addProjectV2ItemById`, then moves the card to Backlog with the existing `moveCard`. `main.ts` wires it as `board.add`.
- server `engine.ts`: the `end-run` action calls `fileMinorFindings` before ending the run. It stores `minorIssue` right after the create, so a later pass or a restart doesn't file again. A failed create sets `minorIssue` to null (not retried) and raises a flag note naming the PR. A failed Backlog add keeps the issue number and raises the same note. Either way the run still ends. It only runs for `merge`-autonomy repos.

Tests (all pass):
- The four cases in `engine.test.ts`: files one issue and adds it in Backlog, a second pass and a restart don't file again, no minor findings files nothing, and a failed create raises the note. A fifth covers the failed Backlog add.
- New tests for the publisher's argv, labels and body, for `addCard`, and for the parser.

Checks: lint and typecheck are clean. The full `pnpm -s test` run has 4687 passing and 4 failing. All 4 are in `checkouts.test.ts` ("installs dependencies…" and similar), which timed out at 5 s while running a pnpm install. That file isn't touched by this change, and I didn't re-run it on main to confirm it fails there too.

Security note (new GitHub write): this creates an issue and adds a project item. It runs only for the hub's own runs, only in a `merge` repo, and only after the PR has merged. The issue text is the minor-findings lines RETRO already put in the PR body, which went through the PR text screening when they were written. Nothing user-controlled goes into a shell or a query. GraphQL variables are parameterised, and the title, labels and body file are passed as separate argv entries.

Limitation: if the PR body carries RETRO's fallback sentence ("N minor findings; listed in Mission Control") instead of a list, no findings can be parsed and nothing is filed.

Deploy: no migration or config change. It goes live when the hub updates.

## Minor findings (logged, not looped)

RETRO-1 reviewed 9aa7a9f. These were logged, not sent back for fixing.

- `apps/server/src/engine/publish.ts:327` — When the PR body's list is capped (minorMoreLine) or has a line withheld (MINOR_WITHHELD), the issue is filed with those placeholder lines and no note, so the findings left out of the PR body are never filed.

Closes #80.

Opened by GUIDO-1 (Mission Control).

Corpus bump 55, stage 2. Pins the corpus to master 2effb2ee (CI run 39791298313). This also brings in bump 54: its stage-2 pull request was never opened, so this branch starts from main.

Refs #5681, refs #5666.

## What changed

- **Dataset header address lines (BC 29).** `CompanyAddressLine1..8` now follow the address format of the company's country:
  - Post Code+City (`AhDatasetHeader.al:309`), City+Post Code (`:327`), City+County+Post Code, the format of the CRONUS GB row (`:345`), and Blank Line+Post Code+City (`:363`).
  - Custom, with the rows that Validate writes from City+Post Code (`:382`).
  - A code without a Country/Region row: City+Post Code, with the code as the country line (`:382`).
  - The General Ledger Setup "Local Address Format" 0 to 3 when the country is blank (`:409`).
  - Name 2 is written. Contact Person is never written.
  - Still refused: only one of City and Post Code (except the cases pinned before), Custom rows of any other shape, country translations.
- **SaveAs in another language or region** (`W3ReportObjectIdPreviewLanguage.al:870, :893, :912`):
  - SaveAs runs after `GlobalLanguage(1031)`, and with `Language := 1031` or `FormatRegion := 'de-DE'` set on the report variable before it.
  - Before this change, a language set on the variable was dropped by the SaveAs without any message.
  - The language changes `Format` and the dataset's `language` attribute, not the column values. The region changes both.
  - de-DE columns and `Format` now cover a Time, a negative decimal, and a one-digit day and hour, as `:912` pins them.
  - `CurrReport.Language := 1031` in a SaveAs trigger now writes `language="de-DE"` (`:605`).
  - Refused: any other combination, Run or Execute of such a variable, a Labels block in German, and on BC 29 a German SaveAs of a header with the company block (its captions in German are not pinned).
- **Bump housekeeping.**
  - Removed 79013 QT_FieldTable_NoKeyOnRowVersion_Control from the baselines in its own commit. It passed by accident: it asserted nothing before bump 54.
  - Listed the checker gaps of four bump 54 files in `corpus_resolve`.
  - Cited `AjMisc.al` in the BC 29 metadata gate.

## Assumptions added

None.

## Numbers

Corpus after the bump (pass / fail / not run). No baseline case lost except the accidental pass above. No case fails.

- BC 27: 14637 / 0 / 3029 (8 new passes)
- BC 28: 14680 / 0 / 3082 (8 new passes)
- BC 29: 14723 / 0 / 3140 (11 new passes)

Microsoft Tests-ERM, BC 29.0.54011.56262:

- main 59288796c: 2930 passed, 26 failed, 1081 not run.
- This branch: the same counts, with 0 per-test differences.

The issue repros, run with this branch:

- #5666: passes.
- #5681: now fails instead of being refused. The header logo holds the new PNG followed by the tail of the old CRONUS picture. The cause is a separate Blob issue: writing a Blob field after `Get` without `CalcFields`, then `Modify`, keeps the old bytes after the new ones.

## Not done / probes wanted

- A Blob field after `Get` without `CalcFields`: `CreateOutStream`, write a shorter text, `Modify`, then read. This blocks #5681.
- The full header of a SaveAs after `GlobalLanguage(1031)`, `Rpt.Language := 1031` and `Rpt.FormatRegion := 'de-DE'`: the root attributes, Language, FormatRegion, ReportCaption and the company captions. The runtime writes the run's language and region, as `BdRegionTests.al:809, :928` pin for a trigger's setter.
- One of City and Post Code alone, per format.

author: oduwax
body:
## Summary

Repairs the inherited bloom-filter unit tests without changing production bloom, transaction, merkle, wallet, staking, RPC, or consensus code.

### Why

The remaining `bloom_tests` failures come from Bitcoin-era fixtures that serialize transactions without OduwaCoin's `nTime` field. Reading those bytes directly as current OduwaCoin transactions shifts the stream and causes decode failures, stale transaction hashes, and stale merkle roots.

### Included

- adds a test-only legacy transaction decoder for the inherited fixture layout
- converts legacy transactions into current OduwaCoin transactions with `nTime = 0`
- preserves in-block spending relationships when converted transaction hashes change
- recomputes the block merkle root after conversion
- replaces stale hard-coded Bitcoin txid expectations with the converted transaction hashes
- re-encodes the existing private-key fixture with the OduwaCoin mainnet secret prefix while preserving the same underlying key
- changes the obsolete exact Bitcoin merkle-block byte vector to an OduwaCoin serialization round-trip check

### Safety boundary

Test code only. No production behavior is changed.

Expected result: `bloom_tests` should leave the failing inventory, reducing legacy failures from 4 to 3 if the full suite passes.

author: neerajhariyale
body:
## What
Settings → Login & Signup gets a new switch, **Also replace a typed username** (`signup.usernameOverrideTyped`, default off). It shows under **Apply to all enrollments** when the username rule is email, phone or custom field.

| Apply to all | Replace typed | Admin typed a username | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | – | – | today's behaviour |
| on | off | yes | typed username kept (today's behaviour) |
| on | on | yes | rule value (email / phone / field) is used |
| on | on | yes, but rule value is empty | typed username kept |

The random rule never replaces a typed username.

## Changes
- **auth_service:**
  - `InstituteSignupPolicy.usernameOverrideTyped`, parsed in `InstitutePolicyService`.
  - `AuthService.usernameFromInstituteStrategy` now checks `usernameExplicit` only after it reads the policy.
  - Removed a hard-coded "email always wins" check, so the behaviour is decided only by the setting.
- **Admin:**
  - New switch in `UsernameStrategyFields`, and the setting is kept in the settings merge.
  - New `useLearnerUsernamePolicy` hook. It reads the server copy, not the 24h cache.
  - Bulk **Manual entry:** the username box is locked when the switch is on, and shows the email when the rule is Email.
  - **Enroll Manually:** when the Email rule applies to admin adds, the generated username is the email. The server already saved the email while the form showed a random name.
  - New strings in en/hi/fr/ar.

## Deploy note
Deploy admin FE together with or before an institute starts using the switch. The old settings merge drops unknown keys, so saving Login & Signup from an old admin build would remove `usernameOverrideTyped`.

## Testing
- `AuthServiceUsernameDedupeTest`: 23/23 pass. The 4 new tests cover:
  - email replaces a typed username when the switch is on
  - the typed username is kept when the switch is off
  - the typed username is kept when the email is empty
  - random never replaces a typed username
- Admin typecheck: 0 errors. Design-lint: clean.

author: chhawchharia
body:
Superseded by #15044 after the source branch was renamed.

Image builds currently accept stale PHP packages without verifying the fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. This adds build-time validation for every Ubuntu PHP source package, every installed Homebrew PHP formula (including Composer's runtime), and the Windows PHP binary through the existing ImageHelpers module.

The selected PHP branches/extensions stay intact. Ubuntu 22.04 keeps PHP 8.1 through the official USN-8948-1 backport; upstream release floors are 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12. Later stable patches and future stable branches pass; prereleases, stale packages and unverified vendor revisions fail. Package metadata is refreshed before installation; cached Homebrew PHP formulas are upgraded before validation.

Validation:
- Regression suites passed in Ubuntu 24.04, including patch boundaries, official vendor revisions, prereleases/future releases and mixed patched CLI/unpatched FPM inventories. The macOS policy was executed with PHP CLI.
- Pester 5 tests passed through the actual ImageHelpers module (20 cases in this repository).
- Bash syntax and ShellCheck warning checks passed for the new helper.
- Added a focused Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 and Windows CI matrix and docs/php-security.md.

Full native Windows/macOS and cloud VM image builds, existing image smoke tests, final artifact scans and fleet rollout remain required before release. Historical generated software inventories are unchanged until new images are built.

author: ordaxos-admin
body:
## Project-First M1 #266 — staged handlers, NO deployment

Completes the source-only HTTP contract for Platform #276's **unapplied** SQL proposal, reusing canonical authentication and one Product grant ledger:
- `POST /v3/owner/workspace-resources/approvals` is hosted by `product_owner_grant_admin` and derives Owner ID only from signed Product JWT, never body; strict 9-field allowlist and bounded JSON; invokes `ordax_approve_project_workspace_resource_v1` via existing parameterized `callRpc`.
- `POST /v3/device/transport/workspace-confirm` is hosted by `product_device_transport` and derives device ID only from existing Device token authentication; strict 5-field allowlist with no path, Owner identity, Project/Space, token, capability, or grant selection. Invokes `ordax_commit_project_workspace_resource_v1` via existing PostgreSQL allowlisted RPC.
- `project_workspace_issue_contract.ts` is the **single** input contract for both; no duplicate MCP, bearer secret, grant ledger, or filesystem executor.
- Both endpoints require **two explicit opt-in flags**: the already-default-off `WORKSPACE_RESOURCE_VERIFIER_ENABLED=enabled` **and** independent new `WORKSPACE_RESOURCE_ISSUANCE_ENABLED=enabled`. Deploying source code alone does not enable issuance; enabling only verifier/revocation cannot issue permissions.
- Negative source/HTTP contract tests verify signed Owner/session gate, enrolled Device/POST gate, strict IDs, no path/Owner in payload and separate flags; canonical PGlite issuance tests remain green on Platform main.

**NOT OPERATIONAL**: SQL remains under `proposals/`, not `migrations/`; no production schema writes, Worker deploy, flags, Owner UI/native picker composition or real resource issuance. Device confirmation must come ONLY from trusted Windows Runtime after interactive Owner folder approval, not model or arbitrary generic MCP request. Keep Orchestrator `capability_unavailable`.

Merge only if all Platform control-plane, Worker bundle and connector packaging gates green.

author: eightman999
body:
## 概要
`\![execute,filewatch]` / `\![cancel,filewatch]` と、OnExecuteFileWatchChange / OnExecuteFileWatchFailure（UKADOC 2.8.91）を実装しました。

Closes #133
Part of #141

## 変更
- `FileWatchRegistry`（FSEvents のファイル単位イベント）でファイル・ディレクトリを監視します。
  - ファイル: `created` / `modified` / `deleted`。まだ存在しないファイルも指定できます（親ディレクトリは必要）。
  - ディレクトリ: 直下の作成・削除・名前変更・更新を `changed`、ディレクトリ自体の消失を `deleted` で通知したあと、Failure `notfound` を送って監視を終えます。
- Reference: Change は R0=--async R1=指定パス R2=種類 R3=フルパス、Failure は R0=--async R1=指定パス R2=理由。
- `--async` が On 始まりなら Change はその ID、Failure は ID+Failure に置き換えます。
- `--debounce`（既定 500ms、0 で即時。変化が止まなくても最初の変化から3倍で通知）。
- Failure の理由: `notauthorized`（SSTP など外部のスクリプト）、`invalid`（パスなし）、`notfound`、`limit`（全体で63ディレクトリ）。
- 同じパスの再指定は置き換え、ゴースト終了時に全解除します。
- 再生中のスクリプトが SSTP 由来かを `currentPlaybackIsExternal` として記録します（`runScript` / SSTP 経由の再生で更新）。schedule-add など、外部から実行できない他のコマンドでも使えます。

## 検証
- `FileWatchRegistryTests`（7件）: 作成・更新・削除、デバウンス、ディレクトリの changed / deleted と Failure、invalid / notfound / notauthorized、置き換えと cancel、SSTP 由来の記録 → 成功
- 単体テスト全体（`-only-testing:OurinTests`）→ `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`
- 開発中に、FSEvents へ監視オブジェクトを保持させていなかったことによる解放後参照のクラッシュと、`/private/tmp` と `/tmp` のパス表記の違いによる取りこぼしを見つけて直しました。

## Ce que fait la PR

Le débarcadère du 4e d'Archipéo, derrière `?monde=ouvert`, d'après la piste A « La place de l'usine » choisie par le mainteneur le 22/10 à 15 h 50, et les restes des Fabriques.

**La Crique** (intention du directeur artistique, planche du Mac) :
- La rangée de l'Escale et de la Lisière passe en brique `#945C58`, posée par assises sur un soubassement de pierre `#8F8B88`, avec des chaînes d'angle (`PortSite.masonry`, facultatif). L'Escale et la Lisière gardent leurs triangles (testé). La place est dallée en `#F0E6D6`.
- L'aire de l'aéronef est sur pilotis, au bout de sa passerelle : anneau de fer froid, quatre bittes, deux lanternes. L'aéronef est au repos (GD-21) et il n'y a jamais deux Nefs. Les pièces déposées du dirigeable partent une à une. Après le départ, une bouée reste sur le flanc de l'aire.
- Autour : la digue en six blocs bas séparés par l'eau ; le Rafiot à quai, le flanc tourné vers le quai, avec six bronzes et une fumée courte ; les Aiguilles au loin. Cinq îles du ciel immobiles au nord-est, que le départ traverse. Elles n'apparaissent pas sur la Carte (`NefSite.offMap`).
- La vue d'arrivée montre la place, la rangée, puis la Forge et le volcan. La grue reste hors du cadre et la fiche du 4e a été corrigée en ce sens.

**Les restes des Fabriques** :
- Les joints d'assise de la brique du Bastion passent à la Soute, à la Porte et à l'Étalon (`brickCourses`, `place4eKit.ts`).
- La Forge, la Soute, la Porte et l'Étalon lisent le sol à la première demande, et non plus au chargement. Un test le vérifie pour les neuf lieux des Fabriques et du Bastion.
- Pendant que le nom d'un Détour est écrit, la marque du lieu suggéré se masque, à tous les niveaux. Un seul nom est ainsi à l'écran.

## Budget (`npm run rendu:budget -- --archipel 6e,5e,4e,3e`)

| Vue du 4e | Avant (preview) | Après |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Monde, scénette ouverte | 83 300 / 17 | 84 581 / 17 |
| Carte | 72 600 env. / 12 | 73 626 / 12 |

Les chiffres sont en triangles / appels. L'enveloppe du 4e est de 118 000 / 22 et ne change pas. Le plafond du test est `CRIQUE_CEILING` (celui des Coteaux plus 2 000). Le 6e (111 408 / 20), le 5e (114 658 / 19) et le 3e (46 021 / 13) sont identiques à preview.

## Relectures (sur commits figés)

- directeur-artistique : **Validé** (2e passe sur `1f1d5b37`). Les restes des Fabriques étaient validés dès la 1re passe.
- consultant-archipeo : **Fidèle** (1re passe sur `567f722b`). Ses trois ajustements facultatifs ont été faits à la retouche 1 : la fumée, la coque et l'anneau de fer.
- referent-dys : **Adapté** (1re passe). Avec « Réduire les animations », le départ se fait sans vol ni rotation (vérifié).
- consultant-ux-ui : **Clair** (2e passe). En portrait 800 × 1280, au quart de tour, une île du ciel passe sous un bouton. Ce n'est pas bloquant : c'est noté dans `chantiers.md` et sera vu avec la caméra du 4e.
- expert-frontend : **Conforme** (1re passe). Ses deux points facultatifs, `depositOnce` et `fichiers.md`, ont été faits à la retouche 1.

Restent, notés dans `docs/pilotage/chantiers.md` : la fumée du Rafiot, encore un peu en blocs de près ; les chaînes d'angle jusqu'au soubassement ; le portrait 800 × 1280 ; les lieux de l'Épaule, qui lisent encore le sol au chargement ; la mesure sur iPad.

## Documentation

`docs/pilotage/chantiers.md`, `docs/rendu/style.md`, `docs/architecture/monde.md` et `fichiers.md`, `docs/ux-ui/bonnes-pratiques.md`. GD-21 et GD-24 sont inchangées. Le manuel n'a pas de page à changer : le 4e reste derrière `?monde=ouvert`.

## Vérifications

`tsc`, lint (aucun avertissement de plus), `code-mort`, `contenu --check` et `www:build` passent. vitest passe sur le jeu (6 194 tests) et, après la fusion de preview, sur `src/game/world` et `src/game/three` (5 120 tests). Les captures sont hors dépôt, dans la Bibliothèque du projet : `archipeo/univers-challenge/niveaux/4e/monde-ouvert/crique/captures/` (`restes/`, `crique/`, `retouche1/`, chacun avec son `comparaison.md`).

author: pierrealexispozzi
body:
### Villages et végétation
Les villages vus de loin étaient semés au hasard : des maisons tombaient sur les routes, les plages ou les marais, et la végétation poussait au travers.

- Chaque village est maintenant organisé le long de la route qui le traverse : maisons mitoyennes en rangées, façade sur la rue avec porte, fenêtres et volets.
- L'église est en retrait sur son parvis, et une ruelle transversale traverse les gros bourgs.
- Un village sans route reçoit une rue de terre raccordée à la route la plus proche.
- Une carte d'occupation du sol (routes, ruelles, bâtiments) est consultée par les arbres, buissons, herbes, vignes, tas de sel, moulins et bunkers, qui ne traversent plus routes ni maisons.
- Les routes de l'île entrent dans la ville active jusqu'à rejoindre une de ses rues, au lieu d'être coupées net à 52 unités du centre. La ville du phare est réorientée pour que sa rue prolonge la route de Saint-Clément.
- Loix et Saint-Clément sont bâtis sur une éminence sèche au milieu des marais.

### Personnages réalistes
- **Corps humains MakeHuman (CC0)**, en douze morphologies : hommes et femmes, adultes, âgés et enfants, de carrure normale, forte ou mince. Ils sont générés hors ligne par `dev/tools/gen_humans.py`, avec :
  - les cibles de morphologie ;
  - les poids de peau ramenés à notre squelette ;
  - une occlusion ambiante cuite ;
  - des masques du visage peints dans l'espace UV.

  Les données pèsent environ 2 Mo dans `assets/humans/`.
- **Squelette** calé sur les articulations réelles. Toutes les animations, accessoires et objets tenus existants sont conservés.
- **Visage** :
  - vrais yeux texturés, avec iris recoloré, regard qui suit et clignements ;
  - cils et dents ;
  - mâchoire qui bouge à la parole.
- **Peau** composée dans le shader par personnage : carnation, lèvres, joues, sourcils, barbe de quelques jours, rides, cheveux ras.
- **Cheveux et barbes** : une calotte de mèches rayonnant depuis l'épi, effilées à la lisière, complétée de mèches libres. Coupes : courte, raie sur le côté, frange romaine, carré, longue, queue de cheval, chignon, nattes, rouleaux, tonsure, perruque.
- **Vêtements ajustés** :
  - gonflés depuis le corps, lissés par un flou spatial (la peau cachée n'est pas dessinée) ;
  - découpés en ourlets nets, avec poids de peau interpolés ;
  - souliers et bottes ajustés au pied ;
  - vestes ouvertes, bavettes, scapulaires et fichus en coques ;
  - jupes et pans d'habit qui enveloppent le bassin réel ;
  - les autres accessoires (ceintures, cols, boutons, écharpes, sacs…) recalés sur la nouvelle silhouette.
- **Niveau de détail** : les habitants éloignés (au-delà de 13 m de la caméra) utilisent un maillage simplifié ; la tête garde toute sa résolution.
- **Correctif** : un pas de temps négatif à la première image faisait diverger le lissage de l'animation.
- Retrait de l'ancien corps procédural (`body.js`) et du visage peint (`face.js`).

### Vérifications
- Partie complète jouée par le bot jusqu'à la fin, sans erreur.
- Tous les lieux accessibles dans les 7 époques.
- Chargement d'une époque : 1,6 à 1,8 s, comme avant.
- Environ 36 000 triangles par personnage de près.
- Nouvelle page `dev/human.html` pour examiner un personnage seul (visage, buste, dos, pieds, niveau de détail).

author: khaledabdulbasit
body:
اختيار (ب) من رحلة المدرّس الشريك، والفلوس للشريك نفسه (قرار المالك 2026-10-22).

**المشكلة:** المدرّس اللي انضمّ بدعوة لمكان مدرّس تاني مكانش له ملف تدريسي، ولا كان فيه طريق يعمل بيه واحد. فكورساته عمرها ما ظهرت في السوق، وحصصه كانت بتتحسب على ملف صاحب المكان.

**اللي اتعمل:**
- صفحة «ملفّي» عند المدرّس الشريك بقى فيها زرار «قدّم على ملفّ تدريسي». الزرار بيفتح نفس استمارة طلب المدرّس من الخطوة ٢.
- الطلب والملف بيتعملوا جوّه مكان صاحب المكان اللي دعاه، مش في مكان جديد. كده السعر والتسوية والظهور في السوق بيقروا من نفس المكان.
- الطلب بيروح لنفس طابور «طلبات المدرّسين» في لوحة الإدارة.
- لما الطلب يتعتمد، كورسات الشريك بتتنقل لملفه، فبتتحسب بسعره وبتظهر باسمه. كورسات صاحب المكان ومدرّسينه التانيين مابتتلمسش.
- صفحة «طلبك قيد المراجعة» بقت بتظهر للي بيقدّم وهو داخل بحسابه. كانت بتحوّله للصفحة الرئيسية وتقول له «أنت مسجَّل الدخول بالفعل».
- الكلام اتعدّل علشان يقول اللي بيحصل فعلاً، في التلات أماكن دول:
  - رسالة المانع في صفحة الكورس.
  - شرح دور «مدرّس» في شاشة الدعوة.
  - وصف كشف التسوية.

**اللي اتجرّب:**
- الرحلة كاملة في المتصفح:
  - عمر دخل «ملفّي» وضغط «قدّم على ملفّ تدريسي»، وكمّل الاستمارة وبعتها، وشاف «طلبك قيد المراجعة».
  - المدير قبل الطلب من «طلبات المدرّسين».
  - ملف عمر طلع جوّه مكان مريم، وكورسه اتنقل لملفه، والمانع الوحيد الباقي قدّام ظهوره في السوق إنه لسه مسودّة.
  - صفحة «كشف التسوية» بقت بتظهر لعمر.
- اختبارات الخلفية (٣):
  - الطلب بيبدأ مرة واحدة بس، وجوّه المكان الصح.
  - المساعد بيترفض.
  - نقل الكورسات وقت الاعتماد مابيلمسش كورسات الزملاء.

body:
**READ ME FIRST**: Please understand that in most cases we will not be able to merge a pull request because there are a lot of internal activities needed when updating the LaTeX2e sources. If you have a code suggestion please discuss it with the team first.

Package a nightly TDS archive after every commit and distribute it through a custom TeX Live repository.

Usage:

```
tlmgr repository add https://nightly.typesetting.eu nightly
tlmgr pinning add nightly "*-dev"
tlmgr install --reinstall latex-bin-dev l3kernel-dev latex-base-dev latex-firstaid-dev latex-graphics-dev
```
Afterwards `tlmgr` automatically install nightly versions of the `-dev` packages.
Alternatively
```
tlmgr pinning add nightly "*-nightly"
tlmgr install latex-bin-nightly
```
allows to install this in parallel to regular `-dev` as a separate format, but this requires some manual adjustments to `texmf.cnf` to make the lookup work.

body:
## What this PR does
Explore's category tabs show how many events each has, for example "All events (639)" and "Workshop (4)". The Interest filter shows a count beside each interest. Every count is of different events: a repeating event counts once, and duplicate copies are skipped.

## Changes
- **New database function `discovery_counts(p_interests)`** (migration `20261022000400`). One call returns the overall total, a count per category and a count per interest, computed in Postgres. The page gets a few dozen numbers instead of event rows.
  - Interests are matched on their tags plus synonyms, so an event with two synonym tags still counts once.
  - It runs as the caller, so RLS applies.
- **Category tabs** (including All events) show `(N)`, and the **Interest** dropdown shows a count beside each option.
- **Removed** the old category counter, which read every upcoming event row.
- **If the function is missing or fails,** the page still works and simply shows no numbers.

## Why
To show how many events are in each category and interest without loading the events to count them.

## Testing
- On local data, every tab and interest count matches the results you get when you click it: All 31, Workshop 4, Networking 3, Technology 21, Consulting 4.
- Removed the function locally: the page still loaded with no numbers. Then restored it.
- 720 tests pass, including new `optionsFor` tests; lint, typecheck and `next build` pass.

## Notes
- **Apply the migration with `npx supabase db push`, ideally before this deploys.** Until then the tabs show no numbers.
- Category tabs and searches still list at most 80 events, so a tab can say (120) but show 80.

author: theguriev
body:
## What

The answering card now draws a request exactly as Claude Code will run it. A request with any text that is not ASCII can be allowed only after it has been read **as written**.

Four commits: the research items (`2d72f60d`), then fixes from three security reviews (`071e0cf5`, `f07a0e82`, `ae1138e9`).

### The guarantee: Allow waits for the view as written (owner decision)
No list of lookalikes is ever complete. The third review drew `rm -rf ~` as quoted, commented or heredoc data with:
- U+A78B `Ꞌ`
- U+29E3 `⧣`
- U+2572 `╲`
- U+275C `❜`
- `⟨⟨` used as `<<`
- a Nerd Font private-use `#`

So the owner chose to gate Allow on the exact view:
- **When it applies:** any text the card shows of a request is not ASCII. That is the command, the agent's note, an Edit/MultiEdit/Write path or change, or the working directory.
- **What Allow waits for:** the request has been shown as written (every non-ASCII character written out as a muted `⟨U+XXXX⟩`, so what is drawn is printable ASCII plus marks nothing can pass for) and read to its end in that view. Showing it so restarts the keyboard and pointer waits, so the usual settle applies after that.
- **Where it is enforced:** everything goes through `Body::read_to_end()`. The keyboard never stands on Allow, the pointer gets an inert Allow, and the press-time re-check in `view.rs` refuses it. Deny, Go to tab and Not now are unchanged, and Not now stays the default stop.
- **The notice** says why Allow waits: "Contains text that is not ASCII · Show as written to allow", then "Shown as written · read it to its end to allow".
- **Switching back to the drawn view keeps Allow live.** It is the same request, already read as what it is. Making the person read the exact view again on every switch would add no information, so this is the simplest correct rule.
- **An ASCII-only request** (the common case) is unchanged.

### Drawn view: readability and defence in depth (no guarantee)
- **Rows and widths:** rows are broken by drawn grapheme width and never painted past the box. A row drawn wider than measured keeps Allow inert.
- **Wrap marks:** `↳` in a gutter marks a soft wrap.
- **Whitespace marks:** leading tabs and trailing whitespace in commands are marked.
- **Order:**
  - Rows, paths, the directory line and the sidebar/list summary read left to right.
  - An LRM goes after every run of R/AL letters or AN digits.
  - A 50,000-line fuzz test asserts ASCII is always drawn in logical order.
- **Written out, muted** (everything written out is muted):
  - controls, bidi controls, zero-width characters, non-U+0020 spaces;
  - U+2800;
  - private-use and unassigned code points;
  - combining marks that do not NFC-compose with their base;
  - spacing marks (Mc) not on a letter;
  - UTS #39 / NFKC lookalikes of shell syntax plus a short hand list;
  - characters no installed font has.
- **Measuring and coverage:**
  - Graphemes in the box's own face are read from its tables; others are shaped, 8 ms per frame.
  - Coverage is a one-bit table read off every font file on its own thread (~79 ms over 777 faces, `std::fs::read`, no mmap).
  - A panic while building it settles to "cannot say" instead of leaving every card measuring.
  - While anything is still measuring, Allow waits.

| | drawn | as written |
|---|---|---|
| review 3's `q1` | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v4-q1-drawn-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v4-q1-exact-card.png) |
| an honest international command (`r1`) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v4-r1-drawn-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v4-r1-exact-card.png) |

Earlier rounds, before → after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ⚠ overflow | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/before-emoji-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v2-after-emoji-card.png) |
| whitespace and wrap marks | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/before-marks-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v2-after-marks-card.png) |
| RTL letters | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v2-before-rtl-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v2-after-rtl-card.png) |
| AN digits, CJK/Hebrew coverage | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v3-before-an-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v3-after-an-card.png) |
| quote lookalikes | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v3-before-q-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v3-after-q-card.png) |
| 15k characters no font has | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v2-before-uncovered-card.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theguriev/crook/pr-assets/card-draws-what-runs/v2-after-uncovered-card.png) |

## Numbers (release, this machine, 777 faces)

| case | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `--snapshot` wall time, 15,000 distinct code points no font has | 33.3 s (`2d72f60d`) | 2.84 s (ASCII baseline 2.65 s) |
| coverage table | 8–9 faces read (`071e0cf5`); 19 ms with mmap (`f07a0e82`) | 79 ms, `fs::read`, off-thread |
| box layout after the first frame | | 4–9 µs |

## Tried

- **Real fonts** (`crook-dev --ask-fixture … --snapshot`): every reviewer fixture plus my own adversarial ones. The fixture now takes `"as_written": true` to picture the exact view. That is a snapshot-only field: the Asking actions stay unregistered.
- **Mutation proofs.** Each test fails with its fix taken out:
  - gate removed
  - the exact view's end never recorded
  - diff, path or note not written out in the exact view
  - note not counted
  - no unsettle on toggle
  - no private-use/unassigned rule
  - spacing marks kept on any base
  - coverage panic not caught (the crookui test)
  - plus every earlier round's fixes
- **Gate tests**, for a command (the `q1` fixture), an Edit change, Write content, a path and the agent's note. Each checks:
  - every route refused before the exact view is read: pointer, keyboard, dispatched press;
  - Deny still live;
  - Allow live after the exact view is read and settled;
  - a long exact view that must be scrolled to its end;
  - an ASCII request unchanged.

## Decisions and costs

- **The gate is the guarantee.** The drawn-view rules are no longer extended. They remain for readability: the lookalike list writes out e.g. curly quotes, Hebrew yod and `١`. Marks that never compose are written out (Arabic harakat, the Devanagari virama, Thai, niqqud), while spacing vowel signs on letters are kept.
- **Cost for non-ASCII requests:** every such request takes one more step (Show as written, read to the end) before Allow. Commit messages with `’` or `é`, and paths in non-Latin scripts, all pay it.
- **What counts toward the gate:** the request's own fields plus the working directory. The tab name is Crook's own and does not count.
- **Snapshot fixture:** `lib.rs` draws the fixture's frames with `frame_drawn` between them, the way the window delegate does.
- **Parallel branch's files:**
  - `view.rs`: 10 lines, the `AsWritten` arm with unsettle and pointer hold.
  - `control/ask.rs`: `summary()` goes left to right.
  - `lib.rs`: the fixture's frames.
  - `answer_list.rs`: the fixture field.
- **New dependencies:** `unicode-security` and `unicode-normalization` (MIT/Apache, new to the lockfile); `unicode-script` and `unicode-bidi` (already in the tree). `memmap2` is no longer a direct dependenc

author: keithcreelman
body:
**Class:** data discrepancy / historical backfill, **dry run only**. Nothing was written to D1 or MFL. No migration was applied. Tracking issue: #1386.

## Plain English

D1 knows who won each UPS auction but not how the bidding went. MFL still has every nomination and bid from 2014 to 2025: 8,065 rows across 2,404 auctions.

This PR builds the load without running it:
- two new D1 tables;
- the loader in dry-run mode;
- a reconciliation report that ties every number back to MFL.

Owners see nothing new until a story or page reads the tables. The load waits for Keith's separate go (the decision comment below).

**Reports (readable on GitHub's phone view):**
- [GAP-01 reconciliation](https://github.com/keithcreelman/upsmflproduction/blob/claude/gap01-auction-bids-dryrun/docs/data_fixes/2026-10-22-gap01-auction-bids-reconciliation.md)
- [Plan for all 17 gaps](https://github.com/keithcreelman/upsmflproduction/blob/claude/gap01-auction-bids-dryrun/docs/data_fixes/2026-10-22-historical-d1-gaps-plan.md)

## What reconciles

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Rows per season = MFL `AUCTION_INIT` + `AUCTION_BID` (2014-2025) | 8,065 = 8,065, every season |
| Rows = June 2026 archive, bid by bid (season, player, second, franchise, amount, type) | 0 differences |
| Won auctions per season = MFL `AUCTION_WON` (blank MFL rows excluded) | 2,369 = 2,369 |
| 2017-2025: last bid = MFL winner and price | 1,790 / 1,790 |
| 2014-2016: replaying MFL's proxy rules over the logged bids gives winner and price | 578 / 579 (Jamison Crowder 2016: 0005's $5,000 bid was logged but never honored) |
| Each season's gap vs `ups_auction_history.total_bids` | fully explained: cancelled bidding, 2 auctions where D1 counted a cancelled first bid, lost second auctions (GAP-02) |
| Spot checks: Henry 2023, Gore 2016, Snead 2017, Foster 2014 | all agree with the audit |

**Findings the audit didn't have:**
- **2014-2016 log every bid placed**, at the amount the owner entered (their maximum). The price comes from MFL's proxy rules, so Gore's $44,000 entry and $43,000 price are correct.
- **GAP-02 is eight lost auctions, not seven.** Danielle Hunter's May 2024 auction (0005, $6,000) is also missing from `ups_auction_history`.
- **35 auctions never produced a winner** (cancelled, or re-nominated later). They are kept as `outcome = no_win`, never merged into the next auction.
- **GAP-16:** D1's weekly tables hold no week past the league's last one. The repeated final week exists only in the June archive (102,383 player-score rows and 16,613 roster rows, all copies).

## Technical why

**Data path:**
- **Source:** MFL `TYPE=transactions` per type, plus O=102 (MFL's auction report, used only to date auctions). The replies are cached outside the repo, because they contain owner comments.
- **Parse:** comment text is dropped. MFL's own "forced bid increase" note becomes `forced` + `forcing_fid`.
- **Auction identity:** events are split into auctions keyed by **season + player + first logged event**.
- **Validate:** against MFL counts, the June archive, `ups_auction_history`, and the proxy replay.
- **Store (proposed):** `ups_hist_auctions` + `ups_hist_auction_bids`.
- **Serve:** no route yet.

**Why new tables and not the existing ones:**
- `ups_auction_history` is built from O=102, which lists one auction per player-season. That is the cause of GAP-02.
- `ups_auction_bids` / `ups_auction_lots` belong to the live 2026 poller and key on (season, league, player), the same flaw. They also store raw transaction text.

**Splitting rules, each backed by evidence (report section 3):**
- an `AUCTION_INIT` opens an auction (2019+);
- a WON closes it;
- 2014-2018 bids before O=102's start are split off;
- for 2016, where O=102 has no start times, a gap over 25 hours with no win splits. In every FA auction O=102 dates, consecutive bids are at most 24.0 hours apart.
- A same-franchise repeat bid is **not** a split signal. 2014-2016 repeat inside real auctions.

**Cost (D1 rules):**
- **Load:** measured on a local Miniflare D1, 12,873 rows written (10,469 rows plus 2,404 index entries), about 13% of the Free plan's daily writes. A second run writes 0; rollback (drop both tables) writes 0.
- **Reads:** 31 rows for one auction's bids, 4 for one player's auctions, 187 for a season, 466 for one franchise's season bids. The only full scans are the one-time post-load checks (8,065 and 4,808 rows).
- **Production reads made here:** 3,099 rows (an index SEARCH on `ups_auction_history`, plus one 735-row `sqlite_master` name check) and 81 rows for the GAP-16 seeks.

## Files
- `pipelines/etl/scripts/dryrun_gap01_auction_bids.py`: `fetch-mfl` (read-only), `extract-d1` (opt-in SELECT), `build`, `local-proof`, `report` (privacy scan included).
- `pipelines/etl/scripts/dryrun_gap01_measure_local_d1.mjs`: D1's billed counters on a local Miniflare D1.
- `pipelines/etl/scripts/check_gap16_last_league_week.py`: offline archive check, plus an opt-in D1 check.
- `pipelines/etl/scripts/test_dryrun_gap01_auction_bids.py`: 20 offline tests. They cover the split rules, the replay, the parsers, privacy-scan leak detection, a synthetic season loaded twice, and default runs making no D1 call.
- `worker/migrations/manual/gap01_ups_hist_auction_bids.sql` + `_rollback.sql`: the proposed schema, **not applied**. It is a manual file, so `migrations apply` cannot pick it up.
- `docs/data_fixes/2026-10-22-*`: the reconciliation report and the 17-gap plan.

## Review on a phone

No UI change, so there is no preview. Open the reconciliation report link above. "Checks at a glance" is the first table, and section 3 lists every auction that was split or never won.

## Verification
- **Local:** `python3 pipelines/etl/scripts/test_dryrun_gap01_auction_bids.py`: 20/20.
- **Safe suite:** `node scripts/safe_tests/run.mjs` PASS, 251 passed / 0 failed, tested `c1eded5d` (branch merged with main), new test included.
- **Pipeline:** `build` → `local-proof` (11/11) → Miniflare measure (4/4) → `report` (privacy scan: 0 owner-comment strings in any output).
- **CI on exact head:** pending at time of writing.
- **Not verified:**
  - any production write (none made);
  - 2016 auction starts, which have no independent source (about 3-4 of 183 may start minutes or hours early; labeled `start_basis = first_logged_bid`);
  - why any bid was cancelled (not in MFL's log).
- **Rollback:** `worker/migrations/manual/gap01_ups_hist_auction_bids_rollback.sql` drops both new tables. Nothing else reads them.

## Decision

See the decision-record comment: one go, for the GAP-01 load only.

author: marcnnn
body:
Closes #1. Stacked on #7's branch.

`AshJsonApiWrapper.Dialect.CubeJs` sends reads as `POST {"query": ...}`:
- selected attributes become `dimensions`
- filters: `==`/`in` → `equals`, `!=` → `notEquals`, comparisons → `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`, `is_nil` → `set`/`notSet`, `contains`, `string_starts_with` → `startsWith`, `string_ends_with` → `endsWith`, and `and`/`or` as nested groups, with `not` pushed down (De Morgan)
- sort → `order`, limit/offset map directly, and page counts send `total: true`
- without a limit, all rows are read in pages of `page_size`

Member names are `<cube>.<camelCase attribute>` (or as is with `member_case: :snake`), with per-attribute `members` overrides. Response keys are matched ignoring case and underscores. Errors such as "Continue wait" are returned as errors.

Tests use a made-up cube (`/v1/meta`) and responses written from the public REST docs. Guide: `documentation/dialects/cube.js.md`.

author: alrayyes
body:
The Branches nav pill and the Main branches page chips could disagree. In the report the pill read 1 failing and 5 running while the page said Failing 2 and Running 4.

Both are tallied by the same server function, so the tally was never the problem. The reads were. The page fetches /api/main-branches every 60 seconds and the layout fetches the dashboard snapshot for the pill every 30. A branch whose run had just failed showed on the page first, and the pill kept the older count until its next read (or won the race and overwrote the page's newer one).

The page now hands the pill its own counts after each read, and the layout keeps them while that page is open, so the two always show one tally. Other pages are unchanged.

Tests: a unit test for the counts mapping, and a Playwright journey (with axe) where the pill's snapshot is a poll behind the page; it fails on main with the pill at 1 failing against the chip's 2. nav-pills had a test that leaned on the layout poll for this page, and now follows the page's read instead.

Closes #2579

body:
Launching a client from the designer on macOS left the designer active even after the client window appeared. The client bundle is started directly, and wxWidgets' Cocoa `Raise()` makes its window key without activating the application.

The existing `ibFrontendMainFrame::Raise()` overrides now activate the application before raising its window on macOS. Both desktop and thin frames use this path, covering launches with and without debugging. The native implementations are built only on macOS; no public names or launch arguments were added.

Validation:
- CMake Debug configuration with Firebird enabled succeeded; both macOS source files appear in the generated build rules.
- Both changed C++ translation units and both Objective-C++ implementations compiled against the existing macOS wxWidgets build.
- A native GUI smoke test instantiated the real desktop main frame, activated Finder, then compared the standard wx raise with the production replacement: `wx Raise active=0; fixed Raise active=1 window=1`.
- `bash .github/lint.sh origin/develop` and `git diff --check origin/develop` passed.

A full client build and toolbar end-to-end run were not performed. An automated focus regression test is impractical in the normal headless suite: it needs an interactive macOS login session and changes the foreground application. The native smoke test covered the application/window activation boundary directly.

author: pedro-pn
body:
Projetos cuja equipe não tem colaborador com conta ativa e acesso ao Relatório ficavam impedidos de iniciar a execução pela exigência de operador. Agora o diálogo oculta essa seleção quando não há candidatos, permite confirmar a data real e atribui automaticamente o Gestor de Contrato como responsável padrão.

O responsável padrão é salvo pela conta de usuário, inclusive quando não tem cadastro de colaborador. Ele recebe o vínculo de acesso ao projeto e aparece como responsável nas consultas, nos cards e na busca do cadastro. O operador de campo continua sendo um vínculo separado: se houver candidatos habilitados na equipe, sua seleção permanece obrigatória e o servidor rejeita responsáveis inválidos.

A entrada sem operador registra na central: “O projeto XXXX iniciou a execução e não possui operador responsável pela criação dos relatórios. Gestor de Contrato definido como responsável padrão.” O aviso é visível a todas as contas ativas de administradores e gestores de qualquer módulo, com leitura individual, sem duplicar o mesmo projeto/data. A pendência deixa de aparecer quando um operador é definido. Início, atribuição, acesso e aviso são gravados na mesma transação; rollback desfaz todos eles.

Missões legadas sem Gestor de Contrato definido também podem iniciar e notificam a ausência de operador; nenhuma conta é presumida nesses casos.

Validação local:

- 2.322 testes do backend aprovados; 30 integrações opcionais sem configuração foram dispensadas pela suíte.
- 84 verificações direcionadas aprovadas, incluindo integração real do Prisma/PostgreSQL: responsável sem vínculo de colaborador, públicos permitidos, leituras individuais, deduplicação, resolução e rollback.
- 824 testes do frontend aprovados e o novo teste de busca pelo responsável padrão aprovado.
- Regressão Playwright no diálogo de produção: seleção oculta, aviso, início sem candidato, operador obrigatório quando elegível, datas inválidas, cancelamento, envio em andamento e celular.
- Lint, build, arquitetura e aplicação da migration em PostgreSQL descartável aprovados. O diff entre os schemas anterior/atual corresponde à migration adicionada.

Implantação requer aplicar `20261022190000_execution_report_responsible` e gerar o Prisma antes de iniciar a API. A migration adiciona somente uma referência opcional de Project para User, sem backfill. Produção permanece sem alterações.

Regressão de navegador: `/test/browser/execution-start.html` e `playwright-cli run-code --filename frontend/test/browser/execution-start.js`.

author: jordan-umusu
body:
Closes ENG-2122. Related: #3919 (ENG-2146) recovers gateway↔CLI stream cuts inside the sandbox; this PR covers browser↔API drops, the other half of the same story. ## What changed - A failed turn renders an error line at the end of the chat. History and the composer stay usable, with Retry below it. - Provider failures show the error text in red. - A dropped connection reads `Connection dropped` in grey, since the server-side turn may still be running. - A failed session refetch keeps the transcript already on screen. The full-page error only shows when there is no transcript yet. - The streamed `StreamError` text the backend also sends as reply text is hidden, so the error shows once. - A dropped send's prompt is kept in `localStorage` per chat and restored with the drop line after a reload, unless the server transcript already holds it. - Retry after a drop checks `GET /stream` first. If the turn is still live, or the transcript holds the prompt, it reconnects through a fresh SDK `Chat` (versioned `useChat` id), because `ai@7` keeps the cut stream's state and the server's full replay would otherwise duplicate it. Otherwise it resends. A dropped reconnect replay never resends. ## Screenshots
Light mode | | Before (main, light) | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Provider error | | | | Stream drop | | | | Failed session refetch | | | | Drop, after refresh | | | | Failed run, reopened | | |
Dark mode | | Before (main, light) | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Provider error | | | | Stream drop | | | | Failed session refetch | | | | Drop, after refresh | | | | Failed run, reopened | | |
## Deferred - `use-chat.ts` grows from 905 to 1019 lines. Splitting the drop and reconnect state into its own hook is a follow-up. - The backend does not persist a prompt when a turn dies before the SDK writes its first line (only `last_error`). - The restore matches on prompt text, so an identical repeated prompt reads as already received. ## LOC | Kind | + | - | | --- | --- | --- | | Logic | 407 | 69 | | Tests | 673 | 1 | --- ## Summary by cubic Closes ENG-2122. Shows chat turn errors inline after the failed turn's transcript, with a Retry action, instead of an alert above the conversation, so history and the composer stay usable. A dropped connection reads as "Connection dropped" in grey, since the server-side turn may still be running. **Bug Fixes** - A failed session refetch keeps the loaded transcript; the full-page error only appears when nothing has loaded, and now offers a Retry that refetches the session. - Failed turns show the bare error text without a heading, and the streamed `StreamError` reply text is hidden so the error shows once. - A dropped prompt is kept in `localStorage` per chat and restored with the drop line after reload, unless the server transcript holds it. - Retry probes `GET /stream`: live turns, server-held prompts, and reconnects that fail early — before the stream opens, leaving status untouched — reconnect through a fresh SDK `Chat` (versioned `useChat` id); otherwise it resends. A reconnect replay that drops, and any Retry-started reconnect that fails, is treated as a drop, never resends, and forgets the prompt once the server confirms it. - Retry is offered even when a dropped first turn has no message on screen. - A dropped approval continuation is never resent, and reconnect replays keep the saved prompt. **Limitations** - A turn that dies before the SDK writes its first line leaves only `last_error`, so the prompt isn't restored. - Prompt restoration matches on text, so an identical repeated prompt reads as already received. Written for commit 4b01b57d979a783d151166c1e98ec9ad1e494d0c. Summary will update on new commits.

author: shawndibble
body:
Root cause (reproduced): the test did `const button = await findByRole('button', {name:'Optimize queue'})` and then polled `expect(button).toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled','true')`. Under CPU load the page replaces that button's DOM node after the first find, so the held node is detached and never gets the attribute. Instrumenting the failure under 16 busy-loop processes plus 8 parallel vitest runs printed `connected=false sameNode=false liveAria=true`: the live button was already `aria-disabled="true"`.

Not the earlier theory (#4729, closed): a previous test's skill-queue read joining this test's read. The global afterEach already settles cache loads, and the MSW error in the CI logs is an unrelated `GET /characters/91/corporationhistory` with no handler.

Fix: re-query the button inside `waitFor` and for the click. No shared-helper changes, no timeouts touched.

Evidence under the same load: before, "is inert" failed in 7 of 8 runs; after, 0 of 8. (The sibling "makes a remapped plan" test still times out on its initial findBy under that artificial starvation; it does not fail on CI.) Unloaded, the whole file passes 69/69; typecheck clean.

body:
## What it changes

**A system and graphics cards per PC**
- A PC runs `desktop` (Ubuntu with XFCE, as before) or `terminal`: no X server and no XFCE. Chrome runs headless on the same DevTools port, so the `browser_*` tools still work. At idle it uses about 350 MB.
- A PC can get the host's NVIDIA cards, all of them or some, through Docker `DeviceRequests` (NVIDIA Container Toolkit). `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all` is set, so CUDA, NVENC and graphics are all available.
- `GET /computers/gpus` lists the host's cards. It runs `nvidia-smi` in a throwaway container with a TTY and caches the result for 10 minutes.
- `PATCH /computers/:id` changes the setup. Each container carries its setup in a `dev.mowbot.setup` label and is recreated when the setup differs. A running PC reports `restartNeeded`.
- A new team can pick its PC, and so can the Chef's `create_team` (`pc`, `gpu`).
- Bots on a PC without a screen get no `screenshot`, `computer` or `request_takeover` tools. Their prompt describes the PC, including its cards.
- Workstation: a new `mowbot-xvnc`; `mowbot-desktop` and `mowbot-chrome` follow `MOWBOT_DESKTOP=0`. Migration `0025_computer_systems`.

**Web**
- The team page has a "team's computer" card: system, cards, and "restart now" when needed. The new-team dialog has the same choices.
- A PC without a screen shows its bots' browser window, in the side panel and on the PC page.
- "Bureau" is renamed "Ordinateur".
- New question card with pill answers and an × that dismisses the question without answering (`POST /questions/:id/dismiss`). The bot isn't told.
- Drafts are kept per bot, and on the home page, until they are sent.
- Opening a bot's conversation marks its notifications as read (`POST /notifications/read` with `botId`).

## Tests
- Hub `pc-systems.test.ts`: terminal boot, `restartNeeded`, GPU checks, a team created with its PC, tools and prompt on a screenless PC, `setupKey`, `parseGpus`. Also question dismissal and notifications marked read per bot.
- Checked by hand on this machine (Docker Desktop with WSL 2, RTX 3050 Ti):
  - the image built with the new scripts boots without Xvnc or XFCE;

  - the hub's own GPU query finds the card.

Windows PCs are not part of this: they need KVM on the host, which Docker Desktop doesn't expose.
