author: ci-robbot
body:
Closes kairos-io/kairos#4267
Part of kairos-io/kairos#4195

## Summary

A fan-out queued one command per node and pushed all of them at once, so a
batch upgrade starts every node downloading the same artifact in the same
instant. That is the condition kairos-io/kairos#4195 reported, and the last
open acceptance criterion of #4267: "support sequential execution or an
explicit concurrency limit". The other five were covered by #874 and #981.

`maxConcurrency` on `POST /api/v1/nodes/commands` and
`POST /api/v1/groups/:id/commands` caps how many nodes of one fan-out hold a
command at a time. `1` makes the rollout sequential; `0`, the default, keeps
today's behaviour exactly.

The limit is applied by phase, not by withholding rows. The first
`maxConcurrency` commands are created `Pending` and pushed, and the rest are
created `Queued`, which `GetPending`, the WebSocket reconnect replay and
`ClaimForDelivery` all ignore, so no node can see them. Every row of the batch
still exists from the first `CreateBatch`, which is what lets fail-fast cancel
the nodes that have not run and lets the batch status count them.

When a node reports a terminal phase, `store.ReleaseBatchSlot` promotes the
oldest queued row and the caller pushes it. It sits next to
`CancelBatchAfterFailure` because both status paths have to apply it, the REST
endpoint and the WebSocket `command_status` frame, and `pkg/ws` cannot import
`pkg/handlers`. Cancelling runs before releasing, so a stopped fail-fast batch
has nothing left to promote.

Three things the new phase would otherwise break are closed with it:

- `CancelPendingInBatch` now cancels `Queued` rows as well as `Pending` ones.
  Without that a stopped batch would strand rows only a promotion could move,
  and the failure that stopped it was the last report anyone will make.
- `CommandExpireBefore` now expires an overdue `Queued` row, the same reason
  it already covers `Pending`.
- The batch status reports `queued` and `maxConcurrency`. `queued` nodes are
  counted in `pending` as well, so `pending` still means "nodes with work
  ahead of them".

Promotion counts the rows actually in flight rather than assuming one report
frees exactly one slot, so a duplicated status report promotes nothing. It is
deliberately not wrapped in a transaction: the gorm store already documents
that a read-then-write transaction fails outright under SQLite WAL, and the
`UPDATE` is a compare-and-set on `phase = Queued`, so the worst a race can do
is run one node over the limit. A concurrency limit paces a rollout, it is not
a lock on a resource.

## Not in this change

- The Web UI does not offer the field yet. Exposing batch pacing and status in
  the UI is kairos-io/kairos#4268, which this unblocks rather than does.
- The agent needs no change. A queued command is one it is never offered.

## How it was tested

- `go test ./pkg/handlers/ ./pkg/store/` on this branch: green, 13 new
  handler specs and 11 new store specs.
- Mutation-checked the new behaviour, 6 of 7 caught: fan-out never queueing,
  the status hook firing only on `Failed`, `ReleaseBatchSlot` ignoring the
  zero-limit guard, `SummarizeBatch` not counting `Queued`, a cancel that
  skips `Queued` rows, and a promote that releases the whole queue at once
  all turn a spec red. The seventh, pushing a `Queued` row, is a no-op by
  construction: `ClaimForDelivery` only matches `phase = Pending`, so the
  guard in `fanOut` saves a lookup rather than preventing a delivery.
- 13 new specs in `internal/store/gorm/command_batch_test.go` cover the store
  itself: `Queued` surviving `CreateBatch`, `GetPending` and
  `ClaimForDelivery` refusing it, promotion filling one slot and every free
  slot, `Delivered`/`Running` holding a slot, batch isolation, the empty
  batch id and zero limit, the cancel, and the expiry. Those need cgo for
  go-sqlite3 and so ran in CI rather than locally; everything else above ran
  here.
- `go vet` over `pkg/handlers pkg/store pkg/ws pkg/server pkg/auth
  pkg/client internal/store/gorm` is clean, and `docs/` is regenerated with
  `make openapi`.

author: valentinyanakiev
body:
## What changed

#820's item 3 (f): the store's writer refuses a run id that is empty or holds a control character, before anything is written, and names the id escaped. Ids a journal already holds still read.

- **One rule, one function.** `import::recordable` (brokkr-store, pub(crate)) holds the writer's whole run-id rule. The 128-byte bound comes first, as before (decision 0089 ruling 2). Then an empty id, or one holding a control character, is the new `StoreError::RunIdUnnameable`. That covers Unicode Cc: NUL, the rest of C0, DEL and C1. Its text: "a run id is not empty and holds no control character; this one is '{0}', and nothing was recorded", with the id escaped by import's own `escaped`.
- **Checked before anything is written.** `Store::create_run_from` calls it first, before the manifest is serialised or a transaction opens. It is the only production path that inserts a new run besides import's adoption, which keeps its own, stricter gate. Both engine starts go through it, so a wire-supplied `forge_run_id` now fails closed at the writer.
- **Readers are unchanged.** The page reader keeps the length bound alone, and its doc says so. Ids the rule now refuses, already in a journal, still read as themselves through section, listing and load.
- `fleet::kept::lasting` (brokkr-cli) decides the new variant as not lasting, beside `RunIdTooLong`.
- The engine's derived ids can't trip the rule: a feature of only control characters derives '-' plus eight hex digits.

Brokkr-Run: landing-pr-for-820-s-item-3-f-a--7b055f9c

## How it's held

- **Exact text and variant** for an empty id, `r\0a`, `line\nbreak`, `r\u{7f}` and `r\u{85}`. A 129-byte id holding a newline is `RunIdTooLong { length: 129 }`, because the bound is decided first. After the six refusals, the journal holds 0 runs and 0 events.
- **Readers:** ids planted by the generator, and by `plant_run` plus `append_next`, read back as themselves.
- **The engine:** a feature of only control characters derives an id the writer records.
- **Five removal controls** are in the commit message, including the bound-before-control order and the page reader staying length-only.
- **Coverage:** the host exact-coverage gate on this head covered every line (69,439), branch (8,674) and function (9,066).
- `git merge-tree` with main 1f7cb426 is clean, and the file-size and duplication ratchets hold on the merged tree.

## Rulings

Ruling: operator 2026-10-22 "accept all" (#820, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/820#issuecomment-6334786407): item 3, (f), as recommended; the writer refuses an empty run id and one holding NUL or another control character with a typed error, and quality/public-api/brokkr-store.txt grows by that one variant

- **2026-10-22, verbatim: "accept all".** It took #820's item 3, option (f): the writer refuses, with a typed error, and the reader keeps reading what a journal already holds.
- `quality/public-api/brokkr-store.txt` grows by exactly one line, `StoreError::RunIdUnnameable(String)`, the ruled typed error. No other baseline moves. The landing named no new ask.

## Notes for the operator

- **Reviews:** the story run was CLEAN at every position, and this landing was residual at INFO, with no security residual.
- **Carried INFO, a doc sentence:** import.rs's doc on `escaped` ends "The predicate is the gate's own, so the two can never drift apart." Now that `recordable` prints by it too, that is false as read from the second caller. The writer's rule is looser than adoption's, so a writer's refusal escapes characters the writer allows: a space prints as `\u{0020}`. Output stays ASCII, because adoption's gate is the stricter one, so nothing functional changes. The one-sentence fix rides with #753's `seat_summary` story, which edits import.rs next.
- **Rebased** onto main db7c5aca, with no conflict, and `git range-diff` marks the commit unchanged.

Closes #820. Part of #330.

body:
M4 of T27F Live (epic #10266). One new spec, no other file touched.

## What

`specs/t27f/live_stream.t27` -- the SSE wire that lets the live page survive a dropped connection.

| Requirement | How it is met | Measured by |
|---|---|---|
| FR-001 strictly increasing seq | starts at `SEQ_FIRST`, +1 forever; `resume_from` never repeats a number | 5000-step walk (15,002 asserts) + a resume sweep |
| FR-002 a keyframe at least every K deltas | `K_DELTAS = 16`; `resume_mode` gives a keyframe to a client that fell behind the newest one the buffer still holds | 4000-event walk (12,238 asserts), `worst == K_DELTAS` |
| FR-003 coalescing keeps the last value of every key, drops no keyframe | compared against a last-write-wins reference over a 400-event window, not asserted | 640 asserts; keyframe retention under 2000 deltas |
| FR-004 an action outside the allowlist is refused | bounds come from `ui_plan.t27`'s catalog | all 256 ids swept |

**The reconnect criterion is met as exact per-key state equality** -- strictly stronger than the "equal scene hash" the issue asks for. The test walks 100 runs, cuts the client at a different point in each, and asserts equality; it also asserts that **both** recovery paths (deltas and keyframe) were exercised, so the 100 runs are not one branch repeated.

Reused rather than reinvented: `hot.t27`'s `HOT_EVENT` and `DIGEST_HEX_LEN` (the live wire and the hot loop are one stream, not two), and `ui_plan.t27`'s action catalog. `HAS_WEBSOCKET` is `false`.

## Evidence (local, t27c 0.5.2)

- `t27c test-report` -- **10/10 pass, 0 FAIL, 0 vacuous**, 2 invariants proved, **41,890 runtime asserts**.
- `t27c seal --save` + `--verify` -- all hashes MATCH.
- `tools/ci/check_specs_still_parse.py --base origin/master HEAD` -- 1 changed spec, 0 newly unparseable.
- Hooks green: own-language, foreign-budget, secret-gate.

## Not claimed here

- **The latency budget is not measured**: 50 ms p50 / 150 ms p99 in a browser against t27-mcp `--watch` is a Railway-lab measurement. This change does not claim it.
- **No `t27b` ledger row**, for the same reason as #11675: the row comes from a lab corpus run, not a guess. That call has since been vindicated -- master run `c986d53696` confirms both rows from #11668 read `t27b pass`.

## Second commit in this batch: the `face.t27` ledger row

`face.t27` (merged in #11675) deliberately shipped without a `t27b` ledger row, because that row is derived from a lab corpus run and a hand-guessed verdict is worse than a missing one. The lab has now run the merge commit:

- **Railway t27b-lab-1, run `f0929487530fb59d1b4ec2815183edaa35b7daba`, finished 2026-10-22T21:11:00Z**
- `specs/t27f/face.t27` -- reference `pass`, **t27b `pass`**, 11 tests, 2 invariants, 4092 asserts, no blockers.

This batch adds that row, so the spec stops reading as UNLISTED. `max_not_pass` is untouched: it adds a pass, not a non-pass.

author: knucklessg1
body:
## Root cause
With `EPISTEMIC_GRAPH_QOS=1` (set in the deployed arbora pod), `transport::admit_qos_request` verifies the envelope **before** dispatch. It mapped every verification error to `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED: Authentication failed` with `.map_err(|_| ...)`. So the typed `AUTH_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH` that dispatch already returned was never reached. The SDK sent audience `epistemic-graph` to a server that expects `agent-services`, and the caller saw only a generic auth failure.

## Change
- One shared refusal mapper, `auth::authentication_refusal`, used by both dispatch and QoS admission.
- `AUTH_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH` now names the deployment's expected audience. That value is configuration, not a secret.
- New typed classes:
  - `AUTH_BAD_SIGNATURE`: the MAC does not verify. The detail still says "Authentication failed".
  - `AUTH_EXPIRED`: the timestamp is outside the skew window.
  - `AUTH_UNKNOWN_PRINCIPAL`: there is no OIDC token, the token does not verify, or its subject does not match the principal.
- Only fixed sentences written by the engine pass through. Node mismatches and all other failures stay redacted. Every class except a bad signature is decided after the MAC verifies.
- The codes are registered in `EngineErrorCode` and the shared engine error set, with class `auth` and HTTP hint 401. The contract was regenerated with `gen_contract` on R820.

## Tests
- `auth::tests::verification_failures_carry_a_typed_safe_cause_class`
- `transport::tests::qos_verification_names_the_audience_mismatch_cause`: the regression test for the hidden cause.
- The catalog test now checks the new codes, their class and their hint.

body:
## What

Three findings from an adopter that sealed its own mission and generated the three `compliance` packs on 0.44.1, re-read in the code at `main@97f3f02`.

1. **Fixed, RWD-2026-0180.** Every regime wrote `runward/compliance/oscal-component-definition.json`, so a second regime erased the first (since 0.11.0). Each regime now also writes `oscal-component-definition.<regime>.json`. The generic name is kept for existing readers (the third-party ingestion job in CI, the golden test, GRC pipelines) and holds the last regime run; `--json` lists the three files.
2. **New option.** `compliance --out <dir>` writes the pack outside the working tree, for a CI that publishes it as an artifact without committing it (the pack is dated, so stale by the next pull request).
3. **Proposed, ADR-0102 / RWD-2026-0181 (not fixed).** The seal hashes bytes (line endings normalised), so a JUnit report rewritten by each run (`time`, `timestamp`, `hostname`, console output, suite order) drifts with no code changed. Three options: a documented normaliser, hashing the projection the gate reads, or not sealing reports. Related to ADR-0098.
4. **Docs.** `docs/operator-role.md`: ratify before sealing, since `ratify` rewrites the ADR it ratifies.

## Process

- Paths: `src/commands/compliance.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, tests and docs; none is in the charter's `pre-merge-paths`.
- Tests: three regimes in a row leave three distinct components and the generic file equals the last; `--out` leaves `runward/compliance/` untouched. The existing JSON contract test lists the three files.
- Register recounted (181 entries, 15 `operator-report`), `what-found-them.md`, interop contract, OSCAL ingest note, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG; reports and delivery report regenerated; `check --strict` exit 0.

Fixes [SYN-11870](https://vertexproject.atlassian.net/browse/SYN-11870) for 2.x. Backport of the `storm.lint` rule from vertexproject/synapse-enterprise#1459.

`$lib.pprint` of a `$lib.inet.http` response or `$lib.axon.wget` result includes the request headers, which carry the vault/config credential. This adds a lint rule so power-ups which print one can be found.

## Changes

- `storm.lint`: new `S016` (`print-http-resp`, medium, **off by default**; turn it on with `--enable S016`) reports printing or logging an HTTP response or `$lib.axon.wget()`/`wput()` result, either the whole object or its `request`, `request_headers` or `history` members. It follows variables assigned from those calls within a scope, including into functions. `_getScopes` resolves the module and function scopes for both `S015` and `S016`.
- Tests in `test_lib_stormlint.py` cover the findings, the cases which are not reported, and that the rule is not in the default set. Each expected line and column was checked against the source text.
- Docs: `S016` row (default `no`), the `S01` range and the `--enable` example in the `storm.lint` guide.
- Changelog fragment.

This repository does not run `storm.lint` in CI and has no `[tool.stormlint]` configuration, so nothing enables the rule here.

The 2.x `storm-packages` spur, teamcymru and mandiant fixes follow once this merges, using this rule to scan that repository.

- ruff is clean.

body:
## Summary

Hi! I set Free My TV up on my TCL Android TV (Android 9, India) and ended up building a batch of features on top of it. Sharing them in case any are useful. Everything is also usable separately, so happy to split this into smaller PRs if you prefer.

## What's new

**Recommendations and browsing**
- **Browse screen** (OK on Explore / Movies / Shows): endless genre rows (popular, top rated, new, "Made in India" when the region is IN) from TMDB, limited to the streaming apps installed on the TV. Title page with description, tagline, cast, director, rating and an *Open in <app>* button.
- **Search + filters**: text search, voice search (Android `SpeechRecognizer`, mic in the field) and Type / Genre / Year / Platform filters. Type defaults to the tab it was opened from. Results load endlessly.
- **Home cards**: the focused card opens into a landscape card and the others are tall posters, one long row with up to 20 titles per tab. It stops at the ends and always starts at the first card when you switch tabs. Cards show the title only; OK opens the title's page first.
- Pool of 60 picks now mixes trending, new and Indian titles. Image cache no longer evicts what's on screen (cards were flashing gray).

**Home screen**
- Clock and date at the top, and a light/dark toggle button.
- **App menu on long-press of OK** (deck and All Apps): open, move, remove from / add to the deck, app info, uninstall (non-system apps only). Deck capped at 6 apps.
- Light-mode deck tile colors; softer selection border on cards, deck and All Apps; IPTV uses its own banner.
- Optional **custom home title** (Home Settings) instead of "For You".

**Quotes space**
- Now a pluggable list: *Off / Crypto / IPL scores / Air quality*, picked from a drop-down in Home Settings (one at a time). Adding another is a line in `HomeData.SPACES`, a fetch and a case in `spaceInfo()`.
- Crypto: live CoinGecko prices in the configured currency (USDT, USDC, SOL) with real 24h change, refreshed every minute; falls back to the previous Binance route.
- Air quality: Open-Meteo, no key.
- IPL: ESPN's public cricket feed; between seasons it shows a countdown.

**Other**
- Optional `omdb_key` in `config.properties` for an IMDb badge on the title page (empty by default).
- Older looks are kept behind switches: `HomeView.POSTER_ROW`, `HomeView.GLASS_TABS`, `Scene.SOFT_GLASS` (a frosted-glass fallback for TVs without AGSL).

author: josephborodach
body:
## Summary

A new subcommand on \`camera-calibration-cli\` that re-runs the hand-eye solver locally against a downloaded pass's sidecars.

\`\`\`bash
camera-calibration-cli solve --pass-id <PASS_ID>
\`\`\`

- Reads \`station-NN.json\` sidecars from \`./downloads/<PASS_ID>/\`.
- Reconstructs the solver input (\`T_be\`, \`T_cw\`, calibration_type).
- Invokes \`python/solve.py\` locally.
- Prints the resulting frame + residuals, same JSON shape as the live module.

Bit-exact against the live run — verified on a 15-station pass: translation matched to 6+ decimals and every residual matched to the full precision reported.

Supports both calibration modes (\`eye_in_hand\` and \`eye_to_hand\`) — the mode is inferred from the sidecar going forward (new field added to \`saveStationMetadata\`), with \`--calibration-type\` as a flag override for older passes that don't carry it.

### Why

Hardware runs give one data point per 2–3 minutes. Local replay gives one in milliseconds. Unlocks the real diagnostic workflow:
- Try all 5 OpenCV solver methods (Tsai, Park, Horaud, Andreff, Daniilidis) on recorded data and pick the tightest.
- Later: drop one station, re-solve, see how much that station was contributing.
- Later: solve with just stations 1-10 vs 6-15 to test sampling-density effects.

The latter experiments need more flags (\`--drop-station N\`, \`--only-stations i-j\`); keeping those out of this PR to keep scope tight. This PR is just \"replay the solve locally.\"

### Also in this PR

- \`calibration_type\` field now written into every \`station-NN.json\` sidecar.
- \`.gitignore\` entry for \`downloads/\` — my earlier commit adding it landed after PR #106 merged, so main never got it.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go build ./...\` clean
- [x] \`go test ./...\` all pass (new tests cover flag registration + station-ID parser for both current and legacy sidecar filenames)
- [x] \`golangci-lint run ./...\` zero issues
- [x] \`camera-calibration-cli solve --pass-id <X>\` on a real downloaded pass produces bit-exact output vs the live module's run
- [ ] On downloaded 25-cap passes from today's njsanding1 runs, test all 5 solver methods and see which gives tightest run-to-run spread.

author: dbferpra
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"DBFerPra"} -->
_Requested by **Albert** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MVAeez9onsyVVA5Y8jeZnx?thread=cmsg_01MVAeez9onsyVVA5Y8jeZnxT5yFXM16LDA1HCcF142FUR)_

<!-- See docs/CONTRIBUTING.md, "Pull requests". -->

## Summary

`train` and `qml.train` take an optional `initial_point`, so a search can start from a point you choose, such as an earlier run's `best_params`. This is the `initial_point` part of #395. It comes first in a series of stacked PRs for the optimizer review (#395–#399) because Adam needs it to refine an L-SHADE result. Refs #395; this PR does not close it.

- **Validation.** It takes `dimensions` finite numbers as a list, tuple or NumPy array. Another length, a `NaN`, an infinity, or for PSO a value outside its `bounds`, raises `ValueError` at the edge, right after the `dimensions` check and before any backend or CUNQA allocation exists. In Rust, each optimizer checks the same again (`OptimizerError::InvalidConfig { parameter: "initial_point" }`, with the same message) after its other preconditions and before any RNG draw or oracle call.
- **What each optimizer does with it.**

  | Optimizer | Use of `initial_point` |
  |---|---|
  | DE (`rand1bin`, `shade`, `lshade`) | First member of the initial population, wrapped into `[0, 2π)` |
  | PSO | First particle's position. A point outside `bounds` is rejected, since positions are clamped to them |
  | QNG | θ₀. Any finite point is accepted, since `bounds` only limit the random start |
  | CMA-ES | Mean of the first run, wrapped into `[0, 2π)` like every candidate. `sigma0` is unchanged; the guide recommends a smaller one, such as `0.3`, to refine. IPOP restarts draw a new mean |

- **No change without it.** Each optimizer still draws everything it drew before and then overwrites one row or the mean, so the RNG stream is untouched. Without a point every optimizer is bit for bit what it was, including the pinned `rand1bin` determinism vectors. With a point, the rest of the first batch is what the same seed draws without it.
- **The two open points of the issue**, as agreed in the design: PSO rejects an out-of-bounds point instead of clamping it, and CMA-ES keeps its default `sigma0`, with the guide recommending a smaller one.
- **QNG's first candidate.** QNG today does not evaluate θ itself in its gradient batch, so its first candidate is θ₀ + h·e₀, the first point of the stencil centred on the given point. The tests assert that stencil. Adam, later in this series, evaluates θ in the same batch as its stencil.

## Scope

- `crates/polypus-optimizers`: the new `initial_point` field in the four `Args` structs; `util::check_initial_point`; CMA-ES's angle wrap moves to `util.rs` unchanged so DE shares it.
- `crates/polypus-orchestration`: `dispatch_optimizer(..., initial_point)` and `TrainFlow::initial_point`.
- `crates/polypus/src/bindings/mod.rs`: the `initial_point` keyword in `train` (last keyword) and `qml.train` (keyword-only), and `validate_initial_point`.
- Stubs: `python/polypus/__init__.pyi` and `python/polypus/qml.pyi`.

## Collateral files

- `crates/polypus-optimizers/tests/{cmaes,de_strategies,optimizers,qng_validation}.rs`, `crates/polypus-orchestration/src/walltime.rs` (tests only), `crates/polypus-optimizers/src/lib.rs` (doctest): `initial_point: None` in full struct literals and `None` in `dispatch_optimizer` calls, forced by the new field and parameter. No assertion or expected value changes.
- `docs/guide/training.md`: the `initial_point` row in the parameter table and a new "Starting point" section with an explore-then-refine example. The L-SHADE then Adam example of #395 lands with the benchmark PR, once Adam exists.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: one `Added` bullet and one `BREAKING (Rust)` bullet.

## Contracts

C-5 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md`): new precondition (`initial_point` length and finiteness, PSO bounds, checked before any RNG draw or oracle call) and postconditions (the point is the first candidate or first mean; without it, outputs are unchanged). Enforced by:
- `crates/polypus-optimizers/tests/initial_point.rs` (new, 12 tests), including PSO and QNG runs without a point pinned bit for bit to values captured from `main`, and the C-5 postconditions over 10 seeds with a point.
- The `util.rs` unit tests `check_initial_point_*` and `wrap_angle_stays_in_the_half_open_circle`.
- `dispatch.rs`: `initial_point_reaches_every_optimizer`, `a_wrong_initial_point_is_a_config_error`.
- `tests/python/test_initial_point.py` (new, 38 tests): errors raised before `connect_to_infrastructure` (PSO's bounds included), the first candidate of all six optimizers through both `train` and `qml.train`, and the accepted input types.

C-7: the point adds no RNG draw. One sentence is added: a run started from a point replays only with the same seed and the same point, since `TrainResult` does not echo the point.

**BREAKING (Rust):** the four optimizer `Args` structs and `TrainFlow` gain a public field, and `dispatch_optimizer` gains a last parameter. `None` keeps the previous behaviour. The Python API only gains an optional keyword.

## Attribution and licences

All code in this PR is original to this change. Nothing was taken from other projects, and no external source was consulted for it. The angle wrap helper is Polypus's own, moved unchanged from `cmaes.rs`. No dependency is added, and `NOTICE` and `CITATION.cff` are unchanged.

- [x] The checks in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` pass locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (also with `qmio`), `cargo test` as in CI, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`, MSRV 1.85 `cargo check`, `ruff`, the wheel and `pytest tests/python`, `stubtest` and `hygiene.py`. One test, `test_interrupt.py::test_statevector_responds_to_sigint_promptly`, timed out locally on this branch and also on a wheel built from `main` on the same machine, so it is not related to this change.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

author: gofrendiasgard
body:
Two CI flakes, both from a test asserting something the moment of sampling cannot guarantee. Neither touches `src/`.

**The stutter warning (`test_pcm_player_underrun.py`).** The player says "Speech stuttered: N block(s)" once, from the playing thread, at the first underrun it hears; later blocks are counted but never mentioned. The test compared that sentence with `utterance.underruns` read after playback ended, so one more block arriving in between failed it — CI caught `3 block(s)` logged against 4 counted, on every platform in one round. It now reads the number out of the line and checks it lies between one and the final count.

**The hook pool (`test_executor.py`).** The burst test proves two hooks ran at once (it waits for the second to enter), then counts threads named `zrb-hook-`. A worker sampled before its name is set is not in that set, so the equality failed with 1 counted where two hooks had provably run. The bound is what a pool promises, and it still catches a thread per hook.

Both blocked open PRs for a round each: #674 on the hook one, #675 on the stutter one.

`pytest test/llm/hook -q` → 316 passed (12 consecutive runs), `pytest test/llm/speech -q` → 381 passed (15 consecutive runs of the file).

Stacked on testpatterndev/patterns#106, which carries the checkers' `(?-i)` and `\K` support.

## What changes

**Protective markings** (14 SITs: AU OFFICIAL / PROTECTED / SECRET-TOP SECRET / SENSITIVE, NZ ×5, UK ×2, CA, EU, NATO)

- Every regex starts with `(?-i)`.
- A marking word introduced by structure matches UPPER CASE or Capitalised. The structures are:
  - a classification label (`Classification: Official`);
  - the `X-Protective-Marking` `SEC=` field;
  - brackets (`[Restricted]`);
  - the NZ `//` form;
  - the UK `- descriptor` form;
  - the EU `UE/EU` form.
- Bare words and unlabelled banners (`OFFICIAL`, `TOP SECRET`, `NATO SECRET`, `POLICY IN-CONFIDENCE`…) stay UPPER CASE only.
- Never all lowercase.
- Labels, header fields and exclusion lookaheads accept any case through a scoped `(?i:...)`; acronyms (UK, EU, UE, LPP, HMG, HR) stay upper case.
- Case-sensitive exclusion terms gain Capitalised twins: Trade Secret, Official Website, Restricted Area, Commercial-In-Confidence…
- Test cases: each SIT gains a capitalised structured form that must match, plus lowercase and capitalised prose that must not.
- Versions bumped and changelogs added.

**`global-lei`, `global-project-codename-reference`**: explicit `(?-i)`. LEIs and codename tokens are upper case.

**Checkers**: new `scripts/lib/boost-to-js.mjs`, used by `ci-check` and `verify-pattern-testcases`.

- It translates Boost's `\K` to a lookbehind, which reports the same text.
- It expands scoped `(?i:...)` groups into explicit both-case classes. In Node 24, a `(?i:...)` group gave wrong results once another pattern's `(?i:...)` inside a lookahead had run in the same process. In `--all` runs that made labelled markings fail, although each passed when checked alone.
- Unit tests are in `scripts/lib/__tests__/boost-to-js.test.mjs`, runnable as `npm run test:boost-to-js` (script added to `package.json`).

> **CI step still needed:** this PR does not change `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, because the token that pushed it lacks GitHub's `workflow` scope. Someone with workflow rights should append `&& npm run test:boost-to-js` to the unit-test step: the line that runs `npm run test:customisation && npm run test:identifiers && npm run test:classification && npm run test:blocks`. Until then the new tests run locally only.

## Tenant evidence (dev tenant, Test-DataClassification)

**Round 1** compared the current SITs with a version allowing Capitalised everywhere (42 SITs, 168 probes):

- Purview treats regex as case-sensitive by default: the current `\bOFFICIAL\b` matched neither "Official" nor "official".
- Allowing Capitalised for bare words took prose to enforcing tiers. "Official figures released by the Queensland Government…" reached 75, and "Top Secret Recipes…" reached 85. Hence bare words stay UPPER CASE only.

**Round 2** compared the current SITs with this PR (28 SITs, 171 probes, 550 checks):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Real markings scoring lower | none |
| Real markings newly caught | 11 capitalised structured forms, at 75 or 85 |
| Should-not-match cases at an enforcing tier | none, in either version |
| Prose decoys | all clean; a bare upper-case "OFFICIAL" in prose stays at 65 (discovery), unchanged |

## Testing

- `npm run check`, `npm run check:quality`, `test:purview-banned`, `test:boost-to-js` (10 tests, run locally): pass.
- `verify-pattern-testcases --all`: all pass.
- `check:compiled`: pass.

## Not in this PR

The other `case_sensitive: true` SITs are unchanged: passports, `my-tax-number` and the crypto addresses.

author: nguyenbinhanltv
body:
Closes #360

## Tóm tắt
Bài `#324: hồn thú sau lưng cùng ô, sát ô chặn` (thêm ở #344) trượt trên CI nhóm 4 của PR #346 (run 39845697044, cả lượt 1 lẫn lượt chạy lại). PR chỉ sửa bài thử, không đổi server, không nới ngưỡng (vẫn chờ 4 giây, vẫn kiểm đánh trúng và không bị `skip`).

## Nguyên nhân
- Cả hai lượt CI: hồn thú thử **chưa bị đánh lần nào** (`hitBy null`, `calm` tính từ lúc sinh), **không bị bỏ qua** (`skip null`); A đã đi xa 50–100 pixel và nhắm con khác (`b1bj`, `b1bh`). Một hồn thú hoang hung hăng (bãi Ngoại vi 300 năm trở lên, hồi sinh liên tục) đánh A trong 4 giây chờ, tự săn đánh trả trước (`attacker()`) và kéo A đi. Đúng luật, không phải lỗi server.
- Bài #324 chỉ dọn quanh A một lần trước khi sinh. Bản sửa đầu (dọn quanh A mỗi 500 ms) vẫn trượt 1/5 lượt ở máy khi máy bận (lượt đó chậm hơn ~40%): A bị kéo đi rồi mới quay lại nhắm hồn thú thử thì hết giờ.

## Cách sửa (bài thử)
- Dọn **cả bản đồ** (giữ tinh anh, `clear {all, keep}`, như bài nợ nhịp) trước khi sinh hồn thú thử, rồi dọn quanh A **mỗi 250 ms** trong lúc chờ (giữ hồn thú thử).
- Dòng ✗ in thêm id hồn thú thử, đích / đường của tự săn, log gần nhất (so được mục tiêu với hồn thú thử).

## Kiểm thử
`npm run bot:local` (RAM), mỗi lượt một server mới, chạy tuần tự:

| Mã | `--only auto` | `--part 4` |
|---|---|---|
| dọn quanh A mỗi 500 ms (commit đầu) | 4/5 ✓ (1 ✗: A cách 22 px, nhắm lại hồn thú thử lúc hết giờ) | 2/2 ✓ |
| head (dọn cả bản đồ + mỗi 250 ms) | **5/5 ✓** (✓ 168, ✗ 0) | **2/2 ✓** (✓ 1267, ✗ 0) |

- CI `bot-ram` head `e9daaf6` (run 39860579237): đạt cả 4 nhóm.
- `npm run check` ✓ (pre-commit).
- Không đổi SQL / `db.ts`: không chạy PostgreSQL.

## Rủi ro / để sau
- `clear {all}` xóa hồn thú tự nhiên cả bản đồ một lần (bài nợ nhịp ngay sau cũng làm vậy); các bài sau trong `autoTest` đã tự dọn / tự sinh hồn thú thử.

author: ikarthikng
body:
## What
The mic stores no color (confirmed by our captures), so a color or effect only lasts while a process keeps streaming it. This adds a background mode for lighting, the same way meeting mode works.

- `micdeck light on <effect> [rrggbb] [brightness 0-100]` starts the stream detached from the terminal. `solid` with a color is a steady color.
- `micdeck light off` stops it; the mic then returns to its own color.
- `micdeck light status` says what is running, with the latest line of its log.

## Changes
- **`cli/src/background.rs`**: refactored into one generic `Job` (display name, command group, process marker) used by both meeting mode and lighting, instead of a second copy. Each job has its own pid and log file in the temp folder, so they can run together. Messages are now uniform ("... started / stopped / is running / is not running").
- **`cli/src/main.rs`**: the `light` commands. The effect name and color are validated before starting, so a typo is reported at once.
- **`drivers/duocast`**: `play` (behind `effect`, `color ... hold` and `light on`) now survives an unplug: it waits and resumes when the mic is back, like meeting mode. A mic missing at the start is still an immediate error.
- `CLAUDE.md`: updated Done and Next step.

## Behaviour change to review
Meeting mode's messages changed wording slightly because the code is now shared (for example "meeting mode started" / "is already running" / "is not running"). Behaviour is unchanged.

## Testing
- `cargo build`: no warnings. `cargo test`: all 24 pass.
- Bad input (unknown effect, bad color, brightness over 100) gives a clear message.
- On the owner's mic: breathing in the background; a second start is refused; switching to cycle works; `light off` returns the mic to its own color; unplug for ~5 s while cycling and it resumes by itself.
- Meeting mode re-checked after the refactor (start, status, refused second start, stop).

author: zacharyzurlomsft
body:
## Summary
Docs-only: records what was verified live against the AI Gateway, and a limitation found on the way (prompt-agent model calls cannot use the gateway tier).

## Verified live (2026-10-22)
- **Tool servers through the gateway:** `release verify` listed exactly the expected tools on all three, and read-only `lookup_policy`, `lookup_claim` and `knowledge_base_retrieve` calls succeeded (the review tool was not called). The temporary Tools User assignment was revoked from its receipt.
- **The API's model client:** the real app, run in-process against the live gateway with the operator's identity (no deployed app touched), reported `/gateway/status` enabled, answered `/safety/check` (`foundry-guardrails via AI Gateway`) and streamed the two-model bake-off, all served by the gateway.
- **The hosted agents' MCP design:** a Responses call through the gateway with an `mcp` tool pointed at a gateway tool server and a runtime key in the `api-key` header made Foundry list and execute the prefixed tool (lookup and knowledge-base) and answer from the result. Canary keys were deleted; only `master` remains.

## Finding 9: prompt agents cannot route models through the AI Gateway tier
Tried with throwaway connections and agents, all deleted afterwards:
- Foundry resolves the connection only with `ApiKey` auth (`AAD` answers `Connection ... not found`).
- It then rejects the gateway's alias as a model id (`Invalid model_id 'aisvc-zurlo-northwind/gpt-4o'`: letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` only).
- The gateway accepts only that `provider/registration` alias in the request body (`A model alias is required in the request body`; a bare name is `model_not_found`), and Foundry sends the entry `name`, so a short-name mapping does not work.

The two live prompt agents stay direct. The docs list the options (hosted agents, a classic API Management Azure OpenAI API, or a platform change).

## Also documented
`AI_GATEWAY_REQUIRED` must not be set in the azd environment yet: `postprovision` runs `create-prompt-agents.py`, which currently refuses to run when it is set (it demands a prompt-agent model connection that cannot work). The code fix, plus a Windows temp-directory bug in the connection scripts, is ready but held because any merge touching `scripts/` makes the release pipeline redeploy every app, including the insurance portal built by #67.

## Impact
No code, workflow, infra or live-resource change. The release planner maps a docs-only diff to no services, so merging this deploys nothing.

author: rdbalceroh0311-jpg
body:
The assessment now produces 15 evidence-backed website status rows, including explicit missing-data states, and carries them into both run reports and customer reports. Checks reuse existing SiteOne, browser, performance and presence evidence; the report retains website attribution when a customer has multiple targets.

Implemented checks:
- Robots groups and broad `Disallow: /`; page noindex and X-Robots-Tag; sitemap URLs against crawl results; canonical accessibility/consistency.
- Duplicate titles/descriptions, heading hierarchy, broken internal links, redirect chains and sampled inbound-link coverage.
- Organization, LocalBusiness/subtypes and BreadcrumbList validation; invalid JSON-LD; heuristic near-duplicate location pages.
- CrUX/PSI p75 CWV with Google's inclusive good and exclusive poor boundaries, including PSI CLS unit conversion. Lighthouse lab results remain separate.
- Booking/CRM/chat signatures in script/link/iframe contexts and recognised inline calls; enquiry/booking/contact/CTA/trust signals; visible conversion-event calls with consent-gated execution labelled Unknown.
- AI crawler policies by search/training/user-initiated purpose; suspected differential CDN/firewall blocking; informational llms.txt; heuristic answer readiness.

Rows use PASS / WARNING / ERROR / NOT ASSESSED / INFO and contain what was checked, evidence IDs, why it matters and recommended correction. Deterministic observations and manual-verification hypotheses have separate confidence labels. Form submissions are always NOT TESTED; optional features are not failures. AI-search readiness does not establish visibility or rankings.

Limits and ownership:
- At most two homepage GETs and one llms.txt GET; no redirects, 64 KiB of raw bytes per body, identity encoding, a 3-second request timeout capped by the remaining shared 10-second deadline. No new sitemap-entry or canonical-target fetches. The existing robots/sitemap collector is reused (only when missing, its existing bounded collector runs: up to one redirect per resource, a shared 10-second deadline).
- Incomplete page/header attribution, iframe coverage, CTA positions and link graphs remain explicit. Structured-data validation is a focused property check, not rich-result certification. Near-duplicate results require manual review; UA comparison cannot reproduce verified crawler IP access.
- New check modules and a registry entry; 11 additive lines inside `presence.sitemap_check()` retain bounded robots content and sitemap URLs. No changes to `dataforseo.py`, `discovery.py`, `store.py`, the existing crawler, browser or performance collectors.
- The fixture adds two synthetic location pages, consent-gated tool/event markup, crawler rules, llms.txt and an internal redirect chain. The e2e test also fixes its run-directory lookup and handles escaped finding IDs.

Cross-review corrections:
1. Noindex parsing accepts exact directives and only unscoped/Googlebot/Bingbot scopes; preview limits and other crawler scopes do not count.
2. Entity validation covers top-level objects and @graph definitions, merges matching @id definitions and skips references/nested publishers/providers.
3. Only homepage noindex is ERROR. Whole-segment key-page candidates are WARNING/needs_verification; completion pages and substring lookalikes are informational.
4. Vendor marketing anchors and resource hints do not establish tool use. Booking/account-specific anchors, scripts and iframes remain supported.
5. Robots matches exact case-insensitive product tokens, strips versions and evaluates effective wildcard rules for the homepage.
6. Numeric-string breadcrumb positions and relative entity URLs/logos produce suggestions rather than errors.
7. PSI origin fallback retains origin scope.
8. Missing HTTP responses, throttling and server failures remain unavailable/NOT ASSESSED with verification guidance, rather than confirmed broken links or non-200 sitemap defects.
9. Probes use min(remaining deadline, 3 seconds), request identity encoding and cap raw bytes; unexpected encoding is incomplete evidence.

Verification after merging origin/feat/progressive-assessment at d283f41:
- `uv run pytest -q` — `325 passed in 20.41s` (325 collected test cases across `tests/`, including local fixture e2e, report revisions, needs_review and multi-site tests).
- `uv run ruff check .` — `All checks passed!` (repository).
- `uv run ty check ams_assess tests` — `All checks passed!` (both named directories).
- Focused site-check coverage: 129 collected cases from 34 test functions in `tests/test_site_checks.py`, including a regression for every review item. Unit HTTP is mocked.
- The normal merge applied without conflicts. store.py/report.py match the upstream versions exactly; report.md.j2 preserves upstream behaviour and the separate site-check block.
- No live customer checks, paid calls, force-pushes or PR merges were performed.

## Qué cambia

Aplica **a la vez** a las aplicaciones (`gsettings`: tema y tamaño) y al escritorio (`wayfire.ini`, `[input]`: `cursor_theme` y `cursor_size`). Con `role="radiogroup"` / `radio`.
- **Se quitan los controles de las otras dos pantallas.** «Tema» sigue leyendo el cursor de ahora y lo manda tal cual al aplicar (su backend lo exige), sin dejar elegirlo. Wayfire ya no inicializa `cursor_theme`/`cursor_size`: de otro modo, guardar esa pantalla pisaría con los valores por omisión el cursor elegido acá.
- **Backend** (`commands/cursors.rs`): los cursores no son imágenes sino archivos Xcursor, así que se decodifica el formato (cuadro de tamaño más cercano, ARGB premultiplicado → RGBA) y se reescribe como PNG en `data:`. Todo con límites comprobados —un archivo de otro programa no puede pedir memoria de más—; el nombre del tema se valida (sin `/` ni `..`); la herencia de `index.theme` se sigue hasta cuatro niveles (ciclos incluidos). `apply_cursor` rechaza un tamaño no ofrecido o un tema que no existe.
- `png` pasa a dependencia directa: **ya estaba en el árbol** por tauri (`ico`), así que no entra ningún paquete nuevo y las listas de dependencias de sistema no cambian.
- Verificado con los temas reales de esta máquina: Adwaita, `default` y `capitaine-cursors` dan sus 4 cursores.

## Lo que no hace
- Las aplicaciones y los widgets ya abiertos toman el cambio al reabrirse (lo dice la pantalla).
- No hay cursor para sesiones de X/`XCURSOR_THEME`: sólo `gsettings` y Wayfire, que es lo que el taller ya usaba.

## Pruebas
- Rust (14 nuevas): decodificado y des-premultiplicado, píxel transparente, cuadro más cercano, archivo truncado o no Xcursor, tabla que miente su largo, cuadro enorme, PNG de ida y vuelta, nombre de tema no es ruta, vista previa con herencia, ciclo de herencia, tema ausente, y que tema y tamaño van juntos a `[input]` conservando el resto. `cargo test --locked -p vasak-settings`: 352 pasan.
- JS (`tests/cursor-view.test.ts`, 7): una tarjeta por tema con sus imágenes y el actual marcado, tema sin cursores legibles, «Aplicar» deshabilitado sin cambios, elegir y aplicar manda tema y tamaño juntos, error del backend, y que «Tema» y Wayfire ya no tengan el control (rojas contra `main`). `bun test` 839, `biome` y `vue-tsc --noEmit` limpios; el catálogo `secciones.json` regenerado.
- La grilla es `auto-fill` en un `@container`: no hay puntos de corte de viewport (decisión 8).

## Dependencias y versión
`bun update` y `cargo update` (13 paquetes); siguen atrasadas, ya explicadas en `bibliotecasAtrasadas`: pinia 4, typescript 7, vite 8, happy-dom 21, zbus 5, reqwest 0.13. Versión 0.58.0; el `pkgver` de `vasak-settings-git` se sube en `PKGBUILDS` al mergear.

## Changelog
- **Configuración**: Ahora el cursor se elige en un solo lugar, «Cursor», dentro de Apariencia: ves cómo es cada tema antes de elegirlo, y el tema y el tamaño valen para las aplicaciones y para el escritorio a la vez.

Closes #199

author: anyingiit
body:
This adds the two deny-list counterparts to the existing layer constraints, as asked for in #154 and #190:

```java
layeredArchitecture()
        .consideringAllDependencies()
        .layer("Controllers").definedBy("..controller..")
        .layer("Services").definedBy("..service..")
        .layer("Repositories").definedBy("..repository..")
        .whereLayer("Controllers").mayNotAccessLayers("Repositories")
        .whereLayer("Repositories").mayNotBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers");
```

`mayNotAccessLayers(..)` forbids dependencies from the layer to the given layers, and `mayNotBeAccessedByLayers(..)` forbids dependencies from the given layers to the layer. Everything else stays allowed, including dependencies from or to classes outside of any layer.

### Motivation

The allow-list methods (`mayOnlyAccessLayers(..)`, `mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(..)`) also forbid dependencies from or to classes that are not part of any layer. So a rule like "controllers must not use repositories directly" can't be written with them unless every class that touches the repositories is put into a layer. That's what #1372 ran into, and #190 describes the "list every other layer" workaround. In #154 the first step was the allow-list `mayOnlyAccessLayers()` (#592), with the deny-list left open in case it is still wanted. #190 and #1372 show it still is. (#154 is still assigned to @GiorgadzeLuka from that first step; I hope it's fine to pick up the remaining part.)

### Implementation

`LayerDependencySpecification` keeps the forbidden layers in their own set. When that set isn't empty, the rule checks that no relevant dependency has its origin (or target) in one of the forbidden layers. It reuses the same `ifDependencyIsRelevant(..)` handling, so the dependency settings and `ignoreDependency(..)` apply as before. Both methods use the same argument checks as the allow-list variants (at least one layer, all layers must exist). They also reject the layer's own name, since forbidding a layer to access itself would flag every dependency inside the layer, while the allow-lists always permit the own layer.

Following the concern in #190 about deny-lists, the Javadoc of both methods points out that the allow-list variants are usually the safer choice, since a deny-list won't catch indirect accesses through other classes.

### Tests

Three new tests in `LayeredArchitectureTest` reuse the `mayonlyaccesslayers` test classes. They check the descriptions and the exact violations: only the direct dependencies between the two layers are reported, and dependencies on `Object` are not, unlike with `mayOnlyAccessLayers(..)`. In the `mayNotBeAccessedByLayers(..)` test, one class accessing the layer is not part of any layer, and its access is not reported. They also check that unknown, missing, or the layer's own names are rejected.

Resolves #154
Resolves #190

### Disclosure

I wrote this with help from an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). I reviewed the change, ran the tests locally, and I'm responsible for it.

author: rociocm
body:
## What

- Every row in the curation list carries a **New** or **Updates** pill: a collection never approved on chain, or changes sent on one approved before. The chip row filters by it (All / New / Updates).
- Status and assignee are now multi-select pickers. Status offers To review / Approved / Rejected / Disabled, where To review covers a pending request whether or not a curator has it. Assignee lists Unassigned first, then the committee.
- The list opens on To review, Unassigned + you, sorted by **Newest requests**. The sort menu gains Oldest requests and drops Latest activity.
- The Last update column is gone, and the search placeholder no longer promises an owner-address search the server never did.
- The row pill, the editor review bar and the mobile header say To review for every pending request; who has it shows in the assignee cell.
- Every dropdown spaces its options a little apart.

## Why

Curators could not tell a first review from pushed changes on a live collection, could not filter on more than one status or curator, and the status pills duplicated what the assignee already said. Reviewing by request age is what the committee wanted to sort on.

Depends on decentraland/builder-server#825, which adds the repeatable `status` and `assignee` params, `assignee=unassigned`, `review_type` and the `REQUESTED_AT_*` sorts. Until it deploys, the default view on `.zone` comes back empty.

## How to test

1. Sign in as a committee member and open Curation. The list shows To review requests that are unassigned or yours, newest first, each with a New or Updates pill and no Last update column.
2. Click Updates: only collections approved before remain. Click New for the rest.
3. Open the Status picker and add Approved or Rejected, or untick everything to see every status. Do the same with Assignee. The URL repeats each picked value and reads `all` for an emptied picker, and a plain `/curation` link always opens the default view.
4. Pick Oldest requests in the sort menu: rows reorder by what the Requested column shows.
5. Open a row: the review bar's pill reads To review, with the assignee next to it.
6. Narrow the window below tablet width: the two pills stack top-right on each card and the pickers wrap two per row.

author: jorgensandhaug
body:
Fix-forward for the main regressions from #5616 (Drive unification, squash `31095f18a`, parent `7308de5c2`). These are the failures in main push CI run 39841373262 (d864): the Package job plus Unit 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11. Each change below follows #5616's stated intent: one Drive MCP connection, native Drive sync and publishing retired, and historical connections kept.

## Classification

Three product fixes:

- **`packages/contracts/tsup.config.ts`**: #5616 exported `./google-drive-native-retirement` but added no build entry. The built package emitted `.d.ts` only and no JS. This broke the Package job ("every published package entry resolves…"), `embedding-package-contract` and the selected publish-closure.
- **`apps/api/src/integration-connect-metrics.ts`**: `google-drive` reached `CONNECT_PROVIDERS` only through `CORE_INTEGRATION_DEFINITIONS`. #5616 removed that definition but kept the `google-drive` connect provider, so Drive OAuth telemetry was classified as `other`. The fix adds `google-drive` to the fixed connect providers.
- **`packages/contracts/src/product-analytics.ts`**: the new curated host `drivemcp.googleapis.com` was not a reviewed `integration:<domain>`. The doc comment there requires every curated MCP host to be listed. The parent passes this test and the culprit fails it. This leaf was not in the CI triage logs; I found it in a wider local sweep.

Dead copy:

- **`packages/capabilities/src/integration-presentations.ts`**: the native `google-drive` presentation is removed. Presentations must equal the core definitions, and Drive is now a curated Connector.

Data and test expectations aligned with #5616's intended retirement (no assertion weakened; each is replaced by the retired behaviour):

- **API routes**: there are 4 core definitions, with no `google-drive`. The schema and presentation checks use `microsoft-onedrive`. The Drive facet replay test becomes "refuses retired native Google Drive facet saves": PUT returns 410 with `GOOGLE_DRIVE_NATIVE_RETIRED_MESSAGE`, and there are zero provider requests and zero `capability_operations` rows.
- **Knowledge preparation (real PG)**: google-drive dispatch now returns `blocked` / `GOOGLE_DRIVE_NATIVE_RETIRED_REASON` with no runs. The contract-system fixture had used `googleapis.com`, which is now classified as retired native Drive; it uses a neutral domain instead. The Drive ACL branch is removed. Ignoring whitespace from the `test.each` reformat, this file's diff is +30/-67.
- **Worker**: the personal pre-read test now covers the local title admission only, and asserts that the publication-attempt tool and Drive connector bindings are absent. `agent-turn` asserts that `resolveGoogleDrivePublicationTarget` is gone and that delegated membership is kept.
- **SDK browser surface**: `disconnectGoogleDriveConnection` and `transitionGoogleDriveLifecycle` are recorded as retired web-console methods that stay public SDK contracts.
- **Catalog**: the snapshot cleaning and probe counts go from 643 to 644. Google Drive's curated row now has `logoSourceUrl: null`, and `drivemcp.googleapis.com` is added to the vendored-logo suppression lists.
- **Also, from #5607 rather than #5616 (same failing leaf on d864)**: `codexUsage` is removed from `legacyBrowserUnusedMethods`. #5607 added a React helper of the same identifier, which the identifier-count guard counts as a use.

## Evidence

All runs used Bun 1.4.4 on at most 4 CPUs. The Postgres runs used a private Postgres 16 with `OPENGENI_REQUIRE_REAL_DB=1`.

**Real-PG leaves:**

| Test file | Parent `7308de5c2` | Culprit `31095f18a` | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `knowledge-document-preparation-postgres` | 4/0 | 2 pass / 2 fail | 4/0 |
| `api-integrations-routes` | 15/0 | 12 pass / 3 fail | 15/0 |

**Other leaves on the fix:**

| Test file | Fix |
|---|---|
| `product-failure-metrics` | 6/0 |
| `embedding-package-contract` | 6/0 |
| `check-public-repo-hygiene` | 21/0 |
| `catalog-vendored-logos` | 15/0 |
| `browser-client-surface` | 4/0 |
| `personal-resource-pre-read-authority` | 2/0 |
| `agent-turn` | 239/0 |

`product-analytics` passes 7/0 on the parent, 6 pass / 1 fail on the culprit and 7/0 on the fix.

**Negative controls on the fix:**

- Reverting the tsup entry fails "every public contracts and SDK source subpath has a matching runtime build entry".
- Reverting the metrics entry fails both connect telemetry tests.

**Wider sweep:** I ran a 567-file unit sweep on the fix head through `run-unit-shard`, with real PG. It covered every #5616-touched or Drive/catalog/analytics-referencing test, plus all unit tests in contracts, capabilities, sdk and scripts. Result: 4283 pass, 5 fail, 3 skip.

- All 5 failures are in `scripts/dependency-export-workflow-contract.test.ts`, which needs a real `node`/`npm`; the test machine has neither. That file fails identically on clean main `c68d9a14c`.
- The 3 skips are opt-in Helm and Garage infrastructure tests.

**Typecheck plan:** all 49 projects clean.

**Guards plan:** format, workspace-billing, docs-refs, generated-fonts, public-hygiene, the migration guards, subscription-contract, public-api, sdk-compat (3/3 with private PG) and publish-closure all pass. Lint fails only on the existing `POOL` no-shadow warning in `packages/runtime/test/codex-tool-search.test.ts`. That warning is identical on main, and #5635 owns it. `oxlint --deny-warnings` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files, and `git diff --check` is clean.

## Limits

- The full 3793-file unit plan was not run locally; impact is `full` because of the changeset/catalog fence, so PR CI covers it.
- `workflow-execution-graph` (the `source-admission.yml` digest) fails on both parent and culprit. It is not caused by #5616 and is out of scope.
- Not self-reviewed; I will not merge this. It needs an independent review.

_Requested by **Louis** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0115feRRso324Y3w8p6SHYxn?thread=cmsg_0115feRRso324Y3w8p6SHYxnPxGnvf7D5oHhW2MYN1zCvt)_

## Summary
This is the first version of the automatic fishing machine. The bot digs its own pond, fills it and fishes until it has made the number of catches it was given (`companion.fishing({ count })`).

- `core/blueprints/fishPond.js` describes a 2×2 pond dug one block into the ground. It lists:
  - the pond cells
  - the two diagonal cells where water is poured
  - the rim cells, which must stay solid so the water stays in
  - the cell the bot stands on at the edge
  - the point the bot aims its cast at
- `core/goals/fishing.js` runs the pond:
  - **Site:** the bot picks flat ground. The pond cells can only be soil or stone, and the floor and rim must be solid.
  - **Digging:** before digging a pond cell, the bot steps off it if it is standing there.
  - **Water:** the bot pours two buckets on diagonal corners. The other two cells each touch both sources, so they turn into sources too.
  - **Fishing:** the bot stands on the edge, casts with `bot.fish()`, and reels in on a bite. If nothing bites within 45 s, it reels in and casts again.
- A catch counts once a new item is in the inventory. Fish, junk and treasure all count, but soil picked up late from the digging never does.
- Also adds the `fishing-flat` scenario, unit tests and a README section.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run test:core`: 132/132 pass
- [x] `fishing-flat` on vanilla 1.21.8: 10/10 pass (seed 101), median 126 s, 0 deaths. For each run, the server confirmed that all 4 pond cells are water sources, that the bot made 5 catches, and that the player holds at least 1 fish.

Permite que funcionários com a role `sponsor` validem somente as missões presenciais da empresa vinculada à sua conta.

- Adiciona a role exclusiva `sponsor` e os vínculos de empresa nos perfis e nas missões.

author: derrynknife
body:
## What

A task whose name was longer than a work-order title may be (200 characters) stopped the whole workspace's daily maintenance run: generating its work order was refused, and that one refusal aborted every other task's work order too.

The long name came in through **applying an RCM study** (`apply_rcm`, and `from_rcm`): a decision's task text, which is free text and often a paragraph, became the task's name without the length check every other way in has.

## Changes

**Titles made from a longer name are shortened, never refused**
- `shortened()` / `derived_title()` in `backend/maintenance/service.py`: text that fits is unchanged. Longer text is cut at the last word boundary that leaves room for a trailing `…` (total at most 200). A single word running past half the limit gets a hard cut. It never cuts between a character and its accent, variation selector, skin tone or zero-width joiner. The cut title is one line.
- A work order from a task with no title (or with the task's own name as its title) gets the shortened name, and the **full name goes first in its notes**. Names that fit get no extra note.
- The same rule applies to alarm work-order titles (made from a point's name), round checklist lines, a position from an RCM study with a long system name (full name first in its description), and copies of tasks or positions whose names are already too long.
- `apply_rcm`: a decision text over 200 characters gives a shortened task name, with the full text in the task's instructions (which travel with its work orders). Re-applying the study shortens names that are already too long. It replaces instructions only when they're empty or an earlier study text, never the user's own.

**One task can't stop the run**
- New `Maintenance.generate()` returns `{work_orders, skipped: [{task: {id, name}, why}]}`. Each task is opened on its own. A refusal (`Invalid`) is logged as a warning and listed in `skipped`. Anything unexpected is still `logger.exception`, so it still alerts, but it's listed too and the other tasks go ahead. `generate_work_orders()` still returns the list.
- REST `POST /api/maintenance/work-orders/generate`, MCP `maintenance_work_orders generate` and so the `/api/v1` twin and the CLI now return `skipped` alongside `work_orders`. This only adds a key.
- The daily run counts `skipped_tasks` in its result, and the digest email lists skipped tasks (when it's sent anyway).

**Every way in refuses an over-long name, saying what to do**
- The one shared validator (`_text`) now says the limit, the current length and what to do, for example: *"The task's name is at most 200 characters; this one is 397. Shorten it and put the detail in the task's instructions."*
- The spreadsheet import now checks names (positions in the path, item, class, serial and so on, failure mode) before writing anything. Before, a long name failed partway through the write.
- `update_position`, `update_item` and the point name now name their field in the message.
- App: names and titles show a count as they near 200 characters. Past 200 they show the same advice in red, and the submit button is disabled. This covers tasks (add, edit), work orders (open, edit), positions, locations, items, item classes, conditions and measurement points. There's no `maxLength`, so a pasted paragraph isn't silently cut. "Raise work order" on a task now sends no title (the server makes it).

## Tests
- `backend/tests/test_maintenance_long_names.py` (20 tests):
  - the 397-character name, set by a raw `task.updated` event as the real data was, goes through `generate` and the daily run (title cut, full name first in notes, no warnings or errors, rebuild matches);
  - per-task isolation (a refused task and a crashing task are both listed, the rest are opened, warning vs error logging);
  - the shortening rule: exact fit, one over, no spaces, early-space hard cut, CJK, combining accents, ZWJ emoji, German, multi-line, bounded full name;
  - RCM apply and re-apply, `from_rcm`, copy, alarm titles;
  - every entry path refusing with the exact message, an all-or-nothing import, the app API.
- MCP and `/api/v1` tests for the message and the `skipped` key. The daily-run isolation test now patches `generate`.
- Frontend: `maintenanceText.test.js`.

body:
Three WebKitBindings speedups: scroll-top 8x faster, append-child 14% and insert-before 15% faster, and repeated `getElementsByTagName()` calls return the same collection.

- `scrollTop`/`scrollLeft` reads now take the clean layout geometry read instead of always running `update_layout()`. To keep these reads exact, a pending re-snap in a document with snap areas now stops its own clean reads, and `scroll-snap-align`/`-stop`/`-type` now count as properties that may affect layout geometry, because a re-snap moves every box in the scroll container. One list in `property_may_resnap_scroll_container()` now serves both the style invalidation and a test that keeps the geometry table in sync with it.
- `ComputedStyleRecordView` now builds its `ComputedValues` only when it has a record. Before, the empty view for an unstyled element (asked for on every removal, to check for list items) built and destroyed a whole `ComputedValues`.
- `getElementsByTagName()` caches its collections weakly per root, keyed by name and by whether the document is HTML, as the DOM spec allows and as other browsers do. Dead entries are swept when a new entry is stored. This makes one more subtest in `webidl/current-realm.html` pass.

## Summary
`event=search_timing` is logged once per search and is the largest share of production log bytes (~16.6 MB of 28.4 MB/day). Most of each record repeats data it already carries. This change keeps one record per search and removes only the repeated values from the **emitted** record (`_emit` / new `_log_fields` in `reflexio/server/search_runtime.py`):

- `phase_work_ms`: an entry is emitted only when it differs from `phases_ms`. They differ only when a phase overlaps itself (parallel work), so that signal is kept. In 500 of 500 sampled prod records the two maps were identical.
- `phase_counts`: entries with a count of 1 are dropped for phases present in `phases_ms`. A reader treats a missing count as 1. Other counts, and counted phases with no `phases_ms` entry, are kept.
- JSON uses `separators=(",", ":")`.

Measured at about 48% smaller per record. `SearchScope.snapshot()` and the Sentry phase metrics are unchanged.

author: zannagh
body:
Hotfix. This makes two changes; the user decided the rules for both on 2026-10-22.

**Kiosk read-only comments and activity**

| Resting kiosk | Published | Draft | Archived |
|---|---|---|---|
| Comments | read-only | hidden | hidden |
| Per-boulder activity | read-only, live | hidden | hidden |
| Wall-wide activity card | not shown ("Log in to see…") | – | – |

- **Names on the tablet:**
  - Members who consented to the kiosk (`WallMember.KioskConsentedAt`) are named.
  - Members who didn't read as **"A member"**, with no id, avatar or identifier. This applies on page reads, in live envelopes and for grade-proposal proposers.
  - Setters and creators stay named on their boulders.
  - Erased and system authors show as Ghost.
- **Acting as a member:** the kiosk shows that member's view (`FeedViewer.KioskActing`). Switching identity is always a full-page POST, so each switch gets a new circuit.
- **Storage and live delivery:** activity rows stay Members-audience in storage. The kiosk is let through at delivery, for boulder entries on published, non-archived boulders only. Share links still get no activity.
- **Cost:** the kiosk-consent and kiosk-activity lookups run only when a kiosk is subscribed (`FeedKioskNeeds`). If those facts are missing, delivery fails closed: no rows and no names.

**Deleting an attempt removes its activity entry**
- **New link:** a nullable `ActivityLogEntry.AttemptId` column, FK → Attempts `ON DELETE CASCADE`, in migration `20261022211019_LinkActivityEntryToAttempt`.
- **Writes and deletes:** the entry is now written in the same save as its attempt and removed in the same save as the delete. Deleting a boulder now also removes its attempts' entries.
- **Live updates:** the new feed kind `activity.removed` goes to members, and to the kiosk for open boulders only.
- **Startup cleanup:** `AttemptActivityBackfill` is idempotent and runs after Migrate inside the existing try/catch. It links existing entries to their attempts and deletes orphans. Verified against prod with read-only SELECTs, it will make **140 links and 4 deletions**:
  - 1 duplicate send written 8 s after the real one;
  - 1 extra flash written 1.6 s before the real flash (the real flash keeps its entry);
  - 2 "attempt" entries whose attempts no longer exist.

  It deletes only when every remaining attempt in the group has an entry, so a real send can never lose its entry.

**Tests**
- Core with Postgres: 5292 passed. The only 2 failures are the OpenCV real-photo tests, which can't run on the Mac.
- Playwright on Chromium and WebKit: 101 passed, 5 skipped.
- Mutation checks: 23 + 12 + 6 + 5 in Core, and 7 in Playwright, all caught except 2 documented redundant survivors.
- Adversarial review: SHIP. Its one finding, the grade-proposal byline, is fixed here.

**Merge note for main → staging:** `FeedFanOut`, `FeedCatchUp`, `FeedHydrated` and `FeedHydration` will conflict semantically with staging #197. Keep both rules: `FeedKioskActivity.Allows && FeedOutsideComments.Allows`, and `FeedHydrated` must carry both `CommentBoulders` and `Kiosk`.

author: lasav
body:
## Summary

Fixes finding 2 of the 2026-10-15 performance audit: related papers are slow for papers not recently viewed. A cold `GET /api/papers/related` read 350–600 HNSW index pages from disk (0.4–0.9 s of DB time). The 133 MB index doesn't stay in 256 MB `shared_buffers`, and most clicks are on papers nobody viewed recently.

- **New `paper_related` table** (`db.py`): one row per relevant paper, holding the ids of its top 20 SPECTER2 neighbours (most similar first) and their cosine sims as parallel arrays. RLS line added to `migrations/enable_rls.sql`.
- **New `compute-related` stage** (`related.py`): exact top-k search in numpy over all relevant papers. The numpy step takes ~13 s for 35k synthetic papers locally. It's a full recompute each run, since new papers change older papers' neighbours. The upsert skips unchanged rows (sims rounded to 4 dp so float noise doesn't rewrite every row), and rows for papers no longer relevant are deleted. Added to the CLI and as the last stage of `run-all`.
- **Route** (`papers.py`): reads the stored row and joins only the first `limit` + 5 neighbours to `papers` by primary key. It re-checks `llm_relevant` on both the source and each neighbour, so a stale row never serves a reclassified paper. Falls back to the existing HNSW query when a paper has no row yet. The response shape is unchanged.
- **`limit` cap lowered from 50 to 20** to match the stored count. The UI always asks for 10; a request over 20 now returns 422.

## Rollout (order matters)

The route queries `paper_related` directly, so the table must exist before the API deploys.

1. Run `aisafety-pipeline init-db` against production, and run `ALTER TABLE public.paper_related ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` in the Supabase SQL editor.
2. Run `aisafety-pipeline compute-related` once. Check the row count is ≈ the relevant-paper count (~34k).
3. Deploy the API.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` against local Postgres (docker compose): 161 passed. New tests cover the numpy top-k against brute force, the stage (ordering, excluding self and non-relevant papers, no-op rerun, stale-row removal), the fast path being used, skipped stale neighbours, 404 for a non-relevant source, and the 422 above 20.
- [x] `ruff check`
- [ ] After rollout: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` the fast-path query in production for a few papers nobody viewed recently. Expect single-digit ms.
- [ ] After rollout: `curl -w` timings for ~10 random papers. Expect close to paper-detail latency (~0.1 s), down from 1.1–1.3 s.
- [ ] The next `pipeline-cron` run logs `compute-related:` and then `run-all: complete`.

## Objet

- Ajout de l'offre **GEDIA All Inclusive GES Électricité**, en Base (#54) et Heures creuses (#335).
- Le moteur accepte maintenant **`abonnement_annuel_ttc`**, car GEDIA publie ses abonnements en €/an.

## Grille

[Grille TTC GEDIA](https://egbyjwbrxlxdjopgyome.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/gediaenergies/all-inclusive-electricite-fixe/grille-tarifaire.pdf), « Prix applicables du 19-10-2026 au 25-10-2026 », page 2, tableau **« Domestique »**. Le second tableau est celui des professionnels. J'ai lu la grille sur le rendu de la page : la ligne 15 kVA (328,78 €) manque dans `pdftotext`.

| | Valeurs |
|---|---|
| kWh Base | 0,26948 € (3 et 6 kVA), 0,26725 € (9 à 36 kVA) |
| kWh HC | HP 0,28965 €, HC 0,21082 €, pas d'option en 3 kVA |
| Abonnement (€ TTC/an) | 145,56 / 190,36 / 238,61 / 285,13 / 328,78 / 373,71 / 469,64 / 557,65 / 646,52, identique en Base et en HC |

Toutes les valeurs correspondent aux fiches #54 et #335.

## Moteur : abonnement annuel

`_puissances()` renvoie maintenant des €/an : soit `abonnement_mensuel_ttc` × 12, comme avant, soit `abonnement_annuel_ttc` repris tel quel. Diviser par 12 ne tombait pas juste (190,36 / 12 = 15,8633…). Les deux champs sont **exclusifs**. Les offres existantes ne changent pas : tous les tests précédents passent.

## Choix à valider

- **Grille hebdomadaire** : GEDIA publie une grille par semaine de souscription, ensuite fixe 12 ou 24 mois. J'ai retenu la grille du 19/10 et 12 mois ; il faudra la mettre à jour comme les autres grilles datées.

- Dans le scénario de `test_init` (consommation du 1er au 3 octobre), GEDIA est **indisponible** : sa grille est postérieure, comme celles de GEG et d'Ohm. Une assertion le vérifie.

- [x] PR vers `dev`
- [x] `pytest --cov` : 104 tests réussis, couverture 99,12 % ; `ruff` et `yamllint --strict` : OK ; audit de journalisation : 0

author: mpmdw
body:
Tier: light

Impact statement (start each answer with Yes or No, then say why; any Yes makes this PR full tier):
(i) Raw-bundle byte or recorded timestamp: No, only five new test modules under tests/ are added; no bundle, byte or timestamp is read or written outside temporary test directories.
(ii) Reduced energy, time, token count or correctness score: No, no production code changes; the tests only check existing calibration and floor arithmetic on synthetic inputs.
(iii) Admit, refuse, select or exclude decision over bundles, nights, blocks, envelopes or items: No, no admission or refusal path is changed; the tests assert the current decisions.
(iv) Unit or uncertainty: No, no unit, tolerance or uncertainty in production is added or changed.
(v) Registration, prospective manifest, analysis plan or estimator constant: No, none is touched.
(vi) Published number or sentence in the paper, README claims or claim renderers: No, none is touched.

## Gate ledger

| # | Gate | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Independent review by a non-author, with a lens that executes the code (light tier: N/A (light tier)) | N/A (light tier) |
| 2 | Whole suite on the merged tree (current main merged into the head), exact tail recorded (light tier, docs only: N/A (docs only)) | RUN c865d3856d9e1ed691998b7c98ac3c0d2ac1ba1e |
| 3 | CI green on the final head; evidence is that head's sha | RUN c865d3856d9e1ed691998b7c98ac3c0d2ac1ba1e |
| 4 | Cold Fable final pass on merge code that touches measurement, calibration or claims (otherwise: N/A (no measurement, calibration or claim code); light tier: N/A (light tier)) | N/A (light tier) |
| 5 | Findings dispositioned: each fixed, deferred to a named lane, or rejected with a reason (light tier: N/A (light tier)) | N/A (light tier) |

## Summary

Tests only. A sampled mutation sweep of the five calibration modules (125 mutants, wave 5, report `solwave5/MUT-CALIB`) left 41 mutants that the existing tests did not catch: small deliberate code changes, such as replacing `max(pre, post)` with `post`, that still passed every covering test. This PR adds tests that fail on 34 of them, so a future regression of the same shape fails CI.

New modules (one per production module, so lanes that edit the existing test files do not conflict):
- `tests/test_calibration_bracketing_mutants.py` (7 tests): endpoint selection, freshness, zero-length window, allowance projection, inclusive budget, epoch-zero capture.
- `tests/test_calibration_ledger_mutants.py` (8 tests): one-slot sessions, claim after all slots finalized, 64-byte journal tail, replaced lock inode, custody worker protocol and teardown.
- `tests/test_detection_floor_mutants.py` (7 tests): allowance embedded twice, transport worst cell, residual-corner floor at n=9, n=16 corner cap, corner helper with a negative mean, wire counts, config-set provenance.
- `tests/test_floor_extraction_mutants.py` (8 tests): member envelope arithmetic, quarter-metric boundary, zero metric, two launch lineages, floor-condition label, point diagnostic, comparative anchor maximum, sub-unit throughput.
- `tests/test_floor_mint_estimator_mutants.py` (2 tests): screen-only allowance projection, inconsistent session bound.

Each test docstring names the mutant it kills. Expected values are hand arithmetic on synthetic inputs, mostly dyadic so they compare exactly; the four float comparisons use 1e-6 relative (the fallback for outputs with no printed half-width), and each targeted mutant moves its value by more than 13,000 times that bar. No test probes within 100x of a production tolerance constant.

Seven survivors are left without a test, on purpose:
- Equivalent: M02612 (comparing the first binding with itself adds no mismatch), M00043 (at n = 16 the fallback factor is sqrt(15/15) = 1.0 exactly), M01653 (`anchor_shift_envelope` refuses an envelope whose max_abs_delta_j is below its reach by more than 1e-12, so the collapse moves the half-width by at most 1e-12 J).
- M01802 (session-bound agreement made exact): the session stores `float(bracket["b_fiducial_s"])` and `registered_common_mode_operative_bound` returns that same value, so exact equality is the real property.
- M03964 (slot-claim predecessor taken from the first receipt): the append engine drops the builder's predecessor and re-seals the stored receipt (`_target_core`, `_intent_target_receipt`), so no stored value changes; it also survived claims made after several receipts.
- M00129 and M00681 (`detection_floor._close`): killing them needs a probe at exactly 1e-12 relative, or between 1e-12 relative and the 1e-6 J cap. The 1e-12 relative bar is below 1e6 times float noise, which makes it a silly number in its own right. It is reported separately for re-derivation and is not pinned by a test here.

No real bug was found.

## Verification

Head under test: c865d3856d9e1ed691998b7c98ac3c0d2ac1ba1e (one commit on main c21c52dfa). The five swept modules are byte-identical to the sweep's head bfab7c950. Interpreter /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 and the repo venv, `JW_B5_SYNTHETIC_ONLY=1`.

2. Each new module under unittest from the worktree root: `Ran 7 / 8 / 7 / 8 / 2 tests ... OK`.

Mutant replay (lead, all 41 survivors, each mutant patched into its module in memory, only the five new modules run): 34 `KILLED` (each by 1 or 2 targeted failures), 7 `SURVIVED` (exactly the seven listed above), clean `PASS`. Tool: `mutkill/tools/verify.py` with `mutoverlay.py` in the night archive.
4. Whole suite: CI on this PR (12 shards).

- The review job is handed only the chosen credential, so the other is never used, not even by the action's inline-comment classifier.
- A comment asking for a credential the stub doesn't pass gets a `Claude review request failed:` reply; a PR description that does so has only its credential ignored, with a warning.
- This repo's `review.yml` now passes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (empty until set) with `default-credential: oauth`, and the iwol config documents the new syntax.
- README covers the new request word, input and secret guidance.

## Test plan
- [x] `actionlint` on both changed workflows
- [ ] The automatic review on this PR runs on the OAuth token (run log: `using oauth`)
- [ ] `/review api-key` on a PR replies `Claude review request failed:` while `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` isn't set
