author: juanpacol
body:
## What

A redesign of the frontend in the manner of the Hermes Agent site, in one PR, one commit per area.

**Surfaces.** Every card, panel and menu has a one-pixel ring and short layered shadows, and nested radii. Along the way: Tailwind makes `shadow-<colour>` utilities too, and the colour called `card` won over the shadow called `card`, so cards had a halo in their own colour instead of a shadow. The shadows are now `raised`, `raised-lg` and `popover`; a test forbids a shadow sharing a name with a colour. Pictures of studies get a fine edge.

**Landing**
- Hero in two columns: the headline and the way in, and an answer as the product gives it (a cited guideline answer, a drug interaction, and a refusal to guess) instead of the terminal animation. Heights never change, it pauses on hover and focus and with a button, and under reduced motion it stays on the first example. The five-step walkthrough moved to "How it works".
- Navy bands (`band-dark`) on the white page, for the hero, the agents and the closing section.
- Header with three menus (this page's sections, the patient portal, the open-source project) whose panels list real destinations with a line about each, a scroll-spy that marks where you are, and the same groups in the phone sheet.
- Feature grid as Hermes lays it out: a huge title, three columns of numbered cells (`#1 ASK`...), each a title, a paragraph and a square deep-blue picture. Cells without a picture get a generated pattern; the See cell cycles through the ten example studies. Pictures drift inside their frames; the README beside them says how to add pictures or video.
- Footer that rises into place as you reach it, with a giant wordmark behind. A hero that drifts away. Both follow the scroll with a little lag and are off under reduced motion.
- A demo to pick a study and read the analysis a vision model wrote for it.
- The sources strip and the image gallery are gone (their code and tests too); the sources moved into the Cite feature's text.

## Notes

- The analyses in the demo, and the three example answers, are written for the page and labelled as examples; nothing on the public page calls a model. The demo's analyses are model output, not reviewed by a clinician.
- Eight of the example images still have no recorded source or licence (see `public/landing/analysis/README.md`).
- No fonts or code from the Hermes site are used.
- Browser specs that scroll use the shared helpers from the previous PR.

## Tests

Vitest 441, Playwright 521 at four viewports (320 px included), tsc, lint and build. New: surface tokens and shadow names, the scroll maths, the answer card, the feature grid and its slides, header menus and scroll-spy, hero layout, footer and parallax, and reduced motion.

## CI

This is the first frontend-only PR under the scoped CI, so it measures the saving: before, about 8 minutes; the result is recorded in a comment below.

author: alanlima
body:
## Summary

Operational failures in Terraform, configuration reconciliation and seeded-place verification were hidden in temporary files or replaced by generic errors. Retain ordinary command output and standard SDK/HTTP error context so the actual failure can be diagnosed across Actions jobs. The existing Terraform wrapper now streams by default, including environment and destroy plans, while preserving exit statuses and the existing approval and exact-plan review gates.

This follows the owner's temporary MVP logging policy for all GitHub Actions jobs. GitHub's built-in secret masking remains active; programmatic plan/state JSON, full response payloads and secret transport remain internal. No custom redactor, additional logging framework or log artifact is introduced. Operational logs can expose infrastructure identifiers and values that are not marked sensitive; broader workflow review, log purging and Environment recreation remain deferred.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests/ci -q` — 279 tests run; suite passed with 14 skipped.
- Configuration tests — 48 passed.
- Seeded-place verification tests — 7 passed.
- `actionlint -shellcheck=` across all workflows and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent review checks operational error visibility, private programmatic outputs, exit handling and unchanged approval gates.

## Runtime acceptance

The initial trusted-main [bootstrap run failed safely at planning](https://github.com/alanlima/pawlocal/actions/runs/39861410781). A local operator plan using the same inputs completed as a no-op with an unchanged state version. A fresh merged trusted-main run is still required to diagnose the workflow identity and complete #191.

author: boffti
body:
## Scope update

This branch grew into Phases 1 through 4 of the roadmap plus the UI P0/P1 fixes. On top of the summary below:

- **Review fixes:** expiring signed sessions, origin-aware Secure cookie, setup-route overwrite guards with one-time server-side state, strict `safeNext`, constant-time comparisons, separate manifest callback route.
- **UI P0/P1:** responsive page header (filters collapse below 1280px), cooldowns shown as next-run times, em-dashes out of UI strings, `prefers-reduced-motion` honored (CSS, particles, framer `MotionProvider`), radius rule, Settings filler removed, one-line Contribute header.
- **Phase 3, container:** `node:24-slim` image with SQLite on `/data`, in-process scheduler for nightly jobs (cron routes accept `CRON_SECRET` or a per-process secret), one-service compose, GHCR workflow on `main` and `v*`. Verified: build 59 s, 306 MB, healthy 1.1 s after start. Vercel builds are skipped via `vercel.json`.
- **Phase 4, MCP + CLI:** `/api/mcp` (mcp-handler 1.x, bearer tokens hashed in `api_tokens`) with `search_stars`, `get_repo`, `list_taxonomy`, `organize_repo`, `radar_feed`, `radar_action`, `star_repo`; Settings → Agents card to mint/revoke tokens with ready-to-paste client config; `bin/stardash.mjs` for the same from a shell. Verified live: handshake, tool list, tool calls, 401 without a token.

## Summary

Phases 1 and 2 of [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/boffti/stardash/blob/main/ROADMAP.md), plus the AI fixes that fell out of running it. StarDash no longer needs Supabase, an OAuth app you create by hand, or Vercel cron to be useful. Tracks #86.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / cleanup

## Changes

### Data layer: node:sqlite, no ORM
- `lib/db.ts` opens `./data/stardash.db` (`DATABASE_PATH`), creates the whole schema inline, exposes one `db` plus `nowIso`/`toJson`/`fromJson`. Postgres arrays and jsonb are JSON text, booleans 0/1, timestamps ISO text.
- All 24 API routes and `lib/user-metadata.ts` rewritten on prepared statements. The two Postgres functions (`get_user_repo_metadata`, `check_and_increment_ai_limit`) are TypeScript. Weekly AI quotas are stubbed open for the self-hosted build.
- Client components mutate tags, collections, status and notes through `"use server"` actions in `lib/metadata-actions.ts` instead of a browser Supabase client.
- `pnpm check:db` exercises sync, stale-star removal, tags, collections, cascade and user scoping in memory.
- Removed: `lib/supabase/*`, `modules/auth`, `supabase/migrations`, `@supabase/ssr`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, the Supabase env vars and CI placeholders.

### Auth: sign in with GitHub through an app the instance creates for itself
- "Connect GitHub" runs the GitHub App manifest flow: GitHub creates an app **owned by the self-hoster**, the instance stores the returned client id and secret in the `meta` table, then runs normal OAuth. No shared client id, no project-owned app, nothing of the maintainer on the consent screen. `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`/`GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` env override for pre-made apps.
- App user tokens expire in 8h; `lib/tokens.ts` refreshes them with the stored refresh token.
- Paste-a-PAT stays as the fallback (`POST /api/auth/login`) for GitHub Enterprise and headless boxes. Both paths share `signInWithGitHubToken()`.
- Session is an HMAC-signed cookie; the secret is minted once into `meta`, so there is no required auth env var.
- Single owner: the first GitHub user to sign in claims the instance.

### AI on cheap models
- `google/gemini-2.0-flash-001` is no longer served on OpenRouter. Default is `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` (`AI_MODEL` overrides); bring-your-own defaults are `gpt-5-mini` and `claude-haiku-5-5`.
- Removed every string/array `.max()` from `generateObject` schemas: hosted models ignore `maxLength`/`maxItems` and overflows were 500s. Rule documented in `AGENTS.md`.
- Categorize reuses an existing taxonomy whenever tags or collections exist, not only when a previous-run timestamp is set.

### Housekeeping
- Node 22 pinned for pnpm scripts (`.npmrc` `use-node-version`), `.nvmrc`, `engines.node >= 22.5`. `node:sqlite` needs it.
- `AGENTS.md`, `.env.example` describe the new stack.

## Verified live on a fresh database
- Connect GitHub end to end: app created, authorized, 469 stars synced, token + refresh token stored.
- Categorize over all 469 repos: 12 collections, 20 tags, every repo assigned (131s, about half a cent).
- Repo intel, contribution brief, Discover search, personalized search all return 200.
- Forged OAuth state, forged cookie, bad and fake PATs are rejected.

Not exercised: Radar scan with a GitHub App token (flag still off; Phase 5).

## How to test

1. `pnpm install && pnpm dev` (no env needed; AI buttons need `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`)
2. Open http://localhost:3000, click **Connect GitHub**, create the app, authorize
3. Stars sync; tag, collect, pin, note from the dashboard and Settings
4. `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm check:db && pnpm check:radar && pnpm build`

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm lint` passes (1 pre-existing warning)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm build` passes from a clean `.next` with no env

author: norejaberahmed-design
body:
## Purpose
Implement the agreed rules in AGENT_RULES.md for a single-chat Arabic-first agent with two capabilities:
1. Public research with source links and explicit coverage/verification limits.
2. AI-project discovery, read-only repository inspection, reviewable skill proposals, and guarded self-improvement.

## Included
- Replaced the multi-tab UI with one mobile-first Arabic chat.
- Added a no-key static fallback: GitHub public repository search, static inspection of a specified repository README/metadata, and Wikipedia search for general questions. The UI labels this mode honestly as limited and not an LLM.
- Added api_server.py endpoints: GET /api/health, POST /api/search, POST /api/chat. Provider keys stay on the server.
- Added web_search.py (Tavily adapter) and github_discovery.py (public GitHub metadata, README excerpt, and file/test/workflow path signals; no external code execution).
- Added skill_runtime.py and skill_proposer.py. New skills remain under skills/proposed and are never auto-activated.
- Hardened request limits, bounded/thread-safe in-memory rate limiting, response security headers, and non-root Docker runtime.
- Added a guarded scheduled/manual skill-proposal workflow that runs validation and regression tests, then opens a draft PR for review.
- Kept guarded AutoDev: bounded source/test changes, checks before a draft PR, no automatic merge.
- Added deployment documentation and dedicated CI with frontend smoke tests and a real container health smoke test.

## Verification on the latest branch commit
- Python compilation passed.
- Offline unit/integration suite: 76 tests passed.
- Inline JavaScript syntax check passed.
- Frontend fallback smoke tests passed for GitHub search, repository inspection, and Wikipedia search.
- All workflow YAML files parsed successfully.
- Docker image build passed.
- Container smoke test passed: /api/health responded successfully.
- Public UI secret scan passed.

## Still required for full live AI mode
- This PR remains draft and unmerged; the live GitHub Pages site still serves main and has not received this UI.
- The no-key fallback works without an API server but is limited to public GitHub/Wikipedia results; it does not generate LLM answers or search the whole web.
- Full chat requires deploying api_server.py to an HTTPS host and configuring TAVILY_API_KEY, SCOUT_LLM_API_KEY, SCOUT_LLM_MODEL, and SCOUT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS in the host's secret/environment settings. No live provider request has been verified yet because those settings are not configured.
- Before exposing the API publicly, configure provider spend limits and stronger hosting/API-gateway abuse controls; in-memory rate limiting is prototype-grade and CORS is not authentication.
- Repository inspection is static evidence only, not proof code runs correctly or is safe.
- No external skill is automatically activated and no code is automatically merged into main.

author: yung-sun-xxi
body:
In solo and friends-link games, once the current round's panorama has shown, the next round (if it is Mapillary) loads in a hidden viewer of the same size. When the round starts, that viewer moves into `#pano`. Rooms get no next place from the server and behave as before. Round 1 still loads cold.

Measured on localhost, from the start of a round to the first image shown:
- before (master, 13 rounds): 0.9–2.5 s (955, 1141, 1196, 1205, 1253, 1446, 1504, 2502 ms …)
- after (two 5-round games on fresh places): rounds 2–5 0 ms in 8 of 8; swapping a ready viewer in takes 30–40 ms
- friends link: every round 1→5 had the next one ready; no hidden viewer left on the final screen

Breakdown before: viewer ~100 ms, Graph lookup ~460 ms, thumbnail 300–2000 ms. A single viewer with `moveTo(id)` was tried and rejected: 1.2–1.6 s with the previous round's image on screen.

mapillary-js does not always emit `load` (a cached image gives only `image`), so a round counts as loaded on whichever comes first.

Closes #46

body:
## Scope
- Add an explicit Settings → Local models action to probe a phone-local OpenAI-compatible GGUF server at loopback and select its advertised Qwen 3.5 **4B** model across shared five-system routing.
- Keep Qwen 3.5 **2B** and **0.8B** optional as separate, verified local helper endpoints for advisory planning/structured output context. Their failure never substitutes the final-answer model.
- Enable native chat template with thinking disabled and streaming; retain existing JSON validation/repair and local-only endpoint restrictions.
- Preserve downloaded LiteRT/ONNX packages; no automatic new downloads, model eviction, or cloud fallback.
- Document setup and add source/identity regression tests (`npm run verify:mobile-qwen-gguf`).

## Risk/limitations
- Native GGUF llama-server must already be available on the phone, CORS/local-network permissions must allow the staging browser, and the model list must advertise Qwen 3.5 4B. Neither actual GGUF file hash nor on-device 5-system functional success can be verified from GitHub alone.
- A previous synthetic 30/31 benchmark used the GGUF runner; the existing 4B LiteRT browser model is a different artifact and should not inherit that score.

Target: staging only. Do not merge to main.

💡 What: Removed empty `observer` functions across modified components and optimized `courselist.js` and `rowscroll.js` by adding strict equality checks before calling `setData` for derived array lengths.
🎯 Why: WeChat Mini Program bridge serializes data and triggers callbacks for all registered observers. Empty observers add unnecessary cross-boundary overhead. Unconditional `setData` inside observers causes redundant secondary render cycles.
📊 Impact: Reduces unnecessary JS bridge communication and eliminates secondary re-renders in list components, minimizing rendering pipeline overhead.
🔬 Measurement: Verify rendering performance and bridge traffic during list updates in the WeChat Developer Tools performance monitor.

author: 7mdalajmi
body:
أرشيف `Laqta-1.0-build71.zip` دخل أولًا كما هو (أول كومِت)، فكل ما بعده يُقرأ كفرق مراجعة على النسخة المُسلَّمة. ثم كومِت واحد لكل مشكلة.

> **حدّ التحقق، أولًا وبصراحة:** الجلسة على Linux بلا Xcode وبلا Swift toolchain (منفذ `download.swift.org` مغلق هنا)، فلم يُبنَ المشروع ولم تُشغَّل الاختبارات. ما جرى بدلًا من ذلك: قراءة كل ملف مُعدَّل، وفحص توازن الأقواس والنصوص في 136 ملف Swift، وفحص `project.pbxproj` بأداة المشروع نفسها (`tools/check_pbxproj.py`، بالنتيجة نفسها قبل التعديل وبعده)، وفحص ملفات plist و xcstrings، ومطابقة محدِّدات `%@` و `%lld` بين كل نص وترجمته (صفر اختلاف). **أول خطوة عندك: Product → Build ثم Product → Test.**

## المشاكل العشر

| # | الكومِت | الإصلاح باختصار |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `No save fails silently…` | `ModelContext.commit()` يحفظ أو يُرجع التغيير ويرمي الخطأ، و`SaveFailureCenter` يعرض شريط «تعذّر الحفظ» مع «أعد المحاولة» التي تعيد نفس العمل، وورقة فيها نص الخطأ ومنفذ الاستعادة. لم يبقَ `try? save()` واحد. وظهر خطآن جانبيان: فشل حفظ أول تشغيل كان يعلّم المكتبة «مُهيّأة» (فتبقى فارغة للأبد)، وكذلك كل علَم ترقية مخطط. |
| 2 | `The app and the share extension…` | الاثنان يقرآن `LaqtaStore.syncIsWanted`، وأُضيفت حاوية iCloud لصلاحيات الإضافة. وإن فشل الفتح مع المزامنة، تفتح الإضافة محليًا وتضع طابعًا، والتطبيق يعيد كتابة فهرس تلك العناصر ليصدّرها CloudKit. |
| 3 | `Keep big files out…` | `loadFileRepresentation` لكل نوع سجّله المرسل قبل أي تحميل في الذاكرة؛ البايتات للصور فقط وبحدّ 64 MB؛ `pngData()` صار JPEG؛ وأكبر من 2 GB يُرفض برسالة تقول «افتح لقطة واستورده من هناك». |
| 4 | `The thirty days come from the App Store…` | حُذف منتج `trial30` من القائمة ومن `Laqta.storekit`، والثلاثون يومًا من `AppTransaction.originalPurchaseDate` — فلا نافذة شراء على تجربة مجانية ولا عدّاد يتصفّر بإعادة التثبيت. ومعرّف المنتج القديم يُقرأ فقط لمن جرّب TestFlight. `AppStore/Checklist.md` محدَّث. |
| 5 | `Arabic, and a layout that turns around with it` | `LaqtaLocale` لم يبقَ يثبّت `en` (وهو ما كان يمنع ظهور أي ترجمة)، وأُزيل الاتجاه المفروض من iOS والماك، و**785 نصًا مترجمًا من 787** في `Localizable.xcstrings`، وجدول ثانٍ `Suggestions.xcstrings` لأسماء الوحدات التي تختلف بين العدّ («12 لقطة») والإضافة («لقطات السفر»)، و`InfoPlist.xcstrings` لاسم التطبيق ونصوص الصلاحيات، و`LayoutDirection.sign` يقلب الإزاحات اليدوية (الشيفرون، السحب في شاشة البداية، كومة الصور في ورقة الحفظ). |
| 6 | `A locked folder stays locked…` | `BackupCrypto`: AES-GCM على دفعات 1 MB، وكل دفعة توثّق اسم الملف وموضعها وطوله؛ المفتاح في Keychain قابل للمزامنة؛ النسخة المختومة باسم `.lqenc` (والمنظّف يحفظها)؛ والاستعادة بلا مفتاح تحسب العناصر وتقولها. مجلد الاستعادة `.complete` والأرشيف `.completeUnlessOpen`. |
| 7 | `No save fails silently…` | مُهيّئ `@AppObject` العادي يشترط `AppObjectStandIn`، فلا يسمح المترجم بشاشة تطلب كائنًا بلا بديل — زال `fatalError` بالبنية لا بحيلة في Release. بديل `LibraryStore` لا يفتح شيئًا. |
| 8 | `No save fails silently…` | `LaunchRecoveryView`: «افتحها من جديد» أو «ابدأ مكتبة جديدة» (تنقل الملفات إلى `Damaged/` بلا حذف)، ثم استعادة أحدث نسخة iCloud تلقائيًا بعلَم يعيش بعد إغلاق التطبيق. |
| 9 | `The app and the share extension…` | `LaqtaSchemaV1` بنسخة 1.0.0 — وهي نسخة `Schema` الافتراضية نفسها فلا تُمَس مكتبة قائمة — و`LaqtaMigrationPlan` مكان المرحلة القادمة. |
| 10 | `A photo leaves Photos only when…` | `AssetMatch` يفرّق بين معرّف من العنصر نفسه ومعرّف من المطابقة. المؤكد وحده يُحذف، والتخمين يذهب إلى `ConfirmOriginalsSheet`: نسخة لقطة والصورة المرشحة جنبًا إلى جنب. |

## الميزتان

1. **واجهة عربية كاملة RTL** — الترجمة تشمل نصوص الواجهة، ورسائل `MediaError` و`BackupError`، وكل حالات النسخ الاحتياطي وiCloud، والتواريخ والمدد («الآن»، «قبل 3 س»، «بعد 16 يوم»)، وأسماء الوحدات في `LaqtaFormat.count`، ومجلدات المكتبة الجديدة، والإشعارات القصيرة (toasts) وأزرار «تراجع»، ونصوص الصلاحيات التي يعرضها النظام.
2. **شاشة عند فشل الحفظ + استعادة تلقائية** — الشريط والورقة (مشكلة 1)، وشاشة الإنقاذ عند فشل فتح المكتبة مع استعادة أحدث نسخة بلا سؤال (مشكلة 8).

## الإضافات الصغيرة

- `as!` في `VideoPlayback` صار `as?`.
- `aps-environment` من `APS_ENVIRONMENT` في xcconfig: development أثناء التطوير، production في Release.
- **أحجام الخطوط:** الفحص لم يجد في build 71 حجمًا ثابتًا: صفر استدعاء لـ`.font(.system(size:))`، وكل النصوص تمرّ بـ`laqtaFont`/`laqtaIconFont`/`laqtaDisplayFont` وتكبر مع Dynamic Type. الموجود هو `maxScale` على العناوين الكبيرة (34–118 pt) وحدّ AX3 العام، وكلها مقصودة. الموضع الثابت الوحيد هو مصغّر معاينة المظهر في الإعدادات.

## اختبارات مضافة

`BackupCryptoTests` (دورة كاملة على عدة دفعات، ملف فارغ، مفتاح آخر، دفعة معدَّلة أو منقولة، ملف ليس مختومًا)، وفي `RestoreTests`: ما يُختم فعلًا (مجلد مقفول وكل ما تحته)، وأسماء الملفات في المانيفست، والاستعادة بمفتاح وبدونه. و`RecoveryTests`: دورة شريط فشل الحفظ، ونقل المكتبة التالفة إلى `Damaged/` دون حذفها. وتحديث `TrialTests` بعد حذف منتج التجربة.

## ما بقي بالإنجليزية (مقصودًا)

الكلمات التي هي بيانات لا نصوص: مفاتيح `origin` و`basis` التي يقارنها الكود، وأوامر نموذج اللغة في `AIWriter`، وأسماء 56 مزاج غلاف، ومحتوى الرسوم التوضيحية في شاشة البداية.

التفاصيل كاملة في `Laqta/FIXES_AR.md`.

body:
## Done

- Lays every lens on one intrinsic grid: the shells, the `DocumentLayout` and `WorkspaceLayout` archetypes, the mode strip, the rail and the canvas share one column model and one gutter (`--grid-gutter`).
- Each component folder carries an `anatomy.yaml`; stylesheets are transcribed from them and checked by the anatomy and stylesheet checks.
- Recomposes the docs pages, the standards index, the definitions explorer and the docsite catalog on the new grid.
- Adds layout measurements (spans and component page width) to the tests.

This PR went through 5 adversarial review rounds (the fifth closed the four docs pages' spans, the strip and colophon bleed, the three-column aside and the remaining findings).

Merge order: this PR must land after the PR for the base branch `claude/prism-s1-metro-navigation` (#1511, "fix(prism-metro): renders an entity page after client navigation").

## QA

- `bun run check` from the repository root passes.
- `bun run lerna run test --ignore '@canonical/svelte-*' --ignore '@canonical/styles-vanilla-adapter' --no-bail` passes (the definitions lens tests can time out when every package runs in parallel and pass when the package runs alone).
- Open the docs app and the metro app at 1440 and 390 in light and dark and check that pages fill the main column and nothing sits in a one-column strip.

### PR readiness check

- [x] PR title follows the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) format, using one of the allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`, `ci`, `revert`.
  - The matching type label is applied automatically from the title — there is no type label to add by hand.
  - Breaking changes are marked with `!` in the title (e.g. `feat(router)!: …`), which adds the `breaking` label.
- [x] The code follows the appropriate [code standards](https://github.com/canonical/pragma-core/tree/main/packages/semantics/code-standards)

body:
## Why

The video page has a Whiteboard view with every episode's cards, but nothing tells the user it exists. A user who
watches the first episode does not know that the agent also wrote the episode's key points as note cards, how the
whiteboard is laid out, or what the yellow, green and red cards mean, so the feature goes unnoticed or confuses.

## What changes

At the first delivery of an episode with cards in a series, the agent adds a few sentences to its delivery message,
next to the feedback sentence it already adds at the first delivery. They say what the cards are for (reviewing
without watching again), where to open them ("Whiteboard" on the video page), how the whiteboard is laid out (a
section per episode, a column of cards per scene, arrows along the reasoning), what the colours mean (as
`references/cards.md` defines them), that later episodes join the same whiteboard, and that "Save to Heptabase" keeps
it.

- **`references/languages/zh-TW.md`**, new section 12, fixes the Chinese wording so the button names match the page;
  `en.md` gets the matching section.

## Trade-offs

The first delivery message gets four sentences longer. It explains the whiteboard in terms the user meets on the page
rather than the guide's own (a series, `notes.yaml`).

author: castrojo
body:
Pins the repo's GitHub Actions to the commit SHAs their version tags currently
resolve to, closing the supply-chain substitution vector described in #114
(consolidated in #118).

## What changed

Every third-party action was referenced by a mutable version tag, and
`ste.yml` called the shared `ste-lint` reusable workflow by the mutable `main`
branch. A tag can be force-moved to point at different code without the version
string changing, and anything landing on the reusable workflow's branch is live
in this repo's checks immediately — both let an attacker swap in malicious code
without the pinned string moving. `pages.yml` in particular holds
`pages: write` and `id-token: write`, so a compromised `deploy-pages` could
publish attacker content to the live site.

Each action is now pinned to its commit SHA with the version kept as a trailing
comment for readability:

- `check-metadata.yml` — `actions/checkout`
- `pages.yml` — `actions/checkout`, `actions/configure-pages`,
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, `actions/deploy-pages`
- `tests.yml` — `actions/checkout` (three jobs), `actions/setup-python`
- `ste.yml` — the `ste-lint` reusable workflow ref

## Notes

- SHAs were resolved live at commit time. `actions/setup-python@v7` and the
  `ste-lint@main` ref had moved since #118 was filed, so these two pins use the
  current resolution (`setup-python@6d4fd22b…`, `ste-lint@f835d4a4…`), not the
  SHAs in that report. The other four tags were unchanged.
- #118's third item — a `permissions: contents: read` block on `ste.yml` — is
  already present on `main` (added after the report), so this PR does not touch
  it.

Validated: all five workflow files parse as YAML and the full test suite
(63 tests) passes unchanged. The diff touches only `.github/workflows/**`.

Closes #114.
Refs #118.

author: jmmshn
body:
The swap (bees-13.9, ADR-0010 build plan): the rebuilt core becomes `bs`. `cmd/bsx` moves to `cmd/bs` over top-level `internal/` (so AGENTS.md's and the skills' `internal/prompt/` paths stay true), and the old core is deleted. Stacked on #110 (bees-13.8). ## What changes - **One bs.** It runs on `~/.config/bees` and the real logbooks; a `herdr --session` toy still reads its own config dir and refuses the real logbooks' dir. `bs epic`, `bs bead` and `bs version`, with its stale-install warning, come over from the old bs (the role prompts send sessions to them). `bs init`, `bs end --all`, multi-bead spawn and `scripts/e2e.sh` go; the live-test skill replaces the script. - **Old sessions.** bs refuses a logbook where a session the old bs started is still open (a spawn before goals, with no `started`), naming each, before it opens (and so migrates) it. `bs end` and `bs status` warn instead, so each can be ended. `bs end` on such a spawn closes no herdr workspace: it recorded no process, and herdr reuses workspace ids after a restart. Such a spawn is never healed from its pane (its pane may run the old bs's live worker), and cross-project `bs send` refuses a target logbook that still has one. - **R48 kept** (bees-13.26): `logbook.Open` refuses a missing file; only `bs queen` and `bs spawn` create one (`logbook.Create`), and say so once they succeed; a spawn refused for its arguments, goal or bead makes none. - **Resume** (bees-13.27): `bs spawn` on an open spawn whose process died restarts it in its recorded pane, in its own conversation once it has read its inbox, and records a `started` that names the dead one. A worker restarted by hand in its pane is healed the same way (a dead recorded start counts as none). - **The abort** (A1): `bs end --incomplete` ends a worker handed off or not; prune, which never removes unlanded work, is the guard. Re-spawning a bead whose last spawn ended reuses the branch it left: its kept worktree, or one checked out again where it was (the old bs's `bs end` removed worktrees and kept branches). Both were refused "already exists" with no way on. Every `next:` puts its flags before the worker's name, so it runs as printed. - **Mail scoped to the open spawn** (B): a worker reads only what was stored after its latest spawn, while it is open; migrated mail and mail between spawns never reach a later spawn. `bs send` to a worker name with no open spawn warns. - **Role prompts**: the queen's merge turn is land → `bs end` → `bs prune` → `bd close`, in one turn; cancel is `bs end --incomplete `; resume is `bs spawn --goal `. Every prompt names the command `{{bs}}`; a beads goal files through `bs bead new`. No PR wording outside the goal and host fragments. - `worker.path` and the claude_code models are read (spawn and the adapter use them) and no longer marked unread. ADR-0010 Amendment 3 and DECISIONS R53 record all of it. ## Rollout checklist 1. In every project, **stop** every session the old `bs` started, without the old `bs end` (it removes the worktree): exit each queen, and exit each worker's Claude in its pane. Their entries stay open for step 6. 2. Unset `BS_PROJECT`, `BS_LOGBOOK` and `BS_LOGBOOK_DIR` in the keeper's shells (`bs doctor` names any left). 3. The keeper merges this PR. 4. In the main checkout: `git pull` on `main`, `go install ./cmd/bs`; `bs version` prints the merge commit. Only the queen or keeper installs, from `main`, after the merge. 5. Migrate each logbook with a read: `cd && bs status`, in each of bees, dotfiles, familysite, pymatgen-analysis-defects and pyrho (the checkout selects the project; `BS_PROJECT` stays unset). The first open copies the old file to `~/.local/share/bees/.db.pre-2`, then migrates; bs warns if a `.pre-2` was already there and kept. Check each `.pre-2` exists, and keep them for a day. 6. `bs status` names the open old sessions (16 on today's copies: bees 8, dotfiles 2, familysite 5, pyrho 1). End each from that checkout with `bs end --as queen- `; bs closes no workspace of theirs and names it, so close it by hand (`herdr workspace close `) once its Claude is gone. 7. Restart each queen with `bs queen` in her pane, and re-spawn each worker with `bs spawn --goal --label "" `: it adopts the branch the old spawn left, in its kept worktree or one checked out again where it was. ## Rollback - **Before the first new spawn** in a logbook: reinstall the old bs (`git checkout && go install ./cmd/bs` in the main checkout). The migrated table still fits it (its kinds are a superset, rows unchanged), so it reads and writes on. - **After a new spawn**: the old bs can't read it (its decoder takes a spawn's `workspace` for a string; this bs writes an object). Rolling back then means, with no bs command and no queen or worker running: delete `.db-wal` and `.db-shm`, then copy `.db.pre-2` over `.db`. That loses every row written since the migration. Keep the new bs instead, and fix forward. ## Migration on copies of the five real logbooks The keeper's copies (`~/.cache/bees-live/logbook-copies-20261022/`, taken 15:10) copied again into a scratch run dir; never the originals. bs ran on a throwaway `herdr --session` config naming that dir, with a stub `herdr` first on PATH that reports every pane gone and refuses (and logs) any other call, since the copies record panes on the keeper's live server, some still running. Per logbook: `bs inbox --as queen-

`, `bs status`, `bs end --as queen-

` each old session named, `bs status`, `bs inbox` again. | logbook | before (schema, rows) | refused command | `bs status` | `.pre-2` | old sessions named → `bs end` | after | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | bees | 1, 1482 | `inbox` exit 2, file untouched (1, 1482), no `.pre-2` | warns, exit 0; migrated to 2, rows 1482 | 1, 1482 | 8: bees-13-2 … bees-13-9 → each exit 0, workspace left open, named | no warning; `inbox` exit 0; 2, 1490 | | dotfiles | 0, 195 | `inbox` exit 2, untouched | warns; 2, 195 | 0, 195 | 2: dotfiles-6-4, 6-5 → exit 0 | 2, 197 | | familysite | 0, 343 | `inbox` exit 2, untouched | warns; 2, 343 | 0, 343 | 5: familysite-1-6, 2-1, 2-2, 2-3, 2-10 → exit 0 | 2, 348 | | pymatgenanalysisdefects | 0, 74 | none open: `inbox` exit 0 (migrated: 2, 74) | exit 0 | 0, 74 | 0 | 2, 74 | | pyrho | 0, 22 | `inbox` exit 2, untouched | warns; 2, 22 | 0, 22 | 1: pyrho-2-1 → exit 0 | 2, 23 | ```text keeper ▸ bs inbox --as queen-bees bs inbox: …/bees.db has 8 open spawns the old bs started, which this bs can neither ring nor see run: bees-13-2, bees-13-3, bees-13-4, bees-13-5, bees-13-6, bees-13-7, bees-13-8, bees-13-9; nothing was read or written next: bs end for each (it names the herdr workspace to close by hand), then run this again keeper ▸ bs end --as queen-bees bees-13-9 bs end: warning: bees-13-9 was started by the old bs, which recorded no process, so bs can't prove herdr workspace w1ZJ (session default) is still its own: left open; close it yourself if it is (herdr workspace close w1ZJ) ended bees-13-9 ``` 16 old sessions across four logbooks (the bead's "9" was this morning's count; the bees-13 fleet has grown since). Every row survived the migration; each `bs end` added one `ended` row, and `bs inbox` its receipts. The stub logged 48 herdr calls, every one `pane process-info`, none that could close or start anything. Verdict: pass, on build 71a92c0 (the reviewer reproduced it on fresh copies at 71a92c0). Two messages read wrong in this run and are fixed: `bs status` now says an old session was "started by the old bs" rather than "never confirmed", and the refusal's `next:` no longer claims `bs end` closes the workspace. ## Live test Run with the `live-test` skill: each toy on its own `herdr --session`, real Claude queen and workers on this build (the queen through her PATH, workers through `worker.path`), torn down w

body:
Requested for the semantic-macro check in gha#1162, which reads "deprecated, use \x" entries from `interpretations.tsv`. Ezra also flagged `\hcoef` in his review of lds#1274 and asked for the semantic form.

## What changes

- Every `h`-prefixed macro that has an `e`-prefixed counterpart now ends its `interpretations.tsv` row with `; deprecated, use \<replacement>`, in the format `\truemeanfn` already uses. `\hcoef` is "deprecated, use \ecoef". 191 rows are newly marked, and 193 carry the marker, since `\truemeanfn` and `\truemeanfnf` already did.
- A pair is marked only when the two definitions in `macros.qmd` match after replacing `\hat` and `\widehat` by `\est` or `\Est` and each `\hX` by `\eX`. A script checked every name-matched pair this way, and the rows were marked from that list.
- The operator and call forms with hats already had `e` forms in `macros.qmd` (`\eset`, `\eSE`, `\evar`, `\eVar`, `\eSD`, `\eATT`, `\eRD`, `\eRR`, `\edifflogodds` and others), so no new macro is needed. Their `h` forms are marked too.
- Added by hand: `\hSEf` and `\HSE` to `\eSEf`, `\hcovf` to `\ecovf`, and `\varht` to `\evar`.
- Not marked here: `\hf` and `\hfx`, which print f̂ while `\epredfn` prints ĝ; macros#280 resolves that. Also unmarked: `\Ehat`, the Hessian family, and `\hatmat`, which are not estimate hats.
- `notation-choices.qmd` says the `h` macros are deprecated, where the marking lives, and records the decision (2026-10-22).
- No macro definition changes, so printed output is unchanged. Checked: no duplicate keys in `interpretations.tsv`, no row without a tab, and the CI build passes.

The counts above are from `git diff origin/main -- interpretations.tsv` on the current head.

author: abrarui12
body:
## Task
Follow-up from C1 (#55's "Risks"): enforce `model_policies.max_external_classification` (plan §25.2). Small and security-relevant. Reviewer: Codex.

## What changed
- `PolicyView` carries `max_external_classification`. The DB default and the default with no policy row are both `internal`.
- `query.prepare` checks the packed evidence against that limit whenever the generator can reach an external model (`provider.is_external`, which the gateway reports conservatively across permitted fallbacks):
  - evidence from documents classified above the limit is removed **before** generation;
  - unknown classifications are withheld (fail closed);
  - withheld chunks are no longer marked `selected_for_context`;
  - the run records `evidence_withheld_external`, and an answer from the remaining evidence is `partial`.
- If everything is withheld, the answer is an abstention (`no_evidence`): an external model never receives restricted text.

## Tests
- `test_external_models_never_see_evidence_above_the_policy_limit`:
  - an external model and a confidential source, no policy row → withheld, abstains, run flagged;
  - with a KB policy allowing `confidential` → answered.
- Query suites: 22 passed. ruff and mypy are clean.

## Note for staging
The demo corpus is mostly `internal`, so Groq still answers it. Confidential or restricted demo documents (e.g. the HR compensation bands) are withheld from Groq unless a KB policy raises the limit, which is the intended behaviour.

Search engines read the canonical on both pages; cleaner social previews.

Revert this PR.

author: fermin03
body:
## Qué cambia

El checkout de la tienda en línea (después de «Ver pedido» → «Continuar») se reordena:

1. **Pantalla completa.** «Ver pedido» sigue siendo una hoja; con «Continuar», el checkout ocupa toda la pantalla (en escritorio, una columna centrada) y el botón queda abajo del todo.
2. **Una sola pantalla, «Finalizar pedido».** Una barra arriba (‹ y título al centro) en vez de dos franjas. Datos, entrega, **resumen del pedido con la cuenta** (productos plegables, subtotal, envío, propina, total) y **¿Cómo pagas?** (con la propina si es en línea) van juntos, separados por franjas. Al pagar en línea sigue solo la pantalla de la tarjeta; la pregunta de la propina sale una vez al ir a pagar, como antes.
3. **Filas con icono.** Dirección / «Recoges en…», tus datos y nota son filas que dicen lo capturado o lo que falta; cada una abre su subpantalla con «Listo», que revisa solo lo suyo. Un dato por corregir (al enviar o rechazado por el servidor) abre la subpantalla que lo tiene, con el foco en el campo.

Lógica: `lib/pasos.ts` pasa de `datos → pago → tarjeta` a `datos → tarjeta` (el pago vive en `datos`); pruebas actualizadas. `Hoja` gana `completa` y deja de llamar `alCerrar` cuando la cierra el propio estado.

## Cómo se probó

- `tsc --noEmit` y `vitest` de `apps/tienda`: 546 pruebas en verde.
- En local con una función `tienda` falsa (datos de prueba del repo), celular y escritorio: recoger y domicilio, enviar con datos vacíos (abre la subpantalla con errores), «Listo», nota, pago en línea → pregunta de propina → pantalla de tarjeta.

## Sin verificar

- iPhone real (teclado de iOS en las subpantallas).
- Cuenta con direcciones guardadas y mapa del envío por distancia.
- Un pedido real de punta a punta.
- A domicilio «por zonas» sin colonia, el resumen muestra «—» en subtotal/total (antes no había resumen aquí; el carrito sí muestra el estimado).

Textos provisionales para James: «Finalizar pedido», «Agrega tus datos», «Para calcular el envío», «Revisa tu dirección», «Dirección de entrega», «Con tu dirección», nota de ejemplo.

body:
#434(fix/home-pull-feedback) 위에 쌓음. #434가 먼저 머지되어야 한다. 이 PR의 자기 커밋은 de414b0·89b83af·fc6aaaa·8bf8fed다. 두 PR이 같은 `refresh()`를 고치기 때문에 origin/main 기점으로는 충돌이 확정이라 쌓았다.

- 결정: vault `decisions/2026-10-23-home-latest-hide-seen.md`(사용자 B, kurl 글 포함)
- 계약: `~/Documents/kurl-ai-local/home-hide-seen/contract.md`(백엔드 D1~D4 a)
- 서버보다 먼저 나가도 안전하다(계약 8절). 옛 서버는 `seen=hide`와 `kurl:` 키를 조용히 무시하므로 지금과 같다.

## 요청
- 홈 최신 `/public/home?tab=latest`의 첫 페이지·다음 페이지·since에 `seen=hide`와 `X-Kurl-Device`를 붙인다(`HomeFeedTab.query`·`headers`, `hidesSeen`은 최신만).
- 홈에 섞는 맞춤은 `FederationAPI.homeStream` → `/federation/for-you?seen=hide`로 부른다. `HomeFeedViewModel`의 기본 로더다.
- 팔로잉·인기·둘러보기 다른 서버는 파라미터 없이 그대로다(테스트로 단언).
- 커서(`h…`·`f…`)는 받은 그대로 돌려준다.

## 노출 (홈 최신만)
- 행이 화면에 나타나는 순간 바로 보낸다. 기준은 `onScrollVisibilityChange(threshold: 0)`, 타이머 없음, 앱 활성 + 홈 탭 + 스택 맨 위다.
- 보내는 키(`HomeMix.Row.seenKey`)
  - kurl 노트: `kurl:note:{id}`
  - 블로그 글: `kurl:post:{id}`
  - 섞인 다른 서버 글: uri
- 기존 노출 묶음에 그대로 싣는다: 20개·10초·백그라운드, 세션 안 중복 제거, 실패 한 번 더, 대기열 200.
- 섞인 다른 서버 행은 체류만 기존 0.5 기준으로 재고, 노출 표시는 이 경로로만 한다(`RemoteStreamRow(marksSeen: false)`).
- 둘러보기 다른 서버는 50%·1초 그대로다.
- 당기기와 30분 복귀 전체 다시 받기 전에는 대기 중인 묶음을 먼저 보내고 응답을 기다린다(`flushSeen`). 서버 버퍼가 조회에 보이므로 방금 본 글이 빠진다. 팔로잉 당기기는 기다리지 않는다.
- 지금 화면의 행은 지우지 않는다. 다음 불러오기부터 서버가 뺀다.

## 당겨서 새로고침 = 본 글을 빼고 처음부터 (fc6aaaa, 8bf8fed)
결정: vault `decisions/2026-10-23-home-pull-reloads-unseen.md`. 오전의 `home-pull-adds-only-new`(#434의 위에 붙이기)를 대체한다. 사용자 보고는 둘이었다. "kurl 글을 보고 새로고침했는데 또 똑같이 나온다", "늘 새 글이 없다고 나온다".
- **당기기(홈 최신)**
  - 대기 중인 본 글 묶음을 보내고 기다린다.
  - `seen=hide`로 내 피드 첫 페이지와 홈 맞춤 첫 페이지를 처음부터 다시 받는다.
  - `HomeMix` 5:2로 새로 배치한다.
- 30분 복귀와 콜드 로드도 같은 `restart` 경로다. 복귀와 콜드는 알리지 않는다.
- **알림**(#434의 `PullOutcome` 한 곳 규칙)
  - 직전에 없던 행 id가 생기면 토스트 없음
  - 결과가 비면 토스트 없이 끝 줄 "다 봤어요"
  - 내 피드가 실패하면 "새로고침하지 못했습니다"
  - 같은 행이거나 본 글만 빠졌으면 "새 글이 없어요"
  - 맞춤만 실패하면 내 피드 결과로 판단한다.
  - 서버 #890 배포 전에는 `seen=hide`가 무시돼 같은 글이 다시 오므로 "새 글이 없어요"가 맞다.
- **없앤 것**: 위에 올린 행 슬롯(`HomeMix.Slot`·`block`·`rows(top:)`), 맞춤 `fresh(since:)`·`prepend`, 작성 시각 필터(`RemoteStreamItem.createdAt`), `pulledAt`.
- `RemoteStreamModel.reload(announcesFailure:)`: 당기기 경로에서는 맞춤 실패를 스스로 알리지 않는다(이중 토스트 방지). 둘러보기는 그대로다.
- 팔로잉 당기기는 그대로 newer로 위에 붙이고, flush를 기다리지 않는다. `HomeFeedRefreshTests`의 위에 붙이기 테스트는 팔로잉으로 옮겼다.
- **테스트**
  - flush → load 순서와 두 첫 페이지 다시 받기
  - 같은 행 → "새 글이 없어요"
  - 본 글이 빠지고 새 글 → 새 배치, 토스트 없음
  - 본 글만 빠짐 → "새 글이 없어요"
  - 빈 응답 → 토스트 없음(끝 줄)
  - 내 피드 실패 → 목록 유지 + "새로고침하지 못했습니다"
  - 맞춤만 실패 → "새 글이 없어요"
  - 팔로잉은 newer만, flush 없음
  - 30분 복귀 → flush 뒤 조용히 다시 받기
- **A/B**: 아래 넷을 되돌리자 테스트 4개가 실패했고, 복원하자 통과했다.
  - flush 빼기
  - 빈 결과도 알리기
  - 실패를 성공으로
  - 새 행 수 0으로

## 첫 페이지 캐시 (#431과의 접점)
- `HomeSeenLog`는 표시한 키를 기록한다. UserDefaults에 두고, 14일 보관, 3,000개 상한(넘으면 오래된 것부터 버림)이다. 쓰기는 2초씩 묶고, 백그라운드로 갈 때 저장한다.
- 콜드 런치 때 캐시된 홈 최신 첫 페이지에서 로컬로 본 글을 빼고 그린다. 그러지 않으면 지난번에 본 글이 열 때 한 번 다시 보인다.
- 내 글(`author.id == me.id`)은 빼지 않는다. 서버도 빼지 않는다.
- 캐시 저장(`HomeFeedCache.store`)은 바꾸지 않았다. 거르기는 읽어서 그릴 때만 한다(`reloadOwn`).
- **계정·기기 분리와 로그아웃(89b83af, #425 정리 규칙)**
  - 저장 키는 `homeSeenLog.user.<id>`와 `homeSeenLog.device`다.
  - 보는 사람이 바뀌면(로그인·로그아웃·계정 전환) 그 사람의 기록으로 바꿔 읽는다. 기기 기록과 계정 기록이 섞이지 않는다.
  - 명시 로그아웃(`signOut`)은 모든 계정 기록을 지우고 기기 기록은 남긴다.
  - 세션 만료는 지우지 않는다. 같은 계정이 다시 들어오면 그대로 쓰고, 다른 계정에는 키가 달라 보이지 않는다.

## 끝: "다 봤어요"
- 홈 최신에서 내 피드와 맞춤이 모두 `next == nil`이면, 목록 끝에 기존 빈 상태 문법(FeedPlaceholder)으로 "다 봤어요" + "팔로잉 보기"를 둔다.
  - "팔로잉 보기"는 팔로잉 탭으로 바꾼다. 비로그인이면 팔로잉 탭이 자기 로그인 안내를 보여 준다.
- 목록이 비면 "아직 노트와 글이 없어요" 대신 같은 줄을 보인다(최신만, 인기는 그대로).
- 새 키 둘(en/ja/vi/hi), 파일 끝에 추가만 했다.
  - "다 봤어요": You're all caught up / すべて見ました / Bạn đã xem hết / आपने सब देख लिया
  - "팔로잉 보기": See Following / フォロー中を見る / Xem Đang theo dõi / फ़ॉलोइंग देखें
- 홈에는 "이미 본 글" 구분선이 나오지 않는다(`seenFrom`이 안 온다).

## 목 서버
- `/public/home`(`--short-latest`)과 `/federation/for-you`가 `seen=hide`를 따른다.
- 맞춤 목은 본 시각과 커서의 asOf를 비교한다. 그래서 스크롤 중에 새로 본 글이 다음 페이지를 흔들지 않는다(서버 계약 6·7절과 같은 성질).

## 검증
- 단위 테스트(`HomeRemoteTailTests`·`RemoteSeenTests`·`RemoteTrendingTests` 65개 통과)
  - 요청 계약: 홈 최신 첫 페이지·h 커서·since에 `seen=hide`·`tab=latest`·기기 헤더. 인기는 없음. 홈 맞춤은 `seen=hide`, 둘러보기 맞춤은 없음. 커서는 원문 그대로.
  - 최신 당기기는 flush → newer 순서. 팔로잉은 flush 안 함. 30분 복귀는 flush 뒤 다시 받기.
  - 캐시 첫 페이지 거르기는 최신만(팔로잉은 그대로).
  - 행 키: `kurl:post:`·`kurl:note:`·uri.
  - `HomeSeenLog`: 14일 경계, 재시작 뒤 읽기, 상한 넘으면 오래된 것부터, 계정 7·기기·계정 8이 서로 안 보임.
  - `LogoutWipeTests`: signOut이 계정 기록(7·8)을 지우고 기기 기록은 남김.
- **A/B**: 아래 다섯을 되돌리자 해당 테스트 7개가 실패했고, 복원하자 통과했다.
  - 홈 최신 `seen=hide` 빼기
  - 홈 맞춤 `hidingSeen` 끄기
  - 당기기 전 flush 빼기
  - 캐시 거르기 빼기
  - 14일 경계 `<`→`<=`
- **A/B(89b83af)**: 아래 둘을 되돌리자 `RemoteSeenTests`·`LogoutWipeTests`에서 6개가 실패했고, 복원하자 통과했다. 두 변경을 한 빌드에서 같이 되돌렸다.
  - 계정 키를 기기 키로 합치기
  - signOut의 `wipeAccounts()` 빼기
- 전체 kurlTests: 8bf8fed를 XCTest 주입(`--screen editor2`)으로 돌려 711개, 실패 0이다. 위에 붙이기 테스트를 지워 수가 줄었다. 89b83af는 720개, de414b0은 718개였고 둘 다 실패 0이다.
- UI 테스트 `HomeRemoteTailUITests.testSeenOtherServerPostsStayOutOfHomeAndTheEndSaysAllSeen`(옛 "본 글은 구분선 아래" 테스트를 바꿈): 본 다른 서버 글이 홈에 없고, 안 본 글은 있고, 끝에 "다 봤어요" 버튼이 있고, 구분선이 없음을 확인한다. 이 맥에서는 XCUITest 러너가 연결 전에 멈춰 돌리지 못해 CI가 처음 돌린다.
- 캡처(`~/Documents/kurl-ai-local/home-hide-seen/ios/shots/`, 목, 끝으로 스크롤한 장면은 커밋하지 않은 캡처 전용 훅): 본 맞춤 글(mina·hana)이 빠지고 목록 끝에 "다 봤어요 / 팔로잉 보기"가 보인다(라이트·다크).
- pre-push 훅이 "The test runner hung before establishing connection"으로 0개 실행에서 멈췄다. 상시 허용 조건을 충족해 `--no-verify`로 푸시했다.
- SwiftLint 래칫 통과.

Não muda chave, carteira, teto financeiro, nonce ou envio. Não executa deploy pago nem broadcast. Qualquer transação continua exigindo prova completa de resultado líquido no contrato e autorizações operacionais. O Railway continua em modo observação até configuração independente e revisão de credenciais/segurança.

author: jovanoviclazar
body:
#### Description

Adds `GoemansWilliamsonSolver`, a randomized approximation algorithm for Max-Cut based on a semidefinite relaxation.

The relaxation is solved with Clarabel.cpp and its solution is factored by an eigendecomposition into one unit vector per vertex. The vertices are then split by a single random hyperplane, whose normal vector has Gaussian components drawn from the provided seed.

Limitation: the relaxation is built as a dense semidefinite program, so memory grows quickly with the number of vertices. It is practical up to roughly 100 vertices, and much larger instances abort with an allocation failure.

Tests (Catch2):
- Determinism: verifies identical cut cost produced when executed with a fixed seed
- Standard graph structures: single edge, path, bipartite even cycle (C4), complete graph (K4), and empty graph with no edges
- Seed sensitivity: verifies variation in cut cost across multiple distinct random seeds on a weighted odd cycle (C5)

## Summary

Expanded visible tools reuse complete retained details or load their missing body through the exact connection's serialized lane. Validated data needs a separate matching completion; failures offer Retry and offline missing details remain distinct from empty contents. The latest repair lets a current presentation withdraw collapsed or offscreen targets while its Loading frame is held. Stale snapshots can only remove already admitted exact targets; additions and Retry still require current ownership and snapshot identity. Compact-v1 remains unadvertised.

Closes #2388

## Testing

Linux candidate: `13d265b8e46dc4bdf1de605c5b77371129fad8be`. The other OS is outside this ticket's verification scope.

Each class ran separately with `python3 scripts/gradle-gate.py testDebugUnitTest --tests <qualified-class> --console=plain`, exit 0. Fresh XML: **74 executed, 74 passed, 0 failures/errors/skips**. Names share the prefix `de.pyryco.mobile.`.

| Class | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `data.repository.ToolBodyQueriesTest` | 16 |
| `data.repository.AuthoritativeThreadQueriesTest` | 23 |
| `e2e.InitialAttentionQueryTest` | 11 |
| `ui.conversations.thread.MissingToolBodyScreenTest` | 3 |
| `ui.conversations.thread.NegotiatedThreadViewModelTest` | 6 |
| `ui.conversations.thread.AuthoritativeReadSightTest` | 12 |
| `ui.conversations.thread.DeferredAuthoritativeScreenTest` | 3 |

Test-first against production `22bbfc6272ebad0a6cb8a4c43266598365fdb861`: **2 executed, 2 failed, 0 errors/skips**. The mounted queued-collapse probe timed out waiting for B's demand to clear; the lane probe found B still Loading. Both now pass without weakening existing assertions. The mounted test also completes A, observes the next catch-up entering the lane, and verifies B never starts or enriches and no read sight is certified. The lane probe rejects stale additions and Retry.

- `python3 scripts/gradle-gate.py spotlessApply lint assembleDebug compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin --console=plain`: passed, exit 0.
- `python3 scripts/android-test-gate.py scripted tool`: passed, exit 0; **1 executed, 1 passed, 0 failures/errors/skips**, `de.pyryco.mobile.e2e.DeterministicInteractiveStreamE2ETest#interactiveTurn_seededChannel_toolStepRunsThenCompletes`. The device phases reached `finished` and the harness exited successfully.
- Final `python3 scripts/gradle-gate.py assembleDebug --console=plain` and `python3 scripts/pre-verify.py --gradle --body-file /tmp/builder-2388/pr.md`: passed, exit 0 after the final main merge check and push. Forced Spotless reruns, all Kotlin compilation and every static/security/body check passed.

Fresh private evidence: `/work/Projects/pyrycode-mobile-agents/logs/evidence/2388/builder-rework2-13d265b8e/`. All **30** manifest entries verified: red/green XML, original phone log, native phases and normalized XML, repair patch, source identities and isolated daemon/relay diagnostics. The native harness also retained `/work/Projects/pyrycode-mobile-agents/logs/evidence/2388/harness/fault-84060e860bcacac95edbf24cd1f999b7/`; all four checksums verified. JVM checks ran on the candidate working tree before commit; per-class metadata records its HEAD base and the evidence identifies the pushed candidate.

Scripted producer: Core `2c68b595440dd7e8e843af9cff0d9a708bcc81a7`, binary SHA-256 `d93c56662d0072e8aec9d1466bee3f6845f7cdc55247273f177b48b209bdb6ac`; Relay `9939bc1ff8afec5021c09862e6f14dadba33ad42`, unmodified binary SHA-256 `27ec11505393dd62fad8c9a2cb672775b230e031b7240ac9c11fddc847324d10`.

Earlier evidence remains preserved: **146 executed/passed** at `22bbfc627` in `builder-rework-20261022-22bbfc627/`, including decoder, fragmentation and tool-row coverage; its original red probes had **22 executed, 17 passed, 5 failed**. The initial **132-pass** proof remains in `builder-20261022-d37187df1/`, under the same persistent `logs/evidence/2388/` directory. Existing Tool use layout and interaction assertions remain intact; the latest repair changes no layout or styling.

Complete configured acceptance remains dispatcher-owned and incomplete after the inherited scripts failure tracked in #2481. The inherited reply-suggestion flake remains tracked in #2436. Genuine paired compact capture/replay remains pending in #2393 before #2376 integrated acceptance. Historical failures and approval/privacy holds remain in force.

## Invariant probes

- Exact ownership: `ownershipInvariantEveryCaptureFieldAndCorrelationMustMatch`, `ownershipInvariantChangedRevisionEpochDeletionAndForeignHostCannotEnrich` and `connectionIdentityCollisionCannotAdmitARetiredOwnersLateBody` retain owner/revision/correlation fencing.
- Separate completion and certification: `completionInvariantDataIsStagedAndOnlyMatchingMarkerEnrichesWithoutCoverage`, `fragmentedProductionLaneStagesTheCompleteRendererUntilItsSeparateMarker` and the mounted screen probes preserve data/marker separation and withhold false sight; the earlier decoder evidence retains kind-free fragment and unsigned-token checks.
- Source facts and placement: `fetchedBodyExpansionPreservesLiveOptionalNullClears` and the completion probe preserve the held DTOs, identity, ordering, metadata and coverage.
- Current demand: `collapsedQueuedBodyWithdrawsDemandBeforeLoadingPresentationArrives` and `staleSnapshotWithdrawsQueuedDemandWithoutAdmittingAdditionsOrRetry` cover partial withdrawal; existing coalescing, multi-consumer, lifecycle, failure, cancellation and drain probes all remain green in the affected classes.

## Documentation handoff

Pending documentation stage: update relevant demand, retention and query sections of `docs/knowledge/features/thread-screen.md` and `docs/knowledge/features/remote-conversation-repository.md` for missing-body demand, retained reuse, separate completion and Loading/Retry/offline states. Explain that current consumers may withdraw demand while presentation frames are held, while additions and Retry require the current snapshot. Fetched bodies are retained in memory; existing complete-fact persistence keeps its contract. Supply counted evidence and source identities to #2376's original handoff; documentation does not produce missing evidence. Preserve #2393's paired-evidence requirement and historical holds.

## Lessons learned

Presentation freshness governs admission, while a current consumer must be able to withdraw part of its demand immediately. Holding the Loading frame while collapsing one of two demanded tools exposes a leak that empty-demand cleanup alone cannot cover.

author: migwynkriid13
body:
Updating the game from 0.110.0 to 0.112.0 prevents startup with `Cannot uniquely locate a compatible native unit creator after this game update`. The creator ABI is still compatible, but the mod's signatures require unrelated native Game-field and stack-local offsets to stay fixed. Scaling setup is also mandatory, so this optional visual feature currently blocks otherwise compatible crab replacement.

## Changes

- Ignore exactly 13 reviewed displacement bytes: the creator's internal Game level member, guardian's position stack local, and guardian/ordinary post-call Game clock members. The DLL never reads these offsets; original native code still uses its own current layout. Keep opcodes, registers, argument slots, prologues, scale-field anchors, unique matches, native boundaries and all four caller-target checks intact. Zero both signature and mask bytes for wildcard positions.
- Separate scaling preparation from the required asset path. Discover/validate both scaling functions and every caller, and prepare both trampolines before writing any hook. If preparation fails, log the reason and enable only independently validated crab asset hooks at the game's original sizes. Preserve 4× bosses/guardians and 2× regular mobs when scaling is compatible.
- Keep hook-write failures fatal: the fallback never continues after a partial installation. Free the prepared creator trampoline if appearance trampoline preparation fails.
- Update regressions, compatibility evidence, troubleshooting and release notes. There is still no EXE hash/version gate or runtime fixed address.

## Evidence and validation

The new installed target is 0.112.0, SHA-256 `dc10453398ceb398076f6d3b6ac7859470de2ff7ccd68ac1d00a02f9f1e5209a`. The old creator pattern has zero matches because its Game member changed `+0x4e8 → +0x4e0`; guardian local position moved `[rbp+0x18] → [rbp+0x20]`; guardian and ordinary post-call clock member changed `+0xa54 → +0xa4c`. Asset reader/availability/allocator signatures remain unique.

Whole-owner comparison confirms unchanged 3,442-byte creator and 520-byte appearance publisher extents, argument capture, prologues and scale encoding; non-relocation differences are native Game member displacements. Current creator is `14593c570..14593d2e2`, updater `145951ab0..145951cb8`; role calls are guardian `145906c44`, ward `145916255`, boss `14593b3eb`, ordinary `14593e2cb`. These are provenance coordinates, not runtime selectors.

- All **25 Python checks pass**, including six authored old/new operand cases and eleven ABI/opcode mutation rejections.
- Independent read-only verification against the installed 0.112.0 EXE passes both unique entries, complete position-independent prologues, declared function boundaries, both internal scale anchors, four unique caller contexts with correct targets, and absence of other direct creator callers.
- Independent source review found no actionable defects in the fallback boundary, partial-write behavior, cleanup or revised masks.
- `git diff --check` passes.

No local compilation, game launch, installation or rendered validation was performed. Build/release remains main-only after merge. The installed DLL has not been replaced by this PR.

author: chrisschneider
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Follow-up to #1113. Replaces all remaining direct `json.loads` / `json.dumps` call sites across 17 files with `orjson`. Covers extension code (bdba, trivy, codeql, crypto, sbom), shared utilities (k8s/logging, rescore, scanner_utils, deliverydb_cache), and client libraries (delivery, odg_client). Key changes: `orjson.dumps()` returns `bytes` — file writes converted to binary mode, gzip encode paths avoid a redundant `bytes→str→bytes` round-trip, and `orjson.OPT_INDENT_2` replaces `indent=2`.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
- `dict_to_json_factory` intentionally retains `.decode('utf-8')` — used as an aiohttp `dumps=` callback which requires `str`
- `dockerutil.py`, `sbom_generator.py`, and `trivy_extension/scanner.py` file writes converted to binary mode (`'wb'`) to match orjson's `bytes` output
- `delivery/util.py` and `odg_client/util.py` `encode_request`: `orjson.dumps(json)` stays as `bytes` and hits the `isinstance(obj, bytes): return obj` branch in `_encode` directly, eliminating the prior `bytes→str→bytes` round-trip
- `scanner_utils/orchestrator.py` has a pre-existing Python 2 comma-style `except` clause (not introduced here)

**Release note**:
```improvement operator
Performance improvement: Replace stdlib json with orjson at all remaining call sites, incl. extensions & utils
```

body: ## Summary Version `0.1.304`. Two cleanups. Top Nav no longer turns a folded dropdown into a disclosure. A collapsing button group no longer clones a child or styles another component's internals. ## Top Nav The bar stays a generic container. It moves nodes into the phone panel and back. A nested `Button::Dropdown` opens its own menu on `document.body`. `data-flat-pack-top-nav-disclosure` is removed. That hook was a host integration signal. `data-flat-pack-top-nav-expanded` is removed with it. There is no compatibility shim. Removed from `top_nav_controller.js`: `prepareDisclosures`, `setDisclosure`, `collapseDisclosures`, `restoreDisclosures`, `writeAttribute`, the capture-phase click, and the disclosure menu id and role rewrite. Removed from `application.css`: the disclosure block, and the unlayered `.fp-top-nav [data-flat-pack-top-nav-section="center"] input { min-width: 0 }` rule. The center section still has `min-w-0`. Kept: `collapseIntoMenu`, the panel, `mobile_menu:`, `mobile_breakpoint:`, `always_display:`, and node restore. The open panel measures its vertical offset the same way it measures the horizontal one. ## Button group `collapse: :menu` still shows a joined row on a wide viewport and one hamburger on a phone. The wide row and the phone menu are separate elements. The contract is `menu_row`. It returns HTML. - `Button::Component#menu_row` is a plain left-aligned row from the label, href, and icon. `style: :danger` is red text, not a red fill. The wide control keeps `id` and button chrome. `menu_row` does not repeat `id`. - `Button::Dropdown#menu_row` renders that dropdown as `Menu::Collapse` (label and icon as the header, items underneath). The wide row is still the floating dropdown. - `PublishableQuickActionsComponent` implements the same method on the button `call` rendered. - A child with no `menu_row`, or whose `menu_row` is not HTML, is rendered once and that HTML is placed in the row and again in the menu. It keeps its own chrome. The group only paints how direct children sit together. A dropdown joins when it is that direct child: its root is the segment, and its trigger copies that box. A wrapper around a dropdown is a different child. The group does not restyle the trigger inside it. ## Deleted - Duck-typing `menu_rows` and `trigger_label`, and the cloned `Menu::Collapse` next to the real dropdown - `.fp-button-group-menu__choice`, `__dropdown`, and `__inline` - `dropdown_trigger_css` and the phone and plain-group rules that styled `[data-flat-pack--button-dropdown-target="trigger"]` - `pointerInChildMenu` in `button_group_menu_controller.js` - `data-flat-pack-dropdown-owner`, and the dropdown id that existed only to stamp it ## Screenshots Device pixel ratio 2. author: btcforplebs
body:
Logen's own note (iPhone 18 Pro, integrate e558cb31) showed "Couldn't reach the owner's vault" almost at once while the web loaded the same photo over FIPS.

**Cause** (his relay.log, 22:05): the engine started at 22:05:24.43 and the first mesh read went out the same millisecond; the route to his vault was only found at 22:05:25.61. That first connection was reset, and `MeshMediaRouter.read` treated one failed GET as "unreachable": it gave up at once and blocked the vault for 30 s. The web's blob-get retries a refused/dropped stream every 1 s for up to 45 s.

**Fix** (`MeshMediaRouter.swift` only):
- A refused or dropped read redials and retries every 1 s until 45 s (web `RETRY_MS` / `READ_TIMEOUT_MS`); only then the 30 s back-off.
- A cancelled read (photo off screen) stops at once and leaves the vault standing.
- A missing 10063 is asked again after 60 s (web `LIST_RETRY_MS`), not 5 min.

**Tests**: `testAConnectionResetBeforeTheRouteIsUpIsTriedAgainAndLoads` + give-up/back-off + cancel tests, all red on the old code (mutation-checked). MediaLogic 1369/1369, iOS build green at 3c64ef0d2. No device install.

author: jmsuzuki
body:
**Requirements** - [x] I have added test coverage for new or changed functionality - [x] I have followed the repository's [pull request submission guidelines](../blob/v7/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-pull-requests) - [x] I have validated my changes against all supported platform versions **Related issues** - FD-6411: data race under `-race` in an internal integration test that uses a hooked SDK client - SEC-8756: the same unsynchronized environment-ID field, filed as a security finding **The race** The environment ID is stored in a plain `ldvalue.OptionalString` field with no synchronization: - FDv1: `DataSourceUpdateSinkImpl.environmentID` - FDv2: `datasystem.environmentIDProvider.environmentID` Readers and writers run on different goroutines: - **Read:** the hook runner calls `GetEnvironmentID()` on the caller's goroutine for every `*Variation*` call (`prepareEvaluationSeries`) and every `Track*` call (`RunTrack`). This only happens when the client has at least one hook, for example `ldotel.NewTracingHook`. - **Write:** the data source goroutine calls `SetEnvironmentID()`: - FDv1 streaming: on every `put` event - FDv1 polling: on every poll that isn't cached - FDv2: on the initializer basis and on every synchronizer result that carries an environment ID The first FDv1 `put` happens before `MakeClient` returns, because the ready channel closes after the write. Every later `put`, on the same connection or after a reconnect, is unordered relative to evaluations. So any hooked client that receives a second `put` races. The field has had no lock since environment ID support was added in #291, and it is unsynchronized in every release up to v7.20.0. **Production impact** In practice the race is benign: each write stores the same environment ID, and the field is two words that are written rarely. But it is undefined behavior under the Go memory model, and it makes `-race` test runs of applications that use hooks flaky. FDv2 clients are hit hardest, because they write on every synchronizer result that carries an environment ID. LaunchDarkly's own services hit this in integration CI (2 of roughly 450 jobs), with these frames: ``` Read: (*DataSourceUpdateSinkImpl).GetEnvironmentID <- (*hooks.Runner).prepareEvaluationSeries Write: (*DataSourceUpdateSinkImpl).SetEnvironmentID <- (*StreamProcessor).consumeStream ``` **Describe the solution you've provided** - Add a dedicated `sync.RWMutex` around the environment ID in `DataSourceUpdateSinkImpl` and in the FDv2 `environmentIDProvider`. The FDv2 provider's `GetEnvironmentID` moves to a pointer receiver; every caller already holds a `*environmentIDProvider`. - The new lock is separate from the sink's existing status `lock`, so evaluations never wait on store updates or status changes. Reads take an uncontended `RLock`. - Add two regression tests, `TestDataSourceUpdateSinkImplEnvironmentIDConcurrentAccess` and `TestEnvironmentIDProviderConcurrentAccess`. Each one runs a setter and a getter concurrently. **Repro and verification** To reproduce end to end, a local SSE server sends a `put`, then 20 more `put`s on the same connection, while 4 goroutines call `StringVariationCtx` on a client with a no-op hook. The repro test is below; it is not included in this PR. The race detector reports each unique pair of racing code locations only once per process. So each failure rate below comes from separate test-binary processes, not from `-count=N`. | Test | Without fix | With fix | | --- | --- | --- | | `TestDataSourceUpdateSinkImplEnvironmentIDConcurrentAccess` | 50/50 processes fail (`DATA RACE`) | 0/50 fail | | `TestEnvironmentIDProviderConcurrentAccess` | 50/50 processes fail (`DATA RACE`) | 0/50 fail | | End-to-end streaming `put` repro | 20/20 processes fail, with the frames above | 0/50 fail | I also ran these checks with the fix: - `go test -race -count=50` on both regression tests passes. - `go test -race ./...`, the `proxytest1`/`proxytest2` tag runs, `ldotel`, and `ldmiddleware` all pass. - `golangci-lint` v2.14.0 reports 0 issues.
End-to-end repro test ```go func TestEnvIDRace(t *testing.T) { secondPut := make(chan struct{}) srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream") w.Header().Set("X-Ld-Envid", "env-123") w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) fl := w.(http.Flusher) fmt.Fprintf(w, "event: put\ndata: %s\n\n", putData) fl.Flush() <-secondPut for range 20 { fmt.Fprintf(w, "event: put\ndata: %s\n\n", putData) fl.Flush() time.Sleep(time.Millisecond) } <-r.Context().Done() })) defer srv.Close() cfg := ld.Config{ DataSource: ldcomponents.StreamingDataSource(), Events: ldcomponents.NoEvents(), Logging: ldcomponents.Logging().Loggers(ldlog.NewDisabledLoggers()), ServiceEndpoints: interfaces.ServiceEndpoints{Streaming: srv.URL, Polling: srv.URL, Events: srv.URL}, Hooks: []ldhooks.Hook{noopHook{}}, } client, err := ld.MakeCustomClient("sdk-key", cfg, 5*time.Second) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } defer client.Close() var wg sync.WaitGroup for range 4 { wg.Go(func() { for range 2000 { _, _ = client.StringVariationCtx(context.Background(), "f", ldcontext.New("u"), "x") } }) } close(secondPut) wg.Wait() } ```
**Describe alternatives you've considered** - **Reuse the sink's existing `lock`:** that would make every hooked evaluation contend with store updates and status changes. A separate `RWMutex` keeps reads cheap. - **`atomic.Pointer[ldvalue.OptionalString]`:** it would also work, but it allocates on every set and doesn't match how this package guards its other state. - **Work around it in applications:** dropping hooks loses tracing data. Wrapping the data source loses stream diagnostics, and it can't reach the FDv2 write at all. **Additional context** The fix is internal only. It changes no public API or behavior.

author: nizovtsevnv
body:
## Summary

An `if` in value position already has a type recorded by sema. That type is the **context** of its branches — the reading #966 took for `unchecked`, and D6 takes for types generally.

```diff
 ib_bx_if := fn(bp, a, e, c, t, x) -> Option(VRegId) {
   k := ib_ty(bp, e)?            # the `if`'s own recorded type
   ...
-  tv0 := ib_bx(bp, a, t)?      # asks the branch its OWN type
+  tv0 := ib_value_ctx(bp, a, t, k)?   # gives it the `if`'s type
   tv := ib_coerce(bp, a, tv0, k, t)?
   ...
-  xv0 := ib_bx(bp, a, x)?
+  xv0 := ib_value_ctx(bp, a, x, k)?
```

A bare literal branch (`else { 1000 }`) has no type of its own — `VcLit`, no context reached it — so
`ib_bx` refused it, the enclosing function was refused as `sema-gap literal`, and it fell back to a
legacy emitter.

```text
if in value position, branch a bare literal
  ib_bx asks the branch its own type → VcLit → refuse
    whole function refused: sema-gap literal: expr Num
      legacy emitter (twins only)
        aggregate literal in argument position built into the SAME frame slot
        as the nested call's own aggregate → delivers p15.k3 where 1 is due   #973
```

`ib_value_ctx` folds a literal at `k` and otherwise builds the branch and coerces it, so for every
non-literal branch nothing changes.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `alatyr ir` on the repro — `fn …::g13 NotYet(sema-gap literal: expr Num, …:10:57)`, the
  span being the `1000` in `else { 1000 }`. Running it: x86_64 **2**, wasm **2**, aarch64 **3**,
  riscv64 **3** — a silent wrong value, no diagnostic.
- **After:** `functions=5 built=5 notyet=0 sema_gaps=0 verify_failed=0`, `g13 Built`; running the same
  two programs: **2 / 2 / 2 / 2**.
- The emitted aarch64 shows the mechanism the fallback produced (`str x0,[x29,#64]` twice — outer
  literal's `k1`, then the inner literal reusing the slot; `bl g8` returns that word).
- Dev build succeeds: `build OK — 1 611 408 GAS lines` for `package.al`. (No before/after comparison is
  offered: the 1 611 402 figure quoted elsewhere is `scripts/full.sh`'s fixpoint count, a different
  measurement of a different compilation, so the two numbers are not comparable.)

## Prediction, made before the gate ran

This changes every `if` in value position that the builder accepts, so **some corpus rows are expected to
move**, and they must all be wins: a twin that trapped, or answered a clobbered word, now answers what
x86_64 and the model answer. Rows that do NOT move are the majority — most programs have no `if` in
value position with a bare literal branch. The xbackend ratchet is expected to **hold or fall**, never
grow; if it grows, the change is wrong and this PR must not land. The oracle will be regenerated only
after the moved rows are read one by one and confirmed to match x86_64.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — four characters in one predicate, plus fixtures.

**Blast radius:** functions with an `if` in value position, built through the shared IR (the twins today;
x86_64 at the flip). No change to refusals that were already `Built`, because a branch that had a type
takes the same coercion path as before.

_Requested by **kuro** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DiwcN7wGvg1jw7GRU3y9Bc?thread=cmsg_01DiwcN7wGvg1jw7GRU3y9Bc7nn2SkvJFrfinhRQq32kdh)_

Before: players couldn't delete their account, block anyone, or report a photo or comment, and the game had no privacy policy. Google Play requires all of these for an app with accounts and user posts.

After: a player can delete their account in the app, on the website, or on a delete-account web page. They can block a player, which works both ways: no photos, comments, likes, friend requests or notifications between the two. Photos, comments and players can be reported. Once three different players report a photo or comment, it is hidden from everyone but its owner until a moderator looks at it. Moderators (`ADMIN_USERNAMES`) get a 🚩 Reports panel on the website and a push notification for each new report. From the panel they can keep the content, remove it, or delete the player's account. A privacy policy is served at `/privacy`.

How: `backend/app/safety.py` holds the new routes (`DELETE /me`, `POST /me/delete` for Android, `/blocks`, `/reports`, `/admin/reports`) and the delete-account page. There are two new tables (`blocks`, `reports`) and a nullable `hidden` column on album photos and comments, all added by the existing `create_all`/`add_missing_columns`. The block and hidden filters go into the existing visibility helpers in `social.py` (`shown_to`, `_visible_photo`, the profile and comment lists) and the activity feed in `notices.py`. The policy lives in `docs/privacy.html` next to `docs/delete-account.html`, so GitHub Pages can publish both at addresses that stay up when the PC is off. `docs/play-store.md` lists the Play Console answers.

Testing: `tests/test_safety.py` covers deletion, blocking both ways, report hiding and moderator actions, and the full suite passes (112 passed, 1 skipped). I also drove the website in a headless browser: reported a photo, blocked and unblocked a player, opened the moderator panel and deleted an account, with no page errors. The Android changes are only checked by CI, because this environment can't download the Android SDK.
