author: danielhanchen
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #14792 (block-FP8 small M: fused `act_quant` + narrow-N w8a8 kernel), which is merged on main. This adds a weight-only block-FP8 GEMV for decode and fixes the order in which the two decode kernels are tried.

**GEMV** (decode: one token per sequence, no grad, sm89+ CUDA): reads the fp8 weight once and applies the block scale to unquantized bf16 / fp16 activations with fp32 accumulation. `M` is not specialized. It only takes shapes where it is faster than main's `act_quant` + block GEMM in both timing modes (L2 flushed, and CUDA graph replay with the weight hot in L2):

- narrow outputs only (2N <= K: k / v, o, down);
- on parts with fewer than 100 SMs: weights up to 16M elements, at most 8 decode rows, and at most 2 rows on weights over 8M elements (L2 hot, its 16-row tile becomes compute bound: on L4, 2048x6144 at 4 / 8 / 16 rows took 1.06x / 1.46x / 1.98x main's time before this cap);
- on parts with 100+ SMs: up to 16 rows.

A weight's eligibility (including its row cap) is decided once per scale tensor. Prefill, training, pre-sm89 and ROCm keep the block path. `UNSLOTH_FP8_BLOCK_GEMV=0` disables it.

**Order between the two kernels**, fixed at import:

| devices | eager decode | compiled regions |
|---|---|---|
| any CUDA device with fewer than 100 SMs (L4) | GEMV where it applies, else the fused small-M kernel | GEMV where it applies, else the block GEMM |
| all CUDA devices with 100+ SMs (RTX PRO 6000, B200), Triton block GEMM | fused small-M kernel, called directly; the GEMV only where the fused kernel does not apply | GEMV where it applies, else the block GEMM (the fused kernel is eager only) |
| FBGEMM / torchao block GEMM | GEMV, else that GEMM | same |

With the GEMV tried first everywhere, the combined path was 3% to 4% faster than #14792 alone on L4 but 2% to 3% slower on RTX PRO 6000 (Qwen3-1.7B / 8B FP8, batch 1 / 4 / 8, A/A at most 3.2%), which is why big parts try the fused kernel first.

## End to end decode

Greedy decode, 64 new tokens, torch 2.14.1. Main, #14792 and this PR run from separate checkouts in separate processes, interleaved main, PR, PR, main, 3 rounds (the two PRs alternate order); tok/s is the median, A/A is the largest main vs main gap within a round.

| GPU | model | batch | main tok/s | #14792 / main | this PR / main | this PR / #14792 | A/A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 1 | 14.1 | 1.276 | 1.323 | 1.036 | 1.9% |
| L4 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 4 | 56.8 | 1.273 | 1.314 | 1.033 | 1.9% |
| L4 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 8 | 113.4 | 1.266 | 1.310 | 1.035 | 2.2% |
| L4 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 1 | 10.8 | 1.231 | 1.302 | 1.058 | 1.8% |
| L4 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 4 | 43.2 | 1.245 | 1.312 | 1.053 | 1.9% |
| L4 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 8 | 86.3 | 1.238 | 1.309 | 1.057 | 2.1% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 1 | 55.5 | 1.150 | 1.206 | 1.049 | 2.0% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 4 | 219.8 | 1.153 | 1.201 | 1.042 | 0.6% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-1.7B-FP8 | 8 | 438.5 | 1.151 | 1.198 | 1.041 | 2.0% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 1 | 42.7 | 1.145 | 1.190 | 1.039 | 1.0% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 4 | 170.3 | 1.154 | 1.192 | 1.033 | 1.3% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 8 | 339.2 | 1.153 | 1.191 | 1.032 | 1.4% |

Engagement per 64-token generate: on L4, Qwen3-1.7B runs 5292 GEMV calls at batch 1 (k, v, down) and 3528 at batch 4 / 8 (k, v; down is past its 2-row cap), the rest on the fused kernel. On RTX PRO 6000 every decode projection runs the fused kernel and the GEMV runs 0 times in eager; the gain over #14792 there is host time, since the fused kernel is called directly instead of through `FP8BlockQuantLinear.forward`.

## Kernel timing, both modes

Every shape and row count the GEMV takes, out of 20 swept projection shapes (Qwen3 0.6B to 8B, Llama 8B) at M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, bf16. GEMV time / main's `act_quant` + block GEMM time, 3 interleaved rounds, medians:

| GPU | N x K | rows taken | L2 flushed device time | CUDA graph replay, L2 hot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 | 1024x2048 | 1 to 8 | 0.73 to 0.81 | 0.55 to 0.60 |
| L4 | 1024x2560 | 1 to 8 | 0.69 to 0.74 | 0.54 to 0.73 |
| L4 | 1024x3072 | 1 to 8 | 0.69 to 0.75 | 0.56 to 0.68 |
| L4 | 1024x4096 | 1 to 8 | 0.72 to 0.73 | 0.56 to 0.64 |
| L4 | 2048x6144 | 1 to 2 | 0.92 to 0.94 | 0.84 to 0.93 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 1024x2048 | 1 to 16 | 0.88 | 0.72 to 0.78 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 1024x2560 | 1 to 16 | 0.78 | 0.58 to 0.66 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 1024x3072 | 1 to 16 | 0.76 to 0.80 | 0.58 to 0.65 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 1024x4096 | 1 to 16 | 0.67 | 0.47 to 0.52 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 2048x6144 | 1 to 16 | 0.67 to 0.72 | 0.45 to 0.54 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 2560x9728 | 1 to 16 | 0.60 | 0.38 to 0.46 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 4096x12288 | 1 to 16 | 0.71 to 0.73 | 0.49 to 0.59 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 4096x14336 | 1 to 16 | 0.73 to 0.77 | 0.47 to 0.61 |

Worst cell: 0.94 (L2 flushed) and 0.93 (graph) on L4, 0.88 and 0.78 on RTX PRO 6000. The main vs main A/A spread is 1.2% (flushed) and 1.0% (graph) at the 90th percentile on L4, 2.2% and 5.3% on RTX PRO 6000 (its event timer ticks at about 2 us). Shapes and row counts it does not take are left to the fused kernel (eager) or the block GEMM (compiled); their numbers are unchanged from #14792.

## Accuracy

Layer 0 `mlp` of Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 on real hidden states (16 decode rows from two prompts), against an fp64 evaluation of the same FP8 weights, B200 (100+ SMs, so eager takes the fused kernel and compiled takes the GEMV for `down_proj`):

| rows | eager (fused small-M, quantized activations) | compiled (GEMV for down, unquantized) | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | mean abs 0.0078, rel RMS 2.45% | mean abs 0.0058, rel RMS 1.94% | same as eager |
| 4 | 0.0074, 2.81% | 0.0057, 2.22% | same as eager |
| 8 | 0.0056, 2.81% | 0.0044, 2.24% | same as eager |
| 16 | 0.0047, 2.87% | 0.0037, 2.28% | same as eager |

The compiled path is closer to fp64 at every row count (about 20% lower error); eager and compiled differ by at most 0.039 on these inputs (largest reference value 3.8). From the GEMV's own branch (B200, Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, 32 prompts x 64 tokens): teacher-forced NLL 0.6201 with it vs 0.6219 without, paired difference 95% CI [-0.0050, +0.0013]. Because it skips activation quantization, greedy text differs from main and from #14792 where it runs.

## Tests

28 existing FP8 test files plus `tests/test_fp8_block_small_m.py` and `tests/test_fp8_block_gemv.py` (GEMV against an fp64 oracle, split K, routing, kill switch and device gates, non-128 blocks, cached eligibility, the small-GPU row cap, a compiled single op, both router orders, the training path, compiled and pre-sm89 fallbacks):

| run | 28 existing files | `test_fp8_block_gemv.py` on #14792 | here |
|---|---|---|---|
| L4, torch 2.14.1 | same 4 failing IDs as main | 37 failed | all pass |
| RTX PRO 6000, torch 2.14.1 | same 4 failing IDs as main | 37 failed | all pass |
| RTX PRO 6000, torch 2.10.0 | same 4 failing IDs as main | 37 failed | all pass |
| B200, torch 2.14, both new files | | | 108 passed |

The 4 failures are in `test_modelopt_fp8_loading.py` and are pre-existing on main. The small-M tests pin the GEMV off and the GEMV tests pin the fused kernel off, so each still tests its own kernel.

## torch.compile

`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8`, LoRA r 8: 3 training steps, HF generate at batch 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then layer 0's `mlp` and `k_proj` compiled at decode batch 1 to 16 plus a prefill:

| torch | GPU | training breaks / recompiles | decode breaks / recompiles | compiled modules breaks / recompiles | Triton variants after batch 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.14.1 | L4 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | GEMV 2, fused small-M 3, w8a8 GEMM 8 |
| 2.14.1 | RTX PRO 6000 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | fused small-M 3, w8a8 GEMM 8 |
| 2.10.0 | RTX PRO 6000 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | mlp 3 (same on main), k_proj 0 / 0 | fused small-M 3, w8a8 GEMM 8 |
